author: jthingelstad
body:
The last of four changes for judging the Discord posts Elixir cannot see (after #511, #513, #514). Admin ▸ Discord is Jamie's view; this is the agent's path to the same evidence.

- **`{discord_review}`**, a migrate read through `npm run op`: the window's summary, one destination whole (a clan tag or a timeline's account id), or the ratings to answer, 👎 and notes first, each marked `superseded` when the same person rated again. It reuses `quality-report.mjs`, so the op and Admin read the same queries.
- **`.claude/skills/discord-review/`**: the reads, a twelve-line rubric, and where findings go. Every rating is answered as feedback, each cause becomes one issue that quotes ids only (this repository is public), and notes go to the private AGENT-TEAM.
- **`npm run editor-replay -- <run_id>`**: replays one raw run from `discord-runs/`, read locally as cloud-engineer, so there is no IAM change.
  - `--checks-only` puts the run's own answer through today's checks, with no key.
  - Otherwise it runs today's editor with the maintainer's own key from `ELIXIR_REPLAY_ANTHROPIC_KEY`, which is never printed. It never uses a clan's key.
  - Lookups are answered from the run's own record. It posts and writes nothing.
- **The two Codex findings on #514, both fixed:**
  - Only a post that reached the channel can be rated. The door and the list both enforce this.
  - Every rating count reads each person's latest rating only.

Docs: OPERATIONS, DECISIONS, AGENTS (the skills list), infra/AGENTS (scripts), a change note, and a wording tweak in timeline and clan-policy. No MCP or `/api/v1` change, no migration, no contract bump.

author: matttgic
body:
## Constat (diagnostic #46 et #47)
- La pagination globale (`/{sport}/events`, les 30 prochains matchs toutes ligues confondues) ne rattachait que 0 à 4 matchs Revue par bookmaker. Le KHL, le base-ball coréen ou la D2 algérienne passent avant la NHL ou la Premier League.
- PS3838 (133 ligues de foot) ne rattachait aucun match de foot.
- L'endpoint par ligue rattache **tous** les matchs Revue des 48 h testées. Côté PS3838 : Premier League 1/1, Liga 1/1, Serie A 2/2. Côté NHL : PMU 3/3.
- Les bookmakers français renvoient des erreurs 429 sur des séries d'appels, même à une requête par seconde.

## Changements
- **Collecte par ligue** (`scan`) : la collecte lit le catalogue `/{sport}/leagues` de chaque bookmaker, puis `/{sport}/leagues/{ligue}/events` pour les seules ligues suivies.
  - `league_matches` compare le nom sans pays ni saison et vérifie le pays quand il est fourni. Il couvre les 30 cas réels du diagnostic, par exemple « England - Premier League » accepté et « Egypt - Premier League » refusé, « Espagne LaLiga » accepté et « LaLiga 2 » refusé, « MLB Cotes des séries » refusé.
  - Si le catalogue échoue ou ne contient pas la ligue, la collecte revient à la pagination pour ce bookmaker et ce sport (`fallback_paging`).
- Un même match vu sous deux noms de ligue chez un même bookmaker n'est compté qu'une fois.
- **429** : jusqu'à 3 nouvelles tentatives dans `_get_json`, en respectant `Retry-After` (30 s maximum). Les erreurs restent sans URL ni clé.
- **NHL** : « prolongations et penaltys inclus » (Betclic) est reconnu comme incluant la prolongation. « Including Overtime » (PMU) l'était déjà.
- Diagnostic dans le rapport : `collection_mode`, `league_names`, `fallback_paging`.

## Tests
- Nouveaux tests :
  - seules les ligues suivies sont interrogées, sans doublon par bookmaker ;
  - retour à la pagination quand la ligue est absente du catalogue ;
  - nouvelle tentative après un 429 avec `Retry-After`, puis abandon propre ;
  - aucun appel quand aucun match n'est à venir.
- Le test de cadence n'appelle plus le réseau : `_get_json` est désormais simulé. La suite `test_pulsescore_v2` passe de 1,9 s à 0,01 s.
- 889 Python et 37 JS passent en local.

author: bompus
body:
Submissions that report a measured result now open with the benefit and a chart of it, so a reader sees the win before the background.

Before this change, `hr-writing-pr` told the author to lead the body with the problem and made the chart optional, and #218 told authors that most comments should stay text. In practice the figure landed in a verification section and a PR such as a 32% faster clean Android build had no chart or number above the fold.

## Change

- `hr-writing-pr`: the body opens with one benefit sentence (the qualified figure and workload, or for a bug who hits it and what they see). The title uses the words of the person who feels the change. A qualified result gets a headline chart under that sentence.
- `skills/hr-writing-pr/scripts/benefit-chart.py` (new): reads a JSON spec and writes a dark PNG with labeled units, zero-based bars and a benefit badge per row. Rows inside the reporting band read "no clear change", and a regression is red. It prints the alt text for the upload, and `--table` prints the same values as a Markdown table so the body carries a text version of the chart. It rejects negative values. It needs matplotlib and says so when it is missing.
- `rules/references/thread-visuals.md`: a qualified measured result is the stated exception to text-first. Every value in a visual must also appear as body text, because many readers are agents that cannot parse images. A comment that only adds data to a thread stays text and a table.
- `rules/modifiers/upstream-contributions.md`: defects are titled by what the person sees and how often. New step 6 asks the author to update the title and opening lines when a later measurement moves the headline.

## Verification

- `bun test skills/hr-writing-pr`: 4 pass, 0 fail (the full `bun test skills/` gave 255 pass before the review fixes). The new tests cover labels, the zero baseline, negative values and `--table`. The first run of the new test caught a real bug, a 30% regression labeled "30% lower". It is fixed and covered.
- `node --test test/*.test.mjs`: 125 pass, 7 skipped, 0 fail.
- `oxfmt --check` on the changed files passes. `rules/references/squash-landing.md` already fails the format check on `main` and is not touched here.
- I read the rendered chart for five rows (four improvements and one no-change row): labels, bar scale and badges are legible.

## Admission criteria

- **Review:** cubic and CodeRabbit raised 11 threads; all were valid and are fixed in 61938e4, replied to and resolved.
- **Observed failure:** in a review of one contributor's open submissions to two large public projects, 6 of 46 had an image, and the measured figure was usually in a verification section. A bare mechanism title ("skip hidden ancestor payloads") told a reader nothing about the win.
- **Existing alternative:** `hr-writing-pr` already preferred a chart, and the `before-and-after` skill formats attachments. Nothing drew the chart, so each one was hand built or skipped.
- **Activation limits:** only a measured result outside the reporting band. A single small change, or rows that are all no clear change, skip it. Comments that add data to a thread stay text.
- **Cost:** about 15 lines of skill and rule text, and one script that needs matplotlib. Without matplotlib the script says so and the author follows the text rule alone.
- **Placement:** the skill owns the script and the writing rule. The thread-visuals reference and the upstream rule carry only the exception and the title rule.

Not covered: adopting this into the host overlay that pins this repository, and the T3 Code specific wording, which lives in a separate repository.

- [x] The checks in the README's Development section pass.
- [x] A change users will notice has a `CHANGELOG.md` entry under `Unreleased`.
- [x] Nothing names a private project or repository, a local path, a home directory or a credential.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Added a charting tool that creates before-and-after visuals with matching alt text and an optional results table. It identifies whether measured changes exceed the reporting threshold and labels small changes as having no clear change.
* **Documentation**
  * Clarified when qualified measured results warrant a headline chart and when reports should remain text and table only. Visual values, labels, and caveats must also appear in the body text.
  * Updated guidance for leading with benefits, titling performance and defect reports, and revising titles and opening lines when headline measurements change.

author: rfontes1987
body:
Step 1 of RFC 0045 (`docs/rfcs/0045-csv-column-map.md`), the whole implementation plan.

## What changed

- `packages/plugin-blob/docs/csv.port.json`: `#parse` and `#write` each accept `columns`, an optional, static object open to strings, after `type`. The two operation descriptions say what it does, in the RFC's words.
- `packages/plugin-blob/src/index.ts`: one function, `headersOf`, computes the header of each field (the key that maps to it, else the field's own name) for both operations. It throws before any byte is read or written, so a bad map fails the node as a fault on every call, even on an empty file. `RowReader` reads each trimmed header cell into the field whose header it is. `lines` writes each field under its header, in the shape's order.
- `packages/plugin-blob/test/blob.test.ts`: the handler tests the RFC lists.
- `packages/plugin-blob/README.md`: the line for `#parse` and `#write`.

No schema change, no checker rule, no `check` on `@blob`. The compiler's P001 and G004 judge the map's form, as before. A repeated header in the file (`a,a`) is unchanged; that is #951.

## Decided during implementation

A key with spaces around it (`" average-revs"`) fails both operations, with the other faults of the map:

```
csv columns: ' average-revs' has spaces around it, and a header cell is read trimmed, so it never matches; write 'average-revs'
```

I chose to fail rather than trim. A trimmed key would read correctly, but `#write` would then write a header that differs from the key the author wrote. Failing keeps one spelling and keeps the round trip exact.

Closes #984

author: im-fran
body:
## Summary

Adds `/editor`, where anyone can create content for Netherite without signing in and turn it into a pull request.

- **Theme editor**: start blank or from a gallery theme. Edit name, appearance, the 5 color pairs, the 6 callout categories and typography; each can stay unset to keep the app default. Live light/dark preview and WCAG contrast warnings with the app's own rules (`ThemeAccessibility.swift`). Blocks names already in the gallery and built-in theme names, which the app ignores.
- **Template editor**: start blank or from any gallery template. Edit language, name, ID (derived from the name), description, SF Symbol, tags and body, with placeholder buttons. Blocks a template that already exists in that language, and a Spanish one without its English version (the catalog build would fail).
- **Output**: copy, download, or **Propose on GitHub**, which opens GitHub's new-file page with the file filled in at its catalog path (`public/themes/…` / `public/templates/<lang>/…`). GitHub forks the repo and opens the PR; only that step needs a GitHub account. Files too long for a URL (over ~8,000 chars) fall back to download. Drafts persist in `localStorage`.
- **Refactor**: the template parser moved to `src/app/catalog-format.ts` (plus `compose`, `slug`, `contrast`) and is shared by the editor and `scripts/build-catalog.mjs`, which Node runs directly (`"type": "module"`). New self-tests cover `compose` ↔ `parse`, `slug` and `contrast`. The theme preview is now a shared component.
- **Routing**: `/editor` is a path check in `App` instead of adding `@angular/router`. `wrangler.jsonc` sets `not_found_handling: "single-page-application"`, so unknown paths now serve `index.html` instead of a 404.
- Nav link, "Create your own" links under both galleries, EN/ES strings and the README are updated.

## Test plan

  - [x] Theme flow: start from Ocean, rename, change a color; the JSON, the path, the contrast warning and the GitHub link are correct

author: lbds137
body:
## Summary

Both commit guards now judge the checkout a commit actually lands in.

**TASK-1216: `board-commit-branch-gate.sh`.** The gate read only line 1 of `lib/branch_switch.py` (the leading switch), so it judged the hook's own checkout even for `git -C <other worktree> commit`. That went wrong in both directions:
- A board commit into a develop worktree, made from a feature checkout, was blocked.
- A board commit into a feature worktree, made from a develop checkout, passed, and the commit stranded on the feature branch.

The gate now reads lines 2 and 3 (commit directory and inertness) and ports the develop guard's whole cross-checkout mechanism:
- Another repository is silent when every other segment is inert.
- A sibling worktree becomes the judged checkout: its branch, staged set, `-a` set and dirty fallback.
- A sibling whose branch a non-inert segment could move is judged as a feature branch, which blocks a board-only commit. That is this gate's fail-closed direction.
- The `?` sentinel keeps the live evaluation, because the develop guard already blocks that command (its probe row "cross-repo: an unreadable directory change before the commit blocks").

**TASK-1217: both guards.** The Bash tool keeps its cwd between calls, so both guards now start from the payload `.cwd` instead of the project dir:
- A bare commit from a shell sitting in a sibling worktree is judged as that worktree.
- One from a shell in another repository is silent.
- A relative commit directory resolves against that start.
- With no usable cwd, the guards fall back to the project dir.

Runtime premise: after one Bash call ran `cd packages/tooling`, the next call was blocked by `cwd-drift-guard` naming `packages/tooling`. That guard reads the same `.cwd` field, so `.cwd` is the persisted shell cwd.

The develop guard now also `cd`s to the judged checkout's toplevel before its toplevel-relative reads (`git diff -- <file>`), so a shell sitting in a subdirectory reads the right paths. Its unreadable banner now leads with `git -C <absolute dir> commit` and says why the override cannot apply. The awkward header sentence is rewritten.

## Acceptance

TASK-1216, quoted: "board probe rows for git -C into a develop sibling (passes), git -C into a feature sibling (blocks), and the sentinel (blocks)."
- Develop sibling: met (board row "cross-checkout" 1, exit 2 → 0).
- Feature sibling: met (row 2, exit 0 → 2).
- **Sentinel: partial, by design.** The board gate keeps the live evaluation for `?`, and the develop guard is the one that blocks it. The board row pins exit 2 on its feature fixture.

TASK-1217, quoted: "probe rows with a payload cwd in a develop sibling (bare commit blocks), in a feature sibling from a develop project dir (passes), in another repository (silent), and with no cwd (unchanged); the board gate mirrors them."
- Met: the develop probe's "cwd:" rows. The board gate's mirror rows are 9–12.
- No cwd: existing rows unchanged. The probe folds `PAYLOAD_CWD` in only when it is set.

## Verification

Main tree, at the final diff:
- `board-commit-branch-gate.probe.sh`: 127 PASS, 0 FAIL at the final head, ca6ab37e1. It was 124 before the round-1 rows.
- `develop-code-commit-guard.probe.sh`: 278 PASS, 0 FAIL at ca6ab37e1.
- `branch_switch_test.py`: OK.
- `bash -n` passes on every hook.
- `pnpm format:check` passes.
- The `pnpm quality` tail from `backlog:lint` through `guard:gate-parity` passes, including `guard:hook-probes`.

No existing probe row changed outcome: the orchestrator compared each PASS label against the base run's labels with `comm -23`, and none was missing.

Canaries on the board gate, each run and then reverted:
- Forcing COMMIT_DIR empty reddened 7 cross-checkout rows (measured before round 1 added rows).
- Trusting the untrusted sibling reddened its row.
- Dropping the inert check on the other-repo exit reddened the non-inert other-repo row.

Probe timings stay well under the 240 s ceiling: board 18 → 24 s, develop 45 → 58 s.

## Review rounds

- **Round 1**, ca6ab37e1:
  - Three new board probe rows: a subdirectory cwd, a foreign shell with an untrusted develop sibling, and `cd -` on develop (exit 0).
  - The SWITCH_TARGET clear now cites its rule row and hedges the untested cd/pushd case.
  - Two comment lines rewrapped.
- **Round 2**, all optional:
  - **Finding 1**, a sibling start plus a non-inert segment plus another repo keeps the start checkout. **Declined**: the develop guard behaves the same way, because a start inside this repository is never foreign, so its fallback doesn't apply. The judged checkout is a real checkout of this repo, which the reviewer also called acceptable.
  - **Finding 2**, the cwd/sibling resolution is duplicated across the two hooks. **Filed** as part of TASK-1218. That task rewrites the same resolution in both hooks, so the shared `lib/` extraction belongs in that diff.
  - **Finding 3**, comment pinning. "A bare commit from a shell in another repository is silent" is pinned by the probe rows "cwd: a bare commit from a shell in another repository is silent" (board) and the develop "cwd:" another-repo row. The cd/pushd case stays hedged.
  - **Finding 4**, a direct `.cwd` probe. **Already done, and not an inference**: a `cd packages/tooling` call followed by a blocked next call that named `packages/tooling` is a runtime observation of the payload field (see Summary).

## Residue

- No purpose canary was run for the develop guard's cwd start in `.claude/hooks/develop-code-commit-guard.sh`. **Declined**: each of its "cwd:" rows was red at the base hook (before → after exits recorded in the orchestrator's table: 2→0, 0→2, 2→0, 0→2), which is the same falsification evidence.

author: boydsoftprez
body:
## Why

"losing the Core lets go of CAT changes and their words, and asks it for nothing" (`ToolsPagesTests.catDisconnect`) failed once on the hosted simulator: job 114574074580, the pull_request run of PR 390, at `ToolsPagesTests.swift:839`, `await settle { cat.reason == nil && cat.global != nil }`, after 30.2 s. It is a race in the test, not a deadline. One line of the test changes. Nothing in the app or in the kit's sources changes.

## Cause

The test drops the link, checks what the CAT page let go, then waits for the app to be connected again before the fake Core sends its CAT records. That wait asked only for `model.connection == .connected`.

Two parts of the app hear of a lost link at different moments:

- The mirror loses it at once (`MirrorStore.linkLost` clears `isSnapshotComplete`), and the CAT page's "not connected" is read from the mirror. That is the check the test makes right after the drop.
- The app model sets `connection` later in the same handler (`AppModel.handle`), after it has waited on the command client and the media client.

So for a moment the page says "not connected" while `connection` still says connected, from the session that just dropped. On a fast machine that moment is over before the test gets to its wait. On a slow one the wait is true the instant it is asked, the fake sends the CAT records to the connection that was dropped, the app's new session never gets them, and the 30 s wait cannot hold.

The hosted job shows exactly that, by the app's own clock:

| Time (UTC) | What |
| --- | --- |
| 23:21:11.202 | the test starts |
| 23:21:11.360 | "The link to the Core was lost" |
| about 23:21:11.39 | the 30 s wait begins (it failed after 30.208 s of test, at 23:21:41.396) |
| 23:21:12.375 | the app redials, one second after the loss |
| 23:21:12.377 | "Signed in to the Core" |
| 23:21:17.394 | two of the app's record stream requests time out, 5 s into the new session: the app is running, and on its new session |
| 23:21:41.396 | the wait gives up |

The 60 s wait for "connected" took no time at all: the next wait began 0.03 s after the loss and a second before the app had even redialed. In the eleven passing job logs on file the same test takes 1.206 to 1.284 s, because it waits out that one second before the redial.

## The change

The wait now asks for `model.connection == .connected && model.mirror.isSnapshotComplete`. A lost link clears the second at once and only the new session's snapshot sets it again, so the old session's state can no longer answer the wait. With the longer comment the wait that failed moves from line 839 to line 841. The neighboring test `catLogReconnect` was already safe in the same way: its wait also asks for `cat.logReason == nil`, which only the new session gives.

## Shown able to fail, both ways

With the app changed on purpose (temporary, never committed), on the local simulator (iPhone 17, iOS 27.0):

- The cause, reproduced with a delay put in on purpose and not with load: with the app model made 150 ms late to take in a session state, the test as on main failed 3 times of 3, each time at `ToolsPagesTests.swift:839` on the same expectation as the hosted job and after 30 s. The app's log has the hosted job's shape: the link lost, the redial 1.0 s later, and the two record stream requests timing out about 5 s after that. Under the same lateness the changed test passed 10 times of 10.
- The behavior the test checks, broken: with the CAT model keeping its held changes and its words through a lost link, the changed test failed after 1.9 s with two issues: `:830`, the check right after the loss (`cat.note(.channel(1)) == nil` was false), and `:842`, the check after the changed wait that nothing is held from before (channel 4 still showed the change the Core never answered).

## Runs

- The whole "Tools pages" suite (51 tests) with the changed test and an unchanged app, five times in a row in one launch: no issue recorded, 50.5 s in all.
- The Mac was busy with other work during all of these runs (load average 43 to 71). Nothing was added to load it.

## Other tests that drop the link

All 37 uses of `dropLink()` in the app's tests (eight files) were read for the same flaw. `ConnectionFlowTests` waits on `flow.linkLost`, which is set from the app model's own state, so it cannot run ahead of it. `TransmitScreenTests.linkLostWhileKeyed` first waits for the PTT's "link lost" state, which the app model sets after `connection` in the same handler. `catLogReconnect` is covered above. The others do not wait for a reconnect. Only this test had the flaw in a form that can fail.

J.J. Boyd ~ KG4VCF

author: jmvbambico
body:
Stacked on #24 — base is `integration/og-session-fixes`, so this diff contains only the two features and the review fix.

Two capabilities the operator asked for while watching the previous batch land, plus one blocking defect found in review and fixed.

## F — a herdr space for every session

herdr showed one space. The Omnigent web sidebar showed eleven sessions. The bridge projected only sessions with a **live runner**, and on this machine exactly one of eleven roots had one — so every past conversation was invisible in the terminal.

Now every non-archived root gets a space, labelled with Omnigent's own auto-generated title. The offline-runner refusal is scoped to sub-agents, which keeps fan-out behaviour byte-for-byte unchanged.

**Nothing resurrects a dead session.** `workspace_create` opens a space whose first tab holds a plain shell, and the pane is given `og chat --resume <id>` as **unsubmitted text** — the trailing newline is what submits, so omitting it leaves the line waiting for the operator's Enter. A new `pane_send_text` carries the wire call and `pane_run` delegates to it with `+ "\n"`, so there is one statement of the method and two spellings of "submit".

`og chat` already forwarded `--resume` to `omnigent run`; that was verified, not assumed, and needed no change.

No cap by default (`0` or absent). A positive `herdr_session_space_cap` caps new history spaces, newest-first; a live root is never subject to it, and lowering the cap governs new spaces without closing open ones — documented and tested, because a space the operator is working in should not vanish on a config edit.

A root whose workspace directory no longer exists is skipped: a pane is a shell, and a shell in a deleted worktree dies on open.

## G — `og sessions`

```
og sessions                   id, title, status, runner, workspace, age
og sessions --all             include archived
og sessions --archive <id>    PATCH {"archived": true}   — reversible
og sessions --unarchive <id>
og sessions --delete <id>     DELETE                     — irreversible
       --yes                  the only way past confirmation
       --force                the only way past the safety refusals
       --delete-branch        the only path to worktree remove --force + branch -D
```

This lives under its own verb rather than as `og chat --delete`. `og chat` starts and resumes conversations; hanging an irreversible flag off it means a mistyped `og chat` can destroy work.

`DELETE /v1/sessions/{id}` tears down tasks, runner resources, session files and the conversation row, so the guards are deliberate: confirmation requires typing the word `delete`, read from stderr; no tty **errors** rather than reading a line, so `echo delete | og sessions --delete x` cannot delete anything; `--yes`, `--force` and `--delete-branch` are refused rather than ignored when `--delete` is absent; and deletion is refused for a session with a live runner or the one the caller is inside.

Archiving is the gentler path and genuinely useful here — `should_project` already excludes archived sessions, so archiving removes a session from herdr's spaces without destroying it.

### Two API facts worth recording

Listing rows carry **neither** `workspace` nor `runner_online` — both are detail-only. And `include_archived` defaults to **false** server-side (401 rows vs 439 measured), so archived sessions were already invisible to og's listing walk.

## The defect review caught

`_delete` discarded `fetch_listing`'s `truncated` flag and resolved prefixes against only the rows fetched. A prefix matching one fetched session **and** one unfetched session was reported unique, no ambiguity warning fired, and after confirmation it would have deleted the wrong conversation. This machine has 401 non-archived rows against caps the walk can really hit.

A prefix is now refused outright when the walk did not finish. Exact ids still resolve (ids are unique, so an unfetched row cannot shadow one) and a full id passes through verbatim, which is the escape hatch and works precisely when the listing is incomplete. **`--force` does not override it** — `--force` is scoped to two facts about a *session*; truncation is a fact about the *listing*, and letting one flag cover both would reopen the hole.

Archive/unarchive warn and proceed instead, since a PATCH flips one boolean and the two flags undo each other by name.

## Gate

```
947 passed in 33.76s          (base 887 → +15 spaces, +34 sessions, +11 review fix)
bash -n bin/og && bash -n install.sh        clean
shellcheck -S error bin/og install.sh       clean
```

Merging F onto the base conflicted in `installer/og_herdr.py` — F was cut before the project-filing feature, and both add to `Bridge.__init__` and `main()`. Resolved keep-both, and the resolution caught auto-merge silently dropping the `filed + …` fold from a new early return in `_added`, which would have lost the filing warning for dead roots while still compiling and passing tests.

## Review

Independent different-vendor reviewer (openai/codex; implementers opencode/zen and deepseek/cmdcode). It found the truncation defect above as blocking, that was fixed, and the re-review verified the fix reaches every route to DELETE and that `--force` cannot bypass it.

One non-blocking note stands: on a truncated listing, archive/unarchive proceeds after warning rather than prompting. Reversible by design, and the warning names the id and the undo flag.

author: tupe12334
body:
## Summary
polyhook has no `.github/dependabot.yml`, so no dependency in any SDK gets automatic version or security updates. The sibling repo steplock already runs Dependabot.

This PR adds weekly Dependabot updates for:
- `cargo` — root workspace (`core`, `packages/sdk-rust`)
- `npm` — `packages/sdk-ts` (pnpm lockfile)
- `gomod` — `packages/sdk-go` (wazero)
- `uv` — `packages/sdk-python` (wasmtime)
- `nuget` — `packages/sdk-dotnet` (Wasmtime, test deps)
- `github-actions` — workflows

Settings match steplock: `dependencies` label, `chore` commit prefix, max 5 open PRs per ecosystem. `gomod` is added to the cspell word list so the Spell Check job passes.

## Why
`cargo audit` reports advisories only for Rust and only weekly. The TS, Go, Python and .NET SDKs had no update path at all.

This adds `publishConfig: { access: "public", provenance: true }` to `package.json`, and removes the now-redundant `NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE` env var from the release job.

The failed run left a `v1.0.0` tag on `main`, but nothing was published to npm or GitHub Releases. If the tag stays, merging this releases **1.0.1** and 1.0.0 is never published. Delete the tag before merging to publish **1.0.0** instead.

Closes #9

> この PR は #10（#6、`refactor/6-drop-usage-window`）の上に積んでいます。base は `refactor/6-drop-usage-window` です。#10 を先に merge してください。

## 背景

usage API の `resets_at` を読む `UsageClient.parseDate` は、呼ばれるたびに `ISO8601DateFormatter` を作り、小数秒ありで失敗したら設定を書き換えて小数秒なしで読み直していました（クロージャをその場で実行する書き方）。呼び出しは 1 回の取得で枠の数（3〜4 回）だけなので性能の問題はありません。ただ、読みにくいうえに、`ISO8601DateFormatter` は参照型で `Sendable` でないため共有の `static let` にしにくく、将来 Swift 6 の言語モードに上げるときに書き直しが必要になります。困るのは開発者で、ユーザから見える問題はありません。

## 目的

開発者にとって `parseDate` が読みやすくなり、Swift 6 の言語モードへの移行で書き直す箇所が 1 つ減ります。挙動（小数秒あり・なしの両方を読む、最も近い分に丸める、文字列以外は `nil`）は変えません。

## 方針

Issue は「`Date.ISO8601FormatStyle` が実レスポンスの形式（小数秒 6 桁・`+00:00`）を読めなければ現状維持で close」としていたので、まずそこを確かめました。このマシン（macOS 27 / Apple Swift 6.4）で、小数秒あり・なしの 2 つの style に実レスポンスの形を含む 7 通りの文字列を読ませたところ、どちらの style も日付文字列はすべて読め、`"not a date"` だけが `nil` になりました（下の「判断の経緯」）。読めることが確かめられたので、置き換えを進めました。

置き換えの形は Issue の提案どおり、値型の style を 2 つ `static let` で持ち、小数秒ありから順に試します。上の確認では 1 つの style でも足りていましたが、この寛容さは文書化されておらず、このパッケージが対象にする macOS 13 で同じかは確かめられません。安全側に倒して 2 段構えを残し、その理由をコメントに書きました。丸めの式はそのままです。

Codex 側にも同じ形の日付解析（`CodexRolloutReader.parseTimestamp`）がありますが、Issue の範囲（`UsageClient`）の外なので触っていません（`## 越境・残置判断`）。

<details>
<summary>判断の経緯（grill: 締めるべき曖昧点なし）</summary>

Issue #9 は修正提案と受け入れ条件が具体的で、残っていた不確かさ（`ISO8601FormatStyle` で読めるか）は判断ではなく実験で決まる事実でした。そのため Issue 本文は更新していません（反証・バックアップも取っていません）。

実験（scratchpad で `swiftc` 実行、macOS 27）:

```swift
let frac = Date.ISO8601FormatStyle(includingFractionalSeconds: true)
let plain = Date.ISO8601FormatStyle()
// 各文字列を try? Date(s, strategy: frac / plain) で読む
```

```
2026-10-05T19:59:59.845644+00:00  frac=1791230399.845644  plain=1791230399.845644
2026-10-05T20:00:00+00:00         frac=1791230400.0       plain=1791230400.0
2026-10-05T20:00:00.195640+00:00  frac=1791230400.19564   plain=1791230400.19564
2026-10-04T00:00:00Z              frac=1791072000.0       plain=1791072000.0
2026-10-01T05:00:00.123+00:00     frac=1790830800.1230001 plain=1790830800.1230001
2026-10-05T20:00:00.1+09:00       frac=1791198000.1       plain=1791198000.1
not a date                        frac=nil                plain=nil
```

| 判断 | 採用 | 代替 | 理由 |
|---|---|---|---|
| style の数 | 2 つ（小数秒あり → なし） | 1 つ | 上の結果では 1 つで足りるが、寛容さは文書化されておらず macOS 13 で未確認。Issue の提案どおり |
| 試す順の書き方 | `(try? 小数秒あり) ?? (try? 小数秒なし)` | style の配列を `lazy.compactMap` | 品質パスで、2 つだけなら直接書く方が読みやすいとの指摘を受けて変更 |

</details>

## 設計

| 区分 | 変更 | 受入条件 |
|---|---|---|
| 修正 | `UsageClient.parseDate` を `Date.ISO8601FormatStyle`（`static let` 2 つ）で書き直し。丸めは不変 | AC-1, AC-4, AC-5 |
| テスト | `testParseDateReadsZuluSuffix`（`Z` 形式が読める） | AC-2 |
| テスト | `testParseDateRejectsNonDates`（`42` と `"not a date"` が `nil`） | AC-3 |

## 受入条件

- [x] AC-1 [LOGIC] `testResetTimesRoundToNearestMinute` → 変更なしで通る（`19:59:59.845644+00:00` / `20:00:00+00:00` / `20:00:00.195640+00:00` が同じ時刻になる）
- [x] AC-2 [LOGIC] `UsageClient.parseDate("2026-10-04T00:00:00Z")` → `nil` でない（`Z` 形式も読める）テストがあり、通る
- [x] AC-3 [LOGIC] `UsageClient.parseDate(42)` と `UsageClient.parseDate("not a date")` → どちらも `nil` になるテストがあり、通る
- [x] AC-4 [LOGIC] `grep -n "ISO8601DateFormatter" Sources/Quotaback/Claude/UsageClient.swift` → 0件
- [x] AC-5 [LOGIC] `swift test` → 全テストが通る（62 件、失敗 0）
- [x] （追加）`swift build` のクリーンビルドで警告 0 件（base と同じ）

検証のコマンド出力は UAT レポート（この PR のコメント）に貼ります。

## 評価観点

- 2 段構えを残した判断。このマシンでは 1 つの style で足りていました。macOS 13 で 1 つで足りると確かめられれば、もう一段簡単にできます
- 読める範囲が変わっていないか。上の実験では、`ISO8601DateFormatter` で読めていた形（小数秒 3 桁・6 桁・なし、`Z`、`+00:00`）はすべて読めています。逆に、以前は読めなかった形が新たに読めるようになった可能性はあります（`ISO8601FormatStyle` の方が寛容な場合）。実 API の形は決まっているので実害は無いと見ています
- コメントに「macOS 27 では」と OS 名を書いた点。OS が上がると古くなる記述です

## 発見

1. **Codex 側の `CodexRolloutReader.parseTimestamp` が、変更前の `parseDate` と同じ形（`ISO8601DateFormatter` を毎回作る）のまま残っている**（メモ）。品質パスの「重複」の観点で挙がった。本 PR 起因ではなく既存。統一するなら別 Issue

## 越境・残置判断

- **対象**: `Sources/Quotaback/Codex/CodexRolloutReader.swift` の `parseTimestamp`（同じく `ISO8601DateFormatter` を毎回作って 2 段で読む）
  - **なぜ残置したか**: Issue #9 の範囲は `UsageClient.parseDate` で、本文も「Codex は epoch 秒なので無関係」としている。共通の関数にまとめると Codex のログ読み取りの挙動確認が要り、範囲が広がる
  - **統合時に確認すべきこと**: Swift 6 の言語モードに上げるときは、こちらも同じ書き換えが要る。共通化する場合は Codex のログの `timestamp` の形（小数秒の桁数）も確かめる
- **対象**: 旧形式フォールバック（`parseLegacy` も `parseDate` を呼ぶ）— #7 の領域
  - **なぜ残置したか**: `parseDate` の挙動は変えておらず、旧形式の扱いは #7 で決める
  - **統合時に確認すべきこと**: #7 で旧形式を消しても `parseDate` は `parseLimit` から使われるので残る。`testLegacyFallbackWithoutLimits` を置き換える場合も、`Z` 形式のテストは本 PR の `testParseDateReadsZuluSuffix` が別に持っている
- **対象**: 旧形式の Usage credits 行の重複 — #8 の領域
  - **なぜ残置したか**: 日付解析とは無関係で、挙動を変える修正のため
  - **統合時に確認すべきこと**: 特になし（本 PR は `parse` の構造に触れていない）
- **対象**: #6（PR #10）の branch
  - **なぜ残置したか**: stacked の取り決めにより、#10 作成後は #6 の branch を変更しない。#9 の作業中に #6 の不備は見つかっていない
  - **統合時に確認すべきこと**: #10 を先に merge し、本 PR の base を `main` に付け替えてから merge する

## Summary

Content updates based on the weekly researcher digest (5–11 October 2026).

### Changes made

- **`safety-standards/ai-australian-legislation.md`** — Added the 6 October 2026 Joint Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence hearing outcome: OpenAI Chief Strategy Officer Jason Kwon's in-person apology over the delayed Medicare-breach disclosure, and both OpenAI's and Anthropic's public support for mandatory AI safety-incident reporting. Also added a new, clearly-labelled note on the previously untracked private member's "AI Kill Switch and Data Centre Control Bill 2026" (introduced by independent MP Andrew Gee, 7 September 2026), explicit that it is not government legislation and distinct from the government's own forthcoming Australian Standards for AI and incident-reporting standards.
- **`safety-standards/ai-data-centres-compute-governance.md`** — Updated the National Cabinet AI infrastructure consultation ("Getting it right") from "submissions due" to "closed 9 October 2026", noting no government response timeline has been published yet. Updated the policy timeline table and "what to watch next" list to match.
- **`business-resources/state-territory-ai-resources.md`** — Refreshed the stale "as of June 2026" reference on the NSW Digital Work Systems Act 2026: confirmed as of 11 October 2026 the core AI/automation WHS duty still has not commenced (only the entry-permit-holder guideline provisions are in force).

All three pages' `last-reviewed` frontmatter dates updated to 2026-10-11.

### Flagged for manual action

- None this cycle — no new pages or nav changes required.

### Not actioned (by design)

- **Privacy Amendment (Personal Data Protection) Bill 2026** — still an exposure draft; not yet introduced to Parliament. Holding off per digest recommendation.
- **Senate AI and Data Centres Inquiry (1 October hearing)** — no new reporting found on hearing substance this cycle; information gap, not a confirmed non-event. No update made.
- **"Kate Pounder — former OpenAI policy liaison" detail** — this cycle's verification search found no support for the claim provisionally noted last cycle. Not published.
- **Capital Brief article on regulator AI-enforcement powers** — appears to be 2024 content resurfacing in search, not a new October 2026 development. Excluded as a quality caution.
- **CRC-P Round 19 outcomes, EU AI Act date conflicts, WA/TAS/NT, Victoria pending bills** — no material change this cycle; unchanged from the 4 October digest.

### Contract version
v1

### Summary
전역 지침(`claude-md/global-guidance.md`)의 "tribunal 심사 단위 축소" 절을 두 군데 고칩니다.

1. **contract 9~11 단락 앞에 적용 조건을 붙였습니다.**
   - 라이브 Tribunal은 report contract 7(핀 `9cc21c2`)인데, 지침은 contract 9~11의 전체 suite 흐름(`final-validation-seal` 등)을 조건 없이 설명합니다.
   - contract 11 도입을 2026-10-12에 보류했습니다(#196).
   - 그래서 설치본 SKILL.md에 그 단계가 없으면 이 단락을 건너뛰도록 명시합니다.
2. **같은 브랜치에서 FAIL이 이어질 때의 규칙(7번)을 더했습니다.**
   - 2026-10-12 Tribunal 텔레메트리 분석(2026-09-10~10-12, 완료 run 223개, 52.5시간)에서 두 브랜치가 반복 심사로 시간을 많이 썼습니다. 각각 14 run 7.6시간, 12 run 3.9시간이고 합쳐서 약 22%입니다.
   - FAIL 뒤 하나씩 고쳐 다시 올리는 대신, 범위부터 다시 보게 합니다.

### Changes
- contract 9~11 단락 앞에 적용 조건을 추가했습니다. 설치본 `~/.claude/skills/pre-pr-tribunal/SKILL.md`에 `final-validation-seal`이 없으면 그 단락을 건너뛰고 설치본 SKILL.md를 따릅니다. 판별 명령은 `grep -c`이고, 0이면 건너뜁니다.
- 7번 규칙을 추가했습니다. 같은 브랜치에서 FAIL이 두 번 이어지면, 다음 재심사를 제안하기 전에 남은 blocker를 모두 재현해 한 번에 고칠지, 통과 가능한 단위로 나눌지를 먼저 제안합니다. 리뷰 강도를 낮추는 것은 선택지에서 뺐습니다.
- 다른 절이나 파일은 바꾸지 않았습니다(1 file, +11).

### Validation
- 판별 명령 `grep -c final-validation-seal ~/.claude/skills/pre-pr-tribunal/SKILL.md`
  - 라이브 핀(contract 7): ugrep과 `/usr/bin/grep` 모두 0
  - 양성 대조, master의 `skills/pre-pr-tribunal/SKILL.md`: 1
- 지침을 참조하는 테스트 4파일 pytest: 변경 전 424 passed, 변경 후 424 passed
  - 대상: `tests/task_nudge/test_change_evidence_guidance.py`, `tests/task_nudge/test_guidance_contract.py`, `tests/test_installer_private_config.py`, `tests/test_jhw_control_host.py`
  - 보존 검사이며, 새 문장을 검출하는 테스트는 아닙니다.
- 커밋 메시지
  - automation `0d97a63`의 validator(`--kind commit --expected-version v1`): PASS
  - commitlint 기준: 제목 50자, 본문 최장 96자로 100자 이내
- 텔레메트리 수치(223 run, 52.5시간, 두 브랜치의 run 수와 시간): 저장소별 `.review/telemetry.json` 모음을 독립 스크립트로 다시 계산해 확인했습니다.
- pre-PR Tribunal 1라운드 PASS(run `e070a2d2aadf6b3e259b76fb5cc4d223`, 335.7초)
  - 대상: head `1839568c953b540c10e01ec4191aeb4ded35f116`, diff SHA-256 `9927c9a9ddfe5b1a872ef18c6b79282481cf685462acf77f8004a2814662cea5`
  - 정책: floor 100, iterative(사용자가 floor 유지를 선택)
  - Reviewer A(opus), B(sonnet) 모두 blocker 0
  - finalize 전에 저장본 검증과 inbox digest 검사를 모두 통과했습니다.

### Impact and risks
- 영향 범위는 지침 문서뿐입니다. 코드, 훅, Tribunal 계약은 바꾸지 않았습니다.
- 머지한 뒤 `claude-config-runtime`에서 `install.sh`를 실행해야 `~/.claude/global-guidance.md`에 반영됩니다. 이때 tribunal 단계가 exit 1로 끝나는 것은 핀 보호에 따른 정상 동작입니다.
- 판별 명령은 설치본 경로가 없는 호스트에서 오류를 내고 개수를 출력하지 않습니다. Tribunal이 없는 호스트에는 해당 절 자체가 적용되지 않으므로 영향은 작다고 봅니다.

### Related issue
- https://github.com/jhw7500/claude-config/issues/196 (관련. 이 PR로 닫지 않습니다)

author: lucas-neuhauss
body:
## Purpose: evidence for an upstream bug report

**Experimental implementation, not a recommendation to merge or deploy.** This draft lives entirely in `lucas-neuhauss/pi-pocket`. It provides a concrete patch, regression tests, and reproducible performance evidence for [upstream issue #57](https://github.com/TannerMidd/pi-pocket/issues/57).

Fork `main` was fast-forwarded to upstream `main`, and this branch is rebased onto `1e8715b45ba172d775994244cf9a62ce19f21112` (0.13.1).

## Reproduction

In a repository with a commit:

1. Replace one line in a tracked file (`+1 −1`).
2. Create an untracked text file with three lines (`+3 −0`).
3. Open Changes; then stage the new file and refresh without changing its contents.

| State | Summary total before patch | New file's diff |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Untracked | `+1 −1` | `+3 −0` |
| Staged, identical content | `+4 −1` | `+3 −0` |

Expected: `+4 −1` in both states. `git status` includes untracked files, while `git diff HEAD --numstat` omits them; missing summary counts become zero in the UI.

## Implementation explored

- Count new files against an empty file using Git's `--no-index --numstat`, preserving Git's binary detection and line-count semantics.
- Merge counts into the existing Changes response, so the top bar, review total, and file tree agree without frontend changes.
- Bound extra Git processes to four globally; share up to 1,000 stat-keyed cache entries across sessions for 30 seconds.
- Invalidate on file metadata changes; recheck attributes on expiry. Failed comparisons are not cached and do not fail the whole review.
- Handle repositories before their first commit, and filenames containing tabs.
- Remove `-U3` from summary-only flags: it enables full patch output even with `--numstat`. Keep it for actual diffs.

## Evidence and trade-offs

- [Regression tests](https://github.com/lucas-neuhauss/pi-pocket/blob/experiment/untracked-change-counts/test/changes-counts.test.ts)
- [Runnable benchmark](https://github.com/lucas-neuhauss/pi-pocket/blob/experiment/untracked-change-counts/test/bench-changes.ts)
- [Benchmark results, methodology, p95, environment and limitations](https://github.com/lucas-neuhauss/pi-pocket/blob/experiment/untracked-change-counts/test/bench-changes-results.md)

Original seven-sample benchmark on an M4 Pro, macOS, Node 22.23.3, Git 2.50.1:

| New files | First count after patch | Cached refresh |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 10 | 87 ms | 48 ms |
| 100 | 360 ms | 49 ms |
| Near the 500-file display cap | 1,577 ms | 53 ms |
| 10 MiB text + 1 MiB binary | 84 ms | 49 ms |

Baseline refreshes were approximately 50 ms but omitted new-file counts. Cold means application cache misses, not flushed OS caches. The 500-new-file fixture includes 10 tracked modifications, so only 490 new files are counted under the existing display cap. Cache expiry, eviction, mutations, or restart require recounting. **Caching preserves ordinary refresh performance but does not eliminate substantial cold-count cost.**

Reproduce from this PR branch:

```sh
npm ci
node --test test/changes-counts.test.ts test/changes.test.ts
node test/bench-changes.ts --runs=7 --warmup=2 --baseline=origin/main
```

The checked-in historical report pins its original baseline (`6067422…`). The count implementation on latest upstream `main` has the same source hash as that original baseline. A three-sample post-rebase smoke benchmark against `origin/main` also passed all count assertions; it ran concurrently with the suite and is not used as the clean performance comparison.

## Validation

- Post-rebase focused Changes tests: **18/18 pass**.
- TypeScript check and ESLint pass.
- Isolated headless mobile check previously verified top bar, review and individual-file counts before/after staging.
- Previous full suite: **458/461 pass** with canonical macOS TMPDIR. Browser-frame delivery and Alt+A failures also reproduced on clean pre-rebase HEAD; a swipe failure passed in isolation.
- **Full suite on the rebased branch is running; results will be added here.**

## Out of scope

This does not introduce a session-start baseline or line-level attribution. Changes still reviews uncommitted checkout changes against HEAD, and π-only still filters whole files Pi touched. Those UX semantics can be mentioned separately in the upstream issue, without making them requirements of this counting fix.

No production deployment or server restart has been performed.

author: helldragger
body:
Changes for the submission version of the manuscript (the manuscript itself is in the private repository), and removal of redistributed third-party data.

**Third-party raw data**
- `data/raw_data.zip` (Mind PDFs; suicide-risk, Reddit depression, Dreaddit and Twitter datasets; CounselChat; Kaggle FAQ and intents) is no longer in the repository: it is git-ignored, and it was also removed from the entire history (all branches rewritten and force-pushed on 2026-10-11).
- README documents the expected layout and states that the evaluation sets, results and trained classifier are included; tables and paper numbers regenerate without the raw data (the CounselChat row count is now saved in `results/eval_sets.json`).
- The Kaggle notebook finds an attached private `raw_data.zip`; the CI Space deployment is skipped without raw data; DEPLOY.md and the missing-data error explain how to supply it.

**Generated paper text and tables**
- No references to a supplementary file and no file names in captions or generated sentences; pointers go to the code repository.
- Tables are placed `[htbp]` so several fit on a page.
- Captions rewritten to be readable on their own: what the table shows, its run, and every abbreviated column defined.

body:

_Requested by **Ziad** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_016UdKZkty2w4pWZwpXCRj2Y?thread=cmsg_016UdKZkty2w4pWZwpXCRj2YCV3auryYnKajb3xy1DB7JU)_

## What and why

Before: 123 of 128 indexable pages had no canonical, so #350's `?platform=` made every page reachable under five more URLs; `og:url` pointed at the homepage on 125 pages, so every shared docs link (including each campaign's `/docs/platforms`) previewed as the homepage; component titles were `Badge — KinetixUI` ×98; there was no BreadcrumbList; component pages had no contextual links to their alternatives; and there was no SEO gate.

After: every indexable page has a clean, absolute, self canonical and a matching `og:url`, query states (`?platform=`, `?filter=`, `?q=`) keep working for visitors but canonicalize to the clean route, component titles and descriptions are generated from the manifest (`Button component for React, Angular, SwiftUI, Compose & Flutter`), docs pages emit a BreadcrumbList built from the visible trail, component pages link related components, platform pages open with a derived "at a glance" block, and `pnpm check:seo` plus a rendered browser check guard all of it in CI.

SEO Phase 1: the technical and metadata foundation for organic visitors who reach Qualified Evaluation. Full baseline, findings P0–P3, inventory, crawlability table, perf and gates: [`marketing/seo/SEO-BASELINE.md`](marketing/seo/SEO-BASELINE.md). Intent map, measurement plan and Phase 2 backlog are beside it.

**How.** One metadata helper (`pageMetadata` in `lib/seo.ts`) writes title, description, canonical, OG, Twitter and image together from `siteConfig.url`. Component pages call `componentMetadata(slug, summary)`; every other page reads its row from `ROUTE_SEO` (`lib/route-seo.ts`). `lib/docs-trail.ts` feeds both the visible breadcrumb and its JSON-LD. `lib/related-components.ts` holds an explicit relation table topped up from category neighbours. `PlatformAtAGlance` reads the manifest, `platform-support.ts` and the generated evidence counts. #350's install strip, platform preference and setup links are reused, not duplicated.

## Platforms affected

- [ ] Tokens / foundations (`tokens/`, `style-dictionary/`)
- [ ] Web · React (`packages/ui`)
- [ ] Web · Angular (`packages/ui-angular`) — Preview
- [ ] iOS · SwiftUI (`packages/ui-swiftui`)
- [ ] Android · Compose (`packages/ui-compose`)
- [ ] Flutter (`packages/ui-flutter`)
- [ ] IoT module (`packages/iot`) — Experimental
- [x] Docs site (`apps/web`) / CLI / tooling only

## Checklist

- [x] Uses design tokens — no hardcoded colors; spacing on the grid (new UI uses existing token classes)
- [x] States, dark mode and RTL considered (logical layout; links wrap at narrow widths)
- [x] Accessible name, keyboard and focus behavior considered; no accessibility claims added
- [x] No changeset: `@kinetixui/web` is private; no published package changes
- [x] Docs and the site updated alongside the code
- [x] `components.manifest.json` unchanged
- [x] Generated files not hand-edited

## Verification

Starting SHA: `main` at `bc62ed7` (#350 merged; `fe4221d` and `eb6957f` are ancestors). kinetixui.com is not reachable from the container (proxy 403), so everything is measured on local production builds of `bc62ed7` and this branch.

- [x] `pnpm --filter @kinetixui/web build`, web tests (91 files, 1,938 tests), typecheck, lint (2 pre-existing warnings)
- [x] `pnpm check:seo`: baseline on `bc62ed7` **fails** (canonical-missing 123, component-title 173, component-related 98, og-url 3, og-image 2, link-broken 3); branch: **129 built pages, 128 indexable, 128 sitemap URLs, 15,470 internal links, all 23 rules pass**
- [x] `node scripts/seo-negative-controls.mjs`: **16/16** defects caught by the named rule, each file restored and its sha256 verified, gate green afterwards
- [x] `pnpm check:seo-browser` against `next start`: baseline 12/13 routes fail; branch **13/13 pass**, including `/docs/components/button?platform=SwiftUI` opening on the SwiftUI tab with canonical `/docs/components/button`
- [x] `check:content`, `check:distribution` and 18 other `check:*` gates from `ci.yml` pass locally
- [x] `check:a11y-site` against `next start`: 29 pages × 2 themes × 4 widths × 2 text sizes (464 views), no axe findings, no horizontal overflow
- [x] Perf, median of 3 (base → branch): LCP and long tasks within noise, JS +6 KB on every route, CLS unchanged except an intermittent first-load font reflow that also occurs on `main` (baseline §9)

Not changed: QE, Adoption Intent, #350's platform preference, native publishing, Angular maturity, Core/Pro, IoT behaviour, packages, positioning. Deferred by instruction: docs readability at 1280px with 200% text (backlog). Out of scope but found: `npx @kinetixui/cli add combobox` (install strip) is not a registry item; `/components?filter=` lab CLS 0.346; PageHeader hard-codes `<h1>`.

Review: CodeQL's two URL-prefix alerts in `check-seo.mjs` were real and fixed (e4a877b, NC-15). Codex's one finding (markup in meta descriptions) was real and fixed (d3c0da5, NC-16).

author: arihant2math
body:
Fixes #273

## What
On a wide page (`@xl`, properties beside the conversation) the Properties pane's sticky wrapper had no bounded height, so its lower fields ran past the viewport and could only be reached by scrolling the conversation.

- `PageBody` gains an opt-in `bounded` prop: the body becomes a size container (`@container-size`). Its height already comes from the flex layout (`flex-1 min-h-0`), never from its content, so this changes nothing else. It is used only on the issue/PR **Conversation** view (not the Files/Commits/Checks tabs, and not other pages).
- The Properties wrapper is now `@xl:sticky @xl:top-0 @xl:max-h-page-body @xl:overflow-y-auto @xl:overscroll-contain`. `--spacing-page-body: 100cqh` is a new token: the page body's height, derived from the layout rather than hard-coded.
- `PageBody` is still the page's scroller, so the Timeline's virtualizer `scroller` ref and the router's scroll restoration (`data-scroll-restoration-id="page"`) stay the same. Width, divider, padding and Primer controls are unchanged. Narrow pages keep the stacked flow: `position: static` and `overflow: visible` are checked.

## Tests
- `src/features/issue/IssueView.test.tsx`: new unit test for the structure (the page body stays the scroller and is a size container; the properties wrapper is bounded and scrolls by itself). It **fails without the fix** (`expected false to be true`) and passes with it. jsdom has no layout, so it only checks structure.
- `e2e/forgejo/issue-layout.spec.ts`: new browser test against a real Forgejo. It uses a 1440×560 viewport and an issue with 12 long comments. It checks that:
  - the properties overflow but fit inside the page body;
  - the mouse wheel over Properties scrolls them to the end without moving the page body;
  - the last control is in view;
  - the wheel over the conversation scrolls the page body, while Properties keep their scroll position and stay at the body's top;
  - at 600px the wrapper is `static`/`visible` again.

  I ran it against the QA Forgejo (:3000), serving this branch's `dist` via Playwright request interception. The shared served build was not touched. **Before the fix it fails** (`overflows: false, fits: false`); **after the fix it passes**.
- A one-off browser check on `/dev/fzf/pulls/15` at 1440×900 (not committed):
  - At first: `{pane:0,page:0,overflows:true,fits:true}`.
  - After the wheel over Properties: `{pane:429,page:0,atEnd:true}`.
  - After the wheel over the conversation: `{pane:429,page:35,top:0}`.
  - The Milestone picker near the bottom opens, and Escape returns focus to "Set milestone".
  - At 600px, "All properties" scrolls to the pane and focuses it (`issue-properties`).
- `pnpm run lint`, `pnpm run typecheck` and `pnpm run build` pass.
- `pnpm test`: 1025 passed and 5 failed under heavy machine load (load average ~36). The failures are timeouts in unrelated files. Running them alone, only `Review.test.tsx` "a click on a line…" and `paths.test.ts` "missing-content sentences…" still fail, and **both fail the same way on unmodified `next/primer`**.

## Verification / remaining scope

This PR addresses confirmed renderer and duration breakpoints. Script-to-clip semantic grounding and baked-in voice-over separation require further integration work and must not be represented as solved by these changes. No running Termux process was touched.

author: karlmdavis
body:
Phase 1 of the Immich public-access work (see #154, `roles/immich/SECURITY.md`). Two fixes to fail2ban that stand on their own; both were found while planning the public virtual host, and both matter more once one exists.

## The finding

`fail2ban-client get apache-auth logpath` on eddings prints "No file is currently monitored". The four `apache-*` jails have never watched any traffic, for two stacked reasons:

1. Ubuntu 24.04's `jail.d/defaults-debian.conf` sets `backend = systemd` for every jail, and a journal-backed jail ignores `logpath` entirely (`client/jailreader.py` in fail2ban 1.0.2). Apache does not log to the journal.
2. Even with a file backend, Debian's default paths are `/var/log/apache2/*error.log`; every virtual host in this repository logs under `/var/apache2/<site>/logs/`.

So the planned fix from the analysis (override the path variables in `jail.local`) would have been inert; the backend had to change too, and a file-backed jail whose logpath matches nothing stops fail2ban from loading at all, so the jails can only be enabled where Apache's logs exist.

## What changes

- The `apache-*` jails move out of `roles/base` (which runs on every host, including the workstation) into the apache role, as `/etc/fail2ban/jail.d/apache.conf` with `backend = auto` and both log locations, one per line (fail2ban treats a space in a `logpath` line as the separator before a head/tail flag, not as a second path).
- A `Reload fail2ban` handler in the apache role, notified by the jail file and by "Create Apache Directories": fail2ban expands globs only when a jail starts, so a fresh host or a new virtual host needs a reload after Apache has created the files. Confirmed from `server/server.py` (`addJail`/`startJail`) that a reload adds and starts jails new to the configuration, so `state: reloaded` is enough and bans survive.
- `ignoreip` gains `{{ network_home_public_cidr }}`, the home network's public /29, for the same reason ufw already exempts it: a LAN device that uses a public site name arrives from that block, so banning it would lock out the whole house.
- `roles/immich/SECURITY.md`: the pre-existing fail2ban row notes the Apache jails now watch the virtual-host logs.

## Tests

- `roles/base/tasks/test.yml`: `fail2ban-client get sshd ignoreip` includes the home public block (sshd exists on every host; `ignoreip` is inherited from `[DEFAULT]`).
- `roles/apache/tasks/test.yml`: after a handler flush, `fail2ban-client get apache-auth logpath` lists paths under both `/var/log/apache2/` and `/var/apache2/`.

Full harness cycle, 2026-10-11: eddings `ok=479 failed=0` (the one `ignored` is the usual `zpool list` on a cloud instance), jordan-u `ok=84 failed=0`, teardown clean. Both new checks passed, and the `Reload fail2ban` handler ran once after Apache's reload. A first attempt of the run failed earlier in `auth_client : Test getent passwd for All Users` (SSSD enumeration took longer than its 20 × 1 s retry window; unrelated to this branch, and the same task needed 3, 6 and 7 retries in the day's other runs); I tore those instances down and re-ran.

## Deploy notes

The base role's restart drops the Apache jails from `jail.local`; the apache role's reload adds them back file-backed moments later. Afterwards `sudo fail2ban-client get apache-auth logpath` should list the global and virtual-host logs. The glob also matches a stale `/var/apache2/justdavis.com-before-restore-2022-05-15/logs/` directory on eddings, which is harmless.

## Known limitation (pre-existing, not changed here)

`apache-badbots` matches on the User-Agent field, which the vhosts' `TransferLog` (common log format) does not write, so that one jail is still inert. A combined-format `CustomLog` would fix it; separate decision.

author: baoduy
body:
- [DRK-2228] product-owner runs a coverage self-check before the spec gate (Workflow B step 3 in `sdlc-flow-po-orchestration`, rerun before every REWORK re-arm): each §3 part, including invariants, a trust-boundary Security line and each "or" alternative, gets a named §5 scenario, and each new behaviour has at least one scenario today's code fails (checked with CodeGraph). The `sdlc-spec-template` §5 section test says those parts count as requirements. No policy amended; no gate bar, cap, weight or severity changed. Narrower than the issue's wording: invariant scenarios may still pass today, as Policy 06 statement 12a allows (`@existing` baseline). — evidence: DRK-2226 retro, 7 `major` uncovered-requirement findings in 5 of 12 spec reviews (DRK-2205, DRK-2195, DRK-2165, DRK-2152, DRK-2119), 2 scenarios already green before the change (DRK-2084, DRK-2102) — watch: spec gate `first_pass_pct` (33%) and `mean_rounds` (0.92) in setup-health lens 6; count of "§3 requirement with no §5 scenario" `major` findings (7/week)
- [DRK-2229] product-owner checks §2 Today claims on `dev` before the spec gate (new sub-bullet under Workflow B step 2 in `sdlc-flow-po-orchestration`): every "no", "none" or "nothing" claim and every count in §2 is checked with CodeGraph on `dev`, plus a direct read of unindexed files for an absence claim; the `file:line`, or the search that came back empty, goes in a clarification round comment, never in the spec. The `sdlc-spec-template` §2 section test adds "and every claim in it holds on `dev` today". No policy amended (implements Policy 06 statement 8); no gate bar, cap, weight or severity changed. — evidence: DRK-2226 retro, 3 spec-gate `blocker` findings where `dev` contradicted a §2 absence or count claim (DRK-2205, DRK-2102, DRK-2119) — watch: count of spec-gate `blocker` findings saying §2 Today is contradicted by the code (3/week); spec gate `first_pass_pct` (33%) in setup-health lens 6
- [DRK-2230] service-architect checks the source of every library package the design relies on, at the version the service will pin, before the design states its defaults, limits, retention or paging (`agents/service-architect.md` step 3 sub-bullet; no source → its docs for that version or an open question); an absence claim ("X is new", "nothing uses Y") is backed by CodeGraph plus a read of unindexed files, citing the empty search. Never list, step 6 self-check, step 8 EVIDENCE table and `service-design-template` self-check item 2 cover library claims too. No gate bar, cap, weight or severity changed. — evidence: DRK-2226 retro, 3 design-review `blocking` findings in 2 of 5 design reviews (DRK-2185 round 1 DKNet list paging, DRK-2185 round 2 idempotency retention, DRK-2138 "Refit is new") — watch: count of `blocking` design-review findings naming a library behaviour the design got wrong (3/week); design reviews reworked (2 of 5, 3 rounds)
  - Policy amended: **Policy 06 statement 14** (v2.18 → v2.19). Old: "Every claim about a neighbouring repo is CodeGraph-verified; what cannot be verified is an open question, never a guess." New: "Every claim about a neighbouring repo is CodeGraph-verified, and every default, limit or behaviour of a library package the design relies on cites that package's source (or its docs, when there is no source) at the version the service will pin; what cannot be verified is an open question, never a guess."
  - Policy amended: **Policy 09, service-architect charter** (v1.35 → v1.36). Responsibilities old: "research the neighbouring repos with CodeGraph so the context map, dependencies and reuse are real" — new: "research the neighbouring repos with CodeGraph, and the library packages the design relies on at the version the service will pin, so the context map, dependencies, reuse and stated library behaviour are real". Never old: "state a neighbour's behaviour or contract it cannot verify in that repo" — new: "state a neighbour's behaviour or contract it cannot verify in that repo, or a library package's behaviour it cannot verify in that package's source or docs at the pinned version".
  - Open point for the owner (not changed: gate severity, setup-steward Never list): `pr-review-gate` Scope, the **On a design PR** paragraph, says "a claim about a neighbouring repo that CodeGraph contradicts is `blocking`, one with no evidence in the author's report is `important`". It names no severity for a library claim. The proposal is to read "a claim about a neighbouring repo or a library package that its source contradicts is `blocking`, one with no evidence in the author's report is `important`". author: h4rkl
body:
Closes #68.

Make telephony `subscribe` return the projected state snapshot from the same registration transaction that starts its event stream. Queue mutations while state is locked, then drain the ordered outbox under the subscriber lock before registering the new stream. This closes the snapshot/event gap and avoids duplicates or reordered fan-out.

Recheck grants after waiting for the subscriber lock, before writing the snapshot. A revoked subscriber receives no snapshot or registration; a downgraded subscriber receives only its current projection. Later events continue to recheck identity.

Validation: `cargo fmt --check`, workspace clippy and tests (767 passed), telephony suites repeated 30 times. Deterministic tests cover apply/subscribe interleavings and grant changes. QEMU not run locally because the Docker-compatible runtime was unavailable; CI covers it.

author: garrett-pz
body:
A search state will compute the connected components of fragments in two places:
1. After fragmentation upon removing a match.
2. In the computation of `matches_to_remove` after the edges that are part of no valid matches are removed.

Since components are calculated by edges, connected component calculations often need to find all edges adjacent to a given edge. The current version of `connected_components_under_edges` does this by taking the two ends of the edge and looping over their neighbors using petgraphs `neighbors` and `find_edge`. This version pre-computes this adjacency information. The new algorithm also uses less allocations:
- A single `stack` is allocated instead of a `queue` for every component.
- The function adds the components to an existing `Vec` of fragments instead of allocating a new `Vec` every time it is called.

Two smaller optimizations are also included in `matches_to_remove`:
- Intermediate frags are only computed if `removable_matches` is non-empty and thus children search states will be spawned.
- The sort on `removable_matches` is changed to unstable.

## Why

There were two settings windows for four owners. The workspace's also held what is the user's own (the defaults for new agents, notifications) and the deployment's (server models, the waiting list), and it opened from the menu on the user's name. Models and computers each appeared at three levels, and moving between them closed one window and opened another.

## What it is now

One window.

- **The top:** General (the theme, and what a new agent starts with), Notifications, a list of **Agents** by workspace, a list of **Workspaces**, and for whoever looks after the deployment, Server (Models, Waiting list).
- **Inside an agent or a workspace:** choosing one from a list turns the window into that one's own sections, with a way back to the list. An agent has Profile, Memory, Model and computers, Skills, Connectors, Permissions and Usage. A workspace has People (a team only), Computers and Models.

author: mattbaldwin
body:
Refs #429 (one of its flakes; the issue stays open for the others)

## What
`map.spec.ts:75` ("draws a patch, shows tile info on tap, and follows land changes live") failed its first attempt on iPad WebKit in CI and passed on retry (run 38186194985, `e2e (ipad-webkit, 4)` group, PR #424 at 3e7ee11).

## Root cause
A timeout budget that matches the test's real runtime, so it is a coin flip:
- the test sets `test.setTimeout(120_000)`;
- on iPad CI the failed attempt took **2.0 min** (it ran out of budget while waiting at the friend's "Join with a code" tap, `map.spec.ts:130`, hence "Test ended" with the lobby button logged as re-attached) and the passing retry took **1.9 min**.

Nothing was wrong with the lobby or the tap: the test just ran past its budget. Two players, two map builds and shader compiles are slow on a software-rendered runner.

## Fix
Budget raised to 240 s, in line with the other two-player specs (hollow 240 s, potions 300 s). The steps inside keep their own bounded polls (15 to 30 s), so a real hang still fails fast on its own step. No assertion or step changed.

author: brynbellomy
body:
`git stash` keeps one `refs/stash` shared by every worktree of a clone, so `stash@{0}` means "whoever stashed last, anywhere" and `git stash clear` in any worktree wipes everyone's entries. `git stow` is `git stash` with a stack per checkout.

## Design
- **Storage:** `refs/worktree/stow` and its reflog, which git keeps private to each worktree. The main checkout has its own.
- **Format:** entries are byte-identical to `git stash` commits (W with parents HEAD and I, plus U for untracked), so `git stash show/apply <sha>` and other tools read them.
- **Reuse:** `git stash create` builds the index/work-tree part; apply, pop, show and branch hand the entry to `git stash`. Only what git doesn't expose (untracked commit, pathspec narrowing, the post-push reset, `-p`) is built from plumbing, following `builtin/stash.c`.
- **Concurrency:** ref updates use old-value checks; `pop`/`drop` refuse to drop an entry that changed underneath them.

## Differences from `git stash`
1. `stow@{n}` naming and "stow" in messages.
2. **Reflog expiry:** git exempts `refs/stash` from reflog expiry by name; every other reflog loses entries after 30 days on `git gc`. The first push sets `gc.*refs/worktree/stow.reflogExpire` and `reflogExpireUnreachable` to `never` in the repo config unless already set. **Open question: keep this config write?**
3. Unmatched pathspecs are echoed as typed, not git's internal `:(prefix:0)` form.
4. `-p` prompts say "Stage this hunk" (they come from `git add -p`); the resulting entry is identical.
5. `list` isn't paged.
6. Removing a worktree removes its stack, without warning.

Refused with a clear `fatal:`: `-S`/`--staged`, `--pathspec-from-file`, and `save`/`create`/`store`.

## Tests
`make check` (gofmt, vet, `go test -count=1 ./...`).
- **Differential conformance:** 44 scenarios run with `git stash` in repo A and `git stow` in an identical repo B, comparing exit status, output, files, index, HEAD, branches and every entry's commit/tree/parents/messages.
- **Isolation:** main checkout plus two linked worktrees; nothing crosses, and the shared `git stash` is untouched.
- **Concurrency:** 8 worktrees pushing simultaneously; no reported entry is ever lost.
- **Durability:** entries survive `gc --prune=now` and `reflog expire --all` with the config; the test shows they're lost without it.
- **Safety harness:** every package's `TestMain` clears `GIT_*`, uses a throwaway config, confines repo discovery to a temp root, refuses to run inside another repo, and runs in a canaried fixture that fails the run if disturbed.

author: sam-t-anderson
body:
Root-caused the "enemy HP doesn't match my damage" report by replaying two diagnostic captures through the real decoder and cross-checking the **game's own combat-analysis screen**.

## Finding
The game killed a mob with **6,420 damage (15 hits)** whose packets report **119,700 HP**. Our damage decode matches the game's meter exactly — so damage is correct. Enemy HP is just carried on a **much larger internal scale** (measured **16.3×–21.7×** across mobs — not a clean constant), so printing the raw HP next to damage (e.g. `0 / 810K`) can never line up.

| enemy packet HP | damage to kill | ratio |
|---|---|---|
| 119,700 | 6,420 (game meter) | 18.6× |
| 1,350,000 | 62,328 | 21.7× |
| 67,500 | 4,135 | 16.3× |

Because the ratio isn't constant, there's no honest fixed divisor to convert packet HP into damage units — so I don't invent one.

## Fix (display only — nothing rescaled or invented)
- Overlay shows the target's remaining HP as a **percentage** (the HP bar already renders). The raw internal current/max values move to a **labelled hover tooltip** ("game internal HP … a different, larger scale than damage numbers").
- Settings toggle text clarified.

The exact raw HP is still available on hover.

## Tests
Overlay shows the percentage and no longer prints raw current/max inline. Full suite: 324 passing.

author: rakesh3136
body:
## Milestone: overlap-aware prospective validation

### Why
NIC's frozen forward-only cohort needs to avoid treating repeated hourly signals on the same coin as independent trades. Overlapping holding windows can overstate sample size and make confidence metrics too optimistic.

### Changes
- Added a chronological same-symbol overlap filter within each frozen strategy/side/horizon group.
- When a prior forecast's holding window is still open, later same-symbol forecasts are excluded from portfolio metrics and minimum-sample eligibility.
- Reports preserve the pre-filter resolved count, show exclusions, and report the effective non-overlapping sample count.
- Added regression coverage for overlapping same-symbol forecasts and retained fail-closed shadow-only authorization.

### Safety
This does not promote a strategy or authorize publication/trading. Profitability remains unproven until a sufficient prospective cohort matures and passes held-out cost-stress evaluation.

author: viveministeriointernacional-dev
body:
## Qué resuelve

El usuario abrió `/taller/mis` y vio la pantalla negra **«This page couldn't load · A server error occurred · ERROR 1850100685»**. Al revisarlo apareció la causa de raíz, y es más grande que el caso:

> **El proyecto no tenía ni un solo `error.tsx`.** Ni uno.

Así que **cualquier** tropiezo, en **cualquier** pantalla del sistema, caía directo en la pantalla genérica de Cloudflare: en inglés, sin un botón, sin decir nada y sin forma de rastrearla.

Y con Supabase en plan **FREE** (§9) esos tropiezos los hay. El error **no se pudo reproducir** al medirlo (8 peticiones seguidas a `/taller/mis` → **200 las 8**, entre 0,24 s y 1,7 s), igual que en el incidente del 6-oct: es **intermitente**, no permanente. Por eso «volver a intentar» casi siempre funciona — y por eso no había ningún botón que lo ofreciera.

**⚠️ Donde más duele es en el taller, y esto es lo que decide el diseño:** quien ve esa pantalla **no es del equipo**. Es un miembro de una Casa de Fe con el celular en la mano, en la calle, sin cuenta y sin nadie a quien preguntar (§6). Ante una pantalla negra en inglés **abandona** y el taller se queda sin llenar.

## Cuatro pantallas, una por público

| Archivo | Para quién | Lo propio de ella |
|---|---|---|
| `taller/error.tsx` | La persona, desde el QR | **«No perdiste nada de lo que escribiste»** + «Volver a intentar» y «Entrar con mi código» |
| `(interno)/error.tsx` | El equipo | **Sí** enseña el `digest` |
| `error.tsx` (raíz) | `/ingresar`, `/registro`, `/actualizar-datos`, `/nueva-clave`, `/recuperar`, `/calendario` | Red de seguridad de todo lo demás |
| `global-error.tsx` | Un fallo del layout raíz | `html`/`body` propios y estilos **en línea** |

**⚠️ Lo primero que dice la del taller es que no perdió nada, y no es un consuelo vacío:** el taller se guarda solo 1,5 s después de la última tecla (regla del 27-sep), así que lo escrito **está en la base**. Sin esa frase, quien llevaba media hora escribiendo da su trabajo por perdido, y es entonces cuando de verdad no vuelve.

**⚠️ La del taller NO enseña el mensaje técnico y la interna SÍ el `digest`, y la asimetría es a propósito.** A la persona el mensaje no le dice nada y puede traer detalles de la consulta. A quien es del equipo el `digest` es **lo único** con lo que se puede rastrear el fallo en el log del worker de Cloudflare — que es **el único sitio donde queda escrito** (la lección del 24-sep: en Supabase no queda nada).

**⚠️ La de la raíz va en la raíz a propósito, para no tener que acordarse.** Cualquier pantalla que se añada mañana queda cubierta sin hacer nada: Next busca el `error.tsx` más cercano y, si el tramo no tiene uno propio, cae ahí.

**⚠️ Y `global-error.tsx` lleva los estilos en línea** porque cuando el layout raíz es el que falló no se puede contar con que haya cargado la hoja de estilos ni las tipografías. Una pantalla de error que depende de lo que acaba de romperse no sirve de nada.

## La mitad que le faltaba: `statement_timeout = 10 s`

**Una pantalla de error solo se puede pintar si el worker llega a contestar.** Sin tope, una consulta que se queda esperando —un candado, o el pooler sin responder— **se lleva por delante al worker entero**, y eso **no se puede atrapar desde el código**: ahí la pantalla negra sale igual.

Con el tope, Postgres corta la consulta, Prisma lanza el error y el `error.tsx` pinta «Volver a intentar». Es la decisión del **24-sep en `scripts/migrar.mjs`** —*fallar rápido en vez de colgarse*— aplicada ahora al worker.

**10 s son muchísimo margen, y está medido:** la consulta más pesada del proyecto (la de consolidadores del informe, con cinco `EXISTS` correlacionados) tarda **20 ms**, y la pantalla más lenta del sitio (`/taller/mis`) se midió entre **0,2 y 4,4 s entera**, con sus cuatro viajes. No corta nada que funcione: solo lo que ya estaba perdido.

`scripts/migrar.mjs` **no pasa por ahí** (abre su propio cliente en el build, con sus propios topes), así que las migraciones no se ven afectadas.

## Probado al derecho y con su control

En un **build de producción**, con dos páginas que fallan a propósito (ya retiradas del commit):

| Prueba | Resultado |
|---|---|
| Una `/taller/…` que falla | **500** y el documento pide `33yt6tugk_-3j.js`, que contiene **«La conexión se demoró»** |
| **control** | **ningún** chunk de ese documento trae el texto de la raíz |
| Una `/actualizar-datos/…` que falla | **500** y pide `0fu1ng01zbynt.js`, que contiene **«Ir al inicio»** |
| **control** | **ninguno** trae el texto del taller |

O sea que cada tramo pinta **su** pantalla y no se cuelan entre sí. **La huella positiva necesita su control** (regla del 5-oct): sin los dos renglones de control, encontrar el texto no probaría que cada tramo resuelve al suyo.

Comprobado además que las cuatro pantallas quedaron en el paquete del navegador, incluidas la interna y la del layout.

**⚠️ Hallazgo de paso, y conviene tenerlo escrito: un fallo del MIDDLEWARE no lo atrapa ningún `error.tsx`** — se vio en la prueba, da «Internal Server Error» a secas. **No afecta a `/taller/mis`** (es prefijo público y el middleware pasa de largo), pero es el hueco que queda.

**⚠️ Y la otra limitación honesta: estas pantallas necesitan JavaScript.** En producción Next manda un documento mínimo y el `error.tsx` lo pinta React al hidratar — es así por diseño del framework, no una decisión nuestra. El resto del taller sí es todo de servidor.

## Lo que esto NO arregla

**No evita que el tropiezo ocurra.** Eso es **Hyperdrive**, que sigue esperando el `id` de la configuración de Cloudflare: hoy cada petición abre una conexión nueva contra Supabase y paga el saludo TCP + TLS + Postgres completo, multiplicado por los viajes de la pantalla. El bloque comentado de `wrangler.jsonc` ya tiene las dos correcciones medidas (**Session pooler**, no la conexión directa; y **caché desactivada**).

## Verificación

- `npx tsc --noEmit` ✅
- `npx eslint src` ✅
- **193/193 pruebas** ✅
- `npm run cf:build` ✅ (y confirmado que **no tocó producción**: «Sin DATABASE_URL del entorno: no se aplican migraciones aquí»)

**Sin migraciones**, así que **se puede fusionar a cualquier hora** (§24-sep).

body:
GitHub progress/status now applies its existing network timeout only while an actual HTTP request is dispatched. Mandatory Git checkpoint preparation and acknowledgments retain the original owner deadline and configured Git bounds.

Runner finalization waits for its original control/progress work even after failure, independently attempts the existing token-authenticated quiescent claim settlement when handoff conditions hold, and preserves the primary execution error plus any finalization failures. A stopped preparation can also use the existing handoff control path to authenticate its original producer-bound claim, saved snapshots and exclusive recovery owner before retaining a typed quiescent proof and a full Git acknowledgment. This changes local claim history; it leaves the original run and unknown remote Project-status outcome intact and activates no work.

Validation: build, scoped lint/format/type checks and the affected existing real Git/storage/queue workflow passed. Focused ownership/state review and normal CI are required before integration. Installed milestone verification and supported reconciliation remain pending; historical failures, receipts, accounting and limits stay unchanged.

Refs #1142. Keep the issue open until its installed milestone exit is complete.
