body: ## Summary **Mentions in a todo's discussion** - Typing `@` in a post (or in the description, which is the first post) opens a list of the people assigned to the project. It filters as you type, by first name or surname, ignoring diacritics; arrows + Enter/Tab or a click pick a person, Escape closes it. - A mention is stored as `@Name` and rendered as a highlighted chip. - Only people assigned to the project can be mentioned. `@Name` of anyone else stays plain text. **People assigned to a project** - Projects had no list of people until now. New "Lidé v projektu" section on the project detail adds and removes them. - Whoever creates a project is assigned to it. - The migration assigns to each existing project everyone who already takes part in it: its owner, people with their own rate, assignees and creators of todos, authors of comments and work reports. **MCP** - `get-project` returns `members`, `update-project` accepts `member_ids` (replaces the list). - A comment or description sent with `@Name Surname` as text gets the mention the same way as from the web. ## How it works - The editor only inserts `@Name` as text. `App\Support\Mentions` links it on save (`saving` hook of `TodoComment` and `Todo`), so the web UI, the MCP tools and imports share one path. - The sanitizer strips the mention attributes from incoming HTML, so a mention is re-checked against the project's current members on every save and cannot be forged for someone outside the project. - Text inside links, `code` and `pre` is left alone, as is an `@` right after a letter (e-mail addresses). ## Notes - Mentions do not notify anyone yet; they only mark the person in the text. - Posts saved before this change keep `@Name` as plain text until they are saved again. - Removing a person from a project keeps their existing mentions until the post is next saved. - Assigning a todo is not limited to project members. ## Testing - `tests/Feature/MentionsTest.php`; whole suite passes (254 tests). - Checked in the browser: adding a person on the project detail, the `@` list, picking a person, the rendered mention, and that editing and saving a post keeps it. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: prabeshbhetwal
body:
## Summary

A focus session from today or yesterday that ended without a name is offered one in a Story rail notice, one session at a time. Nothing is written until the person presses "Name it". Undo sits right in the notice.

```text
ended, unnamed focus session (today, then yesterday; ≥ 10 min; not kept; not running)
  NameCandidates (Core): earlier names ranked by shared app time + 0.1 same-category bonus
     ≥ 0.3 shared, top 3, and a clear lead of ≥ 0.1 over the next (else: no offer)
  ├─ clear earlier name  → model confirms (always "1" in every probe)
  │     → "Name this morning's 1h session “Landing page”?"   From your earlier names
  └─ no earlier name     → on-device model: new | none   (guided generation)
        → NameAudit: 1–4 words, ≤ 30 chars, no digits/quotes, not a category or bare app; first letter capitalised
        → "Name … “Podcast mix”?"   ✦ Suggested by on-device AI
  [Name it] → renameSession (a correction) → "Named “X” · Undo" in the notice
  [Keep as is] → remembered for two days (fc.nameSuggestionKept)
```

The model runs only when the "Use on-device AI" switch is on and `ModelGate.modelAvailable`. It runs once per session, with a 10 s timeout, and never on the 1 Hz ticker. The refresh key follows sessions, notes, the day and the kept list, not the minute app-use checkpoint. `Sources/App/ModelGate.swift` is byte-identical to main.

## Evidence

- **Checks:** 1104/1104 in Sydney and `TZ=Europe/Berlin` at b917d14. The fix-reviewer's scratch run under `TZ=UTC`, the CI zone, also passed. The Codex cache-key fix (#57) adds 1105–1106; CI (UTC) passes 1106/1106 at the head, aae1f85. Name-suggestion checks are 1000–1033 and 1102–1106, after main's suites.
- **Before/after:** each fix round's new check fails on the old code. For example, the final wave restored the old behaviour and got 1097/1104, failing exactly the seven H-checks.
- **Live on-device probe**, recorded in spec §5a (macOS 27.2), with 20 hand-built sessions and the expected answers written first:
  - **Run 1:** 19/20 right-or-none, but the free-text answer field was ignored, so 10 of 14 deserving sessions got nothing.
  - **Run 2:** with the answer constrained, the model always answered "1" and never offered a fresh name.
  - **Run 3:** after adding a no-candidate question and a 0.1 margin rule, 20/20 against the updated expectations, 0 wrong, and 4 of 4 fitting fresh names ("landing page design", "design candidate interview", …).
  - Because the model only confirms the ranking, earlier-name offers are captioned honestly: "From your earlier names", with no AI mark.
- **Snapshots:** `storyNameSuggestion` (fresh name, ✦) and `storyNameSuggestionEarlier` (earlier name, no mark). Each scene asserts its offer before capture.
- **Reviews:**
  - Each of the 5 tasks: a Sonnet or Opus task review plus fix rounds.
  - Two fix-reviewer passes. The second said SHIP.
  - A final Opus whole-branch review ("with fixes"); those fixes are in and were re-reviewed.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way. It adds one preference key (`fc.nameSuggestionKept`, a list of thread UUIDs trimmed to two days, cleared by `removeAll`). Accepted names are ordinary rename corrections with Undo. There's no migration.

**Blast Radius:** Story rail (today's tile)

- A new notice sits under the name/category notice in today's tile while unnamed sessions qualify.
- `ChipFlow` and other shared components are untouched.
- The snapshot matrix gains two scenes.
- Known minors left for later:
  - a session named, then undone from its card after another rename landed in between, can be offered again that run (the accepted list is keyed by the cache key, which now carries the ranking)
  - Undo via the Story row leaves the notice's Undo stale (it then says "no longer available")
  - model availability isn't observed while an offer is showing
  - possessive fresh names are rejected, which is safe

**Hand checks pending** (spec §6, on the installed build):
1. An unnamed 15-min session offers the earlier name.
2. Name it shows "Named … · Undo", and Undo restores it.
3. Keep as is shows the next session.
4. Turning the switch off shows nothing.
5. A fresh name for new work.
6. Two close earlier names offer nothing.

body:
@harsha-sharma356 , I’ve pushed the branch Ocr_Progress_popup (subtask 2.14a, OCR loading and progress popup for guests). Could you test whether the popup opens and shows the state of each task?

What I changed

Pressing Process on the preview page no longer blocks the page or redirects. It adds the selected pages to a global queue, and a floating popup shows the progress.
The popup can be dragged, resized and minimised to a pill, and it stays visible when you navigate to other pages. It is hidden only on /validation.
Each task shows a progress bar, how many documents are done, and an estimated time remaining. Statuses are queued, processing, completed, failed and cancelled.
There is a Cancel button per task and a Cancel all button. When a task finishes, a Review results button takes you to validation. There is no more automatic redirect.
Pages that are queued or processing are marked as busy in the preview, so they can’t be sent twice.
Files: OcrProgressProvider and OcrProgressContext (the queue and state), OcrProgressPopup (the UI), utils/ocrProgress.ts (estimates), models/OcrTask.ts, plus edits to App.tsx, UploadPage.tsx, uploadService.ts and the UploadPage tests.
There is no backend change.

Please check

The popup opens after Process and shows the task as queued, then processing.
Minimise and restore work, and the position persists after a reload.
The popup stays visible when you navigate to other pages, and is hidden on /validation.
Queuing a second batch while the first runs shows it as queued, then it starts afterwards.
Cancel and Cancel all work. Review results opens validation with the results.

Known limitations

The progress bar is an estimate based on page count. The backend only reports when each document finishes.
Cancel is client-side only. The server still finishes its current batch.
Batches run one at a time.
This covers guests only. The signed-in version (2.14b) needs a different design, because /api/documents/process doesn’t send progress events.
With OCR_MODE=mock the popup works, but the validation page goes blank because the mock returns a flat list instead of pages.

## ⚠️ Breaking change

These 8 patterns are **no longer exported** from `agentic-ds-kit` and are gone from `dist`:

`ActivityPattern`, `AssistantWorkspacePattern`, `DashboardPattern`, `EmptyFirstRunPattern`, `InboxPattern`, `InviteMembersPattern`, `ListDetailPattern`, `SettingsFormPattern` (plus their `*Props` / `ListDetailItem` types).

`import { DashboardPattern } from "agentic-ds-kit"` now fails with TS2305. To migrate:

```bash
npx agentic-ds-kit add dashboard
```

```tsx
import { DashboardPattern } from "@/components/patterns/dashboard";
```

`AppShellPattern` and `SignInPattern` are unchanged and stay as imports. No version bump in this PR: the planner releases it, and it needs to be **0.3.0**.

## What changed

- **Kit source:** the 8 patterns move from `packages/kit/ui/patterns/` to `packages/kit/patterns/<Name>Pattern/`, with imports changed to `../../ui/X`. They're not in the published `files`, so only `patterns-src/` ships. Demo data now sits in sibling files so a copy reads as "replace this data": `activity-data.ts`, `assistant-workspace-data.ts`, `dashboard-data.ts`, `invite-members-data.ts`, `list-detail-data.ts`, `settings-form-data.ts`, and the existing `inbox-data.ts`. EmptyFirstRun has no data, only UI copy.
- **`src/index.ts`:** exports only AppShellPattern and SignInPattern.
- **`scripts/build-patterns-src.mjs`:** reads both `patterns/` (content) and `ui/patterns/` (chrome), so all 10 patterns and both recipes can still be copied with `add`. Kit `tsconfig` now includes `patterns/`.
- **Contracts:** each pattern entry in `index.json` has `"delivery": "copy-in" | "import"`, and copy-in entries also have `"add"`. Each of the 8 pattern contracts adds `delivery`, `add`, `import` (the local path), a `copyNote`, and a first `doNot`: "Do not import XPattern from agentic-ds-kit".
- **Docs app:** `DashboardDemo` imports the 8 by relative path from `packages/kit/patterns/`. `/patterns` shows `npx agentic-ds-kit add <id>` above each content pattern, and the import line above AppShell and SignIn. The installation page is updated too.
- **Agent docs:** the pattern rule in `AGENTS.md`, `packages/kit/AGENTS.md` and `.cursor/rules/kit.mdc` now says: content patterns are copied in, AppShell and SignIn are imported. Also updated: `README.md` (pattern list and eval expectations), `packages/kit/README.md`, `docs/getting-started.md` (usage, copy-in, checklist, and the "Add a pattern" steps), and `prototype-from-kit/SKILL.md` (kit copy plus the `.claude` and `.cursor` mirrors).

## Checks

- `npm run build` passes. `patterns-src: 10 patterns, 2 recipes`. `dist/ui/patterns` holds only AppShellPattern and SignInPattern.
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` returns 0, and so does `-p packages/kit`.
- **Scratch Next 16.3.3 app** installed from the `npm pack` tarball:
  - `add` copied all 8 cleanly.
  - `tsc` returns 0, and `next build` passes.
  - All 8 pages render styled inside AppShellPattern, with no console errors.
  - `import { DashboardPattern } from "agentic-ds-kit"` fails with TS2305.
  - `AppShellPattern` and `SignInPattern` imports work.
- **Docs `/patterns`:** I hashed DOM geometry (each element's box relative to `.layout-shell`) and innerText for all 10 hashes, before (main) and after.
  - The 8 content patterns and app-shell match main exactly.
  - Sign-in text matches. Its geometry hash only differs by the new usage block's nodes inside `main`.
  - No console errors on a fresh load or while switching between all hashes.

## Known, not from this PR

- Loading `/patterns#<hash>` directly with a non-dashboard hash throws React hydration error #418. `DashboardDemo`'s `useState` initializer reads `window.location.hash`, so the server renders Overview and the client renders the hashed page. That logic is unchanged from main. I didn't confirm it on a main build.
- `eslint` reports `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` in InboxPattern and ListDetailPattern. The code moved unchanged; only the paths are new.

author: beyondworks
body:
## 요약

패널 입력창 하나로 맡기면 답하는 에이전트(조율자)가 직무가 맞는 동료에게 맡기고 결과를 검토해 답합니다(유건 10/10 요구 2·3). 답 아래에 '맡은 동료'와 '다른 에이전트에게 맡기기'(배분의 안전장치)가 보입니다. **PR2 위에 쌓인 PR**입니다.

## 동작

- 패널 턴의 `delegate`는 채널 넘김이 아니라 **동기 실행**(데스크톱과 같은 경로) — 같은 워크스페이스 동료의 결과를 그 턴에 받아 모읍니다. 동료 명단 = 로컬 명단, 위임 안내도 데스크톱 형식. 메신저 일반 턴은 지금 그대로(채널 넘김).
- 위임받은 동료 턴은 `msgr-rules`라 오피스 쓰기를 하지 않습니다 — 쓰기는 조율자의 확인 카드(PR1)로만.
- 패널 턴의 동기 위임 알림은 메신저 미러가 처리한 것으로 끝냅니다(방에 따로 올리지 않음, 출처가 있어 텔레그램·알림으로도 안 감).
- '다른 에이전트에게 맡기기' → 같은 대화에 `meta.office_route = 이름` 글 → 조율자 지시에 JSON 문자열로 싣고, 대상은 delegate가 같은 워크스페이스 명단에서만 찾습니다.
- 패널 턴의 방 문맥은 같은 대화(뿌리)의 글만 — 1단계는 같은 1:1 방의 다른 대화가 섞였습니다. 확인 카드 [실행] 턴에는 조율자 지시 없음.

## 영향 반경

| 축 | 확인 |
|---|---|
| 메신저 일반 턴(넘김·명단·안내문) | 대조군 시험, G-3 소스 검사 |
| 위임 미러·알림 경로 | 패널은 조용히 끝냄 — 시험 |
| 개인 공간 1:1 패널 | 로컬 명단으로 위임 가능(전에는 넘김 자체 거절) — 시험 |
| 화면 | 로컬 스택 — 맡은 동료 줄, 선택 → DB의 `office_route` 확인 |
| 실제 게이트웨이 종단·Windows | 확인 안 함 |

## 시험

- office-panel-route(4)·msgr-bridge '오피스'(8), 관련 루트 시험 2909(실패 0), apps/office 1063
- 변이: 패널 동기 위임 분기·로컬 명단·대화 거르기·위임 미러 생략 각각 빼면 실패

## 도달 범위

패널은 병합 뒤 Vercel, 게이트웨이는 앱 발행·상주 배포 뒤.

- `docs/进度.md`：现在谁在改什么（占位表）、待作者定的事、暂停的事、下一步，以及 #1–#88 每个 PR 一行的合并记录。

- `docs/技术笔记.md`：构建、无头浏览器的坑、代码地图、本机存储。
- `docs/设定/`：项目文件夹里的设定搬进来，每份开头标了现行、参考还是过时。「网站设定」文档转写成 md，后来变了的句子标【已变】。另新写了 `内容方向-2026-10-12.md`、`设定补充.md`（Codex 的提议区），`写稿须知.md` 按现在的设定改写了旧的给朋友的须知（作者还没审）。
- `docs/方案/`、`docs/资料/`：已做完的方案和公版书来源，留着查为什么这样做。
- `AGENTS.md`（Codex 的规矩，以 CLAUDE.md 为准）、`.cursor/rules/`、`docs/给Codex的任务.md`（先列了 4 条候选，作者点头才开工）。
- 每个 PR 自动跑「Check」：构建，加规矩检查（`scripts/check-rules.mjs`，规则在 `scripts/rules.json`）。只看新加的行：`codex/` 分支改受保护文件、加素材会被拦，外部网址会被拦；暗设定词、「稿」当时间用、中英没一起改、加了音频会提醒。
- `CLAUDE.md`、`README.md` 各加一行指向 `docs/`，README 两处旧路径改成仓库里的路径。CLAUDE.md 的内容没动（#88 在改）。

**怎么做的：** 读了项目记忆的全部条目、项目文件夹的 `ideas/`、`review/`、「网站设定」文档和全部 git 历史，逐条对照现在的代码核实文件路径和功能状态。检查脚本在本地拿 #82、#84、#87 等 6 个历史 PR 试跑，没有误拦，只有中英没一起改的提醒；又用一个假文件试了每一条规则都能触发。`npm run build` 通过。

不在这个 PR 里、要作者自己点的：Codex 连上仓库；每个 PR 的预览网址（可选，推荐 Cloudflare Pages）；`main` 分支保护（可选）。

author: copilot
body:
The "Check step work" job fails because no open PR updates `site/content/github-info.md`. The only `update-github-info` run (38216302096) ended in `noop`. Its agent logged that the fetched pages returned raw markup with no readable items, the Awesome Copilot page redirected to a directory listing, and later fetches were denied.

This change makes a `noop` less likely on the next run. It doesn't fix the job by itself. After merge, re-run the workflow with `workflow_dispatch` to get the PR the check expects.

- **Prompt (`.github/workflows/update-github-info.md`)**
  - Added a fallback to `https://github.blog/feed/` and `https://github.blog/changelog/feed/` when a source page returns unreadable markup.
  - Told the agent to add at least one new item when any recent source item is readable and verifiable. The prohibition on speculative or duplicate content is unchanged.
- **Lock file (`.github/workflows/update-github-info.lock.yml`)**
  - Recompiled with `gh aw compile`, so only the `body_hash` in the metadata line changed.
  - I restored the original `cron` value by hand, because compiling without a git remote re-scattered the schedule.

The workflow is still non-deterministic, so the agent can still choose `noop`. If a re-run doesn't open a PR, check the `noop` message in the `safe_outputs` job log to see what it couldn't fetch. The network allowlist is unchanged.

author: piatoss3612
body:
## Summary

Adding several accounts in a row, with no scan in between, can fail on the second or a later
one with `CorruptedData` ("the Ironwood note commitment tree retains checkpoints both above and
below height H, but none at that height to truncate to") once the pools' oldest checkpoints
differ. It affects `import_account_ufvk`, `import_account_hd` and `create_account` whenever
the account's birthday is at or below the last scanned block, which is the usual case for
imported and restored accounts. The data is not corrupted: `rewind_to_chain_state` takes its
pruning floor from `MAX(blocks.height)`, which the previous rewind lowered, instead of from the
chain tip as its documentation says.

Any wallet that imports or restores several accounts in a row can hit this. Vizor's mobile
wallet-link import, which adds the selected desktop accounts one after another, hit it on
mainnet (Ironwood, H = 3514069).

## What happens

For an account whose birthday is at or below the last scanned block, `add_account` rewinds
every pool's note commitment tree to one height that all pools have a checkpoint for, then
queues a rescan from the account's birthday. Each tree keeps its latest 100 ordinary
checkpoints plus ZIP 318 anchors. `update_tree` prunes each pool while inserting that pool's
own commitments and only then adds the heights the other pools checkpointed, so the busiest
pool keeps the fewest old checkpoints. From a regtest run with the tip at 343:

```text
height         144 (anchor)   168   244   343
Sapling             ✓          ✓     ✓     ✓
Orchard             ✓          ✓     ✓     ✓
Ironwood            ✓          –     ✓     ✓
```

1. First rewind: the floor is `MAX(blocks.height) − 99` = 244. Every pool has 244. The
   blocks above it are removed, so `MAX(blocks.height)` is now 244, while the scan queue
   still ends at the chain tip, 343.
2. Second rewind, with no scan in between: the floor is 244 − 99 = 145, and the truncation
   height is the lowest checkpoint at or above it that any pool retains, 168.
3. Ironwood retains checkpoints above 168 (244) and below it (anchor 144) but none at 168, so
   `plan_tree_truncation` classifies it as `DivergedCheckpoints`, reported as `CorruptedData`.

A single rewind of a synced wallet stays within the range all pools share, as does one after a
scan has caught up. The failure needs an earlier rollback that no scan has followed: a
previous `add_account`, as above, or reorg handling (`truncate_to_height`), which lowers both
`MAX(blocks.height)` and the scan-queue end.

## Fix

1. The floor is `max(chain_tip, MAX(blocks.height)) − (PRUNING_DEPTH − 1)`, where `chain_tip`
   is the scan-queue end that `rewind_to_chain_state` already reads before any mutation.
   Successive rewinds share one floor.
2. `rewind_truncation_height` walks up from the lowest candidate at or above the floor. It
   skips a height that a pool straddles while retaining only anchors below it, since that pool
   merely pruned its ordinary checkpoints earlier. A pool that straddles a height with an
   ordinary checkpoint below it is missing one inside its own window; that height is returned
   and still reported as corrupted, so
   `rewind_to_chain_state_with_straddling_ironwood_checkpoints_errors` passes unchanged. This
   is what covers a rewind after reorg handling, where the scan-queue end is lower too and
   the first change alone does not help.
3. The documentation matches the code. There is no schema change or migration.

## What changes

- A synced wallet, one rewind: unchanged, because the chain tip equals `MAX(blocks.height)`.
- Successive rewinds with no scan in between, or a rewind after a truncation that lowered
  the scan-queue end: could fail before, succeed now. Wallets whose pools already diverged
  need no repair.
- A wallet whose known chain tip is above its scanned blocks: the rewind truncates fewer
  blocks, or none. The queued `Historic` rescan re-scans them, as it already did for blocks
  below the old floor, and a block that changed meanwhile surfaces as `BlockConflict` or
  `CheckpointConflict` during that rescan.
- A genuinely missing checkpoint: still `CorruptedData`. `WouldDestroyWitnesses` handling is
  unchanged.
- No rewind truncates below where it did before. Only `rewind_to_chain_state` changes;
  `truncate_to_height` and `truncate_to_chain_state` are untouched.

Not addressed here, as separate issues: `update_tree` still leaves the pools with different
oldest checkpoints, a ZIP 318 anchor added in a long batch for a pool with no output at the
grid height can refer to a pruned leaf, and a first sync that scans the tip range before
history does not record older anchors in a pool that has already pruned.

## Tests

- `wallet::rewind_floor_tests::successive_imports_without_a_scan_share_the_pruning_floor`
  fails before this change with "… the Ironwood note commitment tree retains checkpoints both
  above and below height 100198 …". With the change it passes, rescans, and checks every
  pool's tree root against the chain.
- `wallet::rewind_floor_tests::import_after_reorg_truncation_skips_heights_a_pool_straddles`
  fails before this change with "… height 100190 …", and still fails with the floor change
  alone.
- `wallet::tests::rewind_truncation_height_skips_heights_a_pool_straddles`: a height straddled
  over anchors only is skipped, and one straddled over an ordinary checkpoint is not.
- The repository's CI passes on this branch in every configuration, and the full
  `zakura-client-sqlite` lib suite passes locally under `orchard` (567 tests).
- An out-of-tree sweep of 65,610 synced-wallet and import-sequence combinations (chain
  lengths, per-block pool activity, scan orders, anchor intervals, import sequences) had no
  failures on this branch, against 6,168 before.
- End to end, Vizor's wallet-link import path on regtest fails without this change and passes
  with it vendored (chainapsis/vizor-wallet#976), including recovering and spending the
  imported account's funds.

## Why on a fork

This pull request runs the repository's CI on the change before it is proposed to
zakura-core/wallet-libraries. The base branch is `base/ad96334`, the current upstream `main`.

author: picklehik3
body:
Fixes how releases render in the Discord server:

- **#pre-release (v1.1.0-pre.1):** the rolling notes' `<!-- … -->` maintainer comments showed up as raw text, about a third of the post.
- **#releases (v1.0.4):** the version appeared twice, as the embed title and then as a `## v1.0.4` heading, and the `#### Launcher` / `#### Status Bar` subheadings printed literally, because Discord embeds render `#` to `###` only.

**What changes in `announce_release_discord.yml`:**
- Before posting, the notes are tidied:
  - HTML comments are stripped.
  - A first heading that only repeats the tag is dropped.
  - Headings are rescaled so the top level is `##`. Anything deeper than `###` becomes a bold line, and code fences are left alone.
  - `#N` becomes a link to the issue.
- The manual run gains an optional `edit_message_id` input. With it, the workflow edits the webhook's existing post (`PATCH …/messages/<id>`) instead of posting again, so re-rendering the pre-release post doesn't ping @Testers a second time.

**Tested locally:** I ran the workflow's own script against the real v1.0.3, v1.0.4 and v1.1.0-pre.1 notes, with a local server standing in for the webhook.
- v1.0.3 renders as before.
- v1.0.4 now has `## New` / `### Launcher`, no repeated version and no `####`.
- The pre-release post no longer contains any comments.
- The edit path sends a PATCH without `username`, and a non-numeric ID is refused.

**After merge:** the two existing posts can be re-rendered in place, from the branch that has this file:
- `v1.0.4` with message `1558877832392872077`
- `v1.1.0-pre.1` with message `1558903646975033395`

author: borisj74
body:
## What

**Focus after close**
- In the default preset header (Brand + Toggle), closing the rail with the Toggle used to drop keyboard focus to `<body>`, because that Toggle hides on the closed rail. Now a user close (pointer or keyboard) moves focus to the `SideNav.Brand` mark ("Open"), or to the visible closed-rail Toggle when there's no mark.
- If the control that had focus stays visible (the custom-header Toggle, which moves to the start edge), focus stays on it.
- Same mechanism as K37: `setOpen(next, { focus: true })` / `toggle({ focus: true })`. The request now records the open state asked for and the element that had focus. "Hidden on the closed rail" is decided from the SideNav structure (inert slot, a Toggle beside a Brand, other header content), mirroring the CSS. Computed visibility isn't used because it only flips after the fade-out.
- The focus move runs in a layout effect, in the same commit as the open change.

**Ignored controlled requests (K37 Open #2)**
- If a controlled parent ignores the request, it's dropped after the event (`setTimeout`), so a later programmatic open no longer steals focus. A programmatic `setOpen` without the option also clears any pending request.

**Docs and contract**
- `contracts/sidenav.json`: the reopen a11y line is split in three: reopen, close, and "programmatic changes never move focus; ignored requests are dropped". The Brand and Toggle notes mention focus on close.
- `SideNavContext.ts` doc comment and the SideNav docs "Build your own nav" usage: "Closing moves focus to the mark (Open)".
- No CSS or visual change.

## Checks
- `npm run build` passes, then `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` reports 0 errors.
- Served the build with `next start` and tested with real Enter key presses (`computer` key action, element focused first, no scripted clicks):
  - Default preset (Preview): Enter on Close closes the rail with focus on the mark (`.markButton`, "Open"). Enter reopens it with focus on Close. Repeated, same result.
  - Blocks example: Close → mark "Open"; Enter → Close.
  - Custom-header example: Close → the same Toggle, now "Open" at the start edge; Enter → Close. No K37 regression.
  - Right-side preset: Close → mark; Enter → Close. Closed-by-default preset: Enter on mark → Close; Enter → mark.
  - Pointer click on Close (right-side preset) → focus on the mark.
  - Programmatic Open/Closed controls on the docs page: focus stays on the control button both ways.
- Geometry hash of every `aside` subtree (rects relative to the aside, visibility, opacity; transitions off), Preview and Variants tabs, open and closed, at 1280 and 375. All identical to `main` (04c938c).
- No console errors.

## Not covered by a browser test
- The ignored-request path: no docs example has a controlled parent that ignores `onOpenChange`. Covered by reasoning: the effect only acts when the open state matches the request, and the timeout drops a request that never landed.

body:
Confidence Score: 4/5

Fix the Webpack command before merging; the new build checks cannot pass as written.

Findings

1.  **Webpack build cannot pass** ▶ 2.  **CI ignores saved dependency versions** ▶
Fix with agent prompt `````markdown ### Issue 1 .github/workflows/webpack.yml:28 `npx webpack` cannot build this repository. `package.json` defines a Node CLI and depends only on `license-checker`. Neither `webpack` nor `webpack-cli` is installed, and there is no Webpack config or default entry at `src/index.js`. The new build job therefore fails across all three Node versions. Replace this command with a check that runs the CLI, or add the dependencies and entry needed for a real Webpack build. ### Issue 2 .github/workflows/webpack.yml:27 `npm install` ignores the committed `yarn.lock`, and this repository has no `package-lock.json`. Each CI run therefore resolves dependencies afresh instead of checking the versions recorded in the repository. The same commit can install different versions, making failures harder to reproduce. Use Yarn with its frozen-lockfile option, or commit an npm lockfile and use `npm ci`. Note: If this suggestion doesn't match your team's coding style, reply to this and let me know. I'll remember it for next time! --- For each issue above, determine whether it is valid and should be fixed. If so, fix it directly. `````

Summary

Adds a GitHub Actions workflow for pushes and pull requests targeting `main`. - GitHub builds the project with Webpack on three Node.js versions. body:
Goal-Step: orch-v31/R1

Stage R1 of orchestration policy version 31 (worker registry and provider classes, approved 2026-10-12). The policy and its approval record merged as #2367 (2026-10-12T05:23Z).

## What this adds

1. **Pure core** — `lib/amux/workerRegistryCore.ts`
   - Section 2's class table: claude/codex verified up to contract, cursor/copilot unverified up to implementation.
   - The worker name grammar and the four desired states.
   - The change rule an event must pass.
   - Section 3's effective assignment rule: active, no open latch, latest observation ok.
   - The registry-vs-catalog comparison that ends R1.
2. **Tables** — migration `20261012100000_amux_worker_registry`:
   - `AmuxWorkerRegistryEvent`, append-only owner events. A worker's desired state is its newest event. Its guard enforces:
     - the change rule: a first event is `requested`, or `active` only for the seven catalog workers; nothing follows `retired`; no later event activates a worker (that is R5's trial evidence); a role may only widen while the worker is `requested`;
     - the per-worker revision (compare-and-set);
     - the owner's audit of the same transaction (`amux.worker.register` / `amux.worker.change`);
     - the database clock, READ COMMITTED only, and no update or delete.
   - `AmuxWorkerObservation`, `AmuxWorkerTrialEvidence` and `AmuxWorkerLatchEvent` exist with their vocabularies but **refuse every write** until R4/R5 replace their guards with reviewed writer rules.
3. **Store** — `lib/amux/workerRegistryStore.ts` is the single reader and writer, with fixed statement counts budgeted by two new AMUX DB boundaries.
4. **Admin** — AMUX › Execution › **Workers** and `GET/POST /api/admin/amux/workers`:
   - Any admin can read each worker's desired and effective state, and the comparison with `TOMVERSE_AMUX_WORKER_CATALOG_JSON`.
   - A change takes the owner role, the code latch and a recent step-up, all checked before the body is read.
5. **R1 registration**:
   - The owner's one-click registration of version 27's thirteen workers: the 7 catalog workers as `active`, the 6 Cursor/Copilot sessions as `requested`.
   - It sends one change per worker and continues only on a verified receipt for that worker (name, revision 1, action, event id). It stops at the first answer that is not a verified receipt.
   - After an unknown outcome it sends nothing more and reads the registry again first.

## What it does not do

- **Writes are latched off.** `AMUX_WORKER_REGISTRY_WRITES_LATCH = false` (section 8: each stage ships with its code latch off). Registering the thirteen needs the operator's R1 activation record and a one-line change that sets it to true.
- **Nothing reads the registry for assignment.** Assignment still follows the catalog environment variable until R2.
- No observation, trial or latch writer exists (R4/R5).

## Pins this moves

- **Marketing webhook pipeline fingerprint**: `AdminAuditLog` is a watched model, and this adds three back relations to it.
  - The fingerprint is updated with a history line.
  - **Signed staging evidence for the marketing webhook is stale** and needs a fresh record, as with every earlier AMUX table.
- **Prompt Refiner runtime closure position digest**: only positions in `lib/marketingAutomationAccess.ts` move. The count (228) and the position-free inventory are unchanged.
- **`amuxCommitDeadline` migration order list**: the registry migration changes no commit-deadline guard.

## Independent review

| Round | Job | Codex | Cursor | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `r-20261012-061230-215168` | reject: the seed run treated any 2xx as success | accept, with 1 minor and 2 nits | all fixed |
| 2 | `r-20261012-065817-9594ca` | accept | accept, with 2 nits (test granularity, a comment's line count) | nits applied after the round (test and comment only) |

## After review: develop merge (2026-10-12)

- Merged develop (`f2da208f0`). The one conflict was the Prompt Refiner closure position digest.
  - Both history notes are kept.
  - The digest is re-measured on the merged tree. The count (228) and the position-free inventory are unchanged.
- develop gained `20261012090000_default_model_gpt_6_luna`, which has this migration's old timestamp.
  - This migration is renamed to `20261012100000_amux_worker_registry`, so that it applies after it.
  - It had not been deployed anywhere.
  - Checked on a fresh PostgreSQL 17:
    - order: default-model first, then the registry
    - DB suite: 7 pass
    - schema diff: empty
- Both changes are mechanical (a rename and a re-pin) and came after the accepted review rounds.

## Verification

| Area | Check | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Unit | Core | 20 pass |
| Unit | Store and migration parity, statement counts | 10 pass |
| Client | Panel render and registration run | 29 pass |
| Server contract | Route | 4 pass |

author: okhackjarvis
body:
## Summary
This PR introduces a complete workout tracking web application built with vanilla HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. The app allows users to log exercises, track progress over time, and visualize their performance through graphs.

## Key Changes
- **Workout Logging**: Record exercises with weight and reps, with automatic prefilling of previous values
- **Rest Timer**: Configurable rest timer that starts after each set with vibration feedback
- **Workout History**: Browse past workouts organized by date with quick navigation
- **Progress Graphs**: Visualize performance metrics (max weight, estimated 1RM, total volume) over time for each exercise
- **Exercise Management**: Add/remove exercises from the default list
- **Data Persistence**: All data stored in browser's localStorage with export/import functionality (JSON format)
- **Responsive Design**: Mobile-first design with dark mode support and safe area insets for notched devices
- **Accessibility**: Semantic HTML, ARIA labels, and keyboard-friendly navigation

## Implementation Details
- State management with localStorage serialization and normalization
- Tab-based navigation for different sections (log, history, graph, settings)
- SVG-based graph rendering with dynamic scaling and date labels
- Epley formula for estimated 1RM calculations
- Exercise grouping by name to display multiple sets per exercise
- Utility functions for date formatting, element creation, and calculations
- CSS custom properties for theming with automatic dark mode detection

While a slash-command provider was still searching, the command shelf showed "No commands". Hosts with slow providers looked empty instead of loading.

The plugin sets `slashCommandLoading$` from inside its `slashCommandMenu$` subscription. In reactive-engine-core 0.1.2, the outer propagation then finished with a stale snapshot. author: git-on-my-level
body:
## What changed and why

Mobile and web for the exact item-list link (contract M, messaging channels; iMessage replies that reference 2+ items). The macOS handler and the backend that emits the link are separate PRs.

`https://h.omi.me/items?conversation=<id>&task=<id>&memory=<id>`: one repeated key per item, URL order = display order, at most 10 items, unknown keys ignored, ids percent-encoded, no content in the URL.

**Mobile (Flutter, iOS + Android)**
- The iOS AASA (served by `web/frontend`) claims `/items` (any query); the Android app-link filter adds `path="/items"` beside the singular item paths.
- `HomeDeepLink.parseItemList` reads the raw query into an ordered `(kind, id)` list (drops unknown keys, empty ids and repeats, stops at 10). `itemRouteFromAppLink` maps `https://h.omi.me/items?…` and `omi://h.omi.me/items?…` to `/items?…` with only the recognised pairs.
- The `items` route shows Home behind an "N Items" sheet (`showOmiSheet`). Each row uses the chat chip family for its kind (same icons and captions as edit receipts: `subject` / `checklist` / `psychology_outlined`; no new icons). Rows load independently. A tap opens the existing destination: conversation detail page, task sheet or read-only memory sheet. An item that is gone, foreign, cancelled, superseded or paywalled stays in place as a muted "No longer available" row (`ChatBlockUnavailable`). There is a loading row and an empty state.
- Memory ids resolve in one walk of the owner-wide index (`resolveIndexedMemoriesByIds`); `resolveIndexedMemoryById` now delegates to it. One new l10n key (`itemLinkListTitle`, plural) in all 49 locales via `scripts/l10n.py`.

**h.omi.me fallback (`web/frontend`)**
- `/items` renders the same content-free page as `/conversation/<id>`. It never reads the items. Preview metadata is the generic Omi card, with only the count in the description ("3 items in Omi"), plus `noindex`.
- iPhone and Android get "Open in the Omi App" (`omi://h.omi.me/items?…` / `intent://…`), the store badge, and "Sign in on the web".
- A Mac browser (user agent) gets a primary **Open in Omi for Mac** button to `omi-computer://items?…`, plus the web handoff. `omi-computer` is the released app's scheme (`codemagic.yaml`: tagged macOS builds set `URL_SCHEME="omi-computer"`; `desktop/macos/Desktop/Info.plist` holds the dev value `omi-computer-dev`). iPadOS Safari sends a Mac user agent, so on a touch screen the button switches to the iOS app link on the client.
- A parsed `searchParams` object groups repeated keys, which loses the interleaved order. `src/proxy.ts` therefore passes the raw query to the page in a request header and always overwrites any client copy. If the header is missing, the page falls back to the parsed params.

**Signed-in web app (`web/app`)**
- New protected route `/items?…` lists the items in order. Each row links to the closest existing view: conversations to `/conversations?id=`, tasks to `/tasks?highlight=<id>`, memories to `/memories?highlight=<id>`. Gone or foreign items get a muted "No longer available" row. A memory that a partial index walk did not find is never called deleted; it links to Memories instead. Archived memories are excluded.
- `?highlight=` is new on Tasks and Memories. Tasks switches to the list view, shows Completed when needed, and focuses the row, which scrolls itself into view. Memories reuses its existing scroll-and-highlight. Both act only when the item is in the loaded list.
- The h.omi.me handoff is `/login?next=%2Fitems%3F…`. `safeNextPath` already accepted it; a test now pins `/items?…` round-tripping and an off-site variant falling back to Home.

## Product invariants affected

- INV-MEM-1: memory reads here only resolve ids for display. Mobile keeps the existing Siri/deep-link filter (Short-term + Long-term, not locked). Web drops any row whose `layer` is not `short_term`/`long_term`. No tier, collection or default access policy changes.

## How it was verified

- `bash app/test.sh test/widgets/home/item_list_sheet_test.dart test/widgets/home/home_navigation_test.dart test/unit/chat_edit_receipt_test.dart`: all passed (45, plus `test/spine`). `flutter analyze` on the changed Dart files: no issues.
- `web/frontend`: `npm test` passed 199/199, including the new `/items` cases in `item-link-fallback.test.mjs`. ESLint is clean. `tsc` shows no errors in the touched files; the 34 existing errors are in unrelated files.
- `web/frontend` was run locally with `next dev`, placeholder Firebase config and no backend:
  - `curl` of `/items?task=t-1&conversation=c-1&memory=m-1&x=y` with a Mac UA returned `<title>Omi</title>`, "3 items in Omi" and `noindex, nofollow`. The response contained `omi-computer://items?task=t-1&conversation=c-1&memory=m-1` and `login?next=%2Fitems%3Ftask%3Dt-1%26conversation%3Dc-1%26memory%3Dm-1`, with URL order kept and the unknown key dropped.
  - With an iPhone UA the response contained `omi://h.omi.me/items?…`.
- `web/app`: `bun run check` passed (121 files, 643 tests). `bun run lint` showed no new findings in the touched code.
- **Not verified:**
  - A real universal-link or app-link open on a device: the AASA change takes effect only after `web/frontend` deploys.
  - The `omi-computer://items` open: the macOS handler is in the separate macOS PR.
  - A signed-in render of the web/app `/items` page: it is covered by vitest/jsdom only.

## Tests

- `app/test/widgets/home/item_list_sheet_test.dart`:
  - parsing (order across kinds, unknown keys, repeats, cap at 10, percent-decoding, malformed pairs);
  - h.omi.me/omi:// routing and rejected hosts and schemes;
  - Home tab selection;
  - the batched memory walk stopping early;
  - the sheet: order, unavailable rows in place, taps open only available rows, per-row loading, a failed lookup reading as unavailable, the empty state, and the count title;
  - light and dark renders (`--dart-define=OMI_ITEM_LIST_UI_EVIDENCE_DIR=<dir>` writes the screenshots below).
- `web/frontend/src/__tests__/item-link-fallback.test.mjs`: query parsing, the searchParams fallback, handoff, the Mac scheme and UA detection, count-only metadata, no fetch or echo, the proxy header, and AASA.
- `web/app/src/lib/__tests__/itemList.test.ts`: parsing, hrefs, highlight parsing, task focus index, the `/items` login `next`, and `findMemoriesByIds` (stops early; reports a partial walk as incomplete).
- `web/app/src/components/items/__tests__/ItemListPage.test.tsx`: order and links, the unavailable row, loading, a failed lookup, an unresolved memory, and the empty state.

## UI evidence

![Item list sheet, dark](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BasedHardware/omi/5cb6ea654b056cce3ab981c06be79f0ae690911e/.agent-artifacts/ui-evidence/items-list-link/001-mobile-ios-item-list-sheet-dark.png)
![Item list sheet, light](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BasedHardware/omi/5cb6ea654b056cce3ab981c06be79f0ae690911e/.agent-artifacts/ui-evidence/items-list-link/002-mobile-ios-item-list-sheet-light.png)
![/items fallback, iPhone](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BasedHardware/omi/5cb6ea654b056cce3ab981c06be79f0ae690911e/.agent-artifacts/ui-evidence/items-list-link/003-web-items-fallback-iphone.png)
![/items fallback, Mac browser](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BasedHardware/omi/5cb6ea654b056cce3ab981c06be79f0ae690911e/.agent-artifacts/ui-evidence/items-list-link/004-web-items-fallback-mac.png)

Mobile screenshots come from the widget render test (bundled SF Pro, iOS platform). Web screenshots are headless Chrome against a local `next dev`. The red "1 Issue" badge is the Next dev overlay reporting a third-party widget script, not this page.

## Failure class (fixes)

Failure-Class: none

## Integration

- Backend: emit `/items` only for 2+ items, with exactly these keys, at most 10 pairs, ids percent-encoded; one item keeps the singular link.
- macOS: handle `omi-computer://items?…` with the same query contract (ordered pairs, max 10, unknown keys ignored).

body:
## Why

Numbered terminals reserved the graph-wide maximum badge width on every side. A single-digit badge could inherit an unrelated label's width, and a vertical approach reserved width instead of the badge's 18px height. This forced outward-and-back paths even when a direct approach fitted.

## Changes

- Share provenance grouping, stable numbering and exact badge bounds between routing and SVG rendering.
- Carry separate longitudinal clearance and lateral protection for each endpoint through side selection, search, refinement, shortcuts and final spacing. Preserve directed target-only markers, undirected markers at both ends, and the plain 20px embedded Route source escape.
- Allocate top/bottom slots using each displayed number's width and left/right slots using badge height. Compare bounded side/port alignments again after height refinement.
- Reserve constrained numbered routes before flexible ordinary routes. Preserve distinct attachments, exact marker rectangles and legal approaches through final port exchanges and shortcutting.
- Move entire parallel runs with their two corners during final spacing, preserving separate perpendicular runs.
- Cover 72px vertical and 84px single-digit horizontal approaches, mixed one-/two-/three-digit geometry, reordered input, directed/undirected relationships, necessary detours, marker-corner collisions and large-fixture route quality.
- Update routing documentation and generated examples. Merge current main, preserving moved/import presentation changes and the upstream CI reporting fix.

## Validation

Exact published head: `e4d506821aaebd41abb42fa2380ef841733604d3`.

| CI gate | Result |
| --- | --- |
| [Rust tests](https://github.com/ritz-p/planorama/actions/runs/38221898271) | 521 passed; 1 ignored; no failures |
| [Clippy](https://github.com/ritz-p/planorama/actions/runs/38221898340) | Passed |
| [Formatting](https://github.com/ritz-p/planorama/actions/runs/38221898203) | Passed |
| [Maintained SVGs](https://github.com/ritz-p/planorama/actions/runs/38221898231) | Passed; all committed output current, no additional commit needed |

The large example's private-b → private Route Table numbered relationship is 709px with two bends and no reversal. Its legal single-digit horizontal approach remains 84px wide. The large fixture's close parallel length is 3,766px, within the unchanged 4,000px bound.

Only direct formatting and whitespace inspection ran locally. Builds, tests and SVG generation ran in CI. No Python scripts were added.

Closes #322

Dependent implementation: #333, based on `feature/issue-322`, adds visible border clearance while retaining this terminal geometry.

author: nateisern
body:
## What was wrong

The reviewed-image mechanism (`publish-reviewed-images.yml` + `reviewed-images.json`) had five defects:

1. The manual publisher pushed `oxy/website-api:<sha>`, the same tag `deploy-aws.yml` pushes on every merge, and its vacancy check refuses an existing tag. It could never publish a commit the deploy had already built. ECR repositories are tag-mutable.
2. The hash lived in two places, the JSON and a hardcoded `io.oxy.dockerfile.sha256` label in the workflow, and was only compared after the push.
3. Only the Dockerfile was hashed, not `.dockerignore`.
4. "Reviewed" had no effect on production: the deploy built whatever Dockerfile was on main.
5. Nothing at PR time noticed a Dockerfile change that left the pin stale, and the repo had no CODEOWNERS.

## The fix

This is the same design as OxyHQ/GoWay#164, and the scripts are byte-identical across repos.

**One pin, one script.** `.github/scripts/reviewed-image.py` replaces `publish-reviewed-image.py`. `reviewed-images.json` holds one `buildInputsSha256` per recipe. It is a hash over the Dockerfile bytes, context, target, and both ignore files BuildKit can apply: `<context>/.dockerignore` and `<dockerfile>.dockerignore`, which takes precedence. A missing ignore file is hashed as absent.

- **`check`** runs in `checks.yml`, job **`checks`**, on every `pull_request` and `merge_group`. That job has no `if:` and the trigger has no path filter. `CI complete` requires `checks` to succeed, and the `main: merge queue` ruleset requires `CI complete`, so the existing protection covers it with no ruleset change. `check` fails when a recipe's inputs differ from the pin, when no workflow runs `guard` for a recipe, when a workflow builds from `steps.reviewed.outputs` without running the guard itself, or when a workflow hardcodes a hash label.
- **`guard --recipe website-api`** runs in `deploy-aws.yml` just before `Build and push`. A mismatch stops the job before anything is built or pushed. `-f`, the context and the labels (`org.opencontainers.image.revision`, `org.opencontainers.image.source`, `io.oxy.source.tree`, `io.oxy.build-inputs.sha256`) come from its outputs. The `DOCKERFILE` literal in the workflow `env` is gone.
- **`pin`** is how the owner re-pins after reviewing a change.

**Publisher retired.** `deploy-aws.yml` is automatic (`on: push` to main) and now enforces the gate. The publisher ran once (2026-10-04).

**CODEOWNERS** adds `@NateIsern` for Dockerfiles, `.dockerignore`, the pin, the gate and every workflow.

**Stale pin: inputs this re-pin accepts, please review.** The old `dockerfileSha256` (`ed6b14b0…`) was last true at `0c45fe9`. Since then:

```
0a6d7b7 chore: pin Bun 1.4.3 everywhere (#161)   # Dockerfile: FROM oven/bun:1.3.14-alpine -> oven/bun:1.4.3-alpine
```

That is the only change to `Dockerfile` or `.dockerignore`. The new pin also covers `.dockerignore`, which this PR doesn't change.

## Proof the gates can fail

`test_reviewed_image.py` has 20 tests. Each mutation was asserted to apply, then reverted from a pristine copy, and the tree was green before and after. Every mutant was killed:

| Mutation | Caught by |
|---|---|
| Real `Dockerfile` edited without re-pin | `check` fails |
| Real `.dockerignore` line removed without re-pin | `check` fails |
| Guard step disarmed in `deploy-aws.yml` | `check` fails |
| Script stops hashing the `.dockerignore` files | suite fails |
| Script stops hashing the per-Dockerfile ignore | suite fails |
| Script stops hashing the target | suite fails |
| Absent ignore file hashed the same as an empty one | suite fails |
| `guard` skips the pin comparison | suite fails |
| Hardcoded hash labels allowed | suite fails |
| A commented-out guard counts | suite fails |
| `guard --recipe website-api-x` counts for `website-api` | suite fails |
| Unknown recipe fields accepted | suite fails |
| A workflow building from guard outputs need not run the guard | suite fails |

`bun run validate:bun-pin` still passes (it scans workflows). `actionlint` shows no findings on `checks.yml` or `deploy-aws.yml`, before or after. Biome is clean on the JSON.

## Owner follow-ups (not in this PR)

- **ECR tag immutability.** `oxy-infra/terraform-uswest2/ecr.tf` sets `MUTABLE`. Plain `IMMUTABLE` would break the deploy, which re-pushes `:latest`. The workable setting is `IMMUTABLE_WITH_EXCLUSION` with `latest` excluded, which is an oxy-infra Terraform change.
- **Base image not pinned by digest.** `FROM oven/bun:1.4.3-alpine` is a mutable tag, so a re-pushed tag changes the build without changing a hashed byte. GoWay, Syra and Willo pin `tag@sha256:`.
- **Code-owner review.** CODEOWNERS requests your review. It can't be a hard requirement while you are the only maintainer, because GitHub doesn't let a PR's author satisfy code-owner review.





---
**Final fleet gate (later commit):** `reviewed-image.py` and `test_reviewed_image.py` are byte-identical across all 17 repos (sha256 `c16423c4…` / `bae571cd…`). `check` now also fails any workflow that builds from `steps.reviewed*.outputs` without running the guard itself, so a second build path can no longer lose its guard unnoticed. 21 fixture tests; mutation harness re-run on this branch, every mutant killed.

## Owner sign-off review: build inputs

**Requires owner sign-off: do not merge without the owner's explicit approval.**

One recipe: `website-api` (`Dockerfile`, context `.`, no target). It is the only production image; the frontend ships to Cloudflare Pages and has no image.

### Last reviewed version, accepted commits, new pin

| Input | Last reviewed version | Commits this pin accepts |
|---|---|---|
| `Dockerfile` | `0c45fe9` on main (2026-07-18), the newest main commit whose bytes hash to the old `dockerfileSha256` `ed6b14b0…` | `0a6d7b7` chore: pin Bun 1.4.3 everywhere (#161); `7f51e60` the fixes below |
| `.dockerignore` | never pinned; reviewed in full (last changed `96eea5e`, 2026-06-25) | `7f51e60` |
| `Dockerfile.dockerignore` | absent, stays absent | none |

The "Inputs this re-pin accepts" section above is correct for the PR as it was (`0c45fe9`, then `0a6d7b7` only). It is superseded by `7f51e60`, which changes both files. `origin/main` (`0a6d7b7`) has not moved since the PR branched, so no merge was needed.

New pin: `buildInputsSha256` `064c5f22…fe104` → **`2973865cd335d23b13d54462e15815e62da75e9a4f4af58d0f33625b3da5a90b`**.

### Review: website-api

| Change or finding | Assessment |
|---|---|
| `FROM oven/bun:1.3.14-alpine` → `1.4.3-alpine` (`0a6d7b7`) | Informational. Official Docker Hub image; same Bun as `package.json` and CI, enforced by `validate:bun-pin`. Base is Alpine 3.24.2 minirootfs. |
| Base image was a mutable tag | **Fixed here.** Now `oven/bun:1.4.3-alpine@sha256:629e1741…22373`, the multi-arch index (lists linux/amd64 and linux/arm64), with a comment that a bump needs a new digest and a re-pin. The tag stays for `check-bun-pin.mjs`, which already accepts `@sha256:`. |
| Ran as root (no `USER`) | **Fixed here.** `USER bun` (uid 1000, created by the base image). App and `node_modules` stay root-owned and are readable, not writable, by the app. The server writes nothing to disk (multer uses memory storage; the only `writeFile` is a dev script). The live task definition (`oxy-website-api:33`) sets no `user`, mounts or volumes, and the port is 8080, so no privilege is needed. |
| `.dockerignore` excluded `.env` / `.env.*` at the root only | **Fixed here.** Now `**/.env` and `**/.env.*`. Nothing in the image reads `.env.example`. |
| `.dockerignore` did not exclude `.worktrees/` (gitignored local checkouts) | **Fixed here.** A local build from the main checkout copied every worktree, untracked files included. CI checkouts have none. |
| Other gitignored local files (`review-artifacts/`, `.superdesign/`, `*.local`, `.idea`) are not excluded | Informational. Local builds only; the CI checkout has no untracked files. |
| `.git`, `.github`, `node_modules`, `dist`, logs excluded | I

body:
## Summary
Adds a built-in partner mapping template, «DrDr (قرارداد)», to the bulk provider import. It covers the owner's data-exchange contract with DrDr.

- **Selection:** the template is picked automatically when the file has `site` = «دکتر دکتر» or drdr.ir profile links. It is seeded at boot, editable, and protected from deletion, with a restore-defaults button.
- **Reading the file:**
  - Grouped files (`groups[].items[]`) are read, with `$parent`/`$root` access.
  - Records are keyed by the partner's numeric profile id (`drdr:<id>`).
- **Specialities:** «تخصص / فوق تخصص / فلوشیپ / A-B» titles map to the main speciality, with fellowships as extra specialities.
  - The group slug serves as a hint.
  - A near match is only suggested and never applied silently.
- **City:** taken from the map pin first (geoFromPoint), then the address prefix, then the file's section.
  - Disagreements between pin and address are reported.
- **Extracted from the bio:** the council number, office hours, insurers and Instagram.
  - Lists written as space-joined words are split by greedy catalogue match.
  - Leftover pieces wait for review (create / map / split / skip), with an optional AI split.
- **Bio cleanup:** the partner's booking promos, copied reviews and repeated contact sections are removed. The phrase list is editable.
- **New `DoctorProfile.diseases` field:** shown on the public page, editable in the admin and doctor-panel forms. The public page now also shows weekly hours and splits the introduction into paragraphs.
- **Traceability:** partner, contract ref, file date and profile/photo URLs are kept internally only.

Accuracy on the 50-doctor sample (dry run): 50/50 council numbers, 50/50 main specialities, 50/50 cities, 28/50 hours, 29/50 with insurers, 0 errors. The sample data was removed after testing; the real import is run by the owner.

## Benchmark
- **The leaders:** Doctolib, Docplanner and Paziresh24 build their directories from partner and registry feeds, with unclaimed listings.
- **NoyanAI:** maps the partner's free text into structured fields, with a dry-run accuracy report and per-value review.

## Checks
- `tsc` passes in both repos and lint is clean.
- Backend `npm test` passes 26/26 and the build passes.
- A crawl of the public and admin import pages found no errors.

author: chrisenussbaum
body:
## Problem
On phones, scrolling the Projects page past the live previews (e.g. Moments) crashed the page. Each coded-project preview is a full 1280px desktop page inside a scaled iframe. They loaded as you scrolled and were never unloaded (`previewIO.unobserve(box)` after load), so a phone held every site, with its scripts, images, and any GIFs, in memory at once until the browser killed the tab.

Measured before the fix with a phone-sized browser and stand-in pages: all 4 previews loaded and stayed loaded.

## Fix
- **Phones / touch / data-saver:** previews no longer auto-load. Each card gets a "Load live preview" button; only one preview stays live at a time. The card overlay link still opens the site.
- **Desktop:** previews load near the viewport and unload once scrolled well past.
- Unloading navigates the iframe to `about:blank`, which frees the page and its decoded images/GIFs. Changing the project filter releases previews in hidden cards.

## Testing
Headless browser, phone profile: 0 previews loaded while scrolling; tap loads one, tapping another swaps it, tapping again unloads, filter change unloads, overlay link intact. Desktop: each card loads when reached (4/4), none left loaded at the bottom of the page, no JS errors. Full five-page regression (links, images, overflow, nav state, booking/Calendly params, filters) still passes. Real project sites were not reachable from the test environment, so previews were tested against stand-in pages; I could not confirm the Moments GIF specifically.

author: 1sakshm
body:
### What

The language selector at the top of every page always sends users to the **home page** of the chosen language (#376). The links are built with a hard-coded `/` path in `display_page()`:

```perl
$langs .= "<li><a href=\"" . format_subdomain($osubdomain) . "/\">" ...
```

This PR makes the selector link to the **same page** in the other language.

**Approach (reuses the existing canonical redirects).** URLs are localized (`/facets/labels/bio` in French vs `/facets/labels/organic` in English), and routing only accepts tag paths in the subdomain language or in English. So instead of computing a fully localized URL for every language on every page, each page type records a **language-neutral link** that every subdomain understands. The target subdomain then redirects to its own canonical URL using the redirects that already exist:

| Page | Language-neutral link | Then on the target subdomain |
|---|---|---|
| Facet / tag pages | English tag type + canonical tag id, e.g. `/facets/labels/en:organic` (negative tags `-en:...` and group-by kept) | `canonicalize_request_tags_and_redirect_to_canonical_url` redirects to the translated tag URL |
| Product pages | `/product/[code]` | the product name check redirects to the canonical product URL |
| Text pages | `/[textid]` | `text_route` redirects to the translated route |
| Search | `/search` | — |
| Anything else | `/` (unchanged behaviour) | |

- `$request_ref->{language_neutral_link}` is set where each page already computes its canonical link (`canonicalize_request_tags_and_redirect_to_canonical_url`, `display_product`, `display_text`, `search_route`).
- `get_language_neutral_link()` appends the query parameters with the existing `extension_and_query_parameters_to_redirect_url()` (routing already strips `utm`, `cc` and `lc`), and HTML-escapes the result, since the query string comes from the request and is inserted into an `href` attribute.
- New integration test `tests/integration/language_selector_links.t`: facet page (link + redirect to the French label URL), negative tag + group-by, product page (link + redirect to the English product URL), search query parameters (HTML-escaped), home page.

**Expected test results:** the language selector is in the header of every page, so the stored HTML expected results of non-home pages (web_html, page_crawler, product_read, etc.) will change, in the language menu links only. They need to be regenerated (`/update_tests_results`). I didn't include them here because I couldn't run the stack locally (see below).

**Points for review:**
- One redirect hop when switching language (to the neutral URL, then to the canonical URL). The alternative, computing localized URLs for every language on each page render, felt heavier. Happy to change if you prefer.
- Pages not covered yet still link to the home page: `/cgi/*` pages, missions, the paginated home page. They could be added later the same way.

### Screenshot or video

Not available yet (see above). To be added.

### Related issue(s) and discussion

- Fixes #376

author: chenchaoxu7575
body:
## Purpose

Tracks **P0 in #6867**; depends on **#8202**. This draft is based on the tested R0 revision `8f84247b1`; its diff against `main` currently includes R0. [P0-only diff](https://github.com/chenchaoxu7575/vllm-omni/compare/8f84247b1...perf/pi05-p0-bf16).

Adds opt-in Pi0.5 BF16 and runtime optimizations across vision, request setup, prefix computation, and decoder kernels, with PyTorch/cuBLAS fallbacks for unsupported configurations.

## Test Plan

**vLLM Version:** 0.30.0  
**vLLM-Omni Commit:** GPU-tested `57c5d4fc2` (`bf16_008`), based on #8202 at `8f84247b1`. The published branch has identical inference/benchmark code, DCO sign-offs, and two test-only typing/import-spec fixes; the five affected CPU cases and local pre-commit checks passed. These results do **not** validate the newer R0 head `fceed074` or current `main`.

PyTorch 2.13.0+cu132, Triton 3.7.1, Transformers 5.14.1. Per GPU: **1,440 same-policy eager/fused/graph action comparisons were bit-exact**; **327 unit, 97 kernel, and 71 parity tests passed** (12 kernel / 1 parity cases skipped). NVTX and Nsight Systems CUDA Graph node traces confirmed the selected kernels executed. Independent LeRobot decoder checks matched 110 tensors per GPU; this is decoder precision evidence, not a full-policy or closed-loop quality claim.

<details>
<summary>Repository test and benchmark commands</summary>

```bash
python -m pytest tests/diffusion/models/pi05/test_pi05_units.py \
  tests/diffusion/models/pi05/test_pi05_fused_kernels.py --run-level core_model
PI05_PARITY_MODEL_PATH=/path/to/pi05_base python -m pytest \
  tests/diffusion/models/pi05/test_pi05_cuda_graph_parity.py --run-level full_model
OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 \
python benchmarks/pi05/bench_pi05.py --model /path/to/pi05_base \
  --dtype bfloat16 --bs 1 --views 3 --execution-mode graph \
  --vision-precision selective_bf16 --lm-precision lerobot_bf16 \
  --batch-cameras --precompute-adarms --hoist-denoise-invariants --prefix-kv-only \
  --warmup 20 --iters 50 --out pi05_p0_bench/
```

The command above uses the repository's synthetic fixture. The grouped results below come from a separate 13-configuration fixed-input ablation; publishing that harness and its raw artifacts remains a draft follow-up.

</details>

## Test Result

Compared with **Shijie's optimized R0 (#8202, `8f84247b1`)**, model wall-time p50 improves from **66.99 → 22.32 ms on H100 (66.7% reduction)** and **73.16 → 40.07 ms on RTX 5090 (45.2% reduction)**.

Same physical GPU, checkpoint and fixed inputs per comparison: BS1, three cameras, 50 action tokens, 10 denoise steps, one CPU thread, 20 warmups / 50 unprofiled samples. Timings exclude preprocessing and serving overhead.

| Category | Main changes | H100 time saved | RTX 5090 time saved |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| Vision | Selective BF16, camera batching, contiguous embedding layout | ~40.4 ms | ~28.8 ms |
| Precomputation and reuse | Time/AdaRMS precompute; per-request mask, position and RoPE reuse | ~3.2 ms | ~4.0 ms |
| Prefix computation | Final layer KV-only: skip unused attention and MLP work | ~0.5 ms | ~1.2 ms |
| Decoder precision and fusion | BF16 inputs/residuals; norm, softmax, QK and H100 QKV fusion | ~0.5 ms | **−1.4 ms** |

Grouped savings are rounded, cumulative measurements starting from the P0 source with R0 settings. The decoder group includes a precision-policy change and adds about 1.4 ms on RTX 5090; the overall P0 gain is primarily from vision and runtime optimizations.

Before ready for review: rebase onto the accepted R0 baseline and revalidate, publish the fixed-input harness/raw evidence, and resolve the remaining performance and task-quality evaluation scope.

AI assistance: Codex assisted with implementation, tests, profiling, and this description.

author: ya-luotao
body:
## Why

`tests/pick_cli.rs::max_wait_gives_up_when_the_next_check_is_later` (R23) went red whenever a second turned between its plain run and its first `--wait` run: the fixture's reset was exactly an hour away, the reasons name the reset, and `resets in 1h` became `59m`. The expected next-check timestamp was also computed from a second look at the clock, so a minute turning between the two looks failed the `--max-wait 0` run (found by the local review, reproduced at second 29).

LESSONS.md gets the lesson batch 3 taught on merge: two lanes changed the two ends of one piece of data (`UsageRow.window_minutes` and the pace that reads the window length), each branch was reviewed green alone, and the merge commit was what the GitHub review caught.

## What

- `used_up_for(resets_in)` returns the reset second it wrote (via a new `limit_at`; `limit` now calls it with `now() + resets_in`, same computation as before). `used_up_for_an_hour` keeps its hour and its two-value interface for its other five callers.
- The test's reset sits a day and ninety minutes away (`1d1h` for the next 30 minutes); the expected next check comes from the reset as written; the give-up line is asserted whole for all three `--max-wait` values, not only `0`.
- LESSONS.md: "Review the merge head when two lanes changed the two ends of one piece of data."

## Verified

- Reproduction: a 1.1 s sleep after the plain run turned the test red on main (`resets in 59m` vs `1h`) and green with the fix; the reviewer's boundary-aligned probe (fixture at second 29, sleep across second 30) failed the first version's timestamp assertion and passes the amended one.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --test pick_cli` 55/55.
- Local codex review (gpt-6-astra, max): round 1 CHANGES REQUESTED (the timestamp race above), round 2 APPROVE with no findings.

## Decisions for the maintainer to confirm

- This is a flake fix, so the "red with the fix reverted" rule is met by the sleep reproduction above rather than by a new test.
- The wording stability is bounded (30 minutes), not a frozen clock; the test does not read a clock a second time, so the bound only needs to cover the test's own run.

author: kostagjorgjievski
body:
## What and why

TASK_009 PR B, the deferred second half (the task's split instruction, quoted in #57): the `evolvets foundation` CLI and `compare_rebuild` — the read-only drift diagnostic for caches that are "built once, content-hashed, verified by hash" rather than bit-reproducible.

- **CLI** (`runner/cli.py`): `evolvets foundation build --dataset D --model M [--batch-size N] [--device auto|cpu|cuda] [--per-family N] [--root foundation_cache]`, `foundation verify --dataset D --model M`, `foundation compare --dataset D --model M --sample N --seed S`, with the usual `--cache-root/--data-root/--manifest-dir` defaults. Per the task, until PR C adds the real adapters every command accepts only `--model fake`; the five registry names exit nonzero with a message naming PR C (`feat/foundation-models`). `--device cuda` is likewise refused for the fake (it records `cpu`); `auto`/`cpu` both build on cpu today.
- **`compare_rebuild`** (`foundation/store.py`) + **`RebuildReport`** (`foundation/interfaces.py`, new dataclass — the task names it): draws a seeded sample of `sample` origins without replacement from every (series, origin) pair the cache holds (so the sample spreads over series in proportion to their origin counts; `sample` ≥ all compares all), rebuilds each sampled origin's context exactly as the build did (`values[max(0, t+1-L):t+1]` with the manifest's `max_context`), recomputes it through the adapter (validated and monotone-fixed with the builder's own `_checked_row`/`_fix_crossing`), and reports the max absolute and relative difference of the 0.5 quantile against the stored rows. It is a diagnostic: read-only (tests hash the whole tree before/after), and it reads stored bytes without the manifest's SHA-256 gate — integrity is `verify`'s job, and the diagnostic must be able to describe a cache whose numbers drifted.
- Input guard: the recompute uses `public_inputs` only, and refuses inputs whose `source`, series ids, lengths or `values_sha256` no longer match the manifest, before recomputing anything.

Interface note: the task's sketch is `compare_rebuild(root, dataset, model, adapter, sample, seed)`; I matched those six parameters exactly in position and appended two **defaulted** data paths (`data_root=Path("data")`, `manifest_dir=Path("data/manifests")`) — the recompute needs the public inputs, exactly as the CLI sketch's `--data-root/--manifest-dir` exist alongside the options it names. The CLI always passes them explicitly.

## How it was tested

Full local suite, exactly the CI commands: `uv sync --locked --group dev`, `ruff check .`, `ruff format --check .`, `mypy`, `lint-imports`, the four `import-probe.sh` probes, `pytest` — **643 passed** (631 at #57 + 12 new: 5 store, 7 CLI).

Task test 9 (`tests/foundation/test_store.py`, 5 tests):
- full-sample compare of the intact fake cache: zeros, `n_compared == n_total == 399`, and the cache tree is byte-identical before/after (never edits);
- seeded sampling: same seed redraws the same origins (`n_compared == 10 < n_total`), still zero difference with the deterministic fake;
- one changed stored 0.5 value in a **copy** of the cache: `max_abs_diff ≈ 1.0`, `max_rel_diff > 0` — while `verify_foundation_cache` raises on the same copy (diagnostic vs integrity);
- public inputs from a differently-split fixture (512 rows) are refused before recomputing;
- `sample`/`seed` validation (0, negative, bools) and an adapter/model name mismatch each raise `FoundationError`.

Task test 10 (`tests/foundation/test_cli.py`, 7 tests): build → verify → compare end to end with `--model fake` (manifest records `batch_size 16, device "cpu", dtype "float64"`; verify prints the build's line again; compare prints `compared 20/399 origins, max_abs 0.000e+00, max_rel 0.000e+00`); `--device cuda` refused for the fake; every command on a real model name exits 1 naming PR C and creates no directory; verify catches a flipped byte and passes again after restore; `--sample 0` is a FAIL line; `synthetic-dev` needs `--per-family` (10278 origins with it) and then builds/OKs; an unknown model never reaches the command (argparse exit 2).

Also hand-run end to end through the console entry point on `synthetic-dev` (build/verify/compare + real-model refusal), which is how I caught that the task specifies `--dataset` as a flag, not a positional.

## Part of a stack?

TASK_009 (docs/tasks/TASK_009_foundation_experts.md), PR B of four, second half. PR A merged as #56; the store half of PR B merged as #57; this is the `feat/foundation-cache-cli` follow-up #57 announced. Next: PR C (`feat/foundation-models`, the five real adapters + dependency groups; will be split per the task if it exceeds ~500 lines), then PR D (`feat/foundation-pool`).

## Integrity checklist

- [x] No agent-editable package can reach sealed or live data (import-linter passes; compare reads public inputs through `cache.datasets.public_inputs` only, exactly like the build)
- [x] No look-ahead: targets only reach code through arena label release (the recompute rebuilds contexts with the builder's tested rule `values[max(0, t+1-L):t+1]`; nothing touches targets)
- [x] No frozen component changed (no change to `arena/`, `ledger/` or a tagged component; `foundation/interfaces.py` gains the `RebuildReport` dataclass the task names, beside the dataclasses PR B added)
- [x] All randomness is seeded from config (the origin sample is `random.Random(seed)`; `--seed` is required on compare)
- [x] No data, cache, ledger, secret or large file committed (tests write only under `tmp_path`; no new dependency, no lockfile change)
- [x] No test weakened, skipped or deleted to make CI pass

## Notes for the reviewer

- **Size:** ~700 added lines (219 CLI, 171 store, 20 interfaces, ~290 tests, 9 comment). The task rates PR B ~400 lines *including* this half's CLI + `compare_rebuild` + tests 9–10; PR B's store core alone was ~1350, so this half lands at roughly the size the task budgeted for everything it contains. I did not split further: the CLI without `compare_rebuild` would ship a `compare` command that fails, and `compare_rebuild` without the CLI would be dead code.
- **`--device` today:** parsed and validated on `build` per the task's option list, forwarded to the adapter selector; the fake always records `cpu`, and `cuda` is refused rather than silently ignored. PR C's `make_adapter(spec, device)` consumes it for real.
- **`--batch-size` default 32:** the task names the option but no default; 32 is recorded in every manifest, so any future change is visible per cache. Compare recomputes one context at a time (a diagnostic against stored bytes); batch sensitivity is PR C's smoke check (1e-3 relative), not this PR's question.
- **Compare exit code:** always 0 when the comparison ran, whatever the drift — no threshold is specified anywhere, and inventing one would make a diagnostic into a gate. The numbers are the output.
- `verify` also refuses real model names with the PR C message today: no cache for them can exist before PR C, and PR C rewrites this guard into registry resolution anyway.

author: aaw123m
body:
## Reproduction
An iPhone that successfully QR-pairs with HTDT shows `Receiver cannot stage payload schema frame (bundle would be rejected)` even though the native receiver accepts frame descriptors. Its `accepted_payload_schemas` intentionally advertises only versioned schema IDs; the support-matrix `frame` family has `schema_id: null`, `unversioned: true`. The sender was inventing the wire schema token `frame`, then rejecting it.

## Fix
- Exclude known unversioned/external families when building preflight's advertised-schema inventory. Do **not** change archive bytes, schema validation, or server-side admission.
- Defensive checker exemption strictly for known unversioned families with no schema ID; unknown future schemas remain hard failures.
- Add regression tests for frame compatibility and unknown schema rejection; GitHub Actions runs Swift tests and an iOS build.

## Distinct HTTP 404 issue
HTDT's GET `/capabilities` intentionally responds while the pairing offer is `offered`, but POST `/deliveries` responds 404 until the **desktop** operator enters the code and presses **確認** (the receiver pairing must be `active`). The user must finish the PC-side confirmation; this PR doesn't weaken that authorization requirement or mask invalid tokens. Re-pair and verify active on both ends if the pending offer has expired.

Physical iPhone-to-PC transfer still needs manual confirmation after new app installation.

author: volkiaa
body:
Stacked on #29; GitHub will retarget this PR to `main` once #29 merges.

## What changed

- New `--fail-on CRITICAL|HIGH|MEDIUM|LOW|INFO|none` flag. It's case-insensitive and defaults to `CRITICAL` (PLAN §4.5). It reuses `parseFailOn` and `evaluateSeverityGate` from `src/core/run-severity.ts`, added in #29.
- `analyzeCheckout` builds the run report once, writes it, and returns the same object for gating. New `formatJsonRunReport` and `formatTextRunReport` take an already-built report; the existing `render*` functions stay as thin wrappers.
- Exit policy (agreed in the design review):

| Exit | Meaning |
|---:|---|
| `0` | Nothing reached the threshold, or the lockfile is unchanged (no output) |
| `1` | A finding reached the threshold, or an operational error; stderr says which |
| `2` | `--strict` found unanalyzed content. This takes precedence over the threshold because PLAN §4.5 promises it; stderr still prints both causes |
| `64` | Invalid usage, including a bad `--fail-on` value. Rejected before any Git or network work |

- README: documents the flag and adds an exit-code table. Wording is qualified for runs without `--strict` and for runs that produce no report.

## Why

During verification, a real run that added `esbuild` (with a `postinstall` that uses `https`, `child_process` and `process.env`) produced 5 CRITICAL findings and exited **0**. Only the GitHub Action had a gate, so any other CI let it through silently.

**Behavior change:** CLI users who relied on exit 0 with CRITICAL findings must pass `--fail-on none`. The package is still private and unpublished (`package.json:5`), and no workflow or script in the repo invokes the CLI.

## Design review

Codex reviewed the design and approved it with revisions: strict-over-gate precedence, and operational errors keep exit 1. It then reviewed the diff and found nothing blocking. Its non-blocking suggestions are applied:
- The downgrade test now uses canonical SHA-512 tokens, so the 404 path really runs, and it asserts `fetch/http-status`. Previously the fake integrity strings were rejected before `fetch` was called.
- A callback-order assertion proves the report is written before the gate diagnostic.
- The invalid-threshold test uses a missing directory and a `fetch` that throws, which proves validation happens before any Git or network work.
- A new integration test runs an allowlisted CRITICAL hook through the JSON path. It shows the finding stays visible as suppressed, `gateSeverity.CRITICAL` is 0, and the run exits 0.
- README wording is qualified as described above.

## Non-obvious constructs

- **`catch` that narrows by class and rethrows** (`parseFailOnArgument` in `cli-options.ts`). Only `SeverityGateConfigurationError`, the known parse failure, becomes a `CliUsageError` (exit 64). Anything else is a programming error and is rethrown unchanged, so a bug can't masquerade as a user typo (CLAUDE.md: no bare catches).
- **`...(fetchImpl === undefined ? {} : { fetchImpl })`** in the test helper. With `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`, explicitly passing `fetchImpl: undefined` isn't the same as omitting the property, so the spread leaves the key out entirely when there's no stub.

## Verification

- `npm test`: 247 tests / 27 files pass.
- `lint`, `typecheck`, `format:check` and `check:deps` pass; `package:action` was rebuilt.

## Noticed, not touched

- SARIF still emits nothing for unavailable-package integrity mismatches. That's the next stacked PR, with no invented location, per the design review.
- SARIF still emits nothing for lockfile findings either.
