body:
## Summary

This redesigns the manual "Add ingredients" flow on iOS (Flutter) and the web:
- **Meal sheet:** shows the plate first, with an optional meal name, a macro ring and the ingredient rows.
- **Add sheet:** search, stacked over the meal sheet.
- **Food page:** each food is weighed before it goes in, using a vessel tape (cut / bowl / plate / cup).
- **Web:** phone width mirrors the iOS sheets; on md+ the composer keeps its inline rows, restyled.
- **Search:** results now carry card display fields.
- **Save:** takes an optional meal name.

## Changes

- **Backend**
  - Ingredient search returns `displayNameEn`, a raw/cooked `stateLabel` (only where it changes the weight), `brand` and a `vessel` hint. The card-display rules were audited against the real Vietnamese composition table.
  - The manual save takes an optional `name`. A named meal is saved as one dish; an unnamed one as one dish per food.
- **iOS**
  - New meal sheet, add sheet and food page, plus a `MacroRing` widget.
  - The logic lives in pure `logic/manual/` files (amount, display, peek strip).
  - The open food page is a sealed `NewFood` / `MealFood` type, and grams are never null.
- **Web**
  - Phone sheets under `components/logging/input/manual/sheet/`, each mirroring its Flutter twin.
  - A pure plate model in `lib/domain/logging/` (`macrosAt`, `sumMacros`, `plateTotals`, `manualPeek`).
  - One save path: `useManualSave` taking `ManualMealItem`s, with `manualDishOf` shared by the server action and the optimistic card.
- **Contract bounds:** the 30-food cap, 5,000 g per food and 200-character name each have one owner per platform. The contract reads them from there.

**Deliberate behavior to note**
- **Each open of the meal sheet is a new meal, on both platforms.** Closing it (X, swipe or overlay) discards the plate. Keeping a draft could be a follow-up if wanted.
- **Web, after a successful save:** the plate stays drawn while the sheet slides closed and clears on the next open, so it never blanks mid-animation. iOS still resets before the sheet closes; matching it is a one-line follow-up if wanted.
- **The 31st food:**
  - "Add to meal" is disabled and says "A meal holds up to 30 ingredients".
  - "Add ingredient" is disabled with the same note.
  - The md+ composer stops adding rows at 30.
  - Foods already in the meal can still be updated.
- **Unknown calories read "—", never 0.** An empty plate reads 0.
- **Mid-save:** the iOS meal sheet now holds against the barrier and back gestures. The web add sheet now focuses its search on open (before, the meal sheet's focus trap took focus back).

**Deferred, with reasons**
- **`lib/api/openapi/schema-shapes.ts` is at 399/400 lines** (this PR adds 8 for the four search fields), and `vessel` is described in prose rather than as a `oneOf`. Splitting the file along the `paths/` seams is the fix, but no test pins the emitted document, so it gets its own PR.
- **Vessel tape unification:** the Flutter manual tape is the fourth copy; the other three are base widgets in `feed/` and `scan/`.

- **Duplicate meal on retry:** if a manual save's response is lost, retrying can log the meal twice. Each attempt sends a fresh `mealId`, and the server answers a reused id with CONFLICT. Barcode and label scan already reuse the id and handle "already saved".

author: yonatann
body:
**Not merged / not released / not rolled — review only.**

B5 of the Baileys vs WA Web wire-parity series (login-time traffic).

## What WA Web does (verified offsets, scratchpad/waweb/*.js)
- No `<iq xmlns="encrypt"><count/></iq>` exists anywhere in the 30 bundle files (no `wap("count"` hit). The login upload is the passive task "KeyUpload" in `WAWebRegisterPassiveTasks` (b06.js, after @2406148), registered only when `!waSignalStore.getServerHasPreKeys()`.
- `WAWebHandlePreKeyLow` (b12@1723946): `notification type=encrypt` with `<count>`/`<pq_count>` triggers an upload. `WAWebHandleDigestKey` (b12@1583869): `notification type=encrypt` with `<digest>` triggers `digestKey()`. The only other digest caller is `rotateKey` (b06@2393269).
- `WAWebUploadPreKeysJob` (b06@2278756): 812 keys, retry loop.
- Passive tasks run through `WAWebPassiveModeManager.executePassiveTasks` (b06@2382734), fallback `DEFAULT_MAX_PASSIVE_MODE_TIME_MS` = 60s.

## Change (after review, b537fb69a0)
- CB:success no longer sends the count IQ or the digest IQ. Persisted `creds.serverHasPreKeys` (WA Web `setServerHasPreKeys`): set false BEFORE every upload and on every PreKeyLow, set true only after the upload IQ succeeds (b06@2278756). A failed, timed-out or killed upload leaves it false, so the next login re-uploads. Login policy (`Utils/login-traffic-policy.ts`) checks when it is false, `undefined` (legacy session: one deferred check; if the server has keys it is set true), or the latest prekey is missing locally. The check is deferred to offline-delivery-end (`CB:ib,,offline`), 60s fallback timer cleared on close.
- PreKeyLow handler uploads the full 812 batch unconditionally (was 5, gated on count<5).
- Server `<digest>` notification handled; a 404 from the digest IQ re-uploads 812 (WAWebDigestKeyJob b06@2282389) instead of throwing. Fixes the former `countChild!.attrs` TypeError on count-less encrypt notifications.

## Not done / risks
- `offline_batch count=100` NOT changed. WA Web (b08@645692) is adaptive (200, steps 100/50/10) and re-requests after processing; a bigger batch risks the offline-replay heap OOM (BE#395) and needs a live capture. Follow-up.
- Not live-validated. Known gap: signed-prekey rotation (`rotateKey`, then digest) has zero callers today; separate follow-up.
- Independent of the backend B6 PR.

author: bramlambertjansen
body:
Pakket C. **Gestapeld op #102** (base `docs/nieuwe-app-playbook`), omdat fase 6.2 van het playbook in beide PR's verandert. Eerst #102 mergen; daarna wijst deze PR automatisch naar `main`. Licht pad.

## Wat
- `scripts/github-ruleset.sh <owner>/<repo> [--zonder-codeql]`: zet de ruleset `main` via `gh api`, met `deletion`, `non_fast_forward`, `pull_request` (0 goedkeuringen, `required_review_thread_resolution: true`, merge en squash, `bypass_actors: []`) en `required_status_checks` met `integration_id` 15368 (GitHub Actions). POST als er nog geen ruleset `main` is, anders PUT op hetzelfde id; opnieuw draaien kan dus veilig. Bij "Upgrade to GitHub Pro" volgt een duidelijke melding en exit 1. De zichtbaarheid verandert nooit. De eigenaar draait het script; de agent heeft het niet tegen een echte repo gedraaid.
- `test/scripts/github-ruleset.test.ts`: `gh` als stub op `PATH`. De verwachte checks komen **uit `.github/workflows/*.yml`** (`name:` op jobniveau, de codeql-matrix uitgeschreven, `diff-guard` uitgezonderd volgens ADR 0017). De test controleert:
  - dat de workflows precies de 8 checks uit de opdracht leveren;
  - dat de controle een payload zonder `osv-scanner` vangt (`ontbrekend()` geeft `['osv-scanner']`): de test faalt dus op een ontbrekende check;
  - de payload bij POST, PUT bij een bestaande ruleset, `--zonder-codeql`, de foutmelding voor een private repo, en de gebruiksmelding zonder aanroep van `gh`.
- Playbook fase 6.2: het inline JSON-blok uit #102 is vervangen door een overdracht van het script aan de eigenaar.
- CHANGELOG-notitie.

## Besluiten van de eigenaar (in deze sessie)
- Inhoud volgens de opdracht en framework §10, niet een kopie van `main-dicht`. **`main-dicht` op de template wijkt af**: `required_review_thread_resolution: false`, en `codeql (javascript-typescript)` ontbreekt (`gh api repos/BramLambertJansen/template/rulesets/24914664`). Recht te zetten door de eigenaar, buiten deze PR.
- `--zonder-codeql` voor een private repo zonder GHAS.

Niet gecontroleerd: de checknamen zoals ze echt op een PR staan. `gh api …/check-runs` werd in deze sessie geweigerd (deny-regel `gh api *check-runs*`). De namen komen uit de workflow-bestanden; ze zijn gelijk aan de contexts in `main-dicht`, die op PR's wel groen worden.

## Checks
**Niet gedraaid**: geen Node, pnpm of mise op deze machine. `pnpm gate:fast` en `vitest` zijn dus niet uitgevoerd, en de lokale git-hooks liepen niet. Wel gedaan: `bash -n` (syntax ok), en alle testscenario's in bash nagebootst met dezelfde `gh`-stub:
- POST: exit 0, payload geldige JSON (python `json.load`), regeltypes `deletion, non_fast_forward, pull_request, required_status_checks`, en de checks gelijk aan de jobnamen uit de workflows (`equal True`, 8 checks);
- bestaande ruleset: PUT naar `rulesets/42`;
- `--zonder-codeql`: 6 checks;
- private repo: exit 1 met de melding;
- `[]`, `geen-slash` en `--onbekend`: exit 2 met de gebruiksmelding, zonder aanroep van `gh`.

Dat vervangt de vitest-run in CI niet.

## Werkstraat
De test is geschreven vóór het script, maar in dezelfde sessie. De rolhek-hook draait hier niet (geen `node`; fail-open), dus de testerrol was niet onafhankelijk. Er is ook geen onafhankelijke review gedaan; die ligt bij de eigenaar.

## Gate-paden en tests
- Gate-pad: `scripts/github-ruleset.sh` (nieuw). Label `gate-wijziging` en review van de eigenaar nodig.
- Nieuwe test `test/scripts/github-ruleset.test.ts`. Geen bestaande tests gewijzigd.

author: kubohiroya
body:
## 背景
#873 の「対象外」で挙げた、ローカルプレビュー（`preview-dsl4`）の件です。

ローカルプレビューは `createDsl4BrowserRemoteAssetLoader` を使っておらず、リモートアセットを読み込めません。そのため、リモートのポーズモデルなどを必要とするシーンに入ると `K4-ASSET-REMOTE-DISABLED` で失敗します。ところがこの失敗はユーザに見えず、プレビューが黙って止まっていました。

原因は次の流れです（テストで再現を確認済み）。
1. `dsl4-local-preview-browser-bootstrap.ts` が `loadRemoteAsset` を渡さないため、シーン開始時に `K4-ASSET-REMOTE-DISABLED` になる
2. セッションはこれを `runtime.fail` イベント（diagnostic 付き）として通知する。実行の Promise は reject されないので、`live-reload-session.ts` の `observeRun` は気づかない
3. ローカルプレビューの `onEvent` は `runtime.finish` しか扱っておらず、`runtime.fail` を捨てていた

## 変更内容
### ローカルプレビュー（`src/builder/dsl4-local-preview-browser-runtime.ts`）
- `runtime.fail` を受けたら、パッケージ版ランタイムと同じ `createDsl4RuntimeErrorIndicator` で「紙芝居の実行エラー」ダイアログを表示します。エラーコード、メッセージ、不正な記述箇所に加え、「メニューに戻る」ボタンを出します。
- ダイアログは `runtime.start` と「もう一度」で閉じ、プレビューの破棄時に取り除きます。
- `K4-ASSET-REMOTE-DISABLED` のときは、本文に案内を追加します（日本語・英語、ブラウザの言語で選択）。「ローカルプレビューはリモートの素材を読み込みません。リモート配信を試すには build-dsl4 でビルドするか、プレビュー中はこの素材をローカル配信に切り替えてください。」

### ユーザに見えるもの
**ローカルプレビューは、この PR 後もリモートアセットを読み込みません。変わるのは、失敗を表示するようになる点だけです。**

| ケース | ユーザに見えるもの |
|---|---|
| ローカルプレビューでリモートアセットが必要なシーンに入る | `K4-ASSET-REMOTE-DISABLED` と上の案内を出したエラーダイアログ（これまでは無表示で停止） |
| ローカルプレビューでそれ以外の実行時エラー | エラーコードとメッセージを出したエラーダイアログ（これまでは無表示で停止） |
| ビルドした SB3（パッケージ版ランタイム） | 従来どおりリモートを読み込みます。証明書・CORS・オフラインは #873 の分類で表示 |

生成バンドル `src/builder/generated/dsl4-playback-runtime-extension.js` には影響しません（`pnpm run dsl4:playback-runtime:generate` を実行し、差分なしを確認）。

## ローカルプレビューにリモートアセットのローダーを入れない理由
- プレビューのページは CSP が `connect-src 'self'`（`dsl4-local-preview-host.ts`）のため、ローダーを入れても外部への fetch はブロックされます。
- CSP によるブロックは `TypeError: Failed to fetch` になり、ローダーはこれを `K4-ASSET-REMOTE-CONNECT-001`（証明書の可能性が高い）と分類します。原因が CSP なのに、証明書を疑うよう案内してしまいます。
- integrity 付きのリモートアセットには cacheIdentity も必要ですが、プレビューには用意されていません。

プレビューでリモートを読めるようにするには、CSP を `https:` に広げることも含めた別の設計が必要です。

## 確認
- [x] 再現テスト（`test/dsl4-turbowarp-runtime-host.test.ts`）：`loadRemoteAsset` なしのプレビューセッションで、リモートのポーズモデルを使うシーンが `runtime.fail`（`K4-ASSET-REMOTE-DISABLED`）を通知する
- [x] 表示テスト（`test/dsl4-local-preview-browser-runtime.test.ts`）：失敗した実行がエラーダイアログに表示され、「メニューに戻る」で閉じる。修正前のコードでは失敗することを確認
- [x] origin/main（#873）を取り込んだ `5d963ce` で `pnpm test`：159 ファイル / 1260 件すべて成功
- [x] 同じ `5d963ce` で `pnpm run typecheck` 成功、変更したファイルへの eslint も成功
- [ ] 実際のブラウザでの確認はしていません（ベース SB3・カメラ・Teachable Machine ランタイムが必要なため）

body:
# refactor(handler): consolidate layout and binary paths (#6)

The handler executable and downloaded binaries previously shared the source
layout. This change moves the Go module to the repository root, exposes the
existing daemon as the `handler` package, adds the thin `handler/cmd/nib-handler`
entry and places OS launchers/prebuilt binaries under `bin/`. Existing script
entry points forward to these launchers, with flags, loopback restrictions,
configuration discovery and release asset names preserved. `/v1/status` retains
its fields and additionally exposes the ordered preflight results.

The prepared flat handler package was retained instead of adding separate
`internal/app`, `internal/config` and `internal/docker` packages. Tests reside in
`tests/handler`; CI/release paths follow the migration and their workflows stay
parked. Diagnostics is staged in a separate follow-up change.

Closes #6

## Validation

- `go test ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `go test -race ./...` passed.
- Go 1.22.12 tests and vet passed.
- Cross-build produced all six Linux/macOS/Windows amd64/arm64 binaries.
- Unix launcher regression checks passed, including paths with spaces, argument overrides and exit-code propagation.
- A real macOS/arm64 handler process passed health/status, configuration and loopback rejection checks.
- CI/release jobs remain parked; model/data/Zarr source from main is unchanged.

Full evidence and platform limits: `docs/handler-layout-verification.md`.
Independent agent review was unavailable because its child lacked provider

author: alex
body:
**This is a trust change (`Spec/`).** It adds one contract and changes no existing one.

## What it adds (`Spec/Sm4/Contract.lean`)

* **`directionOf`:** `0 ↦ .encrypt`, otherwise `.decrypt`.
* **`vg_sm4_ecb(schedule, data, n, decrypt)`** (`ecbDirSig`, `ecbDirContract`, `ecbDirApi`).
  * Parameters: the ECB functions' parameters, plus a public `decrypt: usize`.
  * Pre: `decrypt ≤ 1`.
  * Post: the blocks become `ecb (scheduleAt m schedule) (directionOf decrypt) blocks`. That is `ecbPost` with the direction read from the argument.
  * `writeArgs` is set as on the ECB functions.
  * Safety items: "`decrypt` must be 0 or 1".

It is not part of the Rust API: generated modules already `allow(dead_code)`.

## Why

SM4 decryption is encryption with the round keys in reverse order. Yet each ECB function carries its own full body:

* **ARMv7:** `vg_sm4_ecb_encrypt` and `vg_sm4_ecb_decrypt` are 2511 lines each, about 93% identical.
* **AArch64:** the same two functions are 4142 lines each.

With this contract, both targets can keep one body and have both functions call it. That's about −2.3k lines on ARMv7 and −3.1k on AArch64, for one call per ECB call. The implementations, proofs and benchmarks will follow in separate PRs once this one is reviewed. This follows the same shape as #1923 (CAST5) and #1927 (3DES).

## Checks

* `lake build +VerifiedGarbage.Spec.Sm4.Contract` passes.
* `check_lean_speed` passes.

body:
## Summary
The commit-history review found that `CRecoveryEngine::ParseTradeIdentity` passed broker order-comment text directly into `StringToInteger`. The parser did not validate the full numeric token, so malformed or truncated comments could be interpreted as a different decision/leg identity.

This change:
- Requires an exact `MT#<positive-id>[:L<non-negative-leg>]` numeric form.
- Validates ASCII decimal digits before numeric conversion.
- Rejects non-canonical/overflowing integer text and out-of-range leg values.
- Adds a CI contract test for validation order and canonical round-trips.

## Validation
GitHub main was green at `aa22e8894aa2923d27c1b7a2621bb59f1af99d0c`; this branch still needs its PR CI and MQL5 compile results. A clean GitHub CI does not replace MT5 Strategy Tester or Exness demo forward validation.

## Known external blocker
The GitHub-to-GitLab sync workflow is repeatedly failing at GitLab clone authentication with `HTTP Basic: Access denied`. Credential presence passes, but the configured token is rejected by GitLab. This cannot be repaired safely by changing repository source; rotate/replace `GITLAB_SYNC_TOKEN` and set `GITLAB_SYNC_USER` to match the token type in GitHub Actions secrets.

Closes #64 follow-up item only when merged and validated; does not claim the broader release gates are complete.

author: vellusorvari
body:
Closes #27

## Why

Nearly every visit hits a scaled-to-zero backend. App Insights shows every session's first `GetSnapshots` taking 1–2.4 s inside the function before `GetStations` even starts, and one session on 2026-08-25 where requests hung ~16 s until the user reloaded (499s). The frontend made this worse by serialising requests, waiting up to 100 s per request, and retrying only via the 30 s poll.

## Changes

- **Stations first:** `InitAsync` loads live stations in parallel with snapshots and open data; snapshots only add trend badges once they arrive.
- **Quick retries:** the initial live load retries after 2, 5 and 10 s, showing "Loading bike stations…" / "Waking up the bike data service – retrying…" instead of an error. Only the final failure shows the error toast.
- **Timeout:** aggregator requests are capped at 15 s (`AggregatorHttpClient`). `LiveStationService` and `SnapshotService` treat timeouts and invalid JSON as recoverable failures, so `InitAsync` can no longer abort before polling starts.
- **Bug fix:** after a successful load, a failed 30 s poll used to clear all markers and show the "season has not started" message. `LiveStationService.LastRefreshSucceeded` now distinguishes failures from an empty feed, so existing markers are kept.
- **Warm-up:** `index.html` sends a preflight-free `no-cors` GET to `/api/stations` (URL read from `appsettings.json`) while the ~3.5 MB .NET runtime downloads.
- **Snapshots:** a failed initial snapshot fetch is retried after 30 s instead of 15 min.

## Maintenance

- `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly(.DevServer)` 10.0.5 → 10.0.12
- Tests: bUnit 1.36 → 2.11 (`TestContext`/`RenderComponent` → `BunitContext`/`Render`), xunit 2.9.3, xunit.runner.visualstudio 4.0.1, Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk 18.10.1, coverlet 10.1.0, Moq 4.21.0
- Actions: checkout v7, setup-dotnet v6, upload-pages-artifact v5 (with `include-hidden-files: true` to keep `.nojekyll`), deploy-pages v5

## Tests

New tests cover: stations loading while snapshots are still pending, retry with status instead of error, error only after the last retry, snapshot timeout not blocking stations, markers kept after a failed poll, service timeout/invalid-JSON handling, the client timeout and header, and the `index.html` warm-up script. `dotnet build` and `dotnet test` pass locally (158 tests).

Backend-side changes are in Kuoste/HslBikeDataAggregator#94.

author: davidgmbb
body:
Arch's default LDFLAGS previously stopped native x86-64 Linux links at argument validation. This implements the current `/etc/makepkg.conf` set: `-O1`, `--sort-common`, ordered `--as-needed` / `--no-as-needed`, `-z relro`, `-z now`, and `-z pack-relative-relocs`, plus `-z noexecstack`. Together with merged #3749's runtime paths, this covers #3730's completion criteria. Optional still-refused options remain tracked in #3761.

As-needed selection respects input order and preceding objects for both `-l` and direct `.so` / `.so.N` operands, preserves repeated occurrences and explicit-language precedence, and excludes weak-only references. Regular-object demand remains distinct from DSO-only demand: dependencies already named by a retained DSO stay indirect unless an object needs them. Identity uses SONAME, including when the input filename differs. Eager binding places the PIC/shared PLT GOT inside RELRO. RELR packs eligible file-backed relative relocations and records the glibc `GLIBC_ABI_DT_RELR` dependency; symbolic, TLS, COPY, IRELATIVE, unaligned and zero-fill relocations retain RELA. Existing reservations remain padding, so there is no size or throughput claim. `-O1` permits the existing layout; `--sort-common` is vacuous because admitted ordinary definitions are already laid out and SHN_COMMON remains refused. The driver guide documents this subset and its limits.

Current source `5219a5a0bea58f2a07620e46623e6b865269a59f` normally composes repair `24273a80e` with protected cleanup candidate `2b43113c`. Tree `2a04033fa8b541ceeffbf59ad86e61c206328485` matches independent review's predicted composition. Runtime-path parent #3749 is integrated as `fab5f0ed`; this PR targets main and is mergeable. Separate cleanup repair #3767 has integrated as `2b43113c`; fresh main containment is verified. No manual generated-authority edits, process/job timeout changes or protection bypass.

Exact-current-source local validation passes with a clean tree:
- Release full tests: 6,959,742/6,959,742 assertions; 63/63 modules.
- Self-host byte-identical fixed point: 42,416,648 bytes; stage/work gates pass.
- Mode matrix: 12/12 legs (four executed, eight structural; both negative controls pass).
- Source-size against main `fab5f0ed`: production +17,731 / build +6,103 bytes, within both 32 KiB limits; Markdown links and whitespace pass.
- Fresh CMake/Ninja provider/consumer project builds with every current Arch LDFLAG and runs under `env -i`. Independent ELF inspection confirms SONAME DT_NEEDED, RUNPATH, NOW and RELR metadata.
- All four named/direct × PIE/fixed-address DSO-chain startup controls pass. Registered regressions also retain a leaf absent from wrapper's dependencies and a leaf demanded by a regular object.

[Independent exact-head source re-review](https://github.com/buster14a/buster/pull/3760#pullrequestreview-5490349987) clears the original DSO-demand finding and resolves its thread. Both integration prerequisites have landed. All seven exact-head required contexts are green, including CI complete. Protected integration is complete: merged at `21a1aedb3aaacba14490907ce33be52d360c4ac4` on 2026-10-12, with all seven exact-group required contexts passing, both base/head/tree-bound admission receipts verified, and fresh local main containment confirmed. Source-size against integrated main `2b43113c` passes (+16,978 production / zero build bytes).

Retained failed evidence: `e0dc6e3b` failed one existing OS process-group churn assertion, reported on [#2380](https://github.com/buster14a/buster/issues/2380#issuecomment-6122669389). `ecf2a572` passed all local acceptance checks but [Windows Release failed](https://github.com/buster14a/buster/actions/runs/38239221469/job/114778283414) deleting a private bootstrap snapshot; #3765 retains that failure and unknown original native cause. Separate #3767 proves bounded cleanup with native Windows held/released/read-only/invalid-name controls and self-hosting; it does not establish the old cause. `3311a18d` reproduced four DSO-chain loader exit-127 failures before `24273a80e` repaired selection. No failed result was waived or unchanged job rerun.

ABI reference: [glibc's DT_RELR dependency implementation](https://sourceware.org/pipermail/glibc-cvs/2022q2/078142.html). License: first-party licensing remains [unspecified](https://github.com/buster14a/buster/blob/5219a5a0bea58f2a07620e46623e6b865269a59f/LICENSES/README.md); no dependency or vendored code added.

body: ## P1：讓 DEMO 真正顧問化 P1 不讓 AI 幫業務講更多，而是把 DEMO 改造成「提出假設 → 現場驗證 → 修正判斷 → 協助決策」的工作流程。 ### 客製驗證路線 - 第一次 DEMO 可從開發資料產生「待驗證假設」；有 P0 診斷時再用 P0 收斂路線。 - 根據客戶資料與公司實際方案，AI 只產生 1–3 段路線。 - 每段包含：客戶原話、單一待驗證假設、展示前問題、只展示的工作場景、觀察訊號、展示後驗收問題、停損條件與不該展示內容。 - 防止從頭介紹整套產品或把「客戶有看」誤判成「客戶認同價值」。 [P1 客製 DEMO 驗證路線](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-01a12b58-fed0-7ab4-9763-1d8ff93c692e/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fscreenshots%2Fconsultative-p1-routes.png) ### 現場證據與阻力診斷 - 每段標記：待驗證／已驗證／需修正／不適用。 - 記錄客戶反應與現場原話。 - 修改任何現場證據都會清除舊決策結果，避免沿用過期判斷。 - 先保存客戶完整原話，再分類成果、自我效能、流程、決策人、時機、價格或不適配。 - 固定先提供驗證問題，確認後才給建議行動，不直接生成反駁話術。 [P1 阻力診斷](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-01a12b58-fed0-7ab4-9763-1d8ff93c692e/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fscreenshots%2Fconsultative-p1-resistance.png) ### 兩種獨立決策卡 - **主管內部版**：適配判斷、已證實／已修正、風險、真正阻力、策略與跟進投入。 - **客戶共識版**：只保留雙方已確認的現況、目標、驗證場景、最小落地範圍、角色、驗收、前置條件與下一決策點。 - 客戶版欄位採白名單；另有本地內容防線，若模型輸出 A/B/C、成交機率、業務評分、AI 可信度或五字內部標籤，整欄不顯示。 - 兩版皆可預覽、下載 PNG、複製圖片或文字。 [主管內部決策卡](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-01a12b58-fed0-7ab4-9763-1d8ff93c692e/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fscreenshots%2Fconsultative-p1-manager-card.png) [客戶決策共識卡](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-01a12b58-fed0-7ab4-9763-1d8ff93c692e/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fscreenshots%2Fconsultative-p1-customer-card.png) ## 資料與隱私 - `demoGuide` 隨原複盤儲存，納入既有全部備份；第一次 DEMO 規劃會自動建立並綁定目前簡報的複盤。 - 只有勾選同意才會把客戶資料、P0（若有）與現場驗證筆記送到 Gemini；不傳影片或完整逐字稿。 - 每次 AI 完成後自動取消同意。 ## 驗證 - 全部 565 個測試通過。 - 最終 P1／review／deck／module 136 個回歸測試通過。 - eslint 通過。 - Vite production build 通過。 - Playwright 攔截 Gemini 完成兩條 UI 流程： 1. 有 P0：規劃 2 段路線 → 記錄確認／修正與客戶原話 → 阻力診斷 → 切換主管／客戶卡；資料正確持久化、同意自動取消、無瀏覽器錯誤。 2. 無 P0 的第一次 DEMO：填開發目標後按鈕立即啟用，產生路線並自動建立、綁定目前簡報的複盤；無瀏覽器錯誤。 To show artifacts inline, enable in settings.

author: gabrieleleonardi21
body:
Nuovo endpoint \`GET /api/luoghi?q=\`: trasforma il nome di una città o di un luogo in coordinate con Nominatim (OpenStreetMap). Serve alla barra di ricerca della pagina Campetti, quando non trova campetti: la mappa si sposta sul luogo cercato.

Non serve nessuna chiave. La chiamata a Nominatim parte dal server, così il browser non contatta OpenStreetMap e la CSP resta invariata.

## Cosa cambia

- Endpoint pubblico. \`q\` da 2 a 100 caratteri; risposta \`{"nome","lat","lng"}\`; 404 se il luogo non c'è; 502 con messaggio generico se Nominatim non risponde.
- Una chiamata alla volta e almeno un secondo tra una e l'altra, come chiede la politica d'uso di Nominatim.
- Cache in memoria di 500 risposte (anche i 404); il \`q\` non finisce mai nei log.
- User-Agent identificativo del progetto. Attribuzione «© OpenStreetMap contributors» nel README.

## Verifica

- \`./mvnw -B test\`: 688 test, 0 fallimenti.
- \`./mvnw -B verify -Pintegrazione\` su PostgreSQL 18: 251 test, 0 fallimenti.
- Nominatim è simulato in test con un server locale: trovato, non trovato, errore, cache, limite di un secondo.

## Da sapere

- Nominatim trova città e indirizzi, meno bene i nomi di attività: per quelli servirebbe Google Places.




Frontend collegato: Gabrieleleonardi21/Hoops-3x3#30, da unire dopo questa PR.

author: yuubae215
body:
## What & Why（Goal ← Strategy）

- **What**:
  - 判定基準の聞き取りの「やってみる」で、core/ が返す**案**（候補セルと実態値）を ☺ ○ ☹ ? で並べ、本人に選ばせるようにした。
  - 同じ画面に**全員の関心**を出す。
  - 合意済みの線の変更提案には、出した時点で**差し出すもの**（そのマージン）を載せる。
  - 新しいエンドポイント `criteria-trial` を足し、契約は v9。
- **Goal**: 合意の前でも後でも、線の帰結（案の実態値・関心・差し出すもの）が core/ からしか来ない。front はそれを描くだけで、重みから何も計算しない。見た案は、後で読み返せる形で残る。
- **語彙**（原則 #33 — 俯瞰で足した語）:
  - 案と実態値は `candidate {id, label, actuals}`。実態値ごとに出どころ `basis`（nominal / derived / declared）を持つ。
  - 関心は `interest {actor, category, value}`。持ち主は actor。
  - 差し出すものは `offerings`。**空ならマージン内**なので、内外を表す boolean は足さない。
  - 「見せた」（`seen`）と「選んだ」（`chosen`）を別の語に割った。
- **Strategy**: 1 つのコスト関数 J（core/）から 3 つを出す。
  - **満たされ具合**: 期待値をしきい値、重みを超えた分の傾きにした式の部品。
  - **関心**: その感度。線を probe 幅だけ緩めて解き直した有限差分（シャドウプライス）。
  - **差し出すもの**: 提案後の線で解き直した差。
  - 案の出どころは `CellSource` の継ぎ目で差し替えられる。naive 既定は名目セル表（4 型、幅つき）。

## ADR / 設計判断

- 参照/新規 ADR: **ADR-165**（Accepted）に §PR4 の俯瞰と §PR4 を追記した。新しい ADR は起こしていない（D6 の実装であり、判断は ADR-165 の範囲内）。GSN は `IndicatorValuesComeOnlyFromCore` を support-verified に上げた。
- 当事者が俯瞰で決めた 4 点:
  1. 案は名目値と `basis` で出す。シーンと見積の値は後続。
  2. 重みの推し量りは記録だけにする。
  3. `seen` は実態値の写しで残す。
  4. 関心 = 線の張りつめ具合（感度）。
- `docs/adr/README.md` インデックス更新: [x] 済 / [ ] 不要

## Layer & Blast radius（波及範囲）

- 触ったレイヤ: フロント `src/`、契約 `packages/grasp-contract`、BFF `server/`、core `core/`。
- 波及するモジュール:
  - `core/easy_extrude_core/{criteria,contract,api}`
  - `server/src/{routes/criteria.js,grasp/*}`
  - `src/context/{CriteriaTrialWire,CriteriaHearing,CriteriaLine,Agenda}.js`
  - `src/controller/ContextController.js`、`src/view/CriteriaGapMath.js`
  - `src/components/Context/{CriteriaHearingSteps,AgendaPanel}.jsx`、`src/store/uiStore.js`
  - `schema/context-0.6.schema.json`（`trial.seen` を写しに、`chosen` を追加、`proposal.margin` を追加。PR2 の仮の欄 `offerings: string[]` は退役）
  - CI の `contract-wall`、templates のピン留め版
- **触らなかったと宣言したもの**:
  - grasp-search / recommendation の request・response の形。版は全エンドポイント共通なので上がる。
  - stub レーン（GitHub Pages）。`criteria/trial` は 501 で理由を出す。缶詰の関心を返すと、どのコスト関数も計算していない数字を見せることになる（決定であり、残しではない）。
- 越境チェック: src/ は値を作らない。`CriteriaIndicatorCensus.test.js` が数え、変異を入れると赤になることを確認した。
- 契約（response/request スキーマ・`contractVersion`）への影響: **あり（版上げ済 8 → 9）**。response スキーマの変更と `contract-version.json` を同じ PR に入れている。

### 状態表（台帳 `docs/STATE_LEDGER.md` を同じ PR で更新）

| 実体 | 基数 | 権威 |
|---|---|---|
| やってみた回 `seen` | `0..N`。0 は宣言（ソルバに届かない／示す案が無い。理由は画面が言う） | `recordTrial`（core/ の答えが届いた時点。古い線への答えは捨てる） |
| `chosen` | `0..1`（その回の `seen` のどれか） | `chooseCandidate` |
| 提案のマージン `proposal.margin` | PR4 以後の線の提案は必ず 1。ソルバに届かなければ `unassessed`（わからないマージンを内として扱わない — 原則 #31） | 値は core/、`unassessed` は `_assessLineChange`、読むべきかの判定は `marginNeedsReading` |
| `context.criteriaIndicator`（store） | 0..1。関心は送ったエンドユーザ × 4 大項目ちょうど。空欄のある人は `omitted` で名指す | `ContextController._openTrial` |

### 同一性の所有者

- `isAnswerForLine(requestedLine, ctx)`（`src/context/CriteriaTrialWire.js`）を新設し、`IDENTITY_RULES` に登録した。答えがいまの線についてのものかを判定する。
- 楽観ロックで動く（原則 #7）。

## Evidence（証拠 — 鎖を閉じる）

- [x] `pnpm test`（JS スイート）green: **1731 pass / 0 fail**
- [x] `pnpm typecheck` クリーン
- [x] `pnpm build` クリーン
- [x] `pnpm test:contract`: BFF 39 pass、契約パッケージ all green（contractVersion=9）。`core` pytest **311 pass**
- [x] その他: `test:adr` 166 本 OK / `test:gsn` / `test:gsn-debt`（52、baseline 53 → 52）/ `test:deferrals` / `test:stub` 39 / `test:screencast` 21 / `test:commit-meta` / `test:trailers`（unshallow した上で OK）
- [x] 追加/更新したテスト:
  - `core/tests/test_criteria.py`（16）: 当事者に説明した田中さん／佐藤さんの例をそのまま焼いた。関心は重みに依存する。probe が次の案に届かないと 0 になる（naive の限界）。unsatisfiable の場合と、差し出すもの 400 → 200 も確認。
  - `core/tests/test_criteria_contract.py`（12）、`core/tests/test_criteria_api.py`（6）
  - `server/test/criteria.contract.test.js`
  - `src/CriteriaIndicatorCensus.test.js`、`src/view/CriteriaGapMath.test.js`
  - `CriteriaHearing` / `CriteriaLine` / `ContextController` / `ContextSchema` の各テスト。controller では、**答えが届く前に線が動いたら捨てる**ことを焼いた。
  - `e2e/criteria-hearing.spec.js`: 2 本とも pass。2 本目は BFF をネットワーク境界で偽装し、案の表の ☺/☹、選択、2 回目の履歴の「picked」を確かめた。スクリーンショットも目視で確認した。
- **この証拠が構造的に見逃すもの**:
  - e2e の関心の値は偽装した固定値なので、core/ の数値の正しさは見ていない。それは pytest が受け持つ。
  - 実 BFF と core を通しで立てた e2e は無い（このレーンでは立てられない）。両端はそれぞれ契約テストで縛っている。

## Docs / Rules drift（#19）

- [ ] `docs/code_contracts/*.md`（+ index）更新 / [x] 不要（新しい規律は文書ではなく `CriteriaIndicatorCensus.test.js` と `IDENTITY_RULES` に降ろした — Q3）
- [ ] `docs/PHILOSOPHY.md` 原則の追加・研磨 / [x] 不要
- [x] 関連ドキュメント更新:
  - ADR-165、`docs/adr/README.md`、GSN
  - `STATE_LEDGER`、`STATE_TRANSITIONS`（G3 のマージン）、`ALGORITHMS`（J・関心・顔の置き場所）
  - `DEFERRAL_LEDGER`（DEF-062/064 を閉じ、DEF-066/067/068 を追加）
  - `ia-redesign/03` Phase 8、契約の README、core の README、CLAUDE.md のスコープ表

## Notes for reviewers

- 最初に見るファイル:
  - `core/easy_extrude_core/criteria/assessment.py`（式の正本、docstring に式あり）
  - `packages/grasp-contract/schema/criteria-trial-response.schema.json`
  - `src/controller/ContextController.js`（`_openTrial` / `_assessLineChange`）
  - `src/CriteriaIndicatorCensus.test.js`
- **表に出た既存欠陥**: CI の `contract-wall` は response スキーマを名前で 2 つ並べていた（place-list）。新しい `*-response` スキーマは追加したその日から壁の外になっていた。glob に直した。契約テストと `validate.mjs` のエンドポイント一覧も、`schema/` から導くようにした。
- **俯瞰から動いた点**: 関心の比較を「元の線で比べる」から「**同じ緩めた線で 2 案を比べる**」に直した。
  - 元の形では、佐藤さん自身が C の余分な距離を喜ぶとき、緩めても決め手にならないことが分かった。
  - 一律に増える分を打ち消すと、選ぶ案が変わらなければ厳密に 0 になる。
  - 当事者への説明では佐藤さんの距離の重みを暗黙に小さく置いていたので、fixture にはその重みを明示した。
- **本文から動いた点**:
  - 差し出すものは、提案者を含む全エンドユーザについて返す。
  - 関心は「その線集合の中で最も決め手の線 = 1」に正規化した相対値。
- **残し**:
  - DEF-066: シーン由来・見積由来の実態値と、その入力 UIUX。
  - DEF-067: 選択から重みを推し量る。
  - DEF-068: 開いている提案のマージンが 1 版古くなったときの再評価。
- **限界**: マージンは提案を出した時点の線で評価している（DEF-068）。BFF → core の内部トークンヘッダは、grasp-search と同じく未送信のまま（既存の形で、この PR の範囲外）。

author: kourdroid
body:
💡 **What**:
1. Extracted inline `re.search` regular expressions in `src/plugins/supply_chain.py` (`_extract_po_number`) into pre-compiled module-level constants (`_PO_REGEX` and `_PO_DIGITS_REGEX`).
2. Added `@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=2048)` to the `_sanitize_for_match` function in `src/core/graph.py` to memoize the string normalization.

🎯 **Why**:
1. Re-compiling the regex strings inside the `_extract_po_number` function on every call adds unnecessary overhead, especially when parsing large batches of purchase orders.
2. `_sanitize_for_match` is called repeatedly inside a tight loop over the entire `registry_rows` array during vendor identification. Because many schema iterations might process similar or identical cache chunks, repeatedly running `re.sub` is a major bottleneck.

📊 **Impact**:
1. Precompiling regex operations generally reduces execution time by 10-15% on large regex workloads.
2. Memoizing the sanitization step reduces execution time for repeated text strings by over 95% (from ~1.46s to ~0.06s for 100k repetitions based on profiling).

🔬 **Measurement**:
The performance improvements can be verified by running high-volume benchmarks on the graph processing node or by checking the execution time of `execute_3_way_match` with large input lines. Profile data confirms the cache hit rate on repetitive string sanitizations significantly drops the latency in string preprocessing.

author: johnlegionh
body:
Builds on #289 (the branch is cut from it; merge that first).

BulletSim: a physical mesh or sculpt object with every side under 0.2 m now collides on its real mesh and hulls. Before, it was given a bounding box, because the mesher treated BulletSim's physical request as non-physical. Objects 0.2 m or larger on any side, and BulletSim's non-physical request (which asks for the box on purpose), are unchanged. ubODE uses its own mesher and is unchanged.

Two causes in `Meshmerizer`. The 8-argument `CreateMesh`, which BulletSim calls with `isPhysical = true`, passed `false` to the 5-argument overload. And the mesh cache key (asset, size, lod) does not include the physical flag, so a bounding box made for a non-physical request could be handed to a later physical request for the same mesh and size, and the reverse.

The overload now passes the flag on, and bounding-box answers (non-physical, all sides under 0.2 m) are cached apart from meshes, so the two kinds never share an entry and a large mesh is still shared between both kinds of request.

Two cache faults that this exposed are fixed in the same branch. First, decoding a mesh empties the asset bytes of the shape, so a physical request for a small mesh that a non-physical request had already answered with a box found nothing to decode and got null (the reverse order too); BulletSim then fetches the asset again and rebuilds, or marks the prim as failed if the asset had only just been fetched. The mesher now keeps the asset bytes a box was made from, by cache key, until the real mesh is cached, then drops them; in the other order the box is made from the cached mesh. Nothing is kept for a request that is never replaced by a box. The cost is that the compressed asset of each small mesh or sculpt answered with a box stays in memory until a physical request builds the mesh. Second, two threads asking for the same mesh at once both built it and the second `Add` of the same key threw out of `CreateMesh`; the first to finish is now cached and handed to both, in the mesh cache and the box cache.

Left alone: the `shouldCache` argument is still ignored, so BulletSim's `false` is still cached; and the cache is still never emptied. `IMesher` and the physics engines are unchanged.

Tests (`MesherPhysicalRequestTests`, 12): a physical small request gets the mesh through each of the 5-, 6-, 7- and 8-argument forms; a non-physical small request still gets the box; a large request gets the mesh either way; physical then non-physical, and the reverse, each get their own answer from the cache; the hull list and bounding hull follow the mesh asked for; a small mesh asked for non-physical then physical (same shape, asset bytes dropped) gets the mesh, and the reverse gets the box; the kept bytes are dropped once the mesh is cached; two threads asking for the same mesh get the same answer and one cache entry, for the box cache and the mesh cache. Five of these are new in the last two commits and each failed before its fix. `OpenSim.Region.CoreModules.Tests`: 466 of 470 pass; the 4 failures are the `HttpMimeTypeTests.SystemTlsDefaultsConnectToModernServers` cases, which fail on develop too. The BulletSim test project does not restore on develop (package downgrade), so it was not run; the BulletSim source project builds without warnings.

author: flappedear
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"arekkozuch"} -->
_Requested by **Arek** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01CftieFhkjfdcKHGzjBPd8C?thread=cmsg_01CftieFhkjfdcKHGzjBPd8C1j8P5jkYFiryavmSQdq93i)_

**Before:** a denied permission was silent: setup showed only "Allow" or "Settings", and nothing said what a denied camera or nearby-devices permission would break. The app had no credits page (only a "Circuit list" row). The recorder ran only as a `location` foreground service, and claimed it even when location was denied, so on Android 14 startForeground could throw a SecurityException.

**After:**
- **Denied permissions (FBBD-35).** After the dialog answers, the Permissions step in setup lists one amber line per denied group: "Location off: no GNSS from the phone; Bluetooth GPS receivers also need it", "Nearby devices off: no RaceBox, GoPro or Bluetooth receivers", "Camera off: no phone video", "Microphone off: video without sound", "Notifications off: no recording notification". Settings › App has a new **Permissions** row ("All allowed" or "2 off") with the same lines below it. Tapping the row opens the app's page in system settings. Both are checked again on resume. The setup button still switches to "Settings" when a permission is denied for good, and that now covers optional permissions too. Before, "Allow" did nothing for a camera denied twice.
- **About and credits (FBBD-79).** It is a new row in Settings › App and opens its own page. The page shows the version, then grouped cards: circuit directory (Wikidata, CC0 1.0); map tiles (GUGiK orthophoto and OpenStreetMap, with the attribution taken from `TileSources`, the same strings the map draws); fonts (Barlow and Saira Semi Condensed, SIL OFL 1.1); ported code (FlappedEar Telemetry, Apache 2.0, for the analysis and coach logic); and the open-source libraries with their versions from the version catalog. Each credit opens its link in the browser. The separate "Circuit list" row is gone because the page covers it.
- **Connected device (FBBD-34).** The manifest adds `FOREGROUND_SERVICE_CONNECTED_DEVICE`, and `RecorderService` is declared `location|connectedDevice`. When it goes foreground, it claims location only when Android is below 14 or location is granted. It claims connected device only when Android is below 12 or BLUETOOTH_CONNECT is granted. If Android 14 still refuses location, for example on a background restart without while-in-use access, it retries as a connected device only. That is enough because every receiver is external. If no type is allowed, the service reports "allow location or nearby devices in Settings" and does not call startForeground.

**Layout:** About is one column of the existing `ShellCard`s with `SectionLabel` headings, kept to a 720 dp readable width and centred on tablets. The permission lines use the dim body style in the warning colour, under the step or row they belong to. There are no pop-ups.

**How:** `PermissionGroup` (pure) maps permission names to groups and lines. `AboutUi.kt` (pure) builds the credit sections from `TileSources` and a static library list. `recorderForegroundTypes` (pure) holds the Android 10/12/14 rules. `ForegroundStart.kt` turns those types into `ServiceInfo` bits and holds the fallback. `RecorderService.goForeground()` only calls it, so the change there is a few lines. Nothing new runs while a session records.

**Tests** (run locally in a scratch JVM Gradle project, with detekt over all of `app/src`):

body: Part of #90. ## Decisions and corrections - An independent reading of the first commit found four defects, all fixed in the second commit by decision. First, the first part now ends when `Agent.choose` returns, including the `Chosen` record, because under `learn-then-act` the second part runs before the world receives the action; the docs state where the world receives the action in each order. Second, the claim that segments are bounded by constants of the code is narrowed. Third, `demonBankStepCosted_within_capacity` gives a bound that is a function of the configuration alone. Fourth, `Acorn.Cost`'s list of costed definitions now names the learner's, so the list names every costed definition of Acorn. - The second part's bound is not stated. It runs stretches outside the costed definitions, and `DemonRecords.observe`, a loop over the channels with no charge point, is one example. So the claim that every segment is bounded by a constant of the code covers the first part and each costed definition's own call, read over that call's trace. The second part's segments are an open obligation of R8. An earlier version listed the second part's uncosted stretches. That list drifted in three consecutive review rounds, so it was removed rather than patched again. - A witness for the capacity bound, applying it to two sample active sets, was dropped. The corollary has no hypothesis and its domain is inhabited for every layout (`DemonBank.initial`), so it cannot be vacuous. - `Costed.prepend` charges its element's read at the vector it builds, and the segment rule's list of charge points names that position. - The module docstrings of AcornVerif.Resource.Work and ControlWork point to the list in `Acorn.Cost` instead of repeating it. StepWork's references point there too, and StepWork's coverage sentence excepts the two exceptions Work states. Those exceptions are `Transition.updateRows` and `detachedUpdate`. docs/design.md records that the executed `detachedUpdate` is not yet the value of `detachedUpdateCosted`; converting it is a later increment's. - The executed bank step does work quadratic in the number of demons, because each level copies the rest of the bank's error and cumulant vectors. The bound states this. A linear form would change the generated C, and no follow-up issue is filed, since a bank is the reward question plus the world's signals. - Generated C, compared per function with a build of main 72391c6: every Acorn function is identical up to the renaming of the costed symbols and local variables. The exceptions are the constructor-index tables of `Site` and `Library` and `Library.passes`, which gain the new constructors. This is an observation of one build, which no gate repeats. ## What Changed - `DemonBank.step` is now the value of a new costed definition `DemonBank.stepCosted` in `Acorn.Demon`. Each demon is charged its learner step, a `demonOutput` charge, two `Costed.prepend` calls (its error and its cumulant) and a `demonClose` charge, and the end of the bank is charged a visit. The new theorem `DemonBank.step_def` keeps the old equation by `rfl`, and the native route table now lists `step` → `stepCosted` → `NumericState.stepCosted`. `Acorn.Cost` adds the `Costed.prepend` scan, which charges one `read` plus its `Library.vectorAppend` row over the tail, along with the sites `demonOutput` and `demonClose`. Its trusted cost-discipline list and its uncosted entry points now include `prepend` and `DemonBank.stepCosted`, and its learner list names each of the learner's costed definitions. - `AcornVerif.Resource.ControlWork` proves `demonBankStepCosted_within`, a bound that grows with the square of the number of demons, and `demonBankStepCosted_within_capacity`. The second bound uses the dimension's capacity in place of the active set's length, which makes it a function of the configuration alone. - The cost semantics in `Acorn.Cost` and `docs/design.md` now say the first part ends when `Agent.choose` returns. They also define the second part's trace and a costed definition's own trace, and state when the world receives the action under each step order. The claim that every segment is bounded by a constant of the code is now limited to the first part and to each costed definition's own call. The second part's bound is stated as an open obligation of R8 (rbeauchamp/acorn#90), with `DemonRecords.observe` as the example of an uncharged loop. The docstrings of `Work` and `StepWork` now point to `Acorn.Cost` and name the two exceptions: `Transition.updateRows` and `detachedUpdate`. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change is well bounded. `DemonBank.step` is now the value of a costed recursion whose old body `step_def` keeps. Its bound uses the existing `pass`/`control_mono` machinery, and the toolchain source confirms `Costed.prepend`'s row: `Vector.append` → `Array.append` = `foldl push`, one pass. The round-5 fix limits StepWork's coverage sentence, as instructed, by the exceptions Work.lean states. Every costed definition `Acorn.Cost` names has a plain form that is its `.val`, except the two that Work.lean names (`Transition.updateRows`, `detachedUpdate`). So the remaining docs are consistent with the code. ## Testing I provisioned the worktree, then built the head and a disposable copy of base 72391c6. Before/after equivalence ran live against the real binaries: - The three `acorn-core audit` arms on the head match their compiled pins. - Base and head demo telemetry agree in 30 of 30 runs (9,696 frames). The demon bank was active in those runs: there were 291 to 359 distinct prediction vectors per run. - Base and head `agent-native` outputs agree in 240 of 240 configurations. Code and proof checks (static or machine-checked, not live product runs, so their scenarios are recorded as untested): - The generated-C comparison found every Acorn function identical up to renaming, apart from the cost-model enum functions of the new constructors. A swapped-tails mutant showed the comparator detects changes. - A Lean driver checked the new statements and showed they use only the standard axioms. - Six mutants confirmed that `step_def` holds the old body and that the bound rejects linear, one-copy and extra-copy charges. The two controls elaborated. There is no UI change, so there is no visual artifact. The documentation edits (design.md and the docstrings) have no runtime surface. This brings the reviewed native GeoNetwork catalogue workflow into the standalone Merchant Workspace so an operator can install the selected product, open the existing STAC application, receive complete original collections, review and run the native harvester, manage the actual records, and export or reopen the full handover.

The seventeen source files are received from public PR2053 at `c76677a0f26ccd24381454e1c43d0d24fc1e9b7f`. author: feafel
body:
**Problem**
`parseInt(process.env.MAX_SANDBOX_DURATION || "300",10)` returns `NaN` when env var is set to empty string, causing DB default and Zod default to become `NaN`. This propagates to sandbox timeout and task execution.

**Fix**
- Add `parseIntEnv` helper that validates finite positive int, falls back to 300.
- Use helper for both Drizzle schema default and Zod schema default.
- Enforce `.min(1).max(480)` on `insertTaskSchema.maxDuration` to cap cost.

**Impact**
Prevents NaN defaults and unbounded sandbox runtime.

author: kamyarat
body:
## Summary

Delta Chat 2.63 stopped writing the legacy `addr` and `mail_pw` config keys. `get_config("addr")` and `get_config("mail_pw")` come back empty, so `tests/deltachat-test` logged in to SMTP with an empty username and the server answered `535 5.7.8 Invalid credentials`.

That is the failure in the re-run of [chatmail/cmlxc#51](https://github.com/chatmail/cmlxc/pull/51) ([job 114755625946](https://github.com/chatmail/cmlxc/actions/runs/38014618935/job/114755625946)): `tests/fullrun.py::test_madmail` created the account, printed `Account None` once IMAP went idle, then test 2 died in `smtp.login`. The relay suite on that same run had already passed after chatmail/relay `305d83f`.

`account_addr()` and `account_password()` read the first `list_transports()` entry (`addr` and `password`), which is where Delta Chat 2.63 stores the login. When this client has no `list_transports` result, they fall back to the legacy config keys. The scenario, stress, and cmping call sites use those helpers. `configured_addr` is unchanged.

cmlxc's own fullrun calls `cmlxc deploy-madmail` with no `--source`. `MadmailDriver.DEFAULT_REF` is still `v2.29.1`, so that job keeps running the old harness until the pin includes this commit. This pull request does not change cmlxc.

Madmail's cmlxc workflow deploys `--source ./repo` and then runs `cmlxc test-madmail`, so that step on this pull request uses this harness. `cmlxc test-mini` still comes from cmlxc `main` and keeps reading the removed config key until [chatmail/cmlxc#51](https://github.com/chatmail/cmlxc/pull/51) is merged.

author: touseefx
body:
## The problem

`run_source` builds a Luau VM, executes the source, and drops the VM when it returns. A plugin calling `RunService.RenderStepped:Connect(f)` was registering `f` into a VM that no longer existed — the callback could never fire. That VM also never saw `game`, so plugins had no DOM access, and `plugin` was a noop stub that returned one shared table for every `CreateButton` call.

## What this adds

**`PluginSession`** — a VM that lives for the plugin's whole lifetime, wired to a DOM through `install_command_globals` (the same `game`, `workspace`, Selection, ChangeHistoryService and RunService the command bar gets), ticked once per editor frame.

The deferred-scheduler chunk is extracted out of `GuiPlaySession::new` into `install_task_scheduler`, so a plugin VM gets `task.spawn/defer/delay/wait` instead of queueing forever.

**`install_plugin_host`** — replaces the noop `plugin` global. Each button is its own table with its own `Click` signal, recorded in a `PluginHost` the editor reads to draw the toolbar and fire the right signal. `GetSetting`/`SetSetting` serialise through serde_json and persist to `<plugin>.settings.json`.

**`app.rs` wiring** — `run_plugin` now builds a session on the UI thread and keeps it; the frame loop ticks it next to `GuiPlaySession`; `show_plugin_toolbars` draws plugin toolbars and routes presses into that button's `Click`; stopping drops the session and flushes settings.

## Tests

Six, all passing (`test result: ok. 6 passed; 0 failed`): step signals fire on tick and not before, state persists across scripts, `task.defer` resumes, `BindToRenderStep` gets a delta, buttons keep distinct identity and route clicks to their own handler, settings survive into a fresh session.

## Pre-existing breakage this exposed

`x build` only ever cross-compiles the aarch64 cdylib, so `cfg(test)` was never compiled and the crate's tests never ran. Adding a host test job found:

- **master did not compile.** `egui::Key::Digit1..Digit9` do not exist — egui names them `Num0..Num9` (verified against emilk/egui `crates/egui/src/data/key.rs` at 0.31/0.32/0.33). The last green APK build ran 2026-10-11T21:53Z and PR #11 merged 2026-10-12T06:20Z, so the Ctrl+1..9 shortcuts were never built.
- `EditorApp.show_skybox` read and written but never declared.
- A `#[cfg(not(test))]` above a block comment attached itself to `const RBX_TRANSPORT_CAPS_EXT_TYPE`, leaving the ungated `splice_rbx_transport_caps_inner` referencing a symbol that does not exist in test builds.
- `write_pending_rbx_transport_packets` missed when its region was gated.
- `{rep.answer:08x}` field access in a format string; a double deref after `find`; a use-after-move in the RbxTransport decoder test.

## CI

New `check-and-test` job: host-target compile + tests, ~3 min, parallel to the APK build. `build-android` is now gated on `workflow_dispatch` so a push does not spend 10+ minutes producing an APK nobody asked for. Diagnostics are republished as check-run annotations because the log archive host is not reachable from every environment.

The job gates on the `plugin_` tests and runs the full suite with `continue-on-error`, because the suite has pre-existing failures this PR does not fix:

- `challenge::tests::find_challenge_frame_walks_framed_stream` hits a Luau null-pointer deref whose panic is non-unwinding (it crosses the `extern "C"` boundary in `luaur-vm/src/functions/loadsafe.rs`), so it SIGABRTs the test process and takes every other test with it.
- `appflow::tests::build_92_layout`, `routes_parse_as_frames` and `varint_round_trips` fail.

## Known limits

- **Plugins get a snapshot, not the live place.** `EditorApp` owns the DOM as `Option<WeakDom>` with dozens of readers and `WeakDom` is not `Clone`, so the session gets a serialised copy. Plugin edits do not reach the editor yet.
- The editor's toolbar UI is compiled but cannot be exercised headlessly; only the runtime underneath it is covered by tests.
- `CreateDockWidgetPluginGui` is not implemented, so a plugin that builds a dock widget still hits the stub.


---

## QUIC handshake work (added later)

**The 0xFF00 splice never ran.** Two independent bugs, both upstream of any byte
being written:

- The varint codec shifted by 7 bits per byte and masked continuation bytes with
  `0x7F` instead of shifting by 8 (RFC 9000 §16). It decoded 300 as 172 and 15293
  as 7613. The writer was wrong the same way, so a round trip passed while every
  real packet decoded wrong — which is why nothing caught it.
- The frame-type check compared one byte against `0x40`, but CRYPTO is `0x06`.
  Both encodings bail: `0x06` gives `NotInitial`, `40 06` reads the offset as 6 and
  gives `Layout`.

Fixed both, and pinned with RFC 9000 wire vectors plus a splice test over a
synthetic Initial.

**Transport parameters.** Only `max_datagram_frame_size` was set. Four of the
eight values being matched already equalled ngtcp2's own defaults
(`NGTCP2_DEFAULT_MAX_RECV_UDP_PAYLOAD_SIZE` 65527, `..._ACK_DELAY_EXPONENT` 3,
`..._MAX_ACK_DELAY` 25 ms, `..._ACTIVE_CONNECTION_ID_LIMIT` 2); six needed work.
All eight are now stated explicitly. `initial_max_streams_bidi` is deliberately
left alone — it was not in the set, and zeroing it would refuse server-initiated
bidirectional streams.

**OpenSSL backend** (`ossl-tls`, off by default). Registered 0xFF00 with
`SSL_CTX_add_custom_ext`; OpenSSL writes custom extensions ahead of every built-in
one (`ssl/statem/extensions.c:1188`), so it lands first without splicing. Ed25519
raw-public-key authentication is carried across as a DANE-EE / SPKI / Full pin,
and `SSL_set1_client_cert_type` offers RawPublicKey only.

Cross-compiling needed OpenSSL 3.5.9 for Android and the NDK toolchain file:
cmake-rs only enters NDK mode when `ANDROID_ABI` is defined, otherwise it lets the
cc crate pick the API-21 clang, whose sysroot lacks the `stderr` that core
`libcrypto` references — which made ngtcp2's QUIC symbol probe fail at *link* time
and misreport the OpenSSL as unsupported.


**APK build.** `build-android` now cross-compiles OpenSSL 3.5.9 with `-fPIC` and
builds with `--features ossl-tls`, sharing a cache entry with the check job. This
caught a bug the check job structurally could not: it type-checks without linking,
so `rustc-link-lib=dylib=ssl` went unnoticed even though a `no-shared` Android
OpenSSL has no `.so`. The crate now links the archive when no shared library
exists on disk and keeps the dynamic link otherwise.

The job also runs on pushes to `arena/**`, not dispatch only, since an APK that
cannot be produced cannot be tested. `master` is unaffected.


**ClientHello parity.** Diffed against `client/src/quic_client.cpp` in
kingdudely/Boblox, a client that completes the handshake. Ours differed in ways
that all change the bytes on the wire: TLS 1.3 not pinned, default cipher suites
instead of the two the reference offers, default `supported_groups` instead of
X25519 only, a `compress_certificate` extension the reference never sends, 0xFF00
registered for the ClientHello alone rather than ClientHello | EncryptedExtensions,
`initial_max_streams_bidi` 100 instead of 0, `max_datagram_frame_size` set from our
1 MiB receive buffer instead of 65535, and no random initial packet number.

The 0xFF00 payload itself was already correct — `9208b750c7d32d00`, matching the
reference's wire capture in `run/quicdump_settings/ext_65280_1.bin`.

author: skelethorfi
body:
## What changes

- A Rujira liquid bond of bRUNE (`x/brune`) gets RUNE's USD price at its time from Midgard's `/v2/history/rune` (5-minute buckets, any past time). It is stored as a `midgard-rune-price` record keyed by the bucket's start; a bucket still open when fetched is fetched again on the next run. A golden case carries it as `runePriceUsd`. Other contract actions that send bRUNE (FIN trades, account bonds) don't fetch it: they don't use it.
- A bRUNE liquid bond puts it on the activity (`prices`, source `midgard:history.rune`), and the `BRUNE` → `YBRUNE` trade-out row carries it as its reference price (USD).
- `referencePrice()` leaves the columns out when there is no price, instead of setting them to `undefined`. No other row changes.

## Why

Summ has no price for `BRUNE` (the `BRUNE` symbols in its catalogue are unrelated tokens) or `YBRUNE`, so after #93 a bRUNE liquid bond had no value on either side. bRUNE is minted 1:1 for RUNE by the `rujira-brune` contract, so RUNE's price is bRUNE's. Rujira's API has only current prices (and FIN candles priced in RUNE), so Midgard's RUNE history is the source.

## Breaking

An `--offline` replay of a run with bRUNE contract actions needs one online run first, to store the new `midgard-rune-price` records.

## Rows change

A `BRUNE` → `YBRUNE` liquid bond's `bridge-trade-out` row gains `Reference Price Per Unit` (RUNE's USD price at the time) and `Reference Price Currency` `USD`. Row IDs and descriptions are unchanged.

## Checks

`npm run typecheck`, `npm test` (485 pass, new `test/RunePrice.test.ts`: bucket choice, open bucket, missing bucket, which actions fetch). Golden case `rujira/staking-liquid-bond-brune` re-reviewed; re-fetching it through the fixture tool gives the same price. Reviewed by a subagent; its findings are addressed in the second commit (a ybRUNE unbond's price is a backlog item, with unbond mapping).

author: arthur-k-99
body:
## Summary

The test suite mocks every download, so nothing checked what a new machine actually gets. This adds that check, and fixes the two bugs its first runs found.

- **`tests/fresh_install.sh`** installs the checkout in a fresh Debian or Ubuntu container the way the README does: as a user with sudo, with real downloads. It then reruns the installer, starts an interactive zsh (which loads every tool's init script), and loads tmux with its plugins.
  - Fails on any error they report, and requires tmux-continuum's status hook, because TPM silences plugin errors.
  - `--here` runs the same on a disposable machine such as a CI runner.
  - Locally: `bash tests/fresh_install.sh debian:12` (needs Docker).
- **Fresh install workflow:** Debian 12 and 13, Ubuntu 24.04 and 26.04 (x86_64), plus macOS via `--here`.
  - Runs on pull requests that touch the Unix install, every Monday, and on demand.
  - A new push cancels the previous run.
- **Bug 1: a new Linux account has no `~/.local/bin`.** The oh-my-posh installer refuses a missing directory, so the bootstrap stopped there on every distribution. The bootstrap now creates the directory, and the oh-my-posh and zoxide installers honor `DOTFILES_LOCAL_BIN`.
- **Bug 2: the tree-sitter CLI releases need glibc 2.39.** On Debian 12 arm64 (glibc 2.36) the binary does not start, so the bootstrap stopped before mise, the yazi flavors and the Neovim plugins. On x86_64, 0.27.1 starts with a warning; 0.27.0 and 0.26.13 did not start.
  - A release that fails with `GLIBC_x not found` is now left out, and its tag and the system's glibc are recorded in `~/.local/state/dotfiles/tree-sitter-unsupported`.
  - Reruns fetch only a newer release.
  - The doctor marks the CLI and the parsers as skipped while that glibc is installed, as on Windows without a compiler. Neovim highlights those file types with Vim's syntax files.
  - Any other failure still stops the bootstrap and shows the binary's error.

## Review

A review pass before opening this found and fixed:
- **Glibc skip too broad:** it keyed on the glibc version alone, so it could hide a crash. It now keys on the binary's error.
- **Doctor could pass a missing CLI:** with a deleted tree-sitter on Debian 12 x86_64, the doctor passed. It now checks the recorded release instead.
- **Reruns re-downloaded tree-sitter:** fixed by the same record.
- **tmux check was loose:** it now loads the configuration once, fails on run-shell output, and asserts the plugins loaded.
- **The suite created `~/.local/bin`:** one test touched the real home directory; it now uses its own.
- **No concurrency group:** added, so a new push cancels the previous run.

**Tried and dropped:** running zsh's prompt hooks in the check. Without a terminal, Debian 12's fzf scripts fail to restore the `zle` option, which a real terminal never shows.

## Verification

- `bash scripts/test.sh` passes locally: 33 Unix checks and 32 Windows tests.
- Real fresh installs on this Mac (arm64), each including the rerun:
  - debian:13, ubuntu:24.04, ubuntu:26.04: pass.
  - debian:12: passes with the CLI and the parsers skipped, and the rerun fetches nothing.
- An earlier, emulated x86_64 Debian 12 run timed out compiling parsers under load. This PR's own runs are the native x86_64 and macOS results.

## Not covered

- Windows has no fresh-install job: winget on the hosted runners is unreliable, so `install.ps1` stays covered by the mocked suite.
- GitHub pauses the weekly run after 60 days without a commit; the README says how to turn it back on.

author: tanmay-mhatre
body:
## Why
The merge train from #101 doesn't work:
- When it updated a branch using the workflow's own token, GitHub held that PR's CI until someone approved it. The CI the train started itself doesn't count toward the PR's required checks. So #102 stayed blocked with every check green, and the train restarted its CI three times.
- GitHub auto-merge merges any up-to-date, green PR, so #103 merged before #102.

## What
- **`.mergify.yml`**: one queue. A PR joins with the `queue` label. Mergify merges `main` into the front PR (as an app, so CI runs normally), waits for the 5 checks `main` requires, merges with a merge commit, and moves on. PRs that conflict or fail CI leave the queue, and Mergify comments on why.
- **Removed `merge-train.yml`.**
- **`CLAUDE.md`**: sessions queue only their own PR (`gh pr edit N --add-label queue`), never merge any other way (including GitHub auto-merge), and turn on Auto-fix so the app wakes them to fix conflicts.

Mergify reads its config from `main`, so this PR can't go through the queue itself. It merges once with GitHub auto-merge. A follow-up PR, which removes the CI trigger only the train used, goes through the queue as a test.

## Hva som er endret

- **Samlet vurdering**: ny avkryssing der flere prøver før forrige prøve kan legges inn. Gir forrige prøve «kan ikke fastslås», sammenlignes denne prøven med de tidligere, nærmeste først, og den nærmeste som gir nytt inntak gir den nye kommentaren med sin dato.
- **Under cut-off · ikke nødvendigvis nytt**: egen kommentar når forrige prøve var under cut-off.
- **Kort tid mellom prøvene**: samme dag eller færre enn tre døgn imellom (grensen ligger i regelsettet) gir en melding med avkryssingen «Kort tid mellom prøvene», som ikke er huket av. Hukes den av, vurderes ikke prøvene mot hverandre, og den nye kommentaren brukes.
- **Redigeringen**: «Felles setninger» øverst, så én boks per situasjon med når den brukes, tekstfeltet, «Avslutt med spørsmålsetningen» og «Slik blir den:» med kommentaren ferdig satt sammen. Oversikten viser kommentarene på samme måte.
- Beregningene er ikke endret: fasiten ble laget på nytt og kontrollert mot den gamle, og alt annet enn kommentarteksten (konklusjoner, varsler, mangler og tallgrunnlag) er likt.
- Migrasjonen legger inn de 13 nye tekstene som publiserte kommentarer og publiserer en ny revisjon av regelsettet som peker på dem. Den stopper uten å endre noe hvis regelsettet har et upublisert utkast (sjekket: det har det ikke nå). Ingen data slettes; de gamle kommentarene står igjen med sin historikk.
- Antakelse: når forrige prøve var under cut-off og resultatet er «kan ikke fastslås», brukes den vanlige «kan ikke fastslås»-kommentaren (den gamle egne teksten for det tilfellet er tatt bort, siden den nye ordlyden ikke hadde en).

## Summary
Step 5 of the engine plan: `analyze_slide` now scores patches with the trained ONNX model instead of the placeholder.
- `pipeline/inference.py`: `PatchClassifier` loads the model once and scores patches in batches of 16. Provider order DirectML -> OpenVINO -> CPU, falling back if one fails to start. Patches are resized if the model's input size differs.
- Model path: `engine/model/model_fp32.onnx` or `TRIAGE_MODEL_PATH`. **If the model is missing, `analyze_slide` raises a clear `FileNotFoundError`** (the backend marks the slide FAILED) instead of returning fake scores.

- Removed `pipeline/placeholder.py`. Tests use `tests/fixtures/tiny_model.onnx` (449 bytes, same contract), so they need neither torch nor the real model.

- 12 MP capture (~200 tissue patches): ~0.6 s end to end on CPU, including tiling, masking and heatmap

author: woahwhattheheck
body:
## Why this is needed

A CFO or accounting practice operates several client closes at once. Separate runbooks need a shared capacity calendar, client-specific commissioning, named lead/backup/reviewer assignments and a complete handover. Those operations must continue using each client's existing accounting workspace, source files and saved request outcomes.

## Complete operator workflow

This change adds a firm portfolio desk with configurable staff availability and immutable client commissioning. Operators plan staggered preparation, backup and review work, inspect capacity conflicts, save calendar revisions and dispatch prepared operations through the selected original client workspace. A backup can take over a worked period with the full assignment and work history retained.

The same workflow is available through the native CLI, MCP catalog/provider, typed client and managed Applications. The browser retains drafts and exact pending requests before dispatch, including atomic pending selection and retirement across tabs. Original client Runbooks desks are mounted under the portfolio and open the selected period directly.

Full portfolio packets carry the selected original client period packets and source bytes. A receiving operator downloads or reopens the exact incoming package, receives each selected client packet, adopts its commissioning into local client workspaces and starts following periods from fresh local sources. The operating guide covers setup, staff handover, calendar and command recovery, receiving and editable source delivery.

## Integration and lifecycle

- Use the configured accounting.workspaces and coordinator portfolioClients mapping; hold each original client's maintenance admission through its accepted operation.
- Retain original client request UUIDs and digests, recover committed results and preserve corrected command chains.
- Drain owned client work before shutdown and retain failed-close owners for retry.
- Reserve both the coordinator and selected client resources in managed Applications.
- Preserve the existing buyer-accounting startup, issued-source, CLI, Xero and route behavior while adding the portfolio host.
- Include the original Applications createDirectories correction required by the existing Runbooks/Cryptoworth installation path.

## Validation

All 34 changed file leaves were read back from Git; composition preserved the 8,870 other file leaves in the captured current main. Independent reviews covered the complete native lifecycle, packet receiving/adoption, installed provider and typed client, browser requests and source bindings. Changed JavaScript bodies parse in V8; the production calendar allocator ran with 900 requested and 900 allocated minutes across preparation, review and backup.

The complete original native receiving operation is being composed with three source clients, two approved periods each, backup takeover, twelve review rounds, calendar and command correction, receiving/adoption, three fresh following periods and cold reopening of the eight original workspaces. Its browser/CLI/MCP/SDK/Applications append uses this same source and operation. Native execution results will be appended to this PR when the receiving owner returns them.

body:
## Summary

Third batch from the spec review, part B (points 4 and 7). **Stacked on #67.** These are the decisions you made:

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| `{ "type": { "name": "decimal" }, "value": 19.99 }` | `"value": "19.99"`: a string in one spelling (no exponent, no leading/trailing zeros, no `-0`) |
| `groupBy` alias optional and unused, keys referenced as `{ "key": 0, … }` | alias required, keys referenced as `{ "key": "user_id", … }` |
| `uuid` / `boolean` ordered for `orderBy` but rejected by comparisons and `min` / `max` | every type is ordered, everywhere |

- **Why strings for decimal:** a JSON number cannot keep the promise "decimal literals are read exactly". JavaScript rounds after about 16 digits, and `1e400` passed the schema. The canonical pattern gives every value exactly one spelling. `decimalList` items and `decimal` parameter values follow; `integer` stays a JSON number.
- **Why allow comparisons on `uuid` / `boolean`:** `orderBy` already relied on their order. Keyset pagination needs `greaterThan(id, last_id)`, and a unique `id` is the natural final key of a total order (#65).
- **`pattern()`** now checks for a newline only in strings, so a number where a string is expected fails with `must be string` instead of `must NOT be valid`.

## Tests
- Samples and tests are migrated in place:
  - decimal literals become canonical strings;
  - `groupBy` keys get aliases (generated only for computed keys in invalid tests);
  - key references switch to aliases.
- Tests that relied on the old rules are rewritten under the same numbers:
  - 053, 054, 255, 256: comparisons with mixed families or a list;
  - 097, 287: `min` / `max` exactness for uuid and boolean;
  - 162: decimal as a JSON number;
  - 116, 206, 207: key by index, empty alias, key without alias;
  - 376: decimal with a trailing zero.
  
  311 keeps exactly one break.
- New tests 392–394: `"1e3"`, `"-0"`, a number inside a `decimalList`.
- I compared every invalid test's failure reason with #67: the only differences are the intended ones.

- [x] Generator rerun, jsonlint check of the schema and samples

author: d-oit
body:
Four design-token issues that interlock in `globals.css` and the palette modules.

## What

**#852 — the 44px floor is a token now.** `@theme { --spacing-touch: 2.75rem }` in `src/app/globals.css`, so Tailwind v4 generates `min-h-touch`/`min-w-touch`/`size-touch`. ~109 call sites migrated off `min-h-[44px]`; `TOUCH_TARGET_CLASS` exported from `ui/shared-primitives.tsx` for the common icon-button case. AC AGENTS.md already mandated is now expressible instead of being a magic number one typo away from a silent WCAG regression.

**#858 — the utility layer is v4-native.** The custom classes in `@layer utilities` could never compile a variant (`hover:hover-lift`, `dark:glass`, `sm:page-enter` generated nothing). Converted to `@utility`, so variants compile. The hand-rolled `.font-serif` override is gone; its `font-feature-settings` moved to the base heading rule, leaving one `.font-serif` (the generated one).

**#853 — one palette source per palette.** New `src/lib/export/export-theme.ts` replaces two near-identical inline-CSS blocks (`export-helpers.ts`, `lib/export/encrypt.ts`) that were still shipping retired colours; the 12-colour presence palette is defined once in `lib/sync/presence.ts` and imported by `cursors.ts`; `mindmap-export.ts` reads `--paper` from computed styles with the constant as the documented no-DOM fallback.

**#851 — entity-type colours render the tokens they name.** `ENTITY_TYPE_META` said `saffron`/`sage`/`clay`/`sky` but rendered raw `amber-*`/`emerald-*`/`rose-*`/`sky-*`, and the neutral fallback used `zinc-*` (banned: "borders and dividers are warm, never neutral grey"). Now rendered through the bespoke tokens, which finally gives `--sage`/`--clay`/`--sky` real usage and makes one class set work in both themes. The `registerEntityType` doc example follows the same recipe.

## Verification
- `pnpm exec vitest run` — **183 files, 2835 passed | 1 skipped**, type Errors none.
- `pnpm exec eslint <44 changed files>` — clean.
- `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.app.json` — clean.
- `@utility` conversion proven by compiling the real `globals.css` with tailwindcss's `compile()` API and asserting the generated CSS contains the converted utilities with their variants (throwaway harness, deleted afterwards).
- `DESIGN-SYSTEM.md` documents the touch token, the type-utility set, the entity palette and the elevation/shadows.

Closes #851, #852, #853, #858.

author: jonmcwest
body:
## Problem

- The log details drawer shows a trace link, and a recording link when the log has a session ID. It never shows who the log belongs to or whether it has errors.
- To find out whether a log has errors, a reader opens the Related errors tab and waits for it to load.
- Stacked on #115339, which lets Related errors match on the span and the trace.

## Changes

- The drawer header shows, in order: View trace, an error count, the person, and View recording. Each appears only when the log carries its ID.
- The error count reads "3 errors in this span", "No errors in this trace" or similar. Clicking it opens Related errors on the scope it counted.
- The person chip is `PersonDisplay` in a tag, the same as the Tracing drawer's identity chips. Hover shows the person card.
- One new component, `LogContextLinks`, renders all four links. #115343 reuses it in the expanded log row.
- The header count and the Related errors tab bind the same keyed `traceErrorsLogic`, so they share one query. Both build props through one function, `buildLogErrorsLogicProps`.
- The scope the row badge asks for no longer travels as a logic prop. `initialScope` is not part of the logic key, so two callers passing different values would overwrite each other's props. The tab applies it with `setScope` when it changes. As a result, the header count follows the scope the tab selects.
- A `surface` prop (`drawer` or `row`) sets the data-attrs, so autocapture tells drawer clicks from row clicks. The drawer's trace button keeps its shipped `logs-details-view-trace`. New attrs follow `logs-<surface>-context-<link>`, for example `logs-drawer-context-errors`.
- The count shows occurrences, the same unit as the row's session errors badge and the tab's summary line.

### Screenshots

Before: the header shows only View trace and View recording.

![115342-before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PostHog/pr-assets/0bf24e6cf9cc4363943fa6d66b0079d67f854264/2026/10/98a2de11-87a6-4d4a-b119-3a09e8379bc0.png)

After: the same log also shows its error count and the person it belongs to.

![115342-after-user](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PostHog/pr-assets/894c6e9332bc5f17e185bbf473b2a928fa680ffc/2026/10/aea890ff-4278-466c-820c-e06cde06b024.png)

After: a backend log with only a trace ID and no errors shows a muted "No errors in this trace".

![115342-after-backend](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PostHog/pr-assets/d91c4cf58d831543259e46c993a8695018944de9/2026/10/437c4f76-f792-4148-af2f-f7c16a55ad7e.png)

## How did you test this code?

- Ran oxlint on the changed directories.
- Not checked: the drawer in a running app, and the header at narrow widths. The link row uses `flex-wrap`.

**Test rationale:** no new test. The count reads `traceErrorsLogic`, covered by `traceErrorsLogic.test.ts`. The new component only maps that logic's state and the resolved IDs to links.

## Release status

- No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->

## Docs update

None.

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

- PR 2 of 3, built by a subagent against a fixed component contract so PR 3 could be built in parallel.

author: mausworks
body:
# Description of Changes

The TypeScript SDK's log output always goes to `console.log` with `%c` styling. Only the level can be configured (`setGlobalLogLevel`), so there's no way to:

- forward SDK logs to an app's own logger or error reporting, or
- get readable output where `%c` styling isn't supported. In React Native, for example, every line shows the raw `%c` markers and CSS strings.

This adds a pluggable sink next to the existing level setting:

```ts
import { setGlobalLogger, consoleLogger, type Logger } from 'spacetimedb';

setGlobalLogger((level, message, ...args) => {
  console[level === 'trace' ? 'debug' : level](`[stdb] ${message}`, ...args);
});

setGlobalLogger(consoleLogger); // back to the default
```

- `Logger`: `(level, message, ...args) => void`. It's only called for logs that pass the global log level, with lazy messages and arguments already resolved.
- `setGlobalLogger` and `getGlobalLogger`: replace or read the current sink, mirroring `setGlobalLogLevel` and `getGlobalLogLevel`.
- `consoleLogger`: the existing styled `console.log` output, unchanged and still the default.

# API and ABI breaking changes

None. This only adds exports, and the default output is unchanged.

# Rollback safety impact

n/a

# Expected complexity level and risk

1. It's a small, client-only change in `src/sdk/logger.ts`.

# Testing

- [x] Added `tests/logger.test.ts` cases:
  - a custom logger receives resolved logs instead of the console;
  - it still respects the global log level, and lazy messages aren't evaluated when filtered out;
  - `consoleLogger` restores the default output.
- [x] `vitest run`: all 417 tests pass. Locally, `server_test_utils_wasm*.test.ts` can't load because the portable datastore WASM build is missing; that's unrelated to this change.
- [ ] ESLint didn't run locally because the root dependencies weren't installed, so it relies on CI.
