author: mattbaldwin
body:
Closes #473.

The soft contact shadow under each battle-arena prop (trees, rocks, mushrooms…) shrank with the prop's turn, so a prop turned near 90° had almost none.

## Root cause
`buildArena` (`apps/client/src/battle/arena.ts`) sized each prop shadow from its prop matrix: `const s = m.m[0] ?? 1`. On a matrix turned about Y, `m[0]` is scale × cos(turn), not the scale. Props are placed with a random turn in [0, 2π), so each shadow came out somewhere between full size and nothing. The sign went negative past 90°, but X and Z flipped together, so it was never mirrored or culled; it was only too small.

## Fix
The prop loop now keeps each kind's `Placement`s and builds the prop matrices from them. Shadows are sized from the placement's own `scale` and placed at its own `x, z`. That's the same size the `turn = 0` case always got. Nothing else changes: the same props, shadow size factor (`built.shadow × 1.6`), height (0.012) and one thin-instanced mesh.

## Tests
`battle-scene.test.ts`: in the forest arena, every prop's shadow width divided by the prop's width must be the same for every prop of a kind, whatever its turn. Width is the length of the matrix's X row, which ignores rotation. Each shadow is matched to its prop by position, and every shadow must find one. The test fails on the old line (two trees' ratios: 0.319 vs 0.037) and passes with the fix.

## Checks (local)
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck` | ✅ |
| client tests (after merging `main`, which brought #472) | ✅ 1,832 |
| `pnpm build` (plus the client bundle check) | ✅ |

The merge of `main` had one conflict: #472's fighter-shadow test and this PR's prop-shadow test were added at the same spot in `battle-scene.test.ts`. Both are kept.

`changes/473-prop-shadows.md` is the What's new entry.

## How to test on iPhone
1. Start a wild battle in a forest: every tree, stump and mushroom around the edge has a soft shadow under it, about the same size for the same kind of prop. Before, some had almost none.
2. Try a battle on rockier land (hills or mountains): the rocks get their full shadows too.

## Review
- Round 1 (head `698cc1e`): **APPROVE**. The reviewer reproduced the failure on the old line, confirmed no two props share a position across every arena with several seeds, and found 62 of 62 shadows matched. One non-blocking nit is fixed in `e79a3ca`: the test now requires every shadow to find its prop.

author: kataage
body:
Refs #714. Builds on Windows CI-green merged PR #719 (`develop@a069b2e3dc4a023e94053f6a1e5612637be91322`). **CI pending.** Report issued without waiting for CI; do not merge on red.

## Production measurement

- Keep real `ViewerTechnicalMetadataBatcher` max 128 in-flight/admitted background records and max 64 items per SQLite transaction. Add a fixed **10-bucket, exclusive** queue-admitted-to-post-COMMIT elapsed-time histogram with one atomic increment per recorded write and a small copied snapshot only at diagnostic read time. No per-image log lines or unbounded storage.
- Derive production representative-library **coarse** p95/p99 bucket **upper bounds**, never pretend a histogram bin gives an exact percentile. `no_samples` when metadata already exists/no background traffic; `over_1000` when tail is outside numeric bins. Emit each histogram bucket under `viewer.metadata_background_latency_bucket_*` in acceptance JSON.
- Track committed batch-group sizes **2–8**, **9–32**, **33–64**, and `avoided_individual_commits = batched_rows - committed_batches`. This counts transactions potentially saved, **not measured wall-time speedup**. Distinguish failed/canceled/guard-rejected requests from committed writes.
- Add deterministic histogram boundary/percentile assertions and actual 32-PNG Viewer integration smoke validating recorded sample counts and group-commit accounting; no new flaky timing gates.
- Document semantic limitations, post-merge CI variance and open qualification questions.

## Prior evidence

PR #719 Windows CI #38240294310 attempt 1 **FAILED** on independent synthetic Viewer **50k** fast-scroll 1,683.9344ms > unchanged 1,500ms. Exact same head attempt 2 **SUCCESS**, including unchanged 8,000ms 10k individually committed Library gate (3,620.3ms) and real PNG Viewer 32 queued / 4 batches / 30 batched rows. Preserve first red evidence; this is not proof the intermittent strict `develop` failure is fixed.

## Safety / exit

No changes to SQLite transaction safety, WAL/synchronous/foreign-keys, source revision/file stat/source identity guards, queue/batch caps, foreground/interactive routing, 8,000ms Library gate, Viewer 1,500ms gate, or published data formats. No unverified claim of cold/warm speedup. Issue #714 remains OPEN until repeatably green post-merge Windows and final real physical owner acceptance (#634/#635 coordinated once).

author: zyyyyyyyd
body:
## Hardware

Os três encoders ligados, gravados e **medidos**. A pinagem foi reatribuída para seguir a ordem física do deck (ENC1 nos pinos mais altos das duas bordas), o que faz cada trinca do cabo cair em pinos vizinhos e em ordem, com o `clk` sempre no fio do meio.

O decodificador foi substituído. A primeira versão falhou no hardware de duas formas ao mesmo tempo: sentido invertido nos três, e o ENC3 emitindo `CW` no meio de um giro anti-horário contínuo, a cerca de quatro eventos por detente. A causa era o filtro de tempo de `5000 µs` — longo demais para não descartar passos reais num giro rápido, curto demais para barrar o repique do contato.

Agora `encTick()` emite um passo por ciclo completo do `CLK`, e só quando as duas metades concordam no sentido. Isso rejeita repique por construção.

**Medição** (pela API de áudio do Windows, cobrindo a cadeia inteira do contato ao volume): dois cliques em cada sentido nos três deram exatamente ±2; corridas contadas de dez deram exatamente dez em cada sentido; dez pressionadas deram dez trocas de mudo.

Também fecha a contradição `NEO_RGB` × `NEO_GRB` que estava aberta desde 03/10: a fita acesa respondeu vermelho a um pedido de vermelho, então `NEO_GRB` está certo e a nota era o lado velho.

## Som no microfone

O Windows não permite injetar áudio na stream de microfone de outro programa. Os dois caminhos suportados — driver de áudio virtual e APO no `audiodg.exe` protegido — exigem assinatura da Microsoft. O Equalizer APO e o projeto Relay contornam desligando a proteção do sistema, o que não é algo para embutir em silêncio.

Então o app virou o mixer: lê o microfone real, soma o que o pad está tocando, e escreve no cabo virtual. Só é preciso um tubo bobo, então **VoiceMeeter não é necessário** e não há janela de mixer para aprender. Inerte até os dois dispositivos serem escolhidos.

Verificado por `tests/test_mic_mixer.py`, que extrai a seção do `app.py` e roda contra stubs — testa o código que vai ao ar, não uma cópia. Em hardware real: 279 callbacks de entrada contra ~280 esperados em 2,8 s, fila vazia no fim, e um tom de 440 Hz chegou a 0,3076 contra 0,30 pedidos. Confirmado também no binário congelado.

## Dois bugs achados olhando, não sendo avisado

- **A desinstalação deixava a entrada `Run` do registro** apontando para o exe recém-apagado, então o Windows tentava abrir um arquivo inexistente a cada boot. Corrigido e provado num ciclo completo de instalar, rodar e desinstalar.
- **`load_config()` não mesclava com os padrões**, então configuração escrita por versão antiga ficava sem toda chave adicionada desde então — e quebraria só em quem atualiza, nunca em instalação nova.

## Um mistério resolvido, não removido

A entrada "o app às vezes inicia sem registrar nada" estava aberta há mais de uma semana. A causa: o Claude Code roda dentro do contêiner MSIX do app desktop, então um programa que ele lança lê e grava um `%APPDATA%` redirecionado. Dois conjuntos de config e log divergindo desde 1º de setembro — por isso uma execução lançada pelo usuário parecia silenciosa do lado do agente.

Consequência registrada: verificação feita pelo agente no "build instalado" não é o que o usuário vê.

author: vjvarada
body:
**A message sent while the agent works now always steers the live run.** The composer has ONE round control: Stop for an empty box, Send for a box with text. The send-mode menu, stop-and-send and the local send queue are gone. A steer that arrives after the run's last tool call no longer dies: a follow-up turn answers it. No flag. Do not merge until review.

## What the member sees

- One box. The message takes the full width. One bar inside the box holds Attach, the agent's controls and the round control.
- While a run is live and the box is empty, the control is **Stop** (■). Esc does the same.
- As soon as the box has text, it is **Send** (↑), and the status row says "Adds to the current reply".
- The sent words show at once as a small note under the reply: "Adding to the reply…", then "Added to the reply".
- The live stream goes on. The client does not stop it, does not drop the partial reply and opens no second stream.
- On a phone, the agent's controls take their own row above Attach and the control.

## How a steer flows

1. `AgentChat.submitText` asks `sendRoute` (`lib/chatSteer.ts`). A live run on the gateway path gives `steer`.
2. `useAgentChat.steerMessage` calls `sendSteer`. It POSTs `/api/agent/chat` the normal way, then the BFF sends it to `/agent/run/stream`.
3. `_route_incoming_turn` gives STEER. `_apply_turn_decision` answers `202 {steered: true}` with no stream (existing §QM-1 code).
4. `send_steer` writes `cc:steer:` first and sends on the control bus. The owner buffers the note, and the next tool result carries it (`decorate_tool_result`).

## The bug this fixes on the server

Before, a steer that arrived while the model wrote its final answer was **lost**. The applier discarded its durable copy, no tool result came, and the next run start cleared the buffer. Now:

1. `stream_relay.push_event` calls `steer.return_unconsumed` before it writes a terminal event. Each unread note goes back to `cc:steer:` under its own id, and the run takes no more notes.
2. When the stream ends, the chat asks once for a follow-up (`steerFollowUp: true`, no words).
3. The gateway's new gate starts no run while a run is live. It starts none when nothing is stored. Otherwise the existing ENGAGE seam takes the steers and makes them the run's message. It drops their copy from the history (`without_replayed`).

A Stop asks for no follow-up. A steer that the stopped run never read stays stored, and the next message replays it through ENGAGE.

## Fallbacks

| The server answers | The client does |
|---|---|
| `202 {steered: true}` | "Added to the reply". The run owes a follow-up |
| `202 {aborted}` or `{dropped}` (a bare "stop") | The note goes. The server saved no row |
| A stream (the run had ended) | It follows that stream as a normal turn, in place of the note |
| 409, 429 or a network error | The note goes, the words go back to the box, and a plain notice says why |
| The direct model path (`litellm`) | It sends nothing. The words stay in the box with a notice |

An old queued item in a browser goes into the box once, and never sends by itself.

## Tests

- **vitest** `src/lib/chatSteer.test.ts` (21) holds the one control, no send-mode menu, and a steer that never stops, enqueues or drops the reply. It also holds the acknowledgement, a refusal that keeps the words, the follow-up rule and the queue migration. Fences updated: picker counts, chatEdit plan shape, `SOLID_BUTTON_DEBT` 21 → 20, `PALETTE_DEBT` for `AgentChat.tsx` 12 → 3, one stale exemption removed.
- **pytest** `tests/unit/test_steer_routing.py` §8 (8 new) and the new `tests/unit/test_steer_follow_up.py` (4). The route test drives the REAL `_route_incoming_turn` and `_apply_turn_decision`.
- **R8** `tests/unit/test_chat_prompt_saved_at_start.py`: 15 passed against a private pgvector Postgres, 0 skipped. The steered row now carries the `steered` mark.
- **e2e** new `e2e/chat-steer.spec.ts` (3, in the `ci` project). The stream goes on, the follow-up answer draws below the steer, and Stop and Esc halt the run. `chat-card-rollup.spec.ts` stays green (one cold-start flake, then 3 of 3). The quarantined `chat.spec.ts` loses its two send-mode tests.
- Full vitest: the same 6 failures as `main` in 4 files (Windows line-ending source fences), and nothing new.

## Mutation table (each run on the committed branch)

| Mutant | Result |
|---|---|
| The client stops on send | KILLED (`chatSteer.test.ts`) |
| The client enqueues instead of posting | KILLED (`chatSteer.test.ts`) |
| The button ignores the box state | KILLED (`chatSteer.test.ts`) |
| No give-back at the terminal event | KILLED (3 pytest) |
| The give-back saves nothing | KILLED (4 pytest) |
| No follow-up gate | KILLED (`test_steer_follow_up.py`) |
| The replay keeps the history copy | KILLED (`test_steer_follow_up.py`) |
| The hook never asks for the follow-up | KILLED (`chatSteer.test.ts`) |
| The steered row loses its mark | KILLED (R8) |
| No give-back after a refusal | KILLED (`test_steer_follow_up.py`) |
| The replay matches an older turn | KILLED (`test_steer_routing.py`) |

## Review round (adversarial reviewer, fixed in `c26798ab8`)

- **P1.** Only a tab that steered through `sendSteer` asked for the follow-up, and once. Now any 202 with `steered: true` owes one, also a plain send into another member's run. A follow-up that meets `run_in_flight` asks again, with a wait from 2 s to 30 s for 20 tries.
- **P2.** A refusal after ENGAGE lost the steers it took. Now `steer.give_back` puts them back in the store.
- **P2.** `without_replayed` could drop an older turn with the same short words. Now it reads only the turns after the last reply.
- **Note.** A steer that started a run drew a bubble id that differed from its saved row. Now one id serves both.
- **Left open.** The gate reads a stale `cc:active` of a dead owner as `run_in_flight`. The steer stays stored, and the next message replays it.

## Review round 2 (independent review, fixed in `2d198fa2f`)

- **P1, a Stop now stops the follow-up for every tab.** `cancel_run` records the Stop for the thread first (`cc:steer-stopped:`). The gate answers `202 stopped` to any follow-up and drops the stored steers. The next real message drops them too. The next run start clears the mark. The client clears the owed follow-up on Stop and on `stopped`. It cancels a waiting retry, and it ignores a steer 202 that lands after a Stop (`stopEpoch`).
- **Why drop and not replay:** the member said stop after the steer. The words stay in the transcript and the saved row, so the next message's history still carries them.
- **P2, the durable copy goes when the model reads the note.** It no longer goes when the owner buffers it, so a buffered steer survives a dead owner.
- **P2, follow-up refusals.** A 409 or 429 draws no card and asks again with the same wait. After the last try, the steer says "Your added message waits for the next reply."
- **P2, Edit after a steer.** Edit offers the prompt. `plan_supersede` removes the turn with its own steer rows and quotes them as `added_while_running`. Another member's steer still refuses the edit.
- **Nits.** The bar gives the free width to the spacer. The hint shows "⌘ ⏎" on a Mac.

Round-2 mutants: 10 of 10 killed.

| Mutant | Result |
|---|---|
| No Stop mark | KILLED |
| The gate ignores the mark | KILLED |
| A new run never clears the mark | KILLED |
| ENGAGE replays a stopped run's steers | KILLED |
| The client owes a follow-up after a Stop | KILLED |
| A `stopped` answer keeps the retry | KILLED |
| The durable copy goes at buffer time | KILLED |
| A follow-up refusal draws a card | KILLED |
| A steer row refuses the edit (server, R8) | KILLED |
| Edit points at the steer row (client) | KILLED |

## Review round 3 (fixed in `a1a2a429a`)

- **P1, the edit note keeps the steps that already ran.** The steer quotes went into the block before the step budget. A few of

author: ikethepike
body:
Fixes #202. Stacked on #233 (#201), which reworked the water generator; merge #233 first.

## What was wrong
On #201's data:

| Feature | Countries |
|---|---|
| `river-nile` | SD |
| `river-white-nile` | SS SD |
| `river-mountain-nile` | SS |

No river listed EG, and none reached River Run's three-country floor. The causes differ from the issue's guess:
- **Egypt was dropped at Lake Nasser.** The generator skipped every Natural Earth "Lake Centerline" segment. That left a gap of about 13 units at Lake Nasser, wider than the 12-unit join that clusters a river's same-name pieces. Aswan-to-Delta became its own cluster, and only the longest cluster is kept.
- **Uganda was dropped by the length gate.** The Albert Nile and the Victoria Nile are each under `MIN_RIVER_LENGTH`, so they never became features. A merge group alone, as the issue suggested, couldn't bring them back, because the old merge only joined finished features.

## Fix
**Generator (`generators/vendors/naturalearth/create-water.ts`)**
- River merge groups fold their stretches into the canonical name *before* clustering (`RIVER_OF_STRETCH`). This replaces the old feature-level merge, which can no longer run and has been removed.
- `WaterAliasGroup` now allows `merge` only on river groups.
- Lake centerlines are kept only to join the reaches on either side of a lake. They aren't drawn and aren't used to work out which countries a river crosses, so the Victoria Nile can't add Tanzania across Lake Victoria.

**Static tables**
- `data/static/water-aliases.ts`: Nile ← White Nile, Mountain Nile, Albert Nile, Victoria Nile.
- **The Blue Nile stays its own river:** it is distinct and well known, and folding it in would make Ethiopia a required answer for "the Nile".
- `WATER_ROSTER_EXPECTATIONS` pins the Nile (EG SD SS UG), the Salween (CN MM TH) and the Rhine (adds LI). A regeneration that loses any of them throws.

**Data:** `data/water.gen.ts` was regenerated with `bun run generate:water` from Natural Earth v5.1.2. `sea-lanes.gen.ts` is unchanged.

## Effect on the data
Compared feature by feature:

| Feature | Before | After | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Nile | SD | SS SD EG UG | the White, Mountain, Albert and Victoria Nile become its aliases |
| `river-white-nile`, `river-mountain-nile` | present | removed | folded into the Nile |
| Salween | CN MM | CN MM TH | the same fault dropped the Thai border reach |
| Rhine | — | + LI | the Alpine Rhine is the CH–LI border |

No other country list changed. 31 rivers changed only their drawn path: reaches beyond a reservoir now survive, and stretches chain into fewer strokes. No river lost a vertex, and no join got longer than the 12-unit join.

The Nile ranks 6th of River Run's 52 dealable rivers.

## Tests
- **`lib/name-water.test.ts`:** at every difficulty, the world River Run pool
  - holds the Nile with UG, SS, SD and EG, and the Salween with TH;
  - has the Nile as one feature with its stretch aliases, the White and Mountain Nile gone, and the Blue Nile still separate.
- **`generators/lib/water-keys.test.ts`:** the existing pinned-roster test now covers the new expectations.

## Audit
An independent review found nothing blocking:
- regenerating gives a byte-identical file;
- only the three rivers above changed countries;
- nothing references the removed ids, and typing "White Nile" resolves to the Nile.

Its should-fix (deleting the merge code that could no longer run, and narrowing the type) is in the second commit. Two cosmetic items are left as they are:
- the Nile's drawn line breaks at Lake Nasser, since centerlines stay undrawn;
- some rivers chain into two strokes 2–3 units apart.

## Other rivers with similar gaps (not fixed)
- **Irtysh:** NE calls the Kazakh reach "Ertis", plus a gap of about 20 units, so it needs a gap rule rather than a merge.
- **Jordan:** shorter than the minimum length.
- **Yenisey:** Russia only, so it can't deal anyway.
- **Amazon:** shows as "Amazonas" and has no "Amazon" alias.

## Checks
- `typecheck`, `lint` and `format:check` pass; the water tests pass (66).
- Full suite: 2134 of 2135 passed. The one failure was a `seat-model` load timeout that passes alone.

author: drkenmorris
body:
## Diagnosis
- Vercel production on commit `a4e71a8` and Indian Creek Supabase migrations up to date.
- Database has 21 questionnaire sections / 193 unique input fields, all mapped to the backend validator.
- Verified anonymous kiosk-session draft save and read-back inside a rolled-back SQL transaction with synthetic data.
- Site's global body uses `overflow:hidden`; the kiosk route lacked its own scrollport, trapping fields below lengthy legal text.
- Administrators visiting `/patient/intake` saw only a review link, while submitted patient accounts intentionally disable every field with little explanation.

## Repair
- Give kiosk a full-height scroll container and scroll to top when switching questionnaire sections.
- Display full legal document text in accessible expandable sections, while preserving the full expanded public privacy notice.
- Correct patient wizard scrolling inside the fixed-height `intakePage` container.
- Add authenticated staff-only `/admin/intake-preview` with **local-memory-only** editable fields (no database writes), plus a path to test real saved kiosk drafts with fictional data.
- Make completed patient records visibly read-only, with correction instructions.
- Add 21-section all-field input and navigation regression tests.

## Deployment and risk
No DB schema migrations or patient-data changes. Run typecheck, SQL/intake/kiosk tests, Vercel build, then deploy and test with fictional data. HIPAA data is not printed in logs or tests.

author: lmdevv
body:
Account settings, the device sign-in approval page, and the admin screens from Paper pages 09 and 10, all wired through `@movies/sdk/react` and main's session setup (#10).

## Routes

| Route | Screen |
| --- | --- |
| `/device?code=…` | Enter code, Approve device, Approved, Expired / invalid / already used, Denied. Guarded by `RequireSignedIn`, so signed-out visitors go to `/sign-in?redirect=…` first. |
| `/settings/account` | Account and sign-out (`useSignOut`) |
| `/settings/devices` | Signed-in browsers, devices, and key sessions, with sign-out |
| `/settings/api-keys` | API keys: list, Create key (`?dialog=create`), Key created (shown once, copy), Revoke |
| `/admin/libraries` | Libraries and scans, live progress, add (`?dialog=add`) / scan now / scan all / cancel |
| `/admin/libraries/$libraryId` | Library detail: files with posters, Missing / Unmatched filters, missing-files notice, NAS offline state, library settings and remove |
| `/admin/libraries/$libraryId/match/$titleId` | Fix metadata match: TMDB search through the media service's `metadata.searchCandidates`, pick, or edit by hand |
| `/admin/users` | Users (role, disable/enable, library access) and invites (create link, revoke) |
| `/admin/backups` | Back up now, list, restore with an inline confirmation |
| `/admin/server` | Media service health and hardware acceleration from `GET /api/health` |

Admin routes check `manage` / `admin` and show a calm state otherwise; the settings list hides sections the session cannot open and links Profiles to main's `/profiles`.

## On top of main (#8, #10)

- The temporary `src/movies-sdk.tsx` provider is gone; the screens use main's `MoviesProvider` setup, `RequireSignedIn`, `useViewer` / `useScopes` / `useSignOut`, `useNow`, `artworkUrl`, `MEDIA_BASE_URL`, and failure wording. The admin copies of those helpers are deleted.
- Fix match: a search the media service answers with `Internal` (no TMDB key, or the provider failed) or cannot reach shows "TMDB search isn't available on this server" and keeps hand edits working; `RateLimited` asks to retry. Posters load through `artworkUrl`, with the blank placeholder when an image is missing or fails.
- UI kit: one each of `Dialog`, `RadioGroup`, `Checkbox`, and `Switch` (main's). Main's pill radios in the profile and setup forms are a separate look and stay inline.

## Command menu

`src/commands/account.ts` and `src/commands/admin.ts`, gated by scope like the settings list:

- **Go to:** Account, Devices, API keys; Libraries (`manage`); Users, Backups (`admin`); Server (`manage` or `admin`).
- **Actions:** Create API key, Sign in a device, Add library (`manage`), Invite someone, Back up now (`admin`).
- **No results:** a query shaped like a device code (`HD5R-5GTL`) offers "Approve device code HD5R-5GTL".
- Scanning stays in main's `library.ts`.

## Backend and kit changes

- `libraries.files` and `libraries.fileSummary` (manage scope) list a library's files with their titles and count missing files and unmatched titles, with two new indexes. Unmatched pages hold at most 20 titles and 50 files each.
- UI kit: `Dialog`, `RadioGroup`, restyled `Checkbox` (both with the global focus ring), `raised` button variant and `row` / `xs` / `dialog` sizes, a `stale` and `autoFocus` option on `CodeInput`, and `tracking-eyebrow` / `text-wordmark` role tokens.

## Tests

- Unit: date/size formatting (time-zone proof), device code parsing, and the menu's device-code detection.
- Browser, in the `admin` Playwright project (`apps/web/e2e/admin`). It depends on main's `stack` project and signs in as the owner that project creates, so both share one fresh stack. It skips without a stack, like main's suite, and the CI `web-stack` job runs it (17 browser tests pass).
  - Libraries, on the **real media service** with generated clips: add library → Queued until the service starts → Ready with 3 titles → files and quality → a deleted file is marked missing → Missing / Unmatched filters → fix match shows search unavailable (no TMDB key) and a hand edit renames → matched title poster loads from `/artwork/` → folder renamed away shows NAS offline and the log → retry once it is back.
  - API key: Create API key from the command menu → shown once and copied → listed → signs in → revoke ends its session.
  - Device login: code typed in → approve → the device signs in with read and play → code reuse refused; deny, reached by typing the code into the command menu; unknown code; signed-out redirect.
  - Users: invite link create and revoke. Backups: Back up now from the command menu → restore confirmation. Backups use a stand-in that calls `mediaService:*`, because the media service runs no backup jobs yet.

## Still depends on work in flight

- **Migration (Paper 11)** is built on the local branch `w3-web-admin-migration` against the migration agent's contracts (#11). It joins once #11 is on main.
- **Restore** needs the `backups.restore` media route (still unserved); Back up now needs a media-side backup worker.

## Paper deviations

- One settings sidebar (page 10's, with YOU / ADMIN and Server) for every settings screen; Migration appears with the migration screens.
- Scope names are the real ones (`read`, `play`, `account`, `manage`, `admin`), not `library:read` / `playback` / `rooms`.
- Destructive confirmations use the outlined danger button from the design note, not the filled red drawn on Revoke key.
- Not shown because no data exists for them yet: library thumbnails and size, automatic-scan settings, Keep / Purge and "Needs transcode" on files, match scores, "Connecting from" on device approval, "Scan QR code instead", user avatars / profile counts / last active, backup retention and folder, server version / uptime / transcode limits / playing-now table, and "Search unmatched files" in the menu.
- Device copy says "device" instead of "TV", because the CLI uses the same page.

author: ubyndr
body:
Brings over the release process tested in atlas-skills-sandbox.

## What changes

- **Separate tags.** The plugin tags as `cap-tools--v<version>` and the package as `pkg-cap-client--v<version>`. Skills now pin `pkg-cap-client--v0.4.0`, and `cap-tools` moves to 0.4.1.
- **`scripts/versions.py`**, from the sandbox, tested in `tests/test_versions.py`:
  - `check-bumps`: fails a PR that changes the plugin or package without bumping its version
  - `untagged`: lists what the release job should tag
  - `pins`: lists every package pin in use
  - `report`: generates `docs/pins.md`
  - `cli <dir> [--at REF]` (new here): `cap-client` installs `cap`, not a command named after its directory, so the workflows read the command name from `pyproject.toml`, at the pinned tag.
- **`test.yml`** adds: plugin validation, a bump check on PRs, a check that `docs/pins.md` is current, install-from-git on PRs as well as main, and a run of every skill pin exactly as written.
- **`release.yml`** (new): once `test` is green on main, tags untagged packages, then plugins (via `claude plugin tag`), and creates a GitHub Release for each. It sets `permissions: contents: write` itself, so the org's read-only default doesn't block it. The sandbox works the same way.
- **`nightly.yml`** (new): re-installs every pin used by main and the last 3 plugin releases, and runs the package's tests at each pinned tag. `uvx --from git+…` resolves dependencies fresh and ignores `uv.lock`, so a tag can stop working without any new commit.
- **Smaller fixes:**
  - deleted the stale, unused `packages/cap-client/uv.lock`, and made `uv.lock` exempt from the bump check
  - the README example pinned `v0.3.0`
  - the README claimed a committed `enabledPlugins` needs no install step; each person still runs `claude plugin install` once
  - the README now covers pinning a release by `ref`, plus the one-registration-per-machine caveat

## Already done

8 backfill tags are pushed: `cap-tools--v0.1.0…v0.4.0` and `pkg-cap-client--v0.1.0…v0.4.0`. Each is an alias at the same commit as the existing `vX.Y.Z` tag, which stay in place, and old pins still resolve. `uvx --no-cache --from …@pkg-cap-client--v0.4.0 … cap --version` prints `cap-client 0.4.0`.

## After merge

`release` should create only `cap-tools--v0.4.1`, with no package tag. Then run `nightly` once via workflow_dispatch to confirm it is green.

## Local checks

`./dev.sh` passes: 145 package and grader tests, 28 tooling tests, `docs/pins.md` current, plugin validation. `check-bumps --base origin/main` passes and ruff is clean.

author: yqteam-theodore
body:
## Summary

Avoids a page lookup and a page-header parse on every in-leaf cursor step.

`yq_btree_cursor_next()` and `yq_btree_cursor_prev()` always resolved the leaf page with `get_page_data()` and parsed its header with `read_page_header()`, even when the step merely advanced/decremented one slot inside the same leaf. In a full or range scan that happens once per key, so the work is O(keys) even though it is only needed once per leaf.

## Changes

- **next()**: the leaf's key count is already cached in `cursor->slot_count` — every entry point that lands on a leaf (`first`/`last`/`seek`, and the cross-leaf step) keeps it in sync. Return early when `slot_idx + 1 < slot_count`, without touching the page. The page and header are now read only when the step leaves the leaf via the right sibling.
- **prev()**: hoist the `slot_idx > 0` test ahead of the page fetch. That branch never reads the header, so it can run first and the page is only fetched when crossing into the left sibling.

## Behaviour

Unchanged. The fast paths only skip work whose result is already known from `slot_count` (next) or is not needed at all (prev); cross-leaf transitions still fetch the sibling and refresh the cached count.

## Testing

- Builds clean with `-Wall -Wextra`.
- Full suite: `ctest` → 10/10 tests pass. `seek_test` builds a multi-key B+Tree and scans it with `cursor_first` + `cursor_next`, exercising the new fast path on every in-leaf step.

author: dflippojr
body:
Closes #623

## Confirmed first
On the tower (tailscaled **1.102.4**, commit 3caf7d9e7, Windows), `curl https://dflippotower.tail7c9f1e.ts.net/me` run from the tower itself with no credential returned `"role":"owner"`. The same request to `http://127.0.0.1:8100/me` got 401. A temporary echo server behind an existing `tailscale serve` port showed what tailscaled forwards for a local caller:

- `Tailscale-User-Login: <owner>` (WhoIs on the node's own address)
- `X-Forwarded-For: 100.75.184.105`, which is this node's own `tailscale ip`
- A caller-supplied `X-Forwarded-For: 1.2.3.4` was **replaced**, not appended. Serve always sends exactly one value.

## Change
- `harness/tailscale_peer.py`: `PeerCheck.from_other_node(forwarded)` runs only after the peer is verified as tailscaled. It accepts exactly one `X-Forwarded-For` value that parses as an IP and is not one of this node's own addresses. It refuses when the header is missing, has more than one value (repeated headers or a comma list), can't be parsed, or when the node's addresses can't be read. `node_ips()` runs `tailscale.exe ip` from the Tailscale install directory. Results are cached for 60 s; a failure is not cached and refuses the request.
- `harness/api.py`: `_identity_from_tailscaled` applies that check in the verified branch, using a thread on a cache miss. Unverified peers never reach it, so `X-Forwarded-*` is ignored for them as before. The non-Windows `trust_unverified_identity_headers` opt-in is unchanged.
- Tests: the fake tailscaled check now has node IPs. The test client stands in for serve by adding another node's `X-Forwarded-For` to requests that carry a login. New tests cover:
  - self-node address refused (IPv4, IPv6, v4-mapped); the local owner token still works
  - another node accepted
  - multi-valued, malformed and missing header refused
  - unverified peer with XFF still refused, and the node IPs are never read
  - unknown node IPs refused
  - cache and retry behaviour, and `node_ips` parsing
- `docs/INSTALL.md` documents the rule.

## Scope addition: peer must be the Tailscale service (issue comment 2026-10-12, hub review finding A)
Any local user can run the real `tailscaled.exe` (userspace, `--windows-mode=dev`) as a proxy to the daemon and forge `Tailscale-User-Login` and `X-Forwarded-For`, so the exe-path rule alone was not enough. `PeerCheck.verify` now also requires the connection's process to be the `Tailscale` service (`psutil.win_service_get('Tailscale').pid()`) or a child it started (see Review fixes). A missing service, a stopped one (PID `None`) or a failed query fails closed. On the tower the service PID was 7500, running `C:\Program Files\Tailscale	ailscaled.exe`. New tests:
- a right-exe-path peer with a non-service PID is refused, and the refusal is cached
- a missing or stopped service is refused
- `service_pid` queries the `Tailscale` service

## Review fixes
- **Stale node IPs** (review on c521529): after a profile switch, the cached `tailscale ip` result could miss the node's new address. The forwarded address is now also checked on every request against the machine's current interface addresses (`psutil.net_if_addrs()`). A failure there refuses the request.
- **Service child** (review on 155f424): the `Tailscale` service PID is tailscaled's supervisor, and a `tailscaled.exe` child owns Serve's socket. On the tower that's service 7500, child 10312, and connections to `:8100` were owned by 10312. The peer may now be the service or a child it started. The child must be newer than the service (so a recycled PID can't match) and must still be the install-directory tailscaled.exe. Making the SYSTEM service the parent of another process needs admin rights.
- **Live check** with the real `PeerCheck` behind `tailscale serve`, requested from the tower: `verified: true, from_other_node: false` (forwarded address 100.75.184.105). Direct loopback: `verified: false`.

## Scope addition 2: raw TCP forward to the daemon port (issue comment 2026-10-12 15:52, hub review)
A raw TCP forward (`tailscale serve --tcp` or `--tls-terminated-tcp`) passes the caller's bytes through without tailscaled's headers. A tailnet peer could then write its own `Tailscale-User-Login` while the socket still belongs to tailscaled. The daemon now reads the serve config with `tailscale serve status --json` (through the LocalAPI) as part of every new connection's lookup, with no separate cache. While the config has any `TCPForward` to the daemon's listen port it refuses every tailnet identity. That covers any host (loopback, `localhost`, `[::1]`, the tailnet IP), in node ports, foreground sessions and services, and a target whose port can't be read. It also refuses when the config can't be read; that failure is not cached. `PeerCheck.admits(client, server, forwarded)` runs all three checks, and the middleware always runs it in a thread. On the tower the live config parses (`TCP`, `Web`) and has no raw forward to 8100. I didn't add a real `--tcp` forward to test that path live, because that would change the node's serve config. New tests:
- raw forwards on node, foreground and service are refused, as is an unparseable target, and `/keys` can't be created
- a forward to another port leaves the daemon accepted
- an unreadable config is refused and the failure isn't cached
- a forward added after an HTTPS request is caught on the forward's own new connection
- `raw_forward_to` host and port matching
- `serve_config` CLI parsing

- **Stale serve config** (review on c0c6d2d): an earlier 5 s config cache could admit a forward added just after an HTTPS request. The config is now read with each new connection's lookup. A raw forward always opens its own connection from tailscaled, so it always meets the current config.

- **Held raw stream** (review on ca627f0): tailscaled keeps a raw-forwarded stream open after its mapping is removed. Once a raw forward to the daemon's port has been seen, tailnet identity now stays refused until the daemon restarts, which closes every held stream. The log and INSTALL.md say to remove the forward and then restart.
  - **Remaining case, accepted by the owner on #623 (option 1, no further code):** a raw forward that is added and removed with no identity-carrying request checked while it exists is never seen, so a stream held open through it could still forge a login afterwards. Closing that needs continuous watching of the serve config (a background poll, which narrows the window, or an event watch), which the owner declined. INSTALL.md and the docstrings now call the check best effort and describe this gap plainly. Publishing the daemon only through the HTTPS proxy, as INSTALL.md says, avoids it entirely.

## Owner-facing effect
A browser **on the tower itself** that opens the tailnet URL now gets 401, the same as `127.0.0.1:8100`. Use Web from another tailnet device.

## Hub
agent-harness-hub PR #35 (`harness_hub/tailnet.py`) copies `PeerCheck` without these checks. It needs the same service-PID, self-node (`from_other_node`) and raw-TCP-forward steps so the two stay consistent. This PR doesn't touch the hub repo.

author: hafnerst-agent
body:
Part 1 of 5 of "Move simulation into its own Simulate area and extend it with architecture-relevant simulations": **the menu and tab split, simulation-mode indicators, and scenarios**. It branches from the latest `dev` (after #48) and is not stacked. The next PR (shared-risk failures and N-1/N-2) will be opened from a fresh branch only after this one is merged.

## Design decisions

### Analyze vs. Simulate
- **Analyze ▾** answers *what is*. It keeps Addressing overview (`I`), Focus (`Shift+F`) and Trace path (`T`), and has no simulation entries any more.
- **Simulate ▾** is new, right after Analyze, and answers *what if*:
  - Simulate failure of selection (`X`)
  - Scenarios (opens the Simulation tab)
  - Single points of failure…
  - Previous step (`[`) and Next step (`]`)
  - Save scenario…
  - Exit simulation (`Esc`)
- **Side panel:** a new **Simulation** tab holds the scenarios, the step player, each step's changes and its results. The **Analysis** tab keeps only the path tracer.
- **Command registry:** everything is in it (new group `Simulate`, commands `sim.prev`, `sim.next`, `sim.save`, `panel.simulation`), so menus, shortcuts and the palette agree. The palette also offers each saved scenario as *Play scenario: …*.

### Simulation mode (recognisable beyond colour)
- A **banner** with ◈, the scenario name, *step k of n: <step>*, ◀ / ▶, Results and **Exit simulation**.
- A **hatched frame** around the diagram (a pattern, not a tint).
- A **◈ Simulation · step k of n** marker in the status bar, with a dashed border.
- The diagram is labelled **Simulated state**: a badge, and in the SVG's accessible name.
- **Very short windows** (≤ 420 px high): the banner collapses to one line that itself says *Simulated state*, and the badge goes.

### Editing during a simulation: **blocked** (the approach chosen)
- **How it works:** `ModelDoc.lock` makes every network edit throw `EditLocked` and change nothing.
- **What the user sees:**
  - The Edit tab shows the selected object read-only (a disabled fieldset) under a notice with a one-click **Exit simulation**.
  - The YAML text is read-only.
  - Commands marked `edits` (Connect, Auto-arrange, the input helpers, protocol enabling) are unavailable and say why.
  - The outline's Add / Duplicate / Delete are disabled, and dragging nodes is off.
  - Undo and redo are paused, except for scenario edits.
- **Scenario edits** stay allowed and undoable: save, rename, delete, a step added to or removed from a saved scenario.
- **Rejected alternative:** ending the simulation on the first edit. One stray keystroke would throw away the state under review. The decision is documented in the README (*Simulation mode*).

### How the modes combine
- **Trace path** runs on the simulated state. Its banner says *Path trace in the simulated state*, and the Analysis tab carries a note.
- **Focus** counts hops over the cables and relations that are **up** in the simulated state, and says so (`analysis/focus.ts` takes an optional `FocusUp`).
- **Exports** show the simulated state with a dashed frame and a *Simulation: scenario “…”, step k of n: … · …* note (one note line per active mode, as before).
- Opening, closing or replacing a model ends the simulation.

### Scenarios
- A scenario is a named, ordered list of steps, played as an overlay. Step *k* is the state after the first *k* steps; step 0 is the model as written.
- **Steps in this PR:** `fail` / `restore` of a `device`, `cable`, `port`, `relation` or `lag` (a LAG = all its member cables).
  - Group/location and risk-group steps come in PR 2.
  - Maintenance and value changes, and hypothetical cables, relations and routes, come in PR 4.
- **Each step shows:**
  - what changed since the previous step: now down, now degraded, recovered, device pairs lost or regained;
  - what is failed now, each with **Restore** (adds a restore step);
  - its full result: per-kind counts, affected objects with their state as a word, and the device pairs that lose reachability.
- **`X`** starts an **ad-hoc scenario** at once (during a simulation, it inserts a step after the one shown). **Save scenario…** names it and stores it in the model.
- **Pure and deterministic:** `src/analysis/scenario.ts` resolves steps to failed refs and reuses `analysis/failure.ts` (`simulate`, `summarize`, `lostReachability`) for propagation and routing. Nothing is duplicated.
  - Results are cached per model and per set of failed objects.
  - The order of selection, or of steps that fail different objects, never changes a result.
- **Undo:** playing adds **no undo steps**; saving and editing scenarios are normal undoable edits.

### Model additions (format stays `netatlas: 1`)
```yaml
scenarios:
  - id: isp1-outage
    label: ISP 1 outage
    description: …
    steps:
      - fail: {cable: l-hq-isp1}
        note: the carrier reports a fibre cut
      - fail: {device: hq-rtr1}
      - restore: {device: hq-rtr1}
```
- Presentation and analysis data only: scenarios never change network objects.
- **Errors:** unknown keys, a step with zero or two actions, an action with zero or two targets, a duplicate scenario id.
- **Warning:** a step whose object no longer exists. The step is skipped when played, and the Simulation tab marks it.
- **Renames:** renaming a device, interface, cable or relation in NetAtlas updates the steps that name it.
- **Limits:** 500 scenarios × 500 steps.

### Documented approximations
- Routing is model-based.
- No spanning tree, protocol timers or convergence.
- No ACLs, NAT or QoS.
- Results are no more precise than the model.

These are stated in the Simulation tab (*What the simulation approximates*) and in the README Limitations. The N-2 bounds arrive with PR 2.

## What changed
- `src/analysis/scenario.ts` (new): step resolution, `stepView`, `stepDiff`, `scenarioId`, `scenarioProblems`.
- `src/analysis/focus.ts`: optional `FocusUp` for hops in a simulated state.
- `src/model/types.ts`, `src/yaml/schema.ts`, `src/validation/scenarios.ts` (new), `src/validation/validate.ts`: the `scenarios:` section.
- `src/editor/document.ts`:
  - the lock (`EditLocked`, `undoLocked`);
  - `saveScenario` / `setScenarioSteps` / `deleteScenario`;
  - rename propagation into steps.
- `src/ui/simulation.ts` (new; replaces `src/ui/failure.ts`): the Simulation tab and the SPOF dialog.
- `src/ui/app.ts`: scenario state, player, save/delete dialogs, mode indicators, edit blocking, trace/focus integration, export frame.
- `src/ui/commands.ts`, `src/ui/palette.ts`: the Simulate group, the step and save commands, `edits` gating, *Play scenario* entries.
- `src/index.html`, `src/styles.css`: the Simulate menu, the Simulation tab, banner, frame, badge, status marker and lock notice, in both themes.
- `examples/enterprise-wan.yaml`: two saved scenarios (*ISP 1 outage*, *Core peer link and core switch*).
- **Docs:**
  - README: toolbar, Working with the diagram, palette, and a new **Simulation** chapter (*Simulation mode*, *Scenarios*, *Failure propagation*, *Single points of failure*);
  - README Limitations, the verification table and manual check 27;
  - `docs/FORMAT.md` (`scenarios`);
  - `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`;
  - CHANGELOG;
  - the User Manual (*Simulate: what if something fails*, `[` / `]` in its shortcut list) with a new screenshot.
- `scripts/manual-screenshots.mjs`: the simulation shot now plays the saved scenario and shows the whole banner.
- The other manual screenshots were regenerated because the toolbar gained the Simulate menu.
- `dist/netatlas.html` regenerated.

### Test adjustments (worth a look)
- **`test/build.test.mjs`:** the sanity budget for the embedded manual screenshots goes from 512 KiB to **640 KiB** (base64).
  - On `dev` the screenshots were already at 519 KB of the 524 KB limit.
  - This PR adds about 15 KB: the readable full-width simulation shot, plus small growth in the shots whose toolbar gained the Simulate menu. The new total is 534 KB.
  - The next four PRs each add manual screensh

## CP1 14c — lesson page polish (PLAN cycle 14 r2, R189)

**What changes**
- **(a) Pre-join.** Daily's own pre-join check (camera and microphone preview, the browser permission, device pickers, then "Join") is switched on with `enable_prejoin_ui` on the room (`createRoom`) and on every meeting token (`joinToken`). The embedded frame is mounted only after our "Join the lesson here" click, so the room opens only after the check. **The screen renders inside Daily's frame, not in our own markup**: a device ID from our origin means nothing inside the cross-origin frame, so a screen of our own would have decorative pickers. That is a deviation from the wording of R189(a), flagged for the planner (docs/reports/14c.md section 1).
- **(b) Titles.** `LessonRoomView` builds a per-side `title`: tutor "<subject> with <learner>", parent "<subject> with <tutor> · for <learner>". The page no longer receives `learner_display_name` or `tutor_display_name`. The browser tab title keeps the subject only.
- **(c) Join button.** `v-if="!joinUrl"`: it hides once the room is open, in frame mode and link mode. A line says to reload the page to join again.

**Not bypassable by URL.** The page reads nothing from the address bar (a test greps `Show.vue`). The token is minted only by `POST /lessons/{lesson}/room` and lives only in component memory. `join()` has one call site: `@click="join"` on the button (`Show.vue:199`); the only `watch` stops polling, and there is no `onMounted`.

**Disclosed limitations (read before reviewing)**
1. Token-level `enable_prejoin_ui` being accepted and honoured by Daily's API, the screen itself, the pickers and the permission prompt count are **reading-verified only** (daily-js 0.93.0 type definitions and Daily's reference pages). No Daily key is held (R125) and no browser was driven. If the API rejected the token property every join would answer 422; if it rejected the room property, room creation would fail. Each is a one-line deletion. Mitigation: a STATUS owner action to open the room of a lesson created after the deploy, which exercises both payloads.
2. The Daily display name on the parent's side is the learner's display name (`IssueJoinToken`, unchanged). Examined and kept: its only recipient is the lesson's tutor, which R189(b) names.
3. `Show.vue` behaviour is checked by source-reading tests only (there is no JS runner here).
4. Rooms already made keep their old properties (`createRoom` fetches an existing room); the token property covers them.

**Verification (local, on the pre-PR tree)**
- Full suite, 35 per-directory runs: **2266 passed, 11620 assertions**, no failure (`main` at the 14b merge: 2259 / 11533).
- Red check: 5 new or changed tests fail without the app changes.
- `ledger:verify` OK; `npm run build` exit 0; phpstan 0 errors; pint clean; `npm run types:check` exit 0; `RtlCheckTest` 3 passed.

body:
## Summary

Packaged desktop tests stop the app with `taskkill /T /F` on Windows. When one process in the tree is already exiting, `taskkill` fails the whole command, and the test fails even though the app is gone. Cleanup now waits for the app to exit, then fails only if a process that `taskkill` refused is still running, and names it.

## Why

PS-584. The 0.43.0 Windows desktop release job (run 38252503238, attempt 4) failed this way after npm had already published 0.43.0:

```
Error: Command failed: taskkill /PID 1240 /T /F
ERROR: The process with PID 808 (child process of PID 9132) could not be terminated.
Reason: The operation attempted is not supported.
```

The cold-start benchmark had launched and measured the app. Only cleanup failed. The same error failed the 0.42.0 cold-start benchmark and a harness detection test on 2026-10-10. Each Windows desktop job stops the app about 30 times, so a rare refusal blocks releases.

## What

- `clients/desktop/src/testing/stop-packaged-process.ts`:
  - The tree kill returns the process IDs that `taskkill` reports it could not end.
  - The helper always waits for the app's own exit.
  - It throws only when one of the refused processes is still running, and names its PID.
  - `taskkill` exit code 128 (already exited) is still accepted. Any other `taskkill` error that names no process still throws.
- `stop-packaged-process.test.ts`: two tests with real processes and an injected tree kill. One covers a refused process that has already exited, so cleanup succeeds. The other covers a refused process that is still running, so cleanup fails and names it. The injection is the only way to run the Windows `taskkill` path on macOS and Linux.

## How

- **Fail only on a real leak:** Windows refuses to end a process that is already exiting. Once the app has exited, a refused process that is gone is not a leak. One that is still running is a real leak and still fails the test, so cleanup cannot hide a leaked child.
- **No new time limit:** the helper waits within the calling test's limit, as the testing guide requires.
- **Checks:**
  - `bun test src/testing/stop-packaged-process.test.ts`: 3 pass. Both new tests failed before the fix.
  - `bun run --cwd clients/desktop test`: 200 pass.
  - `bun run --cwd clients/desktop lint` (`tsc` and biome) is clean.
- **Release use:** 0.43.0's desktop release can use this fixed helper through Release Desktop's `validation_ref`.
- **No changeset:** test helper only.

author: enjay27
body:
Under ADR-043 (Accepted). Draft: `static.yml` and `smoke.yml` change, so Kade merges it by hand (ADR-030).

## What changed and why

- **Gate (ADR-043 §3):** `gate.py up` installs cert-manager v1.21.2 and the Barman Cloud Plugin v0.15.0 after CNPG, from manifests pinned by sha256 in `gates/pins.json`. The plugin's manifest is refused unless every namespace it names is `NS_CNPG_SYSTEM`.
- **Step 0 (amends ADR-029's precondition):** the install stops unless the plugin runs next to the operator. That means the ObjectStore CRD, a Service labelled `cnpg.io/pluginName=barman-cloud.cloudnative-pg.io`, and a ready pod behind it.
- **Bucket and key (§2):** backups get their own bucket and key: `POLARIS_BACKUP_BUCKET`, the Secret `polaris-backup-s3` (via `init_env.py --apply-secrets`), and a third SeaweedFS identity on the gate allowed only on that bucket.
- **Chart (§1, §2):** `charts/polaris-postgres` 0.2.0. polaris-pg archives its WAL through the plugin to the ObjectStore `polaris-backup` (retention 30d). The ScheduledBackup `polaris-pg-daily` runs at 02:00. The schema refuses unknown keys, a non-http(s) endpoint, an invalid bucket name and a bad retention. `static.yml` lints a chart with its `ci/lint-values.yaml` when it has one.
- **Step 1 (`release.py`):** stops early while `S3_ENDPOINT` or `POLARIS_BACKUP_BUCKET` is empty, requires `polaris-backup-s3`, and passes both values to helm in a values file. After the helm upgrade it waits until polaris-pg reads healthy, with every instance ready, 3 times 10 s apart. Ready alone came before CNPG's restart.
- **`check-restore` (§4):** a new smoke step.
  - It takes an on-demand Backup through the plugin, then bootstraps the Cluster `polaris-pg-restore` from the ObjectStore with all archived WAL replayed.
  - It waits until that Cluster is Ready, then until it is healthy on 3 reads. CNPG restarts the restored instance once after recovery.
  - `check_restore.sh` then reads, as Polaris, the realm's root principal and `gate_catalog`. The restore Cluster is deleted whatever happens.
- **`check-traffic`:**
  - When a must-not rule fails, the output names up to 5 of the matching records by safe fields only: no paths, bodies, statements or messages.
  - Kade's option 1: on an upgrade, FATAL 57P01 and pg `upstream_unreachable` are allowed only inside polaris-pg's restart window. That window runs from its first UpgradingInstance event to the end of the install. Outside it, or on a fresh install, nothing is allowed.
- **Upgrade path:** the gate's upgrade copies the gate's `.env` into the previous release's worktree. Without it, every upgrade from `platform-2026.10.12` stops on "S3_ENDPOINT is empty", **on main too**: main's scheduled smoke [38239860699](https://github.com/enjay27/lakehouse/actions/runs/38239860699) is red for this reason, and this PR fixes it.
- **Docs:** `CLAUDE.md` and the roadmap name the backups, the plugin and cert-manager on the gate.

## Verified

On head `9df8803`:
- [Static 38262378873](https://github.com/enjay27/lakehouse/actions/runs/38262378873) and [dry-run 38262386353](https://github.com/enjay27/lakehouse/actions/runs/38262386353) green.
- [Smoke 38262381612](https://github.com/enjay27/lakehouse/actions/runs/38262381612) green. It installed `platform-2026.10.12` and upgraded it to this commit.
  - Step 0 found the plugin.
  - Step 1 saw polaris-pg healthy on 3 reads.
  - `Backup polaris-pg-gate-36520` completed through the plugin.
  - `polaris-pg-restore` was Ready, healthy on 3 reads, and held "the realm's root principal" and "the catalog gate_catalog".
  - `check-traffic` passed, using the restart window 14:27:02 to 14:31:42: 2 failed statements and 8 unreachable records were let through, with 0 outside the window.
- Locally: unit tests for install (131), gates (303) and scripts (174); charts (81) with helm and kubeconform from the pins; `repo_check`, `adr_check`, `claude_md_check`, `git diff --check`.

## NOT VERIFIED

- **Why the restore's recovery pod is retried:** in an earlier run it was retried 6 times before Ready, cause unknown. This run's cluster state was not dumped because it passed.
- **Target clusters:** cert-manager and the plugin there are the operator team's (#9). Step 0 checks for the plugin; this repository does not install it there.
- **S3 region:** the ObjectStore sets none. The plugin reads one only from a Secret, and boto3 signs for us-east-1 without one.
- **Image pinning:** cert-manager's and the plugin's images are pulled by tag. The manifests themselves are pinned by sha256.
- **Plugin version:** pinned at v0.15.0. v0.15.1 is under two weeks old until 2026-10-14.

## Wrong turns

Each failed smoke run named the next fix:
- [38213173424](https://github.com/enjay27/lakehouse/actions/runs/38213173424): the previous release had no `.env` in its worktree.
- [38215183351](https://github.com/enjay27/lakehouse/actions/runs/38215183351): `kubectl wait` reported Ready before CNPG restarted polaris-pg for the plugin.
- [38217979245](https://github.com/enjay27/lakehouse/actions/runs/38217979245): a must-not rule failed and printed only counts.
- [38236488707](https://github.com/enjay27/lakehouse/actions/runs/38236488707): FATAL 57P01 and unreachable records appeared during polaris-pg's restart, the case behind Kade's option 1.
- [38245393066](https://github.com/enjay27/lakehouse/actions/runs/38245393066): `polaris-pg-restore` read Ready, then refused psql during its post-recovery restart.

Closes #83

author: pcrus1988-bit
body:
## Owner requirement
Publication and factual GEMI identity verification must **not** depend on exact business latitude/longitude. Map pins, 25-km delivery radius and precise premises verification are separate later enrichments.

## Implementation
- Migration 0447 (with SHA-256 registry) adds independently audited registry identity verification, publication_basis = premise|municipality and directory_hub_slug.
- Replaces both geo-only publication constraints with two valid modes. Municipality listings require a verified source/identity, reviewed municipality-to-HUB correspondence, privacy+editorial approval and no active partner/converted CLAIM duplicate. Precise-GEO path preserved.
- RLS permits approved published municipality records to be read by app runtime. No private GEMI or research contacts become public by default.
- Public directory/list/details, category counts, SEO threshold and canonical redirect queries support both modes. Details explicitly state municipality-level geographic precision and unverified ownership.
- Hub landing page shows approved registry listings and does not falsely claim the hub is empty.
- Repeatable bounded approval-gated private municipality staging script; separate deterministic exact official GEMI-cache identity verification script (does NOT approve privacy/editorial or publish).

## Production research snapshot
313,911 research records, 86 administratively reviewed municipality matches covering 97,208 entries, zero public GEMI listings as of the pre-migration snapshot. Publicity remains gated by actual registry identity and privacy/editorial decisions—not absent coordinates.

## Release conditions
Run all CI/SEO/browser suites; apply exact migration and read back RLS constraints, stage reviewed matches privately and exact recent GEMI official cache identities, verify no GEO/personal contact leaks. Do not rubber-stamp legal/privacy reviews, invent human verification or imply any coordinate/radius for an administrative listing.

## Subsequent tasks
Automate officially licensed registry identity matching by safe cohorts, recording deterministic provenance. Obtain separately established legal basis and editorial evidence for publication of personal-identity/sole-trader entries; release approved batches, preserving canonical CLAIM and marketplace sellers. Precise geocoding optional later.

body:
## Resumen

Resuelve [LAU-13](https://linear.app/lautaro124/issue/LAU-13/configurar-turnos-grupales-y-su-capacidad-maxima-en-el-formulario-de). El dueño puede marcar un tipo de turno como grupal: define cuántas personas entran y en qué horarios fijos se da. El asistente respeta esa capacidad al mostrar disponibilidad y al reservar.

## Cambios

**Formulario (`/contanos` y `/reuniones`)**
- Cada tipo de turno tiene un chip "Grupal".
- Al prenderlo aparecen dos campos:
  - la capacidad, un entero de 1 a 100;
  - los horarios fijos, día y hora.
- Mientras falte algo o esté mal, la web muestra el motivo y traba el avance del wizard o el "Guardar". La API valida lo mismo (`normalizarTipoEvento`) y responde 400 con el motivo.
- Todo se guarda dentro de `Agent.tiposEvento`, igual que el precio. Al recargar, se ve lo guardado.

**Agenda del bot**
- Cada horario fijo es una clase que ocupa la agenda aunque nadie se haya anotado, así que ningún turno individual cae encima.
- El prompt lista las próximas clases con los lugares que quedan. Sólo lleva cantidades, nunca nombres de otros clientes.

**Reservas**
- `crear_turno` de un tipo grupal sólo acepta el inicio exacto de una clase. El fin lo toma de la clase, no del modelo.
- Se rechaza una clase completa, o una en la que ese cliente ya está anotado. El rechazo ofrece las próximas clases con lugar.
- Los anotados comparten un único evento de calendario, titulado por ejemplo `Yoga (grupal) · 3/10`.
- La capacidad se vuelve a contar dentro de una transacción con `pg_advisory_xact_lock` por clase, así que dos chats a la vez no se quedan con el último lugar.
- Cancelar libera el lugar. El evento se borra sólo cuando se baja el último anotado.
- Reprogramar primero anota en la clase nueva y después libera la vieja.

**Base y plantilla**
- Columna nueva `Turno.tipo`, con la migración `20261012120000_turno_tipo`. Sólo la llevan los turnos grupales.
- `PLANTILLA_VERSION` pasa a 6: el deploy regenera los prompts guardados.

**Otros**
- Skill `.claude/skills/crear-rama` para crear ramas desde `develop` con prefijo `feature/` o `bug/`.
- `CLAUDE.md` documenta los turnos grupales.

## Decisiones a revisar

- Las clases valen cualquier día de la semana y a cualquier hora: no se les aplica "sólo de lunes a viernes" ni la franja de atención, porque los horarios los fija el dueño.
- Si el dueño vuelve individual un tipo que era grupal, los turnos ya reservados no se pueden reprogramar. El bot propone cancelar y reservar de nuevo.

## Verificación

- **API:** pasan los 1026 tests, incluidos los `*.db.spec.ts` contra un Postgres real con pgvector. Uno nuevo prueba la carrera por el último lugar con cinco chats concurrentes. Lint y tipos limpios. La migración aplica y `prisma migrate diff` no muestra desvío.
- **Web:** lint, tipos y build limpios.
- **E2E:** sin Docker, levanté el stack a mano. Pasan 83, incluido el caso nuevo de `/reuniones`. Fallan los 4 de `login-dev.spec.ts`, porque armé la web en modo producción y ahí no se monta el login de desarrollo. No tiene que ver con este cambio.
- **Seguridad:** `revisor-seguridad` y `security-auditor` no encontraron nada HIGH ni MEDIUM. Corregí dos hallazgos LOW: la baja filtra por dueño y el log de errores de Google lleva sólo el mensaje.

## Pendientes LOW sin tocar

- La llamada a Google corre dentro de la transacción de inscripción y de baja. Con Google lento y muchas inscripciones simultáneas, podrían agotarse las conexiones de la base.
- El nombre del tipo grupal entra al bloque del prompt sin `JSON.stringify`, igual que ya ocurre en `reglasDeAgenda`.

author: dskkato
body:
CDR decoding of large image and point-cloud payloads spends substantial time constructing Python byte lists. This PR moves message decoding to a Rust/PyO3 extension and defaults the MCAP factory's `uint8` arrays to `bytes`, preparing the package for release as 0.2.0.

## Changes

- Compile parsed schemas into reusable native decoding plans for primitives, arrays, nested structs, unions, and enum string mappings. Support plain CDR1 and plain XCDR2 in both byte orders.
- Validate encapsulation, payload bounds, and sequence lengths; fix zero-length fixed-array decoding.
- Add streaming MCAP benchmarks comparing the Python reference decoder, Rust list mode, and Rust bytes mode, with recorded measurements and decoded-value comparisons.
- Switch packaging to maturin. Add CI to build and test CPython 3.10+ abi3 wheels for Linux x86_64/aarch64, macOS Apple Silicon, and Windows x86_64, plus an sdist.
- Add tag-triggered PyPI Trusted Publishing after version validation and distribution tests.
- Bump Python/Rust package versions and the lockfile to 0.2.0, and document release notes and migration steps in `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Breaking changes and migration

- `Ros2DecodeFactory()` returns immutable `bytes` for non-enum `uint8[]` and `uint8[N]`, including nested fields and union members. Use `Ros2DecodeFactory(array_mode="list")` to preserve list mutation, list comparisons, and direct JSON serialization. Direct `MessageReader` usage still defaults to lists; the example CLI explicitly uses list mode.
- The native extension is required, with no automatic Python decoding fallback. Source installs require Rust and Cargo; pure Python wheels and PyPy are no longer supported.
- Malformed payloads raise `ValueError`, parameter-list and delimited encapsulations are rejected, and nesting is limited to 128 levels. Callers may need to adjust exception handling.

## Validation and performance

- Local test suite: **328 passed**. Version consistency and `git diff --check` passed.
- Recorded benchmarks validated all **22,202 messages** across the three decoder modes. Default bytes mode achieved **7.35x and 10.66x** end-to-end speedups on the two recordings.
- These measurements use local warm-cache runs. Most of the gain comes from avoiding byte-list allocation; compatible Rust list mode can be slower than the Python reference. Cross-platform wheel testing is configured in CI.

Four low findings from the #210 and #206 reviews. Each was verified on this
branch before being touched; none was already fixed.

**M1 (done) — `tests/serve_support.py` `free_port()`.** The pinning band is
`range(2048, ephemeral_start())`, so a box whose `ip_local_port_range` starts
at or below 2048 (a sysctl can do that) leaves it empty or tiny and every
pinned-port test raises `RuntimeError` instead of running. A band under 512
ports now falls back to the pre-#210 `bind(0)` pick, with a comment naming the
reopened race window. New test
`test_free_port_falls_back_when_there_is_no_room_to_pin` monkeypatches
`serve_support.ephemeral_start` to 2048 (band empty) and 1500 (band inverted)
and asserts the returned port still binds.

Sabotage: with the `if len(band) < 512:` block removed, that test fails with
`RuntimeError: no free loopback port to pin: nothing bound, nothing was free`
(serve_support.py:478); the block was restored and both `free_port` tests pass.

**M2 (done) — `tests/test_serve_cli.py` `_wait_for_file` docstring.** It said
"the first lines of stderr"; `dead_child()` uses
`(err or out or "").splitlines()[:3]`. The docstring now says the first three
lines of the child's output — stderr when it has any, stdout otherwise.
Docstring only.

**M3 (done) — `changelog.d/verb-named-reserved-key.breaking.md`.** The
sentence about a `body:` collision said it "silently dropped the link with a
clean exit" without saying which of the other collisions errored instead.

Steward 0.35.30. Part of the owner's ask that no staff member can lose data.

Ten stages cleared their work folder with `rmSync(dir, { recursive: true })` whenever its parent was the work root. `workRoot` is a setting, so if it pointed at a projects folder, a stage could delete a clone named like an employee. `clearWorkDir` (`src/stages/common.ts`) now does the clearing for all ten:

- a clone (`.git` a folder) never goes;
- a folder with no `.git` goes only in the Steward's own default work folder, where it's what a crash left.

Anything left in place makes the `worktree add` after it fail, and the stage says so.

author: gobidev
body:
Deleting a single occurrence of a recurring event in Google left it in the imported calendar: Google returns the deleted occurrence as a cancelled exception with no `start`/`end`, which the import skipped, so the RRULE kept generating it. The same timestamp check also missed modified occurrences, since editing one does not change the series' `updated`.

Cancelled occurrences now become `EXDATE`s on their series, and recurring events are regenerated on each sync and only written when the generated data changed. `EXDATE` is used rather than a cancelled override because clients render cancelled instances instead of hiding them.

Verified on 4.3.1 / Nextcloud 35 with a live calendar: deleted occurrences disappear (checked with sabre's recurrence expansion), modified occurrences propagate, and a second sync writes nothing. `php -l` passes.

author: dp-web4
body:
**What the rc found:** `v0.3.0-rc.1` (run 38289872894) passed every job and published all 17 assets as a pre-release. But it published under GitHub's draft placeholder name `untagged-d4c9c308d31f0db84ef6`, so looking it up by `v0.3.0-rc.1` returned nothing.
- **Cause:** GitHub keeps a draft under a placeholder until it's published, and `tools/release_publish.py`'s final PATCH flipped `draft=false` without sending `tag_name`.
- **Why the safeguard missed it:** the pre-publish check read the draft's `tag_name` and passed.
- **Why only a real tag could find it:** the dry run skips draft and publish.

**Live release:** fixed by hand with `PATCH tag_name=v0.3.0-rc.1`. It's now a pre-release on its tag with 17 assets, and `releases/latest` is still `v0.0.4`.

**Fix:**
- The publish PATCH sends `tag_name`.
- After publishing, `GET releases/tags/<tag>` must return this release. If it doesn't, the script re-binds once, then fails loudly with the manual command. A release can never end up silently untagged.

**Test:** the mocked `gh` now models GitHub's placeholder behaviour.
- **Case 13:** both a stable and an rc tag stay bound and are verified by the by-tag lookup.
- **Case 14:** if GitHub ignores `tag_name`, the script fails loudly.
- **Against the previous script:** 7 checks fail, reproducing the rc. All pass now.

Part of dp-web4/web4#904. Blocks tagging `v0.3.0`.

author: seantunley
body:
## What happened

On WhatsApp, asked to quote an existing customer, DAX replied:

> I can't set up the draft quote yet because Test Customer has a customer record but no lead. Once a lead is created, I can prepare the draft… Not in the CRM: I don't have a catalogue result here to verify the Rover XL product.

Sean: "Why is there a requirement to have a lead before a quote can be made? If any existing customer wants a new quote, it is not a new lead, its existing business."

He is right. The CRM has always allowed a quote for a customer with no lead (`createQuoteForContact`, `saveQuoteDraft`). The limit was in the `quote_build` task added in #872.

## The fix

**A quote is for a customer.**
- `quote_build` takes `contactId` (the customer, no deal) **or** `leadId` (one of their deals). A task naming neither proposes nothing.
- The card builder handles it before the lead checks: access to the deal or to the customer, `quotes.create`, and the customer must exist.
- Confirm: with a deal, it must still be that customer's; with none, the customer must still be there. Then the same save as before (`saveQuoteDraft`, which checks the person may quote that customer), still a **draft**, PDF still queued for the person who asked.
- Recorded on the deal when there is one, otherwise on the customer. The card links to the customer when there is no deal.

**DAX is told.** The rule now says a lead is not required, to quote with `contactId`, to ask which deal only when the customer has several open ones, and never to say a lead is needed. The lookup note for "a customer matches but there is no deal" — which mentioned only notes, and is the likely source of that reply — now says a quote can be made for the customer directly.

**The catalogue.** The planner's `knowledge` description and the rule now say to look the catalogue up for any quote, and never to say a product can't be verified without having looked. A line may name its product by catalogue **name** as well as id (`matchCatalogueProduct`): the same name ignoring case and spacing, or the only product whose name contains it. Two candidates, or none, is no match. The price is still only ever the catalogue's.

## Tested

- Gate: tsc 0, eslint 0 errors, unit 5825 pass / 2 fail (the two long-standing ones).
- `tests/assistantQuoteBuild.test.ts`: a customer with no lead parses and is wired through the builder, the run step, both audit entries and the card link; name matching (exact, unique-contains, ambiguous, absent, made-up id falling back to the name); a price still cannot ride on a line.

## Not tested

- **A live model.** Whether DAX now quotes the customer without asking for a lead, and looks the catalogue up first, needs a real conversation after deploy — the instructions and the server-side matching are tested, its replies are not.
- **A real run for the no-lead path.** The webhook walk-through used for #872 covers a quote on a lead; I have not re-run it for a customer with no lead.

author: 2shiraz
body:
Implements docs/design/interaction-polish.md §3 (PR #39) for the owner's request: "auto saving like termius where ever possible so it feels fast and modern". No IPC, contract or Rust change.

## What changes

**Host details panel** (`HostPanel.tsx`, `hostForm.tsx`, new `hostAutosave.ts`)
- Non-secret fields save **400 ms after the last change, or at once on blur / Enter / close**. That covers name, address, port, user, group, tags, protocol, sign-in choice, key, identity, encoding, terminal type, agent forwarding, and the non-secret parts of the jump host and proxy.
- **Per-field validation** (`fieldRules.ts` mirrors `crates/core/src/validate.rs`). An invalid field shows its error inline and keeps its stored value; the other fields still save.
- **Status in the header**: "Saving…", then "Saved" (fades; no fade with reduced motion), or "Couldn't save – **Retry**". The core's message shows in the panel body.
- **Undo** for 10 s per write, with Cmd/Ctrl+Z in the panel or "Undo" in the status. It writes the previous record back exactly, and steps back one write at a time. A text field with unsaved typing keeps the browser's own undo.
- **The route is one unit.** Jump host and proxy are written in one `host_connection_set`, only once every part is valid, in the existing order: before the basics for an existing host (a refused loop changes nothing else), right after creation for a new host.
- **New host**: created on the first valid address, named after it if the name is empty. Closing with nothing valid creates nothing. Values prefilled from discovery are a proposal: they are stored only after an edit or Connect.
- The primary button is always **Connect**. Save, Cancel, "Save and connect" and the unsaved-changes guard are removed.

**Secrets never autosave** (`LiveSecret.tsx`)
- Host password and proxy password get a **Set password** / **Set proxy password** button; Enter in the field also sets it. The value is written once and the field is cleared after the attempt, as before. Secrets are never in the autosave key or a draft.
- Leaving the panel, switching host or connecting with a typed but unset secret asks **"Discard the password you typed?"**, with Keep editing as the default.
- A change that would **drop a stored secret** isn't autosaved, because undo couldn't bring the secret back. That covers switching away from a stored password, switching to Telnet/serial, removing the proxy, or changing the proxy user. The change waits for an explicit "Remove stored password" / "Remove proxy password".

**Group editor** (`GroupEditor.tsx`, `GroupDefaultsSection.tsx`) works the same way:
- per-field validation;
- the group is created on its first valid name;
- the route defaults are one unit, written before the basics;
- undo, and the proxy password set on purpose;
- a "Done" button that writes anything still waiting before it closes.

**Environment dialog**: variables and startup snippets autosave. Each list is saved as one unit once all of it is valid (an invalid name is flagged inline and never sent), with undo and a "Done" button. The "Environment saved" toast is gone because the status replaces it.

**Settings**: nothing to change. Every setting already applies on change. Only the passphrase change, recovery key, quick unlock, backup restore, trust decisions and deletes stay explicit.

**Not changed on purpose**: the quick-connect `HostEditor` dialog (Home and Known hosts) keeps its explicit Save. It only creates a host from prefilled values, so autosaving would create one as soon as it opened. Bulk dialogs, Set OS and the identity dialog are explicit actions and are unchanged.

## Tests (negative ones first)
`tests/ui/host-panel.spec.ts` (rewritten, 18 tests) and the new `tests/ui/group-editor.spec.ts` (5 tests):
- **autosave never sends a secret**: no write carries the typed password until Set password or Enter, which sends it exactly once; later autosaves send `password: null`; the page never holds a copy.
- **an invalid field is never stored**: an invalid port, address, user name or group name keeps its stored value; the valid fields around it save.
- **undo restores the record exactly**: three writes undone one by one, then `toEqual` against the original mock record; also via the status button; a 10 s expiry check on a fake clock.
- **the route is saved in order, never half-saved**: no write while the proxy has no host; then one write with every part, before `host_save` (existing host) or after it (new host); a refused loop stores nothing from that batch.
- **a new host is not created from an invalid address**: four invalid forms produce no `host_save`; closing creates nothing; a valid address creates exactly one host.
- **debounce**: typing coalesces into one write after the delay, and blur writes at once.
- plus a failed write followed by Retry, the held stored-password removal, the discard prompt, and close-flushes-pending.

Updated for autosave: `environment`, `group-defaults`, `startup`, `protocols`, `tunnels`, `inventory` and `discovery` specs, and `tests/native/flows.mjs` and `startup.test.mjs`. The native flow now waits on the panel's `data-autosave="clean"` instead of clicking Save. The mock gained `__mockFailNext` to inject one failure.

- **After**: a single primary **Connect** (enabled once the host exists). The address hint reads "Enter an address to save this host. Everything you change is saved as you go." and the name hint reads "Defaults to the address." The header shows "Saving…" / "Saved" / "Undo" while you edit. See the diff of `tests/ui/__screenshots__/dark-08-host-editor.png`.
