author: albmalamd
body:
Cherry-pick of pytorch/pytorch#200673

## Linked issue or supporting maintainer

Fixes #194679
Fixes #200326

## BC-breaking?

No

## Summary (human written only)

This changes fixes several hangs and timeouts with the same root cause. Since NCCL 2.31, a graceful communicator teardown (`ncclCommFinalize`/`ncclCommDestroy`) waits in a barrier for all of the communicator's ranks on node. Only an aborted communicator skips it. Three places in c10d don't account for that:

- `ProcessGroupNCCL::shutdown()` finalizes a group's communicators one at a time. Each rank goes through them in its own order, so with lazily created P2P communicators, or one communicator per device, ranks wait on each other forever.
- `shrink_group(SHRINK_ABORT)` destroys the original group gracefully, while the excluded ranks abort it (#194679).
- The nccl2 timeout tests abort on the timed-out rank but destroy gracefully on the others (#200326).

This PR finalizes all of a group's communicators in a single NCCL group, aborts the original group when shrinking with `SHRINK_ABORT`, and has the tests abort timed-out subgroups on every rank.

## Agent details (if applicable)

> Authored with assistance from an AI coding assistant (Cursor).
>
> **Root cause.** NCCL 2.31 added a barrier among a communicator's host-local
> ranks to graceful teardown (`bootstrapIntraNodeBarrier` in `commDestroySync`,
> reached from `ncclCommFinalize`, or from `ncclCommDestroy` without a prior
> finalize). Only aborted communicators skip it. RCCL 2.32 has the same code.
> Graceful teardown is therefore a collective over each communicator's ranks,
> and three places in c10d break that. The commits are independent; review in
> order:
>
> 1. `ProcessGroupNCCL::shutdown()` finalizes a group's communicators one at a
>    time, in `unordered_map` order. Ranks hold different communicators (lazily
>    created 2-rank P2P comms, one comm per device for multi-device modules) and
>    deadlock waiting in each other's barrier. Finalize them inside one
>    `ncclGroupStart/End`, as `abortCommsFromMap()` already does for abort.
> 2. `shrink_group(SHRINK_ABORT)` destroys the original group gracefully while
>    the excluded ranks abort it (#194679). Abort it instead.
>    `test_shrink_group_vs_abort_reinit_performance`'s excluded rank destroyed
>    gracefully against an abort-mode shrink, so it now aborts too. Behavior
>    note: with `SHRINK_ABORT`, an excluded rank that is still alive must abort
>    (or simply exit), not destroy, the original group.
> 3. nccl2 timeout tests: rank 0 aborts the timed-out communicator while the
>    other ranks destroy theirs gracefully (#200326). Abort the subgroup on every
>    rank in the 5 affected tests.
>
> **Validation.** Source builds of this branch (main @ `ab41098008a`; the
> rebased commits are identical) for gfx942, 8x MI300X, RCCL 2.32.3, with each
> commit reverted vs. applied:
>
> | Test | Without | With |
> |---|---|---|
> | `test_send_recv_nccl` (+ 2 profiler variants) | 300 s join timeout | pass (75 s total) |
> | `test_nccl_backend_4gpu_module` | 300 s join timeout | pass (42 s) |
> | `test_shrink_group_flags` | 300 s timeout | pass; all 10 `test_shrink*` pass (70 s) |
> | nccl2 timeout tests (5), `RCCL_DDA_ENABLE=0` | hang (killed at 420 s) | 5/5 pass (53 s) |
>
> ```
> cd test
> TEMP_DIR=$T BACKEND=nccl WORLD_SIZE=8 python -m pytest distributed/test_distributed_spawn.py -v -s -k test_send_recv_nccl
> python -m pytest distributed/test_c10d_nccl.py -v -s -k "test_nccl_backend_4gpu_module or (ProcessGroupNCCLGroupTest and test_shrink)"
> RCCL_DDA_ENABLE=0 python -m pytest distributed/test_c10d_nccl2.py -v -s --timeout 240 -k "WatchdogNoTearDownTest or BlockingWaitTest or DumpOnTimeoutTest or DumpTimeoutBoundTest"
> ```
>
> `RCCL_DDA_ENABLE=0` only keeps a separate RCCL bug out of the measurement:
> RCCL's DDA-IPC allreduce ignores the abort flag, so the timed-out rank's
> `ncclCommAbort` doesn't return (reported to the RCCL team). An RCCL-only
> reproducer confirms commit 1's mechanism: two ranks finalizing two
> communicators in opposite orders hang, and the same calls inside
> `ncclGroupStart/End` complete.
>
> **Not covered:** no CUDA run here (the linked issues show the CUDA side with
> NCCL 2.31/2.32). `spin fixlint` was not run in the agent's environment.

author: schlessera
body:
## What changed

Closes #1662. Closes #1653. Closes #1664. Closes #1654.

Users can review a proposed governance-policy change in the existing approval card, inspect its exact diff and approve one validated write. The same policy cache supplies read-only facts in Devices & agents. The existing turn disclosure now supports retained-version review, per-file or whole-turn revert and Undo, with durable receipts and conflicts preserved. Visible outward commands use per-use approvals and retain irreversible admission receipts in that disclosure.

Worker notes describe the actual admitted profile, protected paths, journal and available user recovery. Both first-party adapters receive the same resolved facts; agents do not gain revert authority. Voice remains read-only where approved.

## Why this shape

These features complete the reviewed policy/history flow on top of the merged governed journal, profile preference and command policy. They share the existing approval cards, authenticated session ownership, journal storage and dialogs. Consolidating #1750 and #1751 here avoids replaying their shared prerequisites after each squash.

Policy publication revalidates authority, schema, exact starting bytes and anchored path identity immediately before its privileged write. Revert queues behind active turns, compares raw current state and restores only eligible retained versions; later changes remain conflicts. Interrupted or partial operations report their actual state. Receipts reconcile a lost response without repeating the write. Neither operation relies on evaluating repository Git or configuration on the host.

Outward approvals cover visible Git pushes, the fixed GitHub-write inventory and curl/wget non-GET or data requests. Policy allowances require both command and known destination; force/history rewrites still ask. Named Git destinations resolve only through credential-free isolated maintenance. Receipts describe admission, not external completion. Opaque scripts and unavailable egress-proxy coverage remain explicitly stated.

Migration044/046, additive SDK/HTTP/wire contracts, API reports, minor changesets and moved citations are included. The storage budget and all approved permission, placement and interaction decisions remain unchanged.

## Proof

Candidate `e8cf6d1e18bac88295e6fb634e558c8f6c944447` builds on merged main `52cbd1db182b618706cd7edca72159ba62768a63`; tree `054fb1a0f7e07791134a480c68fcef33deba4464`. Final combined preflight passes 843 tests / 5356 assertions, including types, build, lint/leakage and contract checks. Original component receipts remain in #1750/#1751 and the issue histories; they are not represented as full CI of this combined candidate.

- Policy service, wire roster and both MCP adapters: 39 tests / 247 assertions. Actual mounted HTTP inventory: 88 / 596. Anchored native publication: 19 / 572; original pinned browser: 15 cases. Semantic stale-input and voice-membership mutations fail and restore correctly. Collaborative preview reviewed a real narrow-screen approval, diff focus/return, single write, governance receipt and read-only enforcing facts.
- Revert integration with policy writer, raw file operations, writer gate and HTTP authorization: 110 tests / 693 assertions. Semantic stale-state, selection identity and queued-writer mutations fail correctly. Original browser proof: 13 / 135.
- Outward classifier and actual first-party effect gates: 44 / 166; command-policy compatibility: 64 / 214. Dropping force classification allows a declined fake Git effect and fails three assertions; restored source passes. Removing the outward history section fails its named visibility assertion.
- Host capability notes: four semantic mutations cover admitted history facts, exact protected-path resolution and both adapters' actual prompt/init injection. Original restored proof: 28 / 201 plus strict snapshot.
- Combined runtime integration: 67 passing cases plus two diagnosed note-expectation failures, corrected to include the new outward note; restored exact notes/host facts/outward history pass 6 / 64. Combined offline, non-root pinned Chromium journal/revert/outward flow passes all 13 cases / 175 assertions across live/replayed history, 320/1280px, both themes, focus, lost replies, conflicts, Undo and voice/session exclusions.
- Full component CI exposed an old overlay fixture returning generic successful JSON for the new policy endpoint. Providing valid policy facts restores all 405 cases across three real pointer modes without weakening assertions. The same full run exposed eager policy-root resolution breaking supported startup before a brain is provisioned, missing public bridge-tool conformance coverage, and older device/root-ownership fixtures. The fix tolerates only startup ENOENT, never creates a root and still resolves/validates before proposal approval. Its named mutation fails on eager startup resolution. Restored policy/SDK proof: 21 / 206; actual app/socket proof: 102 / 390; full render suite: 275 / 1730. Final combined policy/SDK/host-note checks: 25 / 255. Both old component runs remain failure evidence; the new combined candidate requires all selected hosted jobs.

- Combined hosted run [38310348385](https://github.com/schlessera/brain-kit/actions/runs/38310348385) exposed a typed conformance-fixture mismatch and five older no-grant activity expectations that omitted the newly recorded outward classification. The expected proposal is now validated through its published schema; activity assertions now include the exact classification and still require the original denial, absent approval card and absent tool effect. Restored conformance: 8 tests / 128 assertions. Two corresponding voice activity expectations and the legacy empty-list force-push expectation were also corrected. The latter now proves an empty legacy list leaves local commands unconfirmed while force pushes still require approval. Restored actual Claude/Pi outward gates, no-grant, voice and legacy cases: 82 tests / 331 assertions across five files. These are fixture corrections; no production gate or classifier was weakened.

## Checklist

- [x] Existing approved policy authority, storage and interaction decisions preserved.
- [x] Meaningful mutation receipts and actual worker/browser proof retained.
- [x] Contracts, API reports, minor changesets and moved citations integrated.
- [x] Final combined preflight passes.
- [x] Complete selected hosted proof passes on the current combined candidate.
- [x] Current head, tested checkout/tree and milestone0.42.0 read back before merge.

All 14 jobs in [selected PR CI](https://github.com/schlessera/brain-kit/actions/runs/38312928259) passed; every actual checkout was `292a293409a944c6ffdb6cdca5ef36d3abfd7684`, with the recorded main/head parents and tree. Steering classification, stale native writes, budgets and scope limits remain with their owning programme issues. #1749 records minor policy-staging journal noise and does not block the main flow. body:

_Requested by **Jonas** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_011TEXuoN8Tq2jXh9kGkT8ir?thread=cmsg_011TEXuoN8Tq2jXh9kGkT8ir95aqTpCkCSFbGNgCeuT2Lq)_

Before: Spelledaren startade låtar och såg poängen men kunde inte gissa själv. Under spelet visade spelledaren en egen ruta med en stor nedräkning och rätt svar. Tiden per låt gick att välja, och nästa låt startade bara med ett klick.

After: Spelledaren anger sitt namn först när spelet skapas och spelar alltid med. Spelledarvyn ser ut och beter sig som spelarvyn, med samma väntetext, gissningsruta med förslagslista, egna svar, poäng och rad i poänglistan. Under spelvyn finns en panel med allt som bara spelledaren har: Nästa låt, Spela klippet, Visa svar nu, Ny match, Inställningar, Avsluta och en soptunna som markerar låten som okänd. QR-koden har kvar sin egen ruta, och Kod och Utseende står längst ner som hos spelarna.

Tiden är alltid 30 sekunder och går inte längre att ändra. När klippet spelas i sidan (Deezer) startar nästa låt av sig själv 30 sekunder efter att svaret visats, om spelledaren inte redan har tryckt. Med Spotify behövs fortfarande ett klick, eftersom appen bara kan öppnas från ett klick. Länkarna längst ner fördelas jämnt över bredden, och Om spelet finns bara kvar på förstasidan.

Spelledaren räknas som en vanlig spelare: svaret visas när alla, även spelledaren, har svarat i båda fälten, och spelledaren kan vinna. Med Spotify syns låtens titel i Spotify-appen, vilket ägaren känner till och har godtagit.

How: Visningen från `play.js` är flyttad till den nya modulen `js/spelvy.js`, som visar en `playerView` och används av både spelare och spelledare. Spelledarens svar går direkt till `game.submitAnswer` med ett eget spelar-id (`state.hostId`), och ett sparat spel utan spelledare får en när det återupptas. Panelens innehåll byggs bara om när det ändras, så att fokus stannar kvar, och nedräkningen till nästa låt uppdateras av tickern. `ROUND_MS` är 30 000 och det enda valet. Bonus kan vara 0, 10, 15 eller 20 sekunder, eftersom 30 sekunder vore lika med hela tiden. Soptunnan är en knapp med `aria-pressed` och en text för skärmläsare. `axe.mjs` fyller i spelledarens namn och kontrollerar även spelledarens förslagslista.

### Kontroller (lokalt)
- `npm test`: 43 godkända (tiderna i testerna ändrade till 30 sekunder)
- HTML (vnu): inga fel
- axe, WCAG 2.2 AA: inga brister i någon vy, ljust och mörkt, även spelledarens förslagslista och panelen när svaret visas
- Automatisk nästa låt provad i webbläsaren med ett ljudklipp i stället för Deezer: nästa låt startade efter 30 sekunder
- Lighthouse mobil, länkkontroll och sidvikt körda på den första versionen av PR:en: index 100, host 99, play 95 i prestanda, alla länkar OK, host 112 kB och play 238 kB med gzip

author: nasyrov
body:
## Summary

```diff
 firstUnblockedUnassignedTicket
-  skip a ticket while a sibling under the same parent is in flight

 confirmRepairingWhatIsRefused
-  any refusal → repair, 2 per pull request
+  conflicts with main → rebase, 5 per pull request
+  anything else       → repair, 2 per pull request
```

#3090's one-ticket-per-parent rule left two of three lanes idle on 2026-10-12. Every unblocked ready ticket was a child of #3035 (#3052, #3056, #3059–#3062), and its sibling #3053 was in flight.

The rule was aimed at the wrong cost. On 2026-10-11, 16 conflict resolutions cost $10 in total. What parked #3084 was conflict-only refusals spending the two repairs while its siblings kept landing. Conflicts now get their own budget of five rebases, so siblings can run in parallel again.

## Evidence

- **Before:** on `origin/main`, these fail:
  - `runShipLoop` › "a branch that keeps conflicting as siblings land is rebased without spending its repairs": three conflict refusals then two red CIs park the ticket, where it should merge.
  - `runShipLoop` › "a branch still conflicting after every rebase is parked": it parks after 2 attempts, not `REBASES_A_PULL_REQUEST_GETS`.

  **After:** both pass. `npx vitest run` in `.sandcastle` gives 289 passed: three sibling-rule tests removed with the rule, two added. `tsc --noEmit`, prettier and commitlint are clean.
- Selection matches its pre-#3090 state apart from #3091's retry (`git diff 1e5a3913c~1 -- .sandcastle/lib/github.ts .sandcastle/lib/in-flight.ts`).

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

`.sandcastle` only.

**Blast Radius:** loop throughput

- Siblings conflict again, and each conflict costs a cheap rebase phase (about $0.64 on average on 2026-10-11).
- A branch can be rebased up to five times before it parks.

body:
Projects had no way to read their logs in Grafana. Everyone outside `webservices-infra` is a Viewer, Viewers cannot open Explore, and no dashboard had a logs panel. The docs said they could, through Explore.

In Grafana 13.1.1, `fixed:datasources:explorer` is granted to Editor, and to Viewer only with `viewers_can_edit`, which we don't set (`pkg/api/accesscontrol.go`). Viewers can still query datasources, which is what dashboards use, so the data was reachable but there was nothing to read it with.

## Changes

- **`dashboards/logs.json`** (+ generated `dashboards-cm/logs.yaml`): a shared "Logs" dashboard.
  - Variables: namespace, container, pod and a case-insensitive text search. The search is regex-escaped with `${search:regex}` in a backtick string, so typed text matches as it is.
  - Panels: lines per container, the log lines, and the namespace's Kubernetes events (Alloy's eventhandler stream).
- **`onboarding.md`**: a new "Logs" section for project developers: what is collected, the labels, 31-day retention, short Jobs, using the dashboard, building their own logs panel, and who else can read their logs.
- **Corrections**: the Explore claim in `onboarding.md` (Grafana) and `decisions.md` entry 29.
- **Pointers**: a row in the `dashboards/README.md` table and in `docs/README.md`.

This makes another namespace's logs one dropdown pick away, but grants no new access: Viewers could already query Loki for any namespace. Separating the logs per project is #68.

## Verified

- Every dashboard query run against the live Loki with variables filled in: the three variable queries, the volume and logs queries with an empty search, a word, and text containing regex characters, and the events query. Events don't leak into the logs panel.
- All six CI checks pass locally.

## After merge

ArgoCD only deploys from `main`, so the dashboard can't be previewed first. Someone who is a **Viewer** (not in `webservices-infra`) should open *Dashboards → Logs* once, pick a project namespace and see lines.

author: luhe19001
body:
## Problem

A Hub outage could leave `hubFailureActive` false or omitted for several minutes, so Local never showed the warning panel. The policy wait loop retried failed contacts once per second, while other check-in paths could continue polling independently.

## Root cause and change

The warning threshold used the Hub's advertised idle cadence, which can be 15 minutes, and the wait loop used a fixed one-second delay after errors. The change reports `hubFailureActive` as an explicit boolean, activates the warning after one minute, and applies jittered exponential backoff from 2 seconds to 60 seconds to retryable Hub transport and availability failures. It honors delta-seconds and HTTP-date `Retry-After` values, suppresses redundant wait and progress requests during a failure streak, and gives the Retry now button and `coslash status --retry` a one-time backoff bypass. The frontend regression test decodes a real sync-status response and verifies the warning panel.

## Tests

- `go test ./cmd/coslash ./internal/syncv4 ./internal/hubclient` passed.
- Frontend lint and `format:check` passed; lint reports one existing purity warning.
- Frontend tests passed: 42 files, 316 tests. The required shared dependency link lacked `jsdom` and `axe-core`, so verification used the existing local package copies as read-only fallbacks.
- Frontend build passed with a temporary type-path mapping to the installed `axe-core` declarations; the configuration was restored afterward.

Fixes Tier5 issue 081

## What changed

- **SPEC.md**:
  - §4 line-name rule replaced with the owner's #59 wording.
  - §5.6 basis definitions now point to `reference/ACCOUNTING_RULES.md` (the old reference, `accounting-views-spec.md`, isn't in the repo).
  - The adopted departures below are recorded in §4, §5.6 and §8 (owner, #61). §4 also says a mixed line's mandatory portion is read at the lead stage.
  - §9: the three accounting rows ("Amount basis, timing", the Account type row, "Defense portion column") read "ready (UI-0 #57, built in UI-3 #61)". New rows: Exclude earmarks and Nondefense, "hidden until UI-0b (views_excluding_earmarks, nondefense)".
- **Filter › Advanced** (shown only when `accounting_views` is on):
  - Amount basis has five options (`amt=`). Each definition follows ACCOUNTING_RULES as `accounting.BASES` applies it.
  - "Advance appropriations count" has two options, When available and When enacted (`timing=`).
  - The summary line reads "<basis> · advances when <timing> · earmarks included".
- **Account type** (All · Discretionary · Mandatory · Mixed, `type=`, gated by `budget_class`) sits between Agency and Status.
- Every non-default choice is a chip and counts in the badge. Reset and Clear all restore the defaults.
- **Cells under a basis other than As printed**:
  - checked or computed: the published view amount
  - excluded: `excl.`
  - not computable: `n/a` for an account, `not checked` for a total, with the published reason on hover
  - Each of these cells is a button to its source.
  - Only checked or computed amounts feed a difference. The lead stage, the account panel and the enacted-history years stay on printed figures.
- **Units-and-basis label** follows the basis and its timing.
- **Overview**: a total shows only where the data marks it checked; otherwise it reads "not checked (n accounts)".
- **Figure-source panel under a basis** shows the view, the printed headline, each component (type, amount, document · page) and the arithmetic. The arithmetic lists the printed figure and the components the view used, then "=" the published amount. The page adds nothing up.
- **Class tags** (owner rule, #61):
  - A line gets "incl. mandatory" when its class is mandatory, or mixed with a `mandatory_portion` tagged at the lead stage.
  - An agency gets the tag when it holds such a line. FY2026: HRSA, CDC, CMS, ACF, OS.
  - The hover names each line behind the tag and its mandatory amount.
  - Mandatory lines sit under "Appropriated mandatory" in their agency.
  - A provisional class has a dashed outline.
- **View › Columns › Defense portion** (`cols=defense`, gated by `defense_split`): the lead stage's `defense_portion` where one is tagged, empty otherwise.
- **Flags**: `exclude_earmarks` and `nondefense` are new flags in `web/ui_contract.json` (contract_version 3). Both are false until UI-0b publishes their data. Nothing is built for them, and they aren't in `BUILT`.
- `docs/` was regenerated with `export_static.py`. `docs/Approps_Pilot_Schema_Loaded.xlsx` is untouched.

### Tests (tests/test_compare.py)
- New `AmountBasis` class:
  - every basis × timing on Medicaid (advances), the NIH Innovation Account (CURES, designated), SAMHSA HSPS (earmark), CMS Program Management (mixed, no tag) and the title total, with FY2025 as the CR year; static and live
  - source-panel arithmetic
  - overview totals
  - Account type, tags (the five agencies, their hovers), the sub-group
  - the defense column
  - URL round-trip of every option
- Test 12 forces all five flags false through a fixture. `exclude_earmarks` and `nondefense` show no control either way.
- The full page suite passed locally: 133 passed (test_web, test_compare, test_static).

### Screenshots (`screenshots/explore-v1-ui3/`, Ours · Design reference)
- `04-filter-panel-side-by-side.png`: Advanced open, NIH chip
- `02-figure-source-all-appropriations-side-by-side.png`: Medicaid under All appropriations
- `03-account-panel-class-tags-side-by-side.png`: CMS expanded with the Appropriated mandatory sub-group

## Departures from SPEC.md
None open. These were adopted by the owner (#61) and are recorded in SPEC.md:
1. Exclude earmarks is hidden behind `exclude_earmarks`. Nondefense is hidden behind `nondefense`, so the column shows the defense portion only.
2. Basis definitions follow ACCOUNTING_RULES. Program level adds no fees and no transfers out (owner decision on #57).
3. `excl.`, `n/a` and `not checked` are new cell tokens under a non-printed basis, explained in a legend line.
4. The units-and-basis label adds "· advances when <timing>" under a non-printed basis.
5. A provisional class has a dashed tag outline, with a legend item.
6. FY2026 shows "incl. mandatory" on HRSA, CDC, CMS, ACF and OS under the owner's tag rule. The mockup's CMS/ACF-only came before the class data.

## Fields the data doesn't have yet (UI-0b)
- `rows[].cells.*.views_excluding_earmarks.<basis>` (proposed path)
- `rows[].cells.*.nondefense` (proposed path)

## Checks on 115f995 (read from GitHub)
changes ✅ · data ✅ · browser ✅ · test ✅

author: derrynknife
body:
Updating per-item records as items age.

Records are updated as items age. Each update returns a new, checked
record (built through the constructor, so every check applies) and
leaves the old one as it was, so data already built from it cannot
change underneath.

Both records: clone(new_id, **changes) (the same record for another
item, any argument replaced), extend(age) (seen working up to a later
age) and update_covariates(age, values) (time-varying covariates take
values from age on: a step added to the schedule; a CovariatePath or a
cyclic schedule is replaced whole with clone).

ItemLifetime, while still running (right censored): fail(age,
event_type) and found_failed(age, event_type) -- found failed at an
inspection, so failed between when it was last seen working and age.

ItemHistory: add_failure(age, event_type), add_failures_between(lower,
upper, failures, event_type), change_state(age, state) and
change_state_between(lower, upper, state); an event after the end of
observation moves the end to it (it was watched until then).

author: xiehuanyi
body: Pattern matching examines all own keys with `Reflect.ownKeys`, while selection discovery uses `Object.values`. Selections under symbol or non-enumerable keys are therefore missing from optional/union handler arguments. In particular, an omitted optional pattern with a symbol-key anonymous selection returns the original input object instead of the declared `undefined` selection. Use the same own-key traversal for selection discovery. Add runtime regressions with handler type assertions for named and anonymous symbol-key selections, an alternate union branch, and non-enumerable own keys. Validation: - Against unchanged helper source, all 4 new regressions fail. - `npm test -- --runInBand`: 48 suites, 457 tests passed. - `npm run check` and `npm run perf`: source and full test type checks pass. - `git diff --check`: pass. - Package building has a local baseline Babel/TypeScript transformation failure reproduced at the unchanged upstream head; no successful package build is claimed. Discovery and implementation: automated OpenAI `gpt-6.1-sol` source review, xhigh reasoning, with the local tests above. --- ## Summary by cubic Fix selection discovery so optional and union patterns find selections under symbol and non-enumerable own keys. Pattern matching already resolves patterns through `Reflect.ownKeys`, but selection discovery walked `Object.values`, dropping selections under symbol keys and non-enumerable keys. As a result, an omitted optional pattern with a symbol-key anonymous selection returned the original input object instead of the declared `undefined`. - Switch `getSelectionKeys` to `Reflect.ownKeys` traversal. - Add regressions for named and anonymous symbol-key selections, an alternate union branch, and non-enumerable own keys. Written for commit 51149ea8737a2546ceeea0ca461a6589756a74e1. Summary will update on new commits. Getter-backed subpatterns are read to discover their selection names. `Object.values` already reads enumerable getters; the new traversal extends the same behavior to symbol and non-enumerable own keys, consistent with ordinary object matching. Reading descriptor `.value` would skip accessor-backed patterns and drop valid selections, including existing enumerable getter patterns. A separate 20-case public matcher comparison passes at this head; the suggested descriptor traversal fails 14 cases, including a typed enumerable getter pattern.

author: lacker
body:
Cleanup batch C. This continues the `term_shape` conversion (the shared operator splits `as_binary`, `as_unary` and `as_bitvector_comparison`). Net −505 lines across 14 files.

There is no behavior change. Every converted function still accepts exactly the operators it accepted before; where a function accepted only some operators, that set is now an explicit filter.

## Changes
- **Equality rewriting:** `rewrite_atomic_proposition_by_exact_equality` had 24 comparison arms, each rebuilding the same raw node over rewritten operands. They are now one `as_bitvector_comparison()` / `build_raw` step. The two smaller comparison blocks elsewhere in that file accept only some comparisons, so I left them alone.
- **`fold_arithmetic` (constant classes):** folds any 32-bit word operator through `as_binary()` and `BitvectorBinaryOp::build`. It used to have 13 arms, one per smart constructor.
- **`signed_arithmetic`:**
  - Drops its own 11-variant copy of the operator enum (`SignedArithmeticBinaryOperator`) and uses `BitvectorBinaryOp`. The accepted operators keep their relative order in the new enum, so the derived ordering of atoms is unchanged.
  - The signed fragment (32-bit word operators except unsigned divide and remainder) is now one `signed_binary` filter.
  - The native 64-bit path still accepts only UInt64 add, subtract, multiply, divide and remainder.
- **Pairwise structural equality:** five functions now compare two binary terms through `as_binary()`, each keeping its own accepted-operator filter:
  - `signed_surface_terms_equal`
  - `bitvector_equal`
  - `bitvector_terms_equal_for_transport_uncached`
  - `match_quantified_int32_term`
  - `bounded_term_equal`
- **Pointer-offset walkers:**
  - `PointerOffsetTerm` gains `for_each_scaled_value` and `any_scaled_value`. They walk left to right without allocating.
  - Seven walkers that only recursed through `+` down to each scaled index now use them.
  - Walkers that stop early on an exhausted work budget, or treat `Variable` offsets specially, keep their own code.
- **Recursive walkers:** four functions now recurse into every binary or unary term through one fallback arm, keeping the same left-then-right order:
  - `bitvector_has_memory`
  - `term_mentions_a_memory_load`
  - `collect_bitvector_memories`
  - `collect_bitvector_memory_load_keys`

## Validation
- `scripts/check.sh` exited 0 on this change based on master with #792 merged: 6,129 lib tests plus the fixture suites.
- #795 has merged since then. It touches none of these files, and the branch merges cleanly with current master.

author: larrygao001
body:
Fixes: N/A

### What was the problem/requirement? (What/Why)

botocore 1.43.112 added the `ListMemberships` operation to the Deadline Cloud service model. Because of that, `test_bundled_models_match_installed_botocore` now fails on every PR whose CI installs the latest botocore (for example #1400 and #1401): the bundled model differs in `paginators-1.json` and `service-2.json.gz`.

### What was the solution? (How)

I ran `scripts/update_bundled_service_models.py` with botocore 1.43.112. Changes:
- `service-2.json.gz`: adds `ListMemberships`, plus the shapes `ListMembershipsRequest`, `ListMembershipsResponse`, `MembershipResourceType`, `MembershipResourceTypes`, `MembershipSummaries` and `MembershipSummary`. No existing operations or shapes changed.
- `paginators-1.json`: adds the `ListMemberships` paginator.
- `BOTOCORE_VERSION`: updated to `1.43.112`.

The script also rewrote `endpoint-rule-set-1.json.gz`, but its decompressed content is identical; only the gzip header changed. I reverted that file to keep the diff minimal.

### What is the impact of this change?

PR CI passes again, and Python 3.9 users get the `ListMemberships` API through the bundled model.

### How was this change tested?

body:
## Related issue
Closes #2082

## Summary
`run_all_analyses()` ran `ancestry` 17th, but `cancer` (1st), `apol1` (8th), `gout` (9th), `nutrigenomics` (14th) and `traits` (15th) all read the stored ancestry call while scoring. So on a sample's first full run they read nothing. The cancer PRS cards then stored "Ancestry inference has not been run" while the Ancestry page showed a result. The same empty read also left those PRS uncalibrated, because `prs_calibration.get_ancestry_fractions` reads the same stored finding.

The same ordering affected more than the cancer card. On a first run, APOL1's `ancestry_gate` (`required_ancestry: AFR`, `min_fraction: 0.5`) always saw `None`. It therefore added the extra-validation caveat and dropped indeterminate disclosures even for AFR-ancestry samples. Gout fell back to its `default` odds ratios instead of the ancestry-specific ones.

The fix moves `ancestry` to the front of `run_all._get_modules()`. `run_ancestry_inference` reads only `annotated_variants` and the bundled PCA panel, never another module's findings, so it has no upstream dependency to break. Modules that already ran after it (allergy, gene_health, imputed_variants) are unaffected.

The regression guard is `tests/backend/annotation_validation/test_run_all_ancestry_order_live.py`. It drives the live `run_annotation` → `run_all_analyses` path and instruments `ancestry._get_latest_ancestry_finding`, the one helper behind `get_inferred_ancestry`, `get_top_ancestry_fraction` and `get_ancestry_fractions`. It asserts that no module reads ancestry before `ancestry` has run, and that every read sees a stored call. A future ancestry consumer placed too early therefore fails without a hand-kept list. It also checks the user-visible symptom: the cancer PRS caveat must be the UNCERTAIN wording, not "has not been run".

`docs/develop/architecture.md` now states the ordering constraint for module authors.

Samples already analysed keep their stored caveat until they are re-annotated or the cancer module is re-run. This PR does not add a reanalysis trigger; the general per-module reanalysis lifecycle is tracked in #2304.

body:
## Summary
This PR adds player elimination mechanics and game-over detection to the Twister game. Players can now be marked as eliminated (when they fall or touch the ground with forbidden body parts), and the game detects when only one player remains, displaying a winner announcement with confetti.

## Key Changes

- **Player Elimination System**: Added `eliminated` array to track eliminated players. Players can be toggled as eliminated by clicking their name chip, with visual feedback (strikethrough, grayscale, reduced opacity).

- **Air Zone Feature**: Introduced a new "Ar" (Air) color that represents body parts lifted off the ground. Added `airData` array to track members in the air, displayed in a dedicated air zone above the mat with visual styling.

- **Game-Over Detection**: Implemented `isGameOver()` function that triggers when only one or zero active players remain. Displays a winner announcement with trophy emoji and triggers confetti animation.

- **Active Player Rotation**: Modified player turn logic to skip eliminated players using `nextActivePlayer()` function, ensuring only active players get turns.

- **UI Enhancements**:
  - Added player hint text explaining how to eliminate players
  - Player chips now show elimination status with ❌ icon
  - Mat legend items show visual indication of eliminated players
  - Spin button hides when game is over or auto-spin is enabled
  - Winner display with animated pop-in effect

- **Game State Management**: 
  - Auto-spin timer respects game-over state
  - Spin button disabled when game is over
  - Current player display shows "Fim de jogo" when game ends
  - Eliminated players' mat cells and air items show reduced opacity

## Implementation Details

- Eliminated players remain visible on the mat and in the legend but with visual distinction (grayscale filter, reduced opacity)
- Air zone displays all members currently lifted, with the latest addition highlighted with pop-in animation
- Winner announcement only shows when exactly one active player remains
- Elimination can be toggled on/off by clicking player chips (with confirmation dialog)
- All mat rendering updates to reflect eliminated player status

author: dallison
body:
## Problem

On the POSIX shared-memory backend (macOS, QNX), `CreatePosixBuffer` first creates `/tmp/subspace_<session>_<channel>_<n>` and ftruncates it to the full buffer size, then creates the real shm object at the same size. The comment assumed the shadow "will not actually allocate any disk space", but on QNX `/tmp` is `/dev/shmem`, so the shadow commits RAM.

Measured on QNX (c4_1m): model data buffers 32.01 MiB, measured shm 64.01 MiB (exactly 2.000×). All 8 copy scenarios matched `2 × N × (size + 192)` within 0.001 MiB, and a 64 MiB sparse file in `/tmp` raised system RAM by 64.7 MiB.

## Fix

**Size stored as data, not file length.** The shadow file holds a fixed 16-byte record (8-byte magic + native-endian `uint64` size), written with a single `write()`. Only the real shm object is sized to the buffer. The magic starts with a NUL byte: the server's `/tmp` cleanup tries to parse `subspace_*` files as split-buffer metadata protos first, and a tag byte of 0 never parses.

**The shm creator owns the size.** Previously every creating publisher wrote its requested size into an empty shadow and then raced on `shm_open(O_CREAT | O_EXCL)`, so two publishers could leave the shadow holding the loser's size while the winner sized the object (this race also existed with the old ftruncate code). Now:
- Only the `O_EXCL` winner writes the record, overwriting any stale record, and it does so **before** sizing the shm object.
- A publisher that loses waits (bounded, ~1 s) until the object has a nonzero size, then reads the record, which is then guaranteed to be the winner's. A creator that crashed mid-creation produces a timeout error rather than a hang.
- A missing record in a file of 16 bytes or less is treated as not-yet-written, never as size 16. Shadows sized by older clients are always larger and still read correctly.

**Rust client.** It had its own copy of this logic (same doubling bug) and now uses the same format and ownership rule. `create_shm` now distinguishes "already exists" from real errors, and an attaching Rust publisher records the buffer's real size in the BCB instead of its requested size (the C++ client already did this).

**Small adjacent fix.** When ftruncate on the shm object fails, unlink the shm object name instead of the shadow file path, which was leaking the object.

## Compatibility

New clients read old shadow files correctly. An old client reading a new shadow file would see a 16-byte buffer, so all C++ and Rust clients on a POSIX (QNX/macOS) host should be upgraded together.

## Testing

- `ClientTest.PosixShadowFileDoesNotReserveBufferSize`: 8 × 1 MiB slots; the shadow file stays under 4 KiB and a subscriber attaches with the full slot size.
- `ClientTest.PosixShadowFileStaleSizeIsReplacedByCreator`: plants a stale record before the publisher exists; the creator must replace it. Verified this test fails against the previous write-only-if-empty logic.
- `bazelisk test //... --config=macos_arm64`: all 27 test targets pass, including the C++/Rust cross-language tests.
- Not yet built or measured on QNX.

author: the-verscienta
body:
## Why

No Playwright spec exercised the CRDT co-editing path (`mountCollab` in `assets/js/rich_text.js`, `assets/js/collab.js`). `:collab_prototype` was unset in `config/e2e.exs`, so every block mounted solo. During the TipTap 3 move (#1957), y-tiptap fired `onUpdate` inside `new Editor` before `hook.slash` existed. The throw aborted the constructor and nothing synced, yet all 33 editor specs passed.

## What

- **`e2e/tests/collab.spec.js`**: admin (A) and the seeded editor (B) open one draft in two contexts.
  - A adds a rich-text block, types, saves and reloads. The host now carries `data-collab-topic` / `data-collab-fragment`.
  - B joins. Both show `Alpha` exactly once, with no duplicated text after the join.
  - A types and B sees it. B's copy is `contenteditable=false` while A holds the field lock (#140).
  - A clicks away, so B's copy becomes editable. B types and A sees it.
  - B's `.collaboration-carets__caret` renders in A's editor with a non-transparent `border-left-color` and the label `DE`.
  - Neither page has any `pageerror`.
  - Text assertions remove the caret widgets before comparing. A remote caret's label sits inside `.ProseMirror`, so `toHaveText` reads `Alpha from A and BDE` once B's caret arrives.
- **Scoped flag, not global.** Enabling it in `config/e2e.exs` broke nothing: all 93 chromium specs passed. But `config/prod.exs` pins the flag **off**. Turning it on suite-wide would move every rich-text spec onto a path production never runs. The solo `buildEditor` mount and the `onReconnected` re-send would lose their only browser coverage, and the dropped-line spec would keep passing through a different path. So `config/e2e.exs` pins it `false`, as prod does. The collab spec turns it on through a new e2e-only `POST /dev/e2e-collab` (`KilnCMSWeb.Plugs.E2ECollab`) and restores the previous value in `finally`.
  - The flag is VM-global, so this is safe only because the suite runs `workers: 1`.
  - The route sits beside `/dev/e2e-identity` in the compile-gated dev-tools scope, which `KilnCMS.Application` refuses in `:prod`.
  - The route is POST-only and CSRF-protected; the spec calls it from a signed-in page.
- Unit tests for the plug, and a changelog entry under Unreleased → Changed.

## Verification

- `npx playwright test tests/collab.spec.js --project=chromium --repeat-each=5`: 5/5 pass.
- Mutation-tested:
  - Removing the #1957 `if (!hook.slash) return` guard: **fails** (B never sees A's typing).
  - A joiner that seeds before the room state arrives: **fails** (`"AlphaAlphaAlpha"`).
- Full chromium suite: 92 passed, 1 failed. The failure is `editor.spec.js`'s "Bold button reports pressed on an empty selection", a pre-existing flake on the solo path: it reproduced 1 in 10 runs with collab never switched on (`"avy"` instead of `"heavy"`). It's unrelated to this diff and has since been fixed by #1964 (the toolbar stole focus), now merged into this branch.
- `mix kiln.changelog --check`, `mix format --check-formatted`, `credo --strict`, `sobelow`: clean.

- `scripts/tier-classify.sh`: reads changed paths on stdin and prints each path's tier and the overall `tier=<low|medium|high>`. The highest tier wins, and unmatched paths are medium. A missing or malformed policy, or an unknown tier, exits 2 without printing a tier.
- `.github/policies/risk-tiers.policy`: `<tier> <glob>` rules, first match wins. High: `.github/*`, `scripts/*`, `gradle/*`, `*.gradle.kts`, `gradle.properties`, `gradlew*`, `app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`, `.gitattributes`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/*`, `.cursor/*`, `.beads/*`, `prompts/*`. Low: `docs/*`, `*.md`. Medium: `app/*`, `core/*`.
- `docs/risk-tiers.md`: the tiers, their paths and the review each one expects, plus how to run it locally and change it.
- `scripts/tier-classify.test.sh`: 70 plain-bash cases covering the engine, every shipped high/medium/low path, and a **doc/policy sync check** (every policy glob must appear in `docs/risk-tiers.md`).

**Why:** website classifies PRs by risk and MinimalUI didn't.

Refs #19: this lands the script, policy, docs and tests. Still open (needs-human: `.github/workflows/tier-classifier.yml` needs the GitHub App `workflows` permission, which this agent's token doesn't have). The exact, actionlint-clean file is in [the comment on #19](https://github.com/Tim-van-Oudheusden/MinimalUI/issues/19). If you add it as a commit on this branch, this PR closes #19 in full.

Claims: new `scripts/tier-classify.sh`, `scripts/tier-classify.test.sh`, `.github/policies/risk-tiers.policy`, `docs/risk-tiers.md`. No existing file changes. This doesn't overlap #30 (`scripts/pr-review-check.test.sh`), #32 (`claude.yml`, CONTRIBUTING) or #33 (`pr-review-check.sh`).

## Testing

I wrote the tests first and confirmed they failed with no script, policy or doc present (`51 case(s) failed`). After the implementation:

```
$ scripts/tier-classify.test.sh
ok: high: .github/workflows/ci.yml
...
ok: doc lists policy glob core/*
all cases passed            # 70 ok
```

Beyond website's suite, the tests cover:
- `.gitattributes` and every Gradle file as high
- `LICENSE` and unmatched paths as medium
- Markdown inside a module as low
- a policy line with CRLF endings
- a rule with a trailing third field (an inline `# comment`) rejected
- the error naming the bad policy line (`:2:`)
- a last path with no trailing newline
- the doc/policy sync check

`shellcheck` 0.10.0 reports nothing for either script. The one `# shellcheck disable=SC2053` marks the intentional unquoted glob match (`[[ $path == ${rule_globs[i]} ]]`), which is the point of the engine.

Classifying every tracked file on `main` gives 36 high, 21 medium and 3 low. Only `.editorconfig`, `.gitignore` and `LICENSE` fall through to medium by default.

- [x] New/changed behaviour covered by a test written first (TDD); test confirmed failing before implementation
- [x] Test asserts observable behaviour, never implementation internals (stdout lines and exit status)
- [ ] UI changes checked on a device or emulator: no UI change

## Quality gates

- [ ] `./gradlew test` / `lint` / `assembleDebug`: not run. No Kotlin or Gradle file changed, and CI runs them. `scripts/tier-classify.test.sh` isn't part of `./gradlew test`, and the proposed workflow runs it.

## Notes for the reviewer

- **Deviations from website, based on gaps found in website's classifier:** the docs and the proposed workflow use `git diff --name-only --no-renames`, because otherwise a workflow `git mv`'d into `docs/` reads as low. The workflow also classifies with the **base** branch's script and policy, so a PR can't lower its own tier. Details and a local simulation of both are in the #19 comment.
- **`.gitattributes` is high**, beyond the issue's list, because it controls line endings and binary handling for every file, including the wrapper jar. Say if you'd rather it fell through to medium.
- `.editorconfig` stays medium (unmatched). It only affects style, and no CI gate reads it.
- The Kotlin `*.gradle.kts` glob also matches `app/build.gradle.kts` and `core/build.gradle.kts`, because `*` crosses `/`. This is pinned by tests.

## Dependencies

- None

author: gravitypdf-bot
body:
Fixes #748 Found while working on #552 ## Problem Inside ``, a table in a block that has a border but no background raised an undefined-key warning for every row, and one more for every header that repeats at the top of a column: ```php $mpdf = new \Mpdf\Mpdf(['mode' => 'c']); $mpdf->WriteHTML('
Cell
'); $mpdf->Output('', 'S'); ``` ``` Warning: Undefined array key "bgcolorarray" in src/Mpdf.php on line 23686 ``` A 250-row table with a `` raised 251 warnings from `_tableWrite()` and 3 from `TableHeaderFooter()`. It happened in both `cssMode`s. ## Cause While columns are active, `_tableWrite()` (for each row) and `TableHeaderFooter()` (for each repeated header) fill the enclosing block down beside the row with `DivLn()`, then set the fill colour back to the block's background: ```php // Reset current block fill $bcor = $this->blk[$this->blklvl]['bgcolorarray']; ``` `GetFirstBlockFill()` counts a block with a border alone as a filled block, but such a block has no `bgcolorarray` key. The same reset in `PaintDivBB()` already checks `isset()` first. ## Fix Both reads now check `isset()` before calling `SetFColor()`, the same way `PaintDivBB()` does. The issue only names the `_tableWrite()` line. The `TableHeaderFooter()` one is the same code with the same warning, so this PR fixes both. I kept the guards and did not give every block a `bgcolorarray` key. Other code (`CssMerger`, `PaintDivBB()`) takes a missing key to mean "no fill". To fill the key in, every place that creates a `blk[]` entry and every place that reads the key would have to change. The output does not change. A missing key read as `null`, and `SetColor(null)` returns without writing anything, so the fill colour stayed as it was. I checked six documents (a single row, a repeated header, and a bordered block inside a filled block, each in both modes) and they are byte-identical before and after. ## Legacy mode The fix applies in both modes. It removes a warning and changes no layout. ## Tests `tests/Mpdf/ColumnTableBlockFillTest.php` runs each case in both CSS modes, through `PageStreams::assertDrawsSilently()`: - A one-row table in a bordered block inside columns renders without raising anything. - A table whose `` repeats in the next column renders without raising anything. A short page makes the header repeat, and the test checks that it did, so the `TableHeaderFooter()` path is covered. With the `src/` change reverted, all 4 tests fail: the warnings come from both lines. There is no snapshot, because the change cannot alter a drawn page. The byte comparison above shows the output is identical. ## Checks - `composer test`: OK, 12736 tests, 31 skipped (none of them snapshots: `--group snapshot` gives OK, 218 tests). No fixture changed - `composer cs`: clean - PHPStan: the same 23 errors as `gravitypdf` (stale baseline, #716), none new 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: liloleblanc
body:
## What changes

**1. "Gate | Porte" fits inside the gate panel during boarding.**
During a takeover (countdown, Now Boarding, Final call, Gate closed) the "Gate | Porte" label could be cut off at the top of the screen. The takeover now has its own, smaller label size, and the gate number's auto-fit also fits to the panel's height, not just its width. Side effect: in a takeover the number can sit up to 18 px further left at 1920x1080.

**2. New Rouge A320 art.**
`fids-current/aircraft/AC/320r.png` is replaced with the new Rouge A320 drawing (C-GFCH, fin 243). It is framed the same way as the old one, and the inside of the airframe is fully opaque so the sky never shows through.

**3. Fix found while checking: the Thanksgiving bouquet no longer hangs over the cards in a takeover.**
In a takeover the bouquet could still hang as the corsage under the panel's corner, over the cards. The corner was only ruled out when a card's words came within 10 px of it. At 2560x1440 that happened in every takeover state on all four test gates (YQM 1, YQM 4, YHZ 20, YUL C75), including YUL C75 over the Départ card, which v24046 also had. At 1680x1050 it happened on YQM gate 4 in boarding, final call and gate closed; that one was new in this release, because the smaller takeover label left the corner clear. `_tgBqWhere` in `fids-current/js/fids-core.js` now skips the corsage whenever `.g8-wrap` has `g8-takeover`, so every takeover uses the pinned place inside the panel. Off a takeover nothing changes.

## What was checked

- **Tests:** full `npm test` after the final edit: 2278 tests, 2277 pass, 0 fail, 1 skipped. New `tests/gate-panel-label-inside.test.js`. In `tests/holiday-thanksgiving.test.js` the corsage-loop check now includes the takeover guard, and a new test runs the real `_tgBqWhere` on the measured 2560x1440 YUL C75 layout: off a takeover it still hangs; in one it is pinned on the right, clear of the number and above the Departure card. That new test fails on v24046.
- **Guards:** `npm run guard`: "Board languages: clean, 132 ledgered items open". `assets:check`: manifest current, 2693 assets. `node --check` passes on `fids-core.js`. The v24014 weather-card block is still the last block in `display-overrides.css`.
- **Test flights:** YQM 1 (WS), YQM 4 (AC), YHZ 20 (AC) and YUL C75 (AC). Countdown, Now Boarding, Final call and Gate closed at 1920x1080, 1680x1050, 1366x768 and 2560x1440 (64 takeover shots), plus idle at all four sizes. For the countdown shots the gate's inbound was removed, because YQM 4's real late inbound shows "Updated boarding time to follow", which keeps the countdown from opening.
- **Gate | Porte and the number:** fully inside the 110 px panel in all 64 takeover shots.
- **Bouquet in takeovers:** pinned every time, never hung. Its real ink (the screenshot minus the same frame without the bouquet) never touches the label or the number, and stays 5 to 9 px above the cards at 1680, 1920 and 2560 (22 to 36 px at 1366).
- **Bouquet when idle:** still hangs under the corner as on main. Main and this release loaded side by side at the same moment placed it the same way; the only differences came from live map content and the airline-card cycle.
- **Rouge A320:** test flight AC1802 operated by RV at YQM gate 3, 1920x1080. The shelf loads `aircraft/AC/320r.png?v=202` at 2000x800. Day and night both render, and the airframe is opaque with no sky showing through.
- **Companion app cache:** not a problem. Live serves `/aircraft/AC/320r.png` with `cache-control: public, max-age=0, must-revalidate` and an ETag, so `app.html` picks up the new art on its next load.

## Also in this release: phone app, a delayed flight no longer hidden
The companion app's codeshare merge (v24045) also merged ONE carrier's two rows. At Moncton, PAL's PB924 (Arrived) and PB9241 (Delayed) share a minute and a gate, so the app kept PB924 and hid the delayed flight. Two rows are now never merged when they belong to the same airline, or when their status or expected time differ. Test: `tests/companion-app-rows.test.js` (the Moncton case).

## Open items

- [ ] In takeovers the gate number moves up to 18 px left at 1920x1080 (side effect of fitting the label to the panel height). Confirm it looks right.
- [ ] Design call: on YUL C75 there is no room on the number's side for the bouquet at 1680x1050 (every takeover), and at 1920x1080 when the gate panel loads 442 px wide instead of 480. It then uses #1043's documented fallback, pinned before the Porte | Gate words, inside the panel and over nothing (v24046 did the same). Putting it beside "C75" would mean tightening the label and number spacing or moving them left (about 45 px between them now). That changes the panel layout, so it was left alone.
- [ ] The pinned bouquet's bottom swirl dips 2 to 5 px below the panel's bottom edge at 1680, 1920 and 2560, as in the approved v24046 look. It does not reach the cards.
- [ ] At the same screen size the gate panel loads either 442 or 480 px wide on different loads. This already happened before this release and decides which side YUL C75's bouquet goes at 1920. Not investigated.
- [ ] After merge: live check on fids.orionconnected.com (takeover label, bouquet placement, Rouge A320 on the shelf).

author: realhasanshoaib
body:
## Why

Every browser that loaded a board changed the stacking order of about a quarter of its elements and sent them back to the whole class.

Each whiteboard element has an order key, a short string such as `aA` or `aa`. The keys say which element is drawn on top, and they compare in byte order: `aZ` comes before `aa`. Sync lists a board sorted by that key, but in the database's own text order, and the production database (`en_US.UTF-8`) puts `aa` before `aA`. Excalidraw takes the order of the list it receives as the truth and rewrites every key that disagrees with it. So a browser that joined a class, came back to it or reconnected did this:

1. It got the board with the upper-case keys in the wrong places.
2. It gave those elements new keys and raised their versions.
3. It sent them to Sync, which stored them and passed them on to everybody.

Seen in a 45-minute class on production (five browsers, one teacher writing):

| Moment | Elements sent back by the browser that loaded the board | Size |
|---|---:|---:|
| A student joins at minute 5 | 44 of about 180 | 58 KB |
| A student returns at minute 21 | 150 of about 760 | 202 KB, in two parts |
| A student's connection is restored at minute 30 | 26 | 35 KB |
| A student reconnects at minute 31 | 108 | 145 KB |

At the end of that class 363 of 1,681 strokes had another order key than the one their writer gave them. The elements sent back are exactly the ones with an upper-case letter in their key (`aA`, `aB`, `b0A`, ...), and the new keys are of the form `aaV`: `aA` moved to between `aa` and `ab`.

What a user can see: an element with the key `aZ` moves above the 26 elements drawn after it. For handwriting that does not overlap nothing changes on screen. A filled shape drawn early can end up on top of what was written on it later.

## What changes

| Side | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Sync, the query that lists a board | `order by element_index, element_id` in the database's text order | `order by element_index collate "C", element_id collate "C"`: the keys' own byte order, and the same for ids when two keys are equal |
| Whiteboard engine in the SDK | Restored the received list in the order it came | Sorts the received list by order key, then id, first. So it keeps the keys also against a Sync without this change |
| `mergeWhiteboardElements` (public helper of the whiteboard package) | Sorted with `localeCompare`, which also puts `aa` before `aA` | The same byte order as the engine, from one shared comparison |

Either side alone stops the rewriting for a browser on the new SDK. The Sync side also stops it for browsers on an older SDK.

No protocol, contract or schema change. The existing index still serves the lookup of a board; its at most 10,000 rows are sorted in memory.

## Completeness: 4 / 5

Not done here:

- Boards that already hold rewritten keys keep them. The order they have now is the order every browser shows, so nothing has to be repaired.
- The Sync side needs a production release, the SDK side goes out with the next SDK version.
- Ids are compared by UTF-16 code unit in the browser and by byte in Sync and the Recording. The two differ only for ids with characters outside the Basic Multilingual Plane, which no client makes, and only as a tie-break between two elements with the same key.
- Two writers who create elements at the same moment can still give them the same key; one of them is then re-keyed and sent again. That is how the keys work and it settles in one step.

## Proof

- Engine test, fails before the change: a board that arrives as `aa`, `aA`, `ab` keeps its three keys and versions, and nothing is submitted. Before the change `aA` became `aaV` at version 2 and was submitted, the same rewrite as in the class.
- Sync test: it runs the real snapshot query against a copy of the table whose text columns sort like a language (`en-US-x-icu`), because the test database sorts by bytes anyway. Keys `aa`, `aA`, `ab`, `ab` come back as `aA`, `aa`, `ab`, `ab`, and the two `ab` elements in the byte order of their ids. The test first checks that the plain order of that copy is the wrong one.
- Two tests for `mergeWhiteboardElements`: order by key, and by id for equal keys.
- Read-only check on the production database: text order gives `aa, aA, ab, aZ, b00`, `collate "C"` gives `aA, aZ, aa, ab, b00`.
- 51 tests in the whiteboard package pass.
- The video of a class was never affected: the Go builder of the Recording already sorts by key and id in byte order.

## Review

The Codex review on the first push found two things, both fixed in the last commit: equal keys were ordered by id in three different ways (now one), and the Sync test could not fail on CI, whose database already sorts by bytes (now it runs against language-sorted columns).

Found and written by Claude Opus 5.5 (high reasoning) from the frame log of a rehearsal class on production.

A4 (§3 D9, §4.2, §12, §19 B23/B29): the Linux `SecretStore` driver.

- Tiers: per-profile environment override (read-only) → `secret-tool` (libsecret-tools; secret on stdin only, labelled attributes) → a labelled plaintext fallback file in the config dir (0600, atomic private temp + rename, symlink refusal, versioned map), reported as the visibly unencrypted tier.

body:
## O que muda
Fase 6 (operação e LGPD), em três partes na mesma branch.

### 1. Dados de uma igreja (ferramenta do dono, `scripts/igrejas.py`; lógica em `scripts/igreja_dados.py`)
- `exportar <igreja> [--sem-senhas]`: `.zip` (modo 600) com as 13 tabelas, a marca e um manifesto (versão do esquema, contagens). Relê e confere o pacote. `--sem-senhas` serve para entregar à igreja (portabilidade LGPD) e não pode ser restaurado.
- `restaurar <zip> [--substituir]`: mantém os ids, acerta as sequências, confere as contagens, tudo numa transação. Recusa esquema diferente; sobre igreja existente exige `--substituir` e salva uma cópia do estado atual antes.
- `remover <igreja> --confirmar-nome "..."`: exige igreja já suspensa, nome exato, não ser a única igreja e um pacote conferido antes de apagar. Desfazer = `restaurar` do pacote.
Só CLI (sem rota HTTP), tudo na auditoria do dono, como na fase 5.

### 2. Termos de uso e política de privacidade
- Páginas públicas `/termos.html`, `/privacidade.html` e `/aceite-termos.html`; `GET /api/legal` entrega versão, igreja (controladora) e operador.
- Aceite obrigatório por usuário e por versão: **migration `0005`** (`usuarios.termos_versao`, `termos_aceitos_em`). Sem aceitar, a API responde 403 "Aceite dos termos obrigatório" (depois da troca de senha temporária); `sessao.js` leva à tela de aceite (`?v=3`, cache do SW `ebd-v6`).
- Nova versão do texto = alterar `TERMOS_VERSAO`. `OPERADOR_NOME` e `OPERADOR_CONTATO` no `.env.prod` (já repassados no compose). Vazio desliga a exigência; nos testes fica desligada.

### 3. Backup diário por igreja e retenção
- `backup-todas --saida <pasta>`: um `.zip` por igreja (ativas e suspensas), cada um relido e conferido; uma igreja que falha não impede as outras (código 1). `conferir <zip>`: integridade sem tocar no banco.
- `ebd-backup.sh` (só Postgres) guarda `ebd-igreja-<id>-<subdominio>-*.zip` (600, 14 dias na VPS); `baixar-backup.ps1` baixa o mais recente de cada igreja (30 dias no PC).
- `/data/exportacoes` (pacotes do dono) é apagado depois de 30 dias (`RETENCAO_EXPORT`) e **fica fora do tar de `/data`**: é o prazo prometido nos termos. O pacote final de uma igreja removida existe só na VPS, por 30 dias.
- Roteiro de restauração de uma igreja em `docs/PLANO_MULTITENANT.md` ("Backup por igreja").

## Antes de subir em produção
- **Copiar os scripts novos**: `scripts/backup/ebd-backup.sh` para `/usr/local/sbin/` na VPS e `baixar-backup.ps1` por cima do do PC; só então o backup por igreja vale.
- **Texto jurídico é rascunho técnico**: revisão por advogado antes de vender (base legal para crença religiosa, consentimento de pais, prazos).
- Definir `OPERADOR_NOME` e `OPERADOR_CONTATO` no `.env.prod` do servidor.
- **Todo usuário existente terá que aceitar os termos uma vez**, inclusive sessões abertas (a fila offline da chamada é preservada). Subir fora do domingo de manhã.
- A migration `0005` roda sozinha no `entrypoint.sh`; fazer o backup manual antes, como nas fases anteriores.

## Testes
**Executados em Postgres 16 na VPS** (pasta, rede e banco descartáveis, sem porta publicada; produção intacta), em 13/10/2026, no commit `0bcf73b`:
- `teste_dados_igreja` (40 OK: exportar, restaurar, remover, backup-todas, conferir, restauração de uma igreja sem afetar a outra, sequências, auditoria), `teste_termos` (25), `teste_igrejas_dono` (92), `teste_isolamento` (46), `teste_multigreja` (27), `teste_marca_igrejas` (22), `teste_senha_temporaria` (16), `teste_rotas` (48), `teste_config` (61), `teste_trimestre` (19), `teste_trocas` (28): **todos passam**. A migration `0005` foi aplicada pelo Alembic nesses testes.
- `ebd-backup.sh` rodado com um `docker` simulado (pacotes copiados, retenção, falha parcial com código 1); `conferir` testado com pacote bom, ruim e inexistente.
- **Ainda não executado de verdade:** o `ebd-backup.sh` e o `baixar-backup.ps1` contra a VPS. O `.ps1` já foi copiado para o PC (sintaxe validada); o `.sh` só deve ir para `/usr/local/sbin/` **depois** do deploy deste PR (ele chama `backup-todas`, que a produção ainda não tem).

## Ainda falta na fase 6
Limite de requisições por igreja; revisão jurídica do texto.

body:
## Resumo

O site agora é **Astro 7 estático**, servido por nginx sem root. Segue o padrão visual N3XUS (o mesmo design system do n3xus.dev), tem um player novo e foi pensado para ser seguro desde o início.

Prévia no ar: https://cyberjus.n3xus.dev (app `cyberjust-web` no Coolify, apontado para esta branch).

### Player
- Web Component `<cj-player>` com um único `<audio>` nativo e streaming por HTTP Range. **Continua tocando ao navegar** entre páginas (`<ClientRouter />` + `transition:persist`).
- Media Session API: título e capa na tela de bloqueio e na Central de Controle, teclas de mídia, fones e barra de posição.
- Continua de onde parou e lembra a velocidade (com tom preservado) e o volume. O controle de volume fica escondido no iOS, que não deixa ajustar volume por JavaScript.
- Atalhos J/K/L, trilha acessível (`aria-valuetext`) e botões com pelo menos 44 px.

### Segurança
- CSP só com `'self'` e **sem `'unsafe-inline'`**: nada inline no build. HSTS, COOP/CORP, `frame-ancestors 'none'` e Permissions-Policy.
- Imagens Docker e actions fixadas por digest/SHA. O pnpm só instala versões com 14 dias ou mais (`minimumReleaseAge`). Dependabot com o mesmo intervalo de 14 dias.
- Sem terceiros, cookies ou rastreadores. Tem `security.txt` e página de privacidade.

### Números
| | Antes (Next.js) | Agora (Astro) |
|---|---|---|
| JavaScript por página | ~232 KB gzip | ~26 KB sem compressão |
| Imagem Docker | 351 MB | 170 MB (44 MB são áudio) |
| Memória do contêiner | 42 MB | 18 MB |
| Dependências de runtime | 14 | 6 |

### Conteúdo
- Um Markdown por episódio, com esquema validado. As durações agora são as reais, medidas com `ffprobe`; as antigas estavam erradas, como 45:30 num áudio de 6:29.
- URLs `/episodios/<slug>/`, com 301 a partir das antigas (`/episodes/7` e similares).
- **Removido por não ser verificável:** os "especialistas" de cada episódio, com e-mails `@pf.gov.br`/`@mpf.mp.br` inventados, as linhas do tempo, as transcrições de 2 linhas e os números "100K+ usuários protegidos". Os 3 especialistas da home continuam.

## Teste
- [x] `pnpm test`: 16 testes unitários
- [x] `pnpm build`: `astro check` sem erros nem avisos
- [x] e2e contra a imagem de produção: 87 de 87 passaram em Chromium, WebKit, iPhone 15, iPad Pro e Pixel 7. Cobrem CSP, headers, redirects, Range/faststart, persistência do player, Media Session, alvos de toque, ausência de rolagem lateral e navegação sem JavaScript.
- [x] Prévia no Coolify: rotas, 404, 301, Range 206 pela Cloudflare e CSP conferidos com `curl`
- [ ] Ouvir num iPhone/iPad/Mac de verdade (som, tela de bloqueio, troca de página tocando)

Depois do merge: trocar a branch do app no Coolify de volta para `main`.

author: agenteinstinct1-max
body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #271

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Config initialization forks an `@opencode-ai/plugin` registry install per config directory (`config.ts` detached fibers, `tui.ts` scoped fibers), and plugin loading joins them via `waitForDependencies`. A stalled registry kept those joins — and instance disposal behind them — waiting indefinitely (the 20-minute HttpApi action timeouts from #264/#265). The #264 fix only disabled the install for one hermetic fixture; production stayed unbounded.

Three coordinated changes:

1. **Bounded install policy (the issue's 60s design proposal, configurable — not a blind timeout).** `Effect.timeout` wraps each forked install in `config.ts` and `tui.ts`. Default 60s; override via `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DEP_INSTALL_TIMEOUT_MS` (missing/invalid/non-positive → default, never unbounded). On expiry the install fiber is interrupted — and `Effect.timeout` waits for the fiber to unwind before failing, so cancellation is complete before the bound reports.
2. **Actual cancellation of Arborist work (an Effect timeout alone does not stop the install).** `Npm.reify` creates an `AbortController` per reify and threads `signal` through Arborist → pacote → npm-registry-fetch → make-fetch-happen (verified against the pinned versions: `npm-registry-fetch@19.1.1` forwards `opts.signal` to the fetch; `make-fetch-happen@15.0.6` passes it to the request). `Effect.onInterrupt` aborts it, so fiber interruption cancels in-flight registry HTTP work instead of orphaning a running promise. The flock is scope-acquired, so interruption releases the per-directory install lock (scoped heartbeat fiber dies with it). `ignoreScripts: true` is unchanged, so no lifecycle child processes can outlive cancellation.
3. **Warn-and-continue only where safe; required plugin installs preserved.** Timeouts log `background dependency install timed out, continuing without it` (`dir`, `timeoutMs`); failures keep the existing `background dependency install failed` warning; config load never fails. This is safe because the bounded install only pre-seeds `@opencode-ai/plugin` for config dirs: plugin loading still joins (now bounded) and `PluginLoader`/`resolvePluginTarget` → `Npm.add` still installs each declared plugin's package with per-plugin error reporting (`stage: "install"` → `publishPluginError`). A plugin whose needed pre-seed timed out fails its entry import and is reported per plugin — never silently dropped. The foreground per-plugin `Npm.add` path is deliberately not bounded here (out of scope).

Files (disjoint from the in-flight #262/#263 work, which lives in `httpapi-exercise/runner.ts`, `script/httpapi-exercise.ts`, `test/server/httpapi-listen.test.ts`):

```
packages/core/src/flag/flag.ts                          timeout flag getter (60s default)
packages/core/src/npm.ts                                AbortSignal wiring in reify
packages/opencode/src/config/config.ts                  bounded forked install + timeout warning
packages/opencode/src/config/tui.ts                     same bound for TUI dep fibers
packages/core/test/npm-interrupt.test.ts         (new)  cancellation + real stalled-registry tests
packages/opencode/test/config/dep-install.test.ts (new) bounded-policy regression tests
```

No workflow, credential, or paid-service changes.

### How did you verify your code works?

New deterministic regressions mapping 1:1 to the issue's required evidence:

| Required evidence | Test | Assertion |
|---|---|---|
| Deterministic stalled-registry (real stack) | `npm-interrupt.test.ts` "interrupting a real install stalled on the registry…" — local TCP blackhole registry (accepts, never replies) driving real Arborist/pacote/npm-registry-fetch, no mocks | Rendezvous is the registry socket: interrupt happens only after Arborist verifiably began registry work; in-flight sockets are then destroyed via the abort signal; flock released; no orphan work |
| Deterministic mock-install (signal level) | `npm-interrupt.test.ts` fake-Arborist tests | `signal.aborted === true` exactly when the fiber is interrupted; success path gets a live un-aborted signal; released lock immediately reusable by a second install |
| Bounded wait + real cancellation at config level | `dep-install.test.ts` "bounds a stalled dependency install…" (mock `Npm.Service` suspends forever, 250ms bound) | `waitForDependencies` returns at the bound (`≥200ms`, `<10s`); install fiber interrupted (`Effect.onInterrupt` recorded); timeout warning logged, no failure warning |
| Prompt disposal | `dep-install.test.ts` "disposes the instance without waiting…" (8s bound) | `disposeAllInstances` returns while the install is still stalled (`interrupted === false`); the detached fiber self-terminates at the bound with nobody joining — bounded lifetime |
| Normal successful installs | `dep-install.test.ts` success path + pre-existing real-Arborist `npm.test.ts` | `@opencode-ai/plugin` requested per config dir, no warnings, not interrupted; real installs unaffected by the signal change |
| Failed/incomplete install reporting | `dep-install.test.ts` failure path | Existing `background dependency install failed` warning; config load continues |
| 60s proposal, not blind | `dep-install.test.ts` flag test | Default `60_000`; override honored; `not-a-number`/`-5`/`0` → default |

Local runs (Linux sandbox): `packages/core` full `bun test` **1353 pass / 0 fail** (156 files); `packages/opencode` `test/config/` **189 pass / 0 fail**, `test/cli/tui/plugin-*` 11 pass, `test/plugin/install*` 24 pass; both packages `bun typecheck` clean; changed files `oxlint` 0/0 and `prettier --check` clean; timing-sensitive tests re-run 3× stable.

CI history on this PR (transparency — first two Windows runs failed and I could not read the job logs from the sandbox):

- `8a5bb5f` / `733b498`: typecheck ✅ linux ✅ **windows ❌ (core)**; hardening test budgets did not change it → deterministic.
- `4891bbc` bisection probe (mock registration kept, test bodies skipped on Windows): **windows still ❌** → the mock registration itself poisoned other core tests there.
- Root cause, reproduced locally: bun's `mock.module` retroactively patches already-imported namespaces, so the mock's disarm branch re-entered itself via a call-time `realArborist.Arborist` read → `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` in any core test doing a real install afterwards (`npm.test.ts`) on Windows; Linux multi-file runs happened to keep the captured namespace intact.
- Fix at `57ff604`: capture the real Arborist constructor by value **before** registering the mock (immune to namespace patching), add the no-mock TCP-blackhole test for cross-platform real-stack coverage, remove the probe skip. Verified: captured const stays the real class after mock registration; `npm-interrupt` + `npm.test` pass combined in both file orders.

Caveats:

- The Windows verdict on the final head is what fresh CI must confirm; the recursion fix is structural, not timing-based.
- Abort cancels in-flight registry HTTP work (the reported stall mode). Arborist's local filesystem steps (extract/move) are not abortable mid-write; they are bounded local operations and the promise is abandoned by the interrupted fiber.
- 60s is the issue's initial proposal, encoded as an overridable default, not tuned against production latency data.
- Unrelated pre-existing sandbox failure: `httpapi-listen.test.ts` PTY-websocket test fails identically on the pristine base here (native node-pty build skipped in the sandbox); repo-wide type-aware `oxlint` OOMs in the sandbox, per-file lint passes.

### Screenshots / recordings

_Not a UI change._

### Checklist

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

author: bottrall
body:
## Problem

Closes #395

When the ACP host relays a `confirm` or `ask(options:)`, the `session/request_permission` it sends has to name a tool call, so it carries a synthetic one: a fresh `toolCallId`, `pending`, with the question as its title. Nothing ever followed for that id, so a client that draws permission requests as tool cards could leave the card spinning until the turn ended. New in 0.13.0 (#337); found by reading, not yet observed in a client.

## Solution

`Host#permit` now follows the client's reply with a `tool_call_update` for the same `toolCallId`, built by a new pure `Mapper.permission_done`. The status reuses the line `selected_option` already draws: `completed` when the client selected an option (`No` included — the question was answered), `failed` for everything else (cancelled outcome, unrecognised outcome, or a `RequestError`, which is also how a dropped connection or a cancelled request comes back).

Two things a reviewer might not expect:

- There is no `rescue`/`ensure` around the request. In acp-sdk 0.11.0 `request_permission` returns every failure as a value (a closed transport yields `CONNECTION_CLOSED`, a malformed reply becomes `RequestError.invalid_response`), and a write to a gone peer is swallowed, so the close is always reached and never raises.
- `permit` captures `@client` in a local so the close goes to the client that was asked. `ACP#adopted` re-points `host.client=` when another connection loads the session, which can happen while a turn is blocked on a question; without the capture the update would go to a connection that never saw the id.

An option id the client selects but that was never offered still closes the card as `completed` while `ask` returns `nil`. Treating that as `failed` would mean moving the "was it offered" check out of `ask`, which I left out of this change.

`docs/ACP.md` gains one sentence, since the extra update is visible on the wire to a client.

## Proof

`test/riffer/rig/acp/mapper_test.rb` pins both arms of the status (a selected `no` completes, no selection fails). `test/riffer/rig/acp/host_test.rb` pins that an `ask` with options and a `confirm` each close the tool call they opened, on their session, and that the close reaches the original client when another adopts the session mid-question. `bin/ci` (tests, lint, typecheck, docs) passed locally before the final test-only tidy-up, after which lint, typecheck and the ACP tests were re-run green; CI covers the full suite.

## Qué

Adopta en el catálogo de consulta los campos nuevos de forward-system #894 (abierto, sin desplegar), salvo `hayDisponible`:

- **Tarjeta:** el renglón dice "12 fragancias · caja de 12" (`cantidadFragancias`, `ventaMinimaUnidades`; "caja de N" solo si es más de una unidad).
- **Ficha:** en el bloque de costos (solo con `CAP_VER_COSTOS`) suma "Última compra: día · proveedor · costo" (día argentino) y la variación con signo, en rojo si el costo sube y en verde si baja. El color sale del valor redondeado que se escribe: "0,0 %" siempre va neutro, y ±0,05 redondean para el mismo lado.
- **No usa `hayDisponible`:** cubre todos los depósitos y el chip de la ficha es el del depósito del usuario; un vendedor podía ver "Hay stock" en la tarjeta y "Sin stock" en la ficha. La disponibilidad sigue por depósito, con `POST /Stocks/disponibilidad` y cantidad 1 en la tarjeta y en la ficha, para que las dos digan siempre lo mismo. La ficha conserva su aviso aparte "No alcanza para la venta mínima".
- Tipos a mano (`Producto`, `ProductoDetailDto`, `UltimaCompraProducto`), sin tocar `generated/schema.ts`. BACKLOG-9B: filas "disponibilidad en la lista", "última compra" y "venta mínima en el listado".

## Compatibilidad

- **Antes del despliegue de #894** (campos ausentes): igual que hoy. Líneas con "Con fragancias", sin "caja de N", sin última compra.
- **Después del despliegue:** lo de arriba. Con `ultimaCompra` null o sin el permiso no se dibuja nada nuevo. El chip no cambia en ningún caso.

`npx tsc --noEmit -p .` limpio. `npx jest -w 2`: 110 suites, 1320 tests en verde. En el catálogo: 32 en `catalogoConsulta.test.tsx` (servidor nuevo con `hayDisponible` contradictorio, servidor anterior, bloque de costos con y sin permiso, colores de la variación) y 10 de helpers en `presentacion.test.ts`.
