Before: tapping points in the route builder drew straight lines between them, cutting across switchbacks. The website's route builder showed no trails at all.

After: with **Follow Trails** on (the default), each tap lands on the nearest trail or road and the route runs along it between taps. **Straight Line** draws straight segments for unmapped ground, and each segment keeps the mode it was drawn in. The website's route builder now draws the OpenStreetMap trails (sand dash, like the phone) and snaps the same way.

How: `core/trail-router.ts` builds a small road-and-trail network from the OpenFreeMap zoom 14 vector squares the trail layer already loads (free, no key, commercial use allowed, attribution shown). It stitches tile seams, T junctions and crossings (but not bridges), then runs A* with highways weighted down. Everything runs on the device, with no routing server, and it works offline wherever the squares are saved. A tap snaps within about a fingertip at the current zoom. If no trail joins two taps, or the only way round is a long detour, that leg falls back to a straight line and the hint says so. Saved routes keep every tap as a point on the line (`core/route-legs.ts`), so editing re-reads the legs. Older straight routes load as straight legs. There's no migration and no native code.

- The CSP adds `https://tiles.openfreemap.org` to connect-src, for the website.
- Showcase: the "Plan It on the Big Screen" copy, ticks and screenshot, the step 1 text, and a new "Routes That Follow the Trail" line.

## What this fixes

The owner asked that the shimmer seen on the church roof in VR affect nothing else.

**Cause, for everything**: the VR render settings. In VR the game drew at only 72% of the headset's resolution at best, dropping to 55% under load. Fixed foveation was also at its strongest. At that resolution every thin or high-contrast edge shimmers as the head moves.

**Fix**: the VR quality ladder now starts at the headset's full resolution with foveation off. It gives up a step only while the frame rate needs it:

| Step | Resolution | Foveation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 (start) | 100% | off |
| 2 | 90% | 0.25 |
| 3 | 82% | 0.5 |
| 4 | 74% | 0.75 |
| 5 | 66% | 1 |

The Event's finale still drops to the lowest step.

**The owner's new rule for the VR games**: never any flickering or z-fighting. It is recorded in `greeblis-rules.md` and `history.md`, with how it is kept:
- no two faces share a plane where both can show;
- no thin, high-contrast lines that shimmer as the head moves;
- full resolution in VR unless the frame rate needs a step down;
- checked with `t_zfight.js` and close renders before every push.

**Checks**: the game script passes a syntax check, and `ordtest.js` passes on desktop and `MOBILE=1`. `tools/index.html` is refreshed. The frame rate at full resolution needs a check on the Quest.

author: lazerwalker
body: Hi! I only ever enter vacation mode via auto-vacation. My mental model of it (matching a certain popular chess site) is "this is just the thing that saves me from running out of time every so often". When that happens, I'm always surprised that I have to go manually turn off vacation mode, because my expectation (based on e.g. said chess site) is that making a move will exit auto-vacation. This adds an optional settings (default false, and stored in the syncable client prefs) that exits vacation mode automatically after you make a correspondence move. It's worth noting that (as far as I can tell) the client doesn't seem to have a way of distinguishing whether vacation mode was entered via auto-vacation or not. I think an ideal version of this would be narrowed to "auto-exit auto-vacation mode on correspondence move". That would require this to be implemented on the server rather than the client; I suspect for several reasons that would actually be a better fit for this feature, but I naturally only have the ability to submit client code, and I wanted to give you working code instead of just an issue, so here we are. Which is to say: this PR has been written to be mergeable as-is, but I also recognize this is primarily a design discussion about "hey, the way auto-vacation is implemented annoys me, what do you think about making it be slightly more configurable?" One edge case to note: this currently detects vacation mode by looking at the game's pause object. For a game that has vacation disabled, you won't show up as on vacation, and thus this won't fire. I don't know if that's expected behavior or not, but since this is the only way I have to detect vacation mode, it's not like there's much of a choice here anyway. (The one alternative would be to _always_ exit vacation mode on every correspondence move, the server doesn't error out if you send the `DELETE` request while not on vacation, but that seemed extraneous). Worth noting that my third-party OGS client already implements this (I do just fire off a DELETE request every correspondence move there, hah) and it seems to work fine, it makes things behave much more like I personally expect. Cheers!

author: t0msilver
body:
Closes #1463

The iPhone listed items without `blobs=open` (#1382), so its first sync after joining downloaded the images of every answered question the server held. Now it lists with the flag: an answered question it did not hold comes without its images, which hold their place at their shape in its detail until the detail fetches the question by id, checks each image against the hash in its signed body, and keeps them. Open questions still come with their images.

Before/after, the simulator on the Mac mini (Release, a dev-box server, 500 answered questions with a 35 KB image each plus 5 open, 5 runs, median):

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| first sync | 1.97 s | 0.64 s |
| downloaded | 24.9 MB | 1.46 MB |
| image files kept | 505 | 5 |

Launch was already cheap (`Store.init` 9 ms with 500 kept questions) and the 10 s poll costs 35 ms, so neither changes here.

Review: GLM 5.3 (medium), 1 finding (P1: the image files were written before the serial step, so a sync in flight could prune them and leave empty thumbnails for good), fixed: the files are written inside it, beside the list that names them. InboxTests on the simulator cover the new path.

Parity: none; the web does this since #1388, Android in #1467.

## Release notes

iOS: joining on an account with a long history no longer downloads the images of answered questions; a question's images load when you open it.

author: anchapin
body:
Wires the from-scratch synthetic checkpoints into the detector provider (#743): a new `scratch` provider runs `detector/train_scratch.py`'s model directly from a `ckpt.pt`, which carries its own config (num_classes, width, imgsz, names), so the model shape never lives in the detector config. One grayscale pass over the full sheet, no tiling; torch imports only inside `detect()`, so the rest of matchline still never needs it and CI (no torch) collects the module fine.

Licensing, the point of the slice (#743): the ledger gets `*/detector_runs/scratch-synth-*/ckpt.pt` trained on `matchline_synthetic` (BSD-3-Clause), so the synthetic-only checkpoints are the first detector weights that may ship — permissive data, no pretrained starting weights, no CubiCasa/AGPL taint. YOLO11n stays evaluation-only. `release=True` behavior is unchanged and now has something permissive to allow.

Validation: 26/26 provider tests (4 new: config wiring, required-key refusal, decode-to-Detection mapping with a stubbed network, and a real tiny checkpoint round-trip); full suite 3157 collected; EXPECTED_TEST_COUNT 3153 -> 3157 with docs/ci.md in the same commit. ruff clean. Trained quality: run 38319984460, best mean F1 0.5777 at 30 epochs and still climbing (doors F1 0.46 recall 1.0, windows F1 0.65 recall 1.0); measurement on commercial sheets is the remaining "Not yet" item.

Docs: `docs/detection_provider.md` (provider list, config block, backend comparison, trimmed "Not yet") and `docs/license_ledger.md` (artifacts table + quarantine note rewritten).

## Summary by Sourcery

Enable deployment of synthetic-trained from-scratch detector checkpoints through the detection provider interface.

New Features:
- Add a permissive `scratch` detector provider that runs from-scratch checkpoints and maps predictions to detections.

Enhancements:
- Keep model configuration embedded in checkpoints and defer PyTorch imports until detection runs.
- Classify synthetic-only scratch checkpoints as shippable while retaining evaluation-only status for YOLO11n weights.

CI:
- Update the CI test-count expectation for the added provider tests.

Documentation:
- Document the scratch provider, backend licensing, and detector artifact classifications.

Tests:
- Add provider configuration, validation, prediction mapping, checkpoint round-trip, and license-ledger coverage.

author: kammce
body:
libhal v5 annotates its APIs with `[[clang::lifetimebound]]` and `[[gsl::Pointer]]` for Clang's lifetime safety analysis (libhal/libhal#234). GCC doesn't know these attributes and warns that each one is ignored, which breaks `-Werror` builds.

This adds `-Wno-attributes=clang::` and `-Wno-attributes=gsl::` to `tools.build:cxxflags` in `package_info()`, through `conf_info`. Every package that tool_requires this toolchain gets them, for both the native and arm-none-eabi variants. No compiler check is needed because this package is always GCC. Clang must never receive these flags; it warns on them as unknown.

Verified with arm-none-eabi-g++ 14.2 on a project that uses the attributes and builds with `-Wall -Wextra -Werror`:
- Both flags appear in the generated `conan_toolchain.cmake` and on the compile line, and the build is clean.
- The same file compiled without the flags emits four "scoped attribute directive ignored" warnings.

author: ianmove
body:
## Resumen ejecutivo

### Qué cambia

- **Regenerar da un resultado nuevo.** Imágenes, clips y segmentos H3 del Director, recursos de juego y Hunyuan3D sacan una semilla nueva en cada intento y la guardan.
- **Producciones distintas.** Cada `production.*` nueva tiene su propia semilla base en lugar de números fijos.
- **Videoclips automáticos más variados.**
  - Cada plano cantado tiene su propio encuadre y su propia semilla.
  - Un estilo que no coincide con ningún preset usa las palabras del brief, no "anime".
- **Páginas publicadas limpias.** Sin el pie de Nintendo ni la frase de otra producción.
- **Prompts honestos.**
  - El repaso de prompts del Director pasa a estar desactivado por defecto.
  - Desaparece el recorte a 1.450 caracteres.
  - Un prompt escrito a mano para regenerar conserva el texto que pide.
  - Nuevo ajuste *Prompts sin capas*.
  - La información extra de cada resultado muestra lo que recibió el modelo.
- **Proveedores a la vista.** Aviso no bloqueante con los proveedores en uso hasta que se guarda el perfil de producción. Un perfil guardado que no se puede leer se avisa en lugar de sustituirse en silencio.

### Para qué sirve

Responde a la crítica de un usuario externo ("prompt enhancers, guard rails, artificial seeds, glass walls pushing the same scenes"). La revisión del código (2026-10-12) confirmó esos puntos en el Director, en `production.*` y en las semillas.

### Impacto para el usuario

- Regenerar ya no repite la misma imagen.
- Las producciones ya no salen todas iguales.
- El prompt que llega al modelo es el planificado y se puede ver.
- Nada bloquea el primer arranque.

### Riesgo

- [ ] Bajo
- [x] Medio
- [ ] Alto

El cambio de semillas y de valores por defecto cambia los resultados nuevos. Las producciones ya empezadas mantienen sus semillas al reanudarse.

### Estado

- [ ] En desarrollo
- [x] Listo para revisión
- [ ] Bloqueado por CI o revisión
- [ ] Requiere migración o acción manual

## Summary

Owner-requested quick wins 1–6 from the outside-critique audit, plus "Director prompt polish off by default" and removal of the 1,450-character cut.

## Overview

1. **Seeds.**
   - **Director reruns.** `_regenerate_seed` draws a fresh seed for every Director image, clip and H3-segment rerun, and records it on the clip, segment or attempt. Comic films keep their PRE-pinned seed.
   - **Director first renders.** The first start image now uses the clip's recorded seed, so the seed shown is the one used. One-job LTX runs record the generation seed on every clip.
   - **Productions.** `production_seeds.ensure_seed_base` draws a per-production `seed_base` before the run is marked started. Records that started before this change keep base 0, so a resume repeats their intent ids. Every default stage seed (song candidates, cast, portraits, frames, sets, model pictures, clips) is `base + offset`. Start frames add `1009 × window`. A seed written in the spec is used as written.
   - **3D.** Hunyuan3D and the external 3D engines draw a seed for none or -1 (UI and Wizard default -1).
   - **Game assets.** A Regenerate derives its seed from the attempt id, so the first attempt keeps seed 1. The seed is recorded in the attempt's provenance.
2. **Auto planner.**
   - Four sung framings rotate, each placed in the song's scene.
   - `production.plan` keeps the brief's own style text when no preset matches.
   - Quality profiles choose how many song candidates to make, not their seeds.
   - The runbook examples no longer hard-code seeds.
3. **Publication page.** No tagline or Nintendo footer.
4. **Prompts.**
   - `director_prompt_polish` defaults to `off`.
   - The three `> 1450` cuts in `policies.py` are removed. MiniMax's `prepare_prompt` keeps its own limit; the test now covers that.
   - `_saved_prompt_contract(..., typed=True)` skips the no-text lock for prompts the user typed.
   - Settings › Services › *Raw prompts* (`raw_prompts`) skips the style prefix, motion-effect strip, locks and polish.
   - WanGP records the prompt a handler rewrote (H3 window timing, outpainting) as `model_prompts`. The runtime copies it into the sidecar, and Extra info shows it per window.
5. **Profile.**
   - `/production-profile` returns `invalid_reason`, and an unreadable saved profile is logged.
   - `ProductionProfileNotice` (dismissible, never blocking) names the text and image providers in use until a profile is saved.
6. **Raw prompts in every pass (follow-up commits `bd60377a`, `246e9684`).** A later review found passes that still added the locks with *Raw prompts* on. Now:
   - `_apply_final_prompt_locks` and `_apply_direct_video_contract` carry the first lock pass, the re-check after the manual review pause, the sequential H3 validation pass and the legacy planner. Neither adds a lock with raw on. `_clip_text_allowed` covers H3 segments and segment reruns.
   - The v2 plan endpoint, `/plan-short-film-script` and `plan_short_film_from_story` skip the locks.
   - `DirectorFlags.raw_prompts`: the orchestrator skips its style lock, the LTX I2V source-style anchor and the compressor, and tells the planner. The Story planner and its screenplay fallback skip their style lock.
   - **Review-pause edits are typed.** `continue_pipeline` compares the plans sent back with the ones shown and marks the changed prompt fields (`_director_typed_prompts`). The re-check and later reruns keep the style locks on them but never put the no-text lock back.
   - **Review-screen prompts are typed.** The UI's review route is the direct-video review screen (`provided_clip_plans`); no UI sends edited plans to `/continue`. `_approved_review_plans` marks those prompts as typed. The plan endpoint already locked the ones the LLM wrote.
   - Raw prompts still keeps, on purpose: the continuity anchor of bounded shots (`apply_independent_shot_context`), the spoken-language line, H3's handler and portrait contracts and the planner instructions (`build_*_contract`).
   - 12 more tests in `tests/test_director_raw_prompts.py` (python-a weight 3552).

## Detailed changes

### Backend
- **Director:** `director_pipeline.py` (seeds, raw prompts, polish default). `director/policies.py` (no length cuts).
- **Server:** `_launch_runtime.py`:
  - `raw_prompts` in the services config;
  - polish default;
  - `model_prompts` in the sidecar;
  - `invalid_reason` on the profile response.
- **WanGP:** `wgp.py` (`model_prompts` metadata).
- **Production:**
  - `production_seeds.py` (new);
  - `production_song.py`, `production_stage_frames.py`, `production_cast_portrait.py`, `production_models.py`, `production_diorama.py`, `production_parallax.py`, `production_stage_clips.py`, `production_stage_run.py`;
  - `production_quality.py`, `production_plan.py`, `production_shot_plan.py`, `production_publication.py`.
- **3D:** `model3d_service.py`, `model3d_external.py`.
- **Game assets:** `game_generators/base.py`, `game_produce.py`.
- **Extra info:** `video_extra_info.py`.

### UI and Wizard
- The Raw prompts toggle and updated polish texts in `ServicesSettingsPanel.tsx`.
- The *What the model received* block in `VideoExtraInfoDialog.tsx`.
- `ProductionProfileNotice` in `App.tsx`.
- Hunyuan3D seed -1 (random) in the panel, the advanced settings, the Wizard and Studio actions.
- en/es strings.

### Data, provenance and compatibility
- **New production record field:** `seed_base`. Old records get base 0 on their next run.
- **New sidecar and metadata key:** `model_prompts`.
- **New services key:** `raw_prompts`.

author: bkdiehl
body:
## Why
On civitai.com, a prompt the orchestrator flags as needing mature content fails with *"The prompt has been blocked due to mature content which is not supported by the current model"*. Usually the model isn't the cause: every green request is sent with `allowMatureContent: false`.

The orchestrator rejects any request sent with `allowMatureContent: false` whose prompt scan says it needs mature content. It doesn't know why we sent `false`, so the reason has to come from our side.

## What changes
`submitWorkflow` rewrites the orchestrator's message according to why the request had `allowMatureContent: false`:
- **Private or in-training resources** (submitted with `nsfwLevel: 'pg13'`): "…which private and in-training resources cannot generate". This now applies on every domain.
- **Any other green request:** "…which is not allowed on this site".
- Any other case keeps the orchestrator's message, as before.

Both new messages keep the `The prompt has been blocked due to mature content` prefix that `classifyException` tags as bizlogic. Its comment and test strings are updated to the new wording.

## Tests
- `src/utils/faro/__tests__/classifyException.test.ts` passes.
- eslint is clean on the changed files.
- `pnpm run typecheck` reports no errors in the changed files.

author: xiehuanyi
body:
Indexed value getters cast `size_t id` to `ssize_t` before advancing the matching iterator. On the current implementation, `SIZE_MAX` becomes a backward offset: looking up header or parameter B can return the preceding A entry. Large positive indexes also keep advancing after the matching entries are exhausted.

Advance only while another matching entry exists, using the original unsigned index. Apply this to header strings/numbers, the shared multimap getter (parameters, trailers, multipart files), and multipart text fields. Add public API regressions for maximum indexes and controls for large positive indexes and nonadjacent duplicate order.

Validation:
- On unchanged source, all 3 maximum-index regression tests fail.
- Final C++11 header-only test binary, without TLS/compression feature macros: 29 tests across the indexed-value, header-value/order, and multipart suites pass. The large-index cases complete in the same run.
- Changed lines formatted with clang-format 23.1.2; `git diff --check` passes.

Discovery and implementation: automated OpenAI `gpt-6.1-sol` source review, xhigh reasoning, with the local public-API reproduction and tests above.

body:
## 背景と目的
#1445 の検討を、実装・検証できる小さな参照例へ進める。#1440/#1444 の「業務意味そのものの未確定」と「意味は定まっているが実取引の値が未取得」を、合成fixture上で区別する。

## 変更
- `tools/reference-purpose-preflight` に、副作用・書込みのない小さなGo参照実装を追加。
- 受注の税込総額50万円以上の承認要否という**合成規則**で、意味未確定／実行時値待ち／49万9999円と50万円の境界／通貨・版不明／旧版をそれぞれ診断。
- `executionAllowed=false` を全ケースで固定し、`meaning=accepted` は**fixtureの自己申告に過ぎない**と明記。Shared Acceptance、正本、Host認可、実Provider、Effect Fenceの模倣をしない。
- `tools/README.md` に参照を追加。

## 検証
- Go 1.23.2、単独ディレクトリの `GO111MODULE=off go test -count=1 -v .`：正常7例／異常JSON／結果の再現性、全PASS（ローカルで同内容のソースを検証）。
- `GO111MODULE=off go vet .`：ローカルPASS。
- **未実施**：現在のリポジトリ `go.mod` 指定Go 1.26.9によるexact-head試験、全リポジトリ健全性検証、受理済みSourceからの実生成、actual Provider/Authority/外部Effect、実Target E2E。

#1120（型付き参照、完了）/ #267（受理）/ #1121（lowering）/ #951（Contract・Provider）/ #1174（Effect Fence）/ #1180（Scenario）は本PRで再実装せず、次段階の実Consumer接続で再利用する。

## 次の判定
合成入力だけの分岐分類に留まるため、TEI製品上で「用途別充足条件を正しく判定できる」とは**未実証**。実Source・Accepted Decision・#1120参照の読取りConsumerと接続して評価するまでDraftとする。

author: rfay
body:
## Short Summary (TL;DR)

An empty or corrupt `~/.ddev/.state.yaml` made `ddev start` panic, and a corrupt `project_list.yaml` made every command fail; DDEV now recovers from both on its own.

## The Issue

- Fixes #8935
- Related: #8344

`os.WriteFile` truncates before writing, so a full disk or a crash mid-write leaves a 0-byte `.state.yaml`. That unmarshals to a nil map, which `stateManager.Set()` then writes into and panics.

## How This PR Solves The Issue

- The state file is a disposable cache, so an empty, `null`, or unparseable one now loads as an empty map and is overwritten on the next save. The state manager also guards against a nil map from any storage backend.
- An unparseable `project_list.yaml` is moved to `project_list.yaml.bad` with a warning and DDEV continues with an empty list, because projects re-register on `ddev start`.
- The state file and `project_list.yaml` are now written through `nodeps.WriteFileAtomic`, which writes a temp file and renames it into place. A failed write leaves the old file intact, and a ddev process reading at the same moment, such as the TUI, never sees a half-written project list that it would then move aside. On Windows the rename is retried for up to a second while another process holds the file open.

`global_config.yaml` still fails with a clear error when unparseable, because it is user-edited config that should not be discarded. The gob caches (`.amplitude.cache`, `.remote-config`, `.sponsorship-data`, `.addon-data`) already fall back to empty data and needed no change.

## Manual Testing Instructions

```bash
ddev utility download-ddev --pr 8936
export PATH="$HOME/tmp/ddev-download-ddev/pr-8936:$PATH"
cp ~/.ddev/.state.yaml ~/.ddev/.state.yaml.orig
: > ~/.ddev/.state.yaml
cd <any project> && ddev start
# Expect no panic, and ~/.ddev/.state.yaml rewritten with a remote_config entry
printf '{{{ not: [yaml\n' > ~/.ddev/.state.yaml && ddev start
# Same result
cp ~/.ddev/project_list.yaml ~/.ddev/project_list.yaml.orig
printf '{{{ not: [yaml\n' > ~/.ddev/project_list.yaml && ddev list
# Expect a warning naming project_list.yaml.bad, then an empty list; restore the .orig files afterward
```

## Automated Testing Overview

`TestReadResetsUnreadableStateFile` covers empty, `null`, `---`, and invalid state files, replacing the old test that expected an error. `TestSetAfterEmptyStateFile` reproduces the panic path and checks that no temp file is left behind. `TestReadProjectListUnparseable` covers the project list fallback. `TestWriteFileAtomic` checks the written content, permissions, symlink handling, and temp-file cleanup, and holds the target open during a write, which exercises the Windows retry when the test runs on Windows.

🤖 Developed with assistance from [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)

author: cosmicspork
body:
Closes the two CI gaps between the GitHub and GitLab tool sets and adds a table and a test so the next gap fails CI instead of going unnoticed.

## What changes

- **GitHub `run_dispatch`** starts a `workflow_dispatch` workflow on a branch with string inputs. It is an asked write like `pipeline_run`, and the node follows the run it started, so `run_wait` and the push notifications work as they do for `run_rerun`.
  - **Workflow guard:** a per-repository allow list in node config, deny by default:
    ```toml
    [github.dispatch]
    "cosmicspork/homelab" = ["renovate.yaml"]
    ```
    Repository names are matched without regard to case; file names must match exactly. A workflow that is not listed is refused before the operator is asked, and checked again before it runs, so an operator editing the card cannot get around the list either. The issue's reasoning holds: a release is a workflow on `main`, so refusing tags is not enough.
  - **Same guards as `pipeline_run`:** branches only (an existing tag of that name is refused, and the branch must exist), string inputs only, and no input value naming production.
  - **Finding the run:** since 2026-02-19 GitHub's dispatch endpoint returns `workflow_run_id`/`html_url` when the call sends `return_run_details: true`, and the call does. If GitHub answers 204 with no id (older GHES), the node finds the newest dispatched run of that workflow and branch that was not listed before the call, polling up to 10 s. If no run shows up, the result has `run_id: null` with a note and nothing is followed.
- **GitLab `pipeline_retry`** calls `POST /projects/:id/pipelines/:pipeline_id/retry`. It is asked like `run_rerun` and followed like `pipeline_run`. Following GitLab's existing rule, it refuses a pipeline that ran on a tag, and one whose variables name production, because a retry reuses those variables.
- **`mcp::parity`** maps every operation to its GitHub tool and its GitLab tool, or to a stated reason why one forge has none (`job_play` and `deploy` have no GitHub equivalent). Tests fail when a name in `github::TOOLS` or `gitlab::TOOLS` is missing from the table, and when the README stops naming a CI write.
- **README:** the CI paragraph now lists every CI write, `pipeline_run` included, plus the `[github.dispatch]` config. It also corrects the description of what is offered: a session's repository only fills in `repo`/`project`; it does not hide the other forge's tools. ARCHITECTURE, approval titles (`summarize`) and the SPA call labels are updated to match.
- **Policy:** neither new tool is named in `brokered-reads`, so both are asked. The policy test that lists every asked write now includes them. I left the shipped bundle's text unchanged, because editing even a comment changes its hash.

## Trade-offs and open questions

- The allow list is file-only. It is not editable through Settings or the operator API, and it is read at startup like the rest of `node.toml`, so changing it needs a node restart. Should it be live-editable like `[[repo]]`?
- It is keyed by forge `owner/name`, not by the `[[repo]]` path entries, because `run_dispatch` names a forge repository and needs no local checkout.
- `pipeline_retry` reads `/pipelines/:id/variables` to check for production values. A token that cannot read pipeline variables gets a clear refusal instead of a retry. Is that the right default?
- A GHES that rejects the unknown `return_run_details` key with an error (instead of ignoring it) would fail the dispatch. I have not observed this.
- I left `run_dispatch` input fields and `workflow` unlocked on the approval card, as with `run_rerun`'s `run_id`. The allow list still applies after an edit.

## Verification

- New tests (stub forges only; nothing real was dispatched or retried): `a_workflow_is_dispatched_only_when_listed_and_asked`, `a_dispatch_github_does_not_name_is_found_in_the_list` (github_tools); `a_pipeline_the_session_retried_is_followed_from_the_retry`, `a_run_the_session_dispatched_is_followed` (pipeline_follow); unit tests for the allow list, the input and branch guards, run finding, retried variables, the parity table, the README CI-write check, and the approval titles; SPA label test.
- `just check`: `check-tests.sh`, `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` pass. nextest: 1477 of 1480 pass. The 3 failures are `opencode_adversarial::{the_runners_own_auth_store_stays_empty_and_the_config_is_the_nodes, two_live_sessions_cannot_read_or_migrate_each_others_state}` and `opencode_pty::a_real_shell_is_spawned_and_read_back_through_the_proxy`. They drive the host's pinned OpenCode binary, which answers HTTP 500 "Unexpected server error", and they still fail when run on their own. They touch no forge code, and the same three tests failed in the other parallel branches' check runs on this host. I did not confirm them on an unmodified origin/main. `cargo test --doc`, `bun run check` and `bun test` (374) pass.
- Not verified: a real GitHub dispatch or GitLab retry, by design.

Fixes #462

author: patriotnewsactivism
body:
## What broke

Apex Copilot is missing on a phone that can otherwise use the dashboard fully, while the same account shows it on desktop.

The toggle is gated on two independent things: the build-time `VITE_FEATURE_COPILOT` (identical on every device) and an **operator dashboard session** (per device, minted only by a password login, 12h TTL). The dashboard's own auth gate checks only the long-lived admin bearer, so a browser can be completely signed in — every panel loading real data — while holding **no operator session at all**. `/chat/copilot/status` then answers `403`, and the client read every non-`enabled` answer as "feature off" and rendered no control, saying nothing.

That is the normal state of a phone whose stored login predates operator sessions: its token still validates, so it is never asked to sign in again, and Copilot can never appear. Desktop looked fine because it had a fresh session.

Confirmed in production, not assumed: `railway variables` shows `FEATURE_COPILOT=true` and `VITE_FEATURE_COPILOT=true` on service `Apex`, and the deployed bundle has `isCopilotClientFeatureEnabled("true")` baked in — so both flags are open and the 403 was the only thing left.

## The fix

`resolveCopilotAvailability` (new, pure, unit-tested) splits the answer three ways instead of two:

- `off` — feature disabled, or a failure the operator cannot act on;
- `ready` — enabled and this device holds a valid operator session;
- `needs-sign-in` — enabled, but the status call answered **403 and only 403**. A transient fault (network, 5xx, 401) still resolves `off`, so nothing ever sends an operator to a login form over a blip.

On `needs-sign-in` the chat header now shows **Apex Copilot · Sign in**, which routes back through the password login and mints a fresh session.

`apiFetch` now throws an `ApiError` carrying the HTTP status — it previously threw a bare `Error`, which is precisely why the caller could not tell "not allowed yet" from "not enabled". A 403 is also no longer retried.

## What this deliberately does NOT do

There is no bearer-only "mint an operator session" endpoint. That credential exists so a bot holding only `APEX_ADMIN_TOKEN` cannot authorize an outbound send (`operator-session.ts`, `send-safeguard.ts`); a mint endpoint gated on the bearer would remove that boundary entirely. The password login remains the only mint path, so the fix is to make the failure visible and give the operator the one action that works.

## Verification

- **Pure resolver, against the real module**: 10 cases pass, including `403 → needs-sign-in` and `401/404/500/502/503/network → off`.
- **Built dashboard, driven in Chromium** (`packages/dashboard/dist`, flag on) at 360px, 390px and desktop:
  - status `403` → sign-in control renders, toggle does not, status endpoint called once (no retry), control fully on screen and topmost at its centre, tapping it reaches the login screen;
  - status `200 {enabled:true}` → toggle renders and still flips ON, no sign-in control.
- `tsc --noEmit` in `packages/dashboard`: clean.
- Repo's own mobile-layout gate: `0/102 view+width combinations failed`.

Not run here: `packages/api-server` vitest cannot load locally (`Cannot find package 'zod'` from the git-hosted `apex-copilot` dist — a pre-existing local-env gap, CI installs it), so the new suite is exercised in CI.

## Operator note

Until this deploys, the workaround on the phone is to sign out and back in. If you are seeing **Apex Copilot · Sign in** after this lands, signing in again is the fix — nothing is misconfigured.

author: danmcfan
body:
Closes #24

## Summary

On a small touch device the game now shows a full-screen notice instead of the title screen. In the notice, Bitbox, looking worried, asks the player to come back on a desktop. A "Continue anyway" link lets the player play anyway.

```diff
 <App> (src/main.tsx)
+  smallTouch = watchSmallTouch(matchMedia)      # live: resize/rotation flips it
+  notice = noticeDismissal(() => localStorage)  # key abstract.desktop-notice-dismissed
+  <Show when={!smallTouch() || notice.dismissed()}
+        fallback={<DesktopNotice onContinue={notice.dismiss} />}>
     <Title> | <Play>
```

- `src/ui/device.ts`: `WIDE_MIN_WIDTH = 900` is shared with Board.tsx, which used to have its own literal 900. `SMALL_TOUCH_QUERY` is `(width < 900px) and (pointer: coarse) and (hover: none)`, so a narrow desktop window, a wide touch laptop and a tablet with a trackpad all still get the game.
- The dismissal is stored under its own key, separate from `abstract.save`, so New Game doesn't bring the notice back. If storage is blocked, the notice still shows and can still be dismissed.
- Bitbox's line is `script.smallScreen` in script.ts.

## Evidence

- **Before:** a 390x844 phone with touch emulation opens straight onto the title screen. Its board is too cramped to build on.
  **After:** the same phone shows the notice: "Play on a desktop", worried Bitbox saying "This board's too small for fingers. Come find me on a desktop.", "Layers of Abstraction needs a bigger screen. Visit **abstract.dannyobrien.dev** on a desktop." and "Continue anyway". It uses the vision board's double-bordered sheet on the blueprint grid.
- `bun run verify` on 1488ef0: 78 pass, 0 fail. tsc, the vite build and the bundle check pass. The playthrough prints "Tested!" for levels 1 to 6.
- `src/ui/device.test.ts` (5 tests) covers the query string, live updates on `change`, the dismissal surviving a reload, the key staying separate from the save, and storage that throws.

## Verification

Each criterion was checked against a private dev server (`scripts/with-server.sh`). Chromium was driven over CDP with `Emulation.setTouchEmulationEnabled`, so `(pointer: coarse)` and `(hover: none)` really match. Device metrics were set with `setDeviceMetricsOverride`. I looked at every screenshot.

| Criterion | Result | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Phone (390x844) with touch shows the notice, not the game | Pass | `coarse: true, hoverNone: true, notice: true, title: false`. The screenshot shows the notice sheet with Bitbox. |
| Narrow window with a fine pointer still gets the game | Pass | 390x844 without touch: `notice: false, title: true`. The screenshot shows the title sheet with Start. |
| Wide touch screen (touch laptop) still gets the game | Pass | 1280x800 with touch: `coarse: true, notice: false, title: true`. The screenshot shows the wide title layout. |
| "Continue anyway" lets the player in, and the choice sticks | Pass | After the click: `title: true`, `abstract.desktop-notice-dismissed = "1"`. After a reload the title still shows. After Start (new game) the board shows and a save exists. After another reload the title shows Continue / New Game and no notice. |
| Re-checks on resize or rotation without a reload | Pass | With the notice showing, a live resize from 390 to 1024 swaps in the title screen. Resizing back to 390 brings the notice back. A tablet at 820x1180 (portrait) shows the notice, and rotating it to 1180x820 (landscape) shows the game. |
| `bun run verify` passes | Pass | 78 pass, 0 fail, typecheck, build and bundle check pass, and the playthrough passes 6/6. |

The screenshots aren't attached here: they were taken in a private local session, and this repo has no place to upload PR images. The CI `playthrough` artifact covers the desktop path.

## Review

`/code-review main` raised two findings. Both were addressed in 1488ef0:

- **Spec**, `src/ui/DesktopNotice.tsx`: the notice said the game "needs a bigger screen and a mouse". That gave the wrong reason and ruled out trackpads. It now reads "Layers of Abstraction needs a bigger screen. Visit abstract.dannyobrien.dev on a desktop."
- **Standards**, `src/ui/device.ts`: the `WIDE_MIN_WIDTH` comment named only the HUD as repeating the 900px breakpoint. It now names the HUD's and Dialogue's Tailwind classes too. A grep confirms they are the only other copies.

Declined: none.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way. Reverting removes the notice. The only state this adds is one localStorage flag, which old code ignores.

**Blast Radius:** mobile.

Only small touch devices see something new. The desktop path is unchanged, as the playthrough shows. A device that is guessed wrong is one tap away from the game.

author: saurav717
body:
## The bug: your repositories weren't listed
The page sent an `X-GitHub-Api-Version` header on its GitHub calls to the Worker. The site (github.io) and the Worker (workers.dev) are on different addresses, so the browser first asks the Worker which headers it accepts (a CORS "preflight"). The Worker doesn't accept that header, so the browser blocked every GitHub call that goes through the server before sending it:
- listing your repositories
- creating one
- pushing code

The code's menu then showed the error as an empty list ("None given to Reader's GitHub App yet").

**Fix:** calls through the server now send only `Content-Type`; the Worker adds GitHub's own headers itself (`src/lib/githubToken.ts`).

**Why the tests missed it:** they ran the site and server on the same address, where the browser doesn't do this check. A new test, `scripts/github-cors.test.mjs`, compares every header the page sends with the Worker's own preflight answer. It fails on the old code (`x-github-api-version isn't allowed by the Worker`) and passes now.

## Also in the code's GitHub menu
- **Errors shown:** when GitHub can't list repositories, the menu says why, with **Try again**, instead of showing an empty list.
- **Account and Disconnect:** the menu shows which GitHub account is connected and how (e.g. "GitHub: saurav717 · Reader's GitHub App"), with a **Disconnect** button. Disconnect revokes Reader's access with GitHub and deletes the stored token, after a confirmation.
- **Disconnect race fixed:** both Disconnect buttons (here and in Connections) now wait for the server to delete the token before clearing the browser's setting. Before, the next status check could find the connection still on the server and reconnect.

## Testing
- `scripts/github-cors.test.mjs` (new), described above.
- `scripts/write-flow-smoke.mjs`: the menu names the account and how it's connected; Disconnect there signs out and the server deletes the token. The whole walkthrough passes.
- `npm run test:unit`: 964 passed, 0 failed. `tsc -b`: clean.

author: jbhirsh
body:
Autofix gets one CI-fix attempt per commit, and it used to start that attempt on the first red workflow. A slower check could fail afterwards and never be seen.

On jbhirsh/fog-and-frontier#235, it started on the visual failure at 18:40. Smoke gate then timed out waiting for Vercel at 18:48. When Smoke's own run finished, autofix skipped it as "already attempted". The agent's prompt did ask it to wait for the remaining checks first, but it didn't.

## What changes

- **Waits before the attempt:** the step that decides whether to start a fix now waits until every check on the PR's head has finished. It gives up after 20 minutes. Only then does it list the failures and post its marker comment.
  - **No self-wait:** autofix's own runs sit on main's commit, not the PR's, so it never waits on itself.
  - **Lookup errors:** a failed check-runs lookup is retried, rather than read as "nothing pending".
- **Head re-check:** after waiting, it checks again that the PR head hasn't moved. A new push gets its own runs.
- **Prompt:** says the wait has already happened, and keeps the `gh pr checks --watch` fallback for a check still running after the 20 minutes.
- **Timeout:** the job's limit goes from 60 to 80 minutes, to leave room for the wait.

## Visual changes

- [x] No visible UI change

## Validation

- The YAML parses, and `bash -n` passes on every `run:` block.
- I simulated the wait loop with a stubbed `gh`: a failed lookup retries, a pending check waits, and an empty result ends the wait.
- **Review:** a subagent reviewed the diff before this PR. It confirmed against #235's check runs that autofix's own job isn't among a PR head's checks, and that no workflow here can sit pending forever (no `environment:` approvals or `needs:` chains). Its two findings are fixed: the lookup-error retry, and the prompt wording.
- **Left as is:** the review also noted that the failure list can include a check whose re-run has since passed. That predates this change, so it isn't changed here.

  - With Google chosen, `fetchGoogleForecast` is laid over the forecast at most hourly. In between, the runner keeps the last forecast and refreshes only the warning.
  - `lib/google-weather.ts` is now runner-safe (no `URLSearchParams` or `structuredClone`). The bundle was checked for both.
- **Widget's own refresh** (`WeatherWidgetData.fetchForecast`):
  - Adds `&models=` for the chosen model, falling back to the best match.
  - With Google chosen, calls Google (current conditions, days and hours: 3 calls), refreshing hourly instead of every 10 minutes to stay within the person's free tier.
  - `googleCode` mirrors `googleTypeToWmo`.
- Version 0.4.2. This also brings the Windows app, which runs its own bundled copy of the site, the source picker in place of the old comparison panel.

**Verified**
- 269 tests pass; typecheck and lint are clean. The runner bundle builds without browser-only APIs.
- The release workflow built the APK and the Windows installer.

비교 결과와 재현 명령: [시나리오 A 임베딩 구현 및 모델 비교](https://github.com/diokim17/rfp-rag/blob/5467031a3439d6f3c66753a9903e976030d47bc4/results/reports/a_embedding_comparison_chy.md).

author: eseidel
body:
This is an **alternative to #174** for side-by-side comparison. It fixes the same bug, with the upstream pattern instead of a per-target build key. Merge only one of the two.

## Bug

The same bug as #174. Targets inside `flutter assemble` read `SHOREBIRD_PUBLIC_KEY` and `SHOREBIRD_DD_MAX_BYTES` from the process environment. The key goes into the generated shorebird.yaml in `flutter_assets`, and DD drives the iOS DD pass. Environment variables are not part of the build hash, the stamps or Gradle's task inputs, so changing one leaves the targets skipped or `compileFlutterBuild*` UP-TO-DATE.

Reproduced on `shorebird/dev` (5bef02a) with this worktree's `bin/flutter`. There was no source change between runs, and the key was read from the built artifact:

| Artifact | Transition | Key in artifact | DD tables |
|---|---|---|---|
| apk | none → A | **none** | |
| apk | A → B | **none** | |
| iOS | none → A | **none** | 0 |
| iOS | DD unset → 100000 | **none** | **0** |
| macOS | none → A | **none** | |

## Design

Upstream never lets a target read an environment variable. A setting goes `flutter build` → `BuildInfo` → native build config → bridge → `flutter assemble -d<Define>`. Defines are part of the `.dart_tool/flutter_build/<hash>` hash and are Gradle `@Input`s, so a change is tracked without extra machinery. This PR moves the two Shorebird values onto that path, using exactly the fields and methods dart-defines and `--code-size-directory` use:

1. `FlutterCommand.getBuildInfo` reads exactly two variables, `SHOREBIRD_PUBLIC_KEY` and `SHOREBIRD_DD_MAX_BYTES`, into `BuildInfo.shorebirdPublicKey` and `BuildInfo.shorebirdDdMaxBytes`. An empty key, `0` and malformed DD values are normalized to null, so they all mean "unset" and produce the same hash. Nothing else is read, so `SHOREBIRD_TOKEN` never reaches a config, a define or Gradle.
2. `BuildInfo` emits them in the three places that carry its other settings:
   - `toBuildSystemEnvironment()` emits `ShorebirdPublicKey` and `ShorebirdDdMaxBytes`. This covers in-process builds: ios-framework, macos-framework, web, bundle and swift-package.
   - `toEnvironmentConfig()` emits `SHOREBIRD_ENCODED_PUBLIC_KEY` and `SHOREBIRD_BUILD_DD_MAX_BYTES`. These land in Generated.xcconfig, flutter_export_environment.sh and the CMake ephemeral config.
   - `toGradleConfig()` emits `-Pshorebird-public-key` and `-Pshorebird-dd-max-bytes`.
3. The bridges forward them as `-d` defines:
   - `xcode_backend.dart` handles iOS and macOS.
   - `tool_backend.dart` handles Linux and Windows.
   - Gradle reads them in `FlutterPlugin`, holds them in two `@Optional @Input` properties on `BaseFlutterTask` (declared like `codeSizeDirectory`), and passes them in `BaseFlutterTaskHelper`.
4. Targets read the define. `copyAssets` passes `decodeShorebirdPublicKey(environment.defines)` to `updateShorebirdYaml`. `AotAssemblyBase` (iOS) passes the DD define to `AOTSnapshotter.build(ddMaxBytes:)`. The snapshotter no longer reads `Platform.environment`, which also drops the fork's `dart:io` import from `base/build.dart`.

The CLI contract is unchanged: the shorebird CLI keeps setting environment variables on `flutter build`.

**The key is encoded, because xcconfig drops everything after `//`.** I checked this: `FOO=abc//def` in an xcconfig gives `FOO = abc` under `xcodebuild -showBuildSettings`. The key is base64 of a DER RSA key, and about 1 in 10 such keys contains `//`. Dart-defines use base64, which has the same latent hole (upstream's `encodeDartDefines` comment anticipates it). So the key travels base64url-encoded (`encodeShorebirdPublicKey`), whose alphabet has no `/`, and is decoded in the target, the way `DartDefines` is decoded. Both build settings have names distinct from the raw variables (`SHOREBIRD_ENCODED_PUBLIC_KEY`, `SHOREBIRD_BUILD_DD_MAX_BYTES`). Xcode and CMake also pass the inherited process environment through to the bridge, so a shared name would let a raw value bypass `getBuildInfo`'s normalization (for example `SHOREBIRD_DD_MAX_BYTES=0` becoming a `-dShorebirdDdMaxBytes=0` define with a different hash). It would also let a variable exported in the shell that launches Xcode apply settings that `flutter build` never configured. Key B in the real builds below contains `//` and arrives intact on every platform.

**No environment fallback inside `flutter assemble`.** Upstream has none for any analogous setting (`SPLIT_DEBUG_INFO`, `CODE_SIZE_DIRECTORY`, dart-defines): the bridge reads the native build settings, and targets read defines only. A fallback would reintroduce the bug for any build where the define is absent but the variable is set, and the value would again go untracked. The IDE case works the upstream way. After `flutter build ios|macos`, Generated.xcconfig keeps the encoded key and DD, exactly as it keeps `DART_DEFINES`, so an Xcode build picks them up. For Android, an Android Studio build without `flutter build` has no `-P` properties, just as it has no dart-defines. Shorebird releases and patches always go through `flutter build`.

**Stale DD tables (ported from #174).** When the iOS AOT step runs without DD, it deletes the five `App.dd*` files an earlier DD build left next to the output dir, so `LinkSupplement` doesn't ship them. The code and the test are the same as #174's. Under this design it is mostly belt-and-braces: a DD change already moves the build to a different `.dart_tool/flutter_build/<hash>` directory, and the no-DD directory never held tables. I kept it so the two PRs behave the same.

New Shorebird-only declarations (the define names and the encode/decode helpers) live in `lib/src/shorebird/shorebird_defines.dart`. Upstream files get only fields, map entries and forwarding lines, each marked `Shorebird` the way the fork already marks `shorebirdTraceFile`.

## Diff compared with #174

| | #174 | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Total | +473 −22, 17 files | +537 −33, 18 files |
| Upstream non-test files | +91 −21, 12 files | +89 −15, 10 files |
| Upstream test files | +117, 2 files | +239, 4 files |
| `shorebird/` lib | +58 −1, 2 files | +34 −10, 2 files |
| `shorebird/` tests | +207, 1 file | +175 −8, 2 files |

Upstream non-test files this PR touches, with lines added/removed:

| File | Lines |
|---|---|
| `build_info.dart` | +23 |
| `runner/flutter_command.dart` | +9 |
| `base/build.dart` | +17 −14 (the −14 is the fork's env read and its `dart:io` import going away; +13 is the ported DD cleanup) |
| `targets/assets.dart` | +2 −1 |
| `targets/ios.dart` | +3 |
| `bin/xcode_backend.dart` | +8 |
| `bin/tool_backend.dart` | +5 |
| `FlutterPlugin.kt` | +7 |
| `BaseFlutterTask.kt` | +9 |
| `BaseFlutterTaskHelper.kt` | +6 |

#174 instead changes `build_system.dart` (`Target.buildKeyFor`, the build-system core) and adds a mixin to eight target classes (android, assets, common, ios ×2, linux, macos, web, windows). This PR leaves `build_system.dart` and every target class declaration untouched. Every line it adds to an upstream file sits next to an existing setting of the same kind.

## Results after the fix

These are real builds with this branch's `bin/flutter`: a `flutter create` app plus a `-t module` app for aar, each with a checked-in shorebird.yaml holding a fake `app_id`. Key A is `AAAAkeyA+x/y=` and key B is `BBBBkey//B+z==` (it contains `//`). The key was read from the built artifact, and the DD tables were counted in `build/ios/shorebird`.

| Artifact | Sequence | Key in artifact | Wall time |
|---|---|---|---|
| apk | none → A → A → B → none → DD=100000 | none, A, A, B, none, none | 31, 15, **4**, 15, 7, 14s |
| aab | none → A → A → B → none → DD=100000 | none, A, A, B, none, none | 9, 28, **4**, 17, 16, 16s |
| aar | none → A → A → B → none → A | none, A, A, B, none, A | 23, 15, **4**, 14, 6, 7s |
| iOS (`--no-codesign`) | none → A → A → B → none | none, A, A, B, none | 30, 23, **9**, 20, 15s |
| macOS | none → A → A → B → none → DD=100000 | none, A, A, B, none, A | 28, 110, **17**, 33, 25, 28s |

body:
## WEB-TEXT-ACCEPTANCE-01 — bounded physical Product Story edit receipt

**Authority:** [canonical Notion task](https://app.notion.com/p/3e432a84beec8144bf24d93effcbaf89). This is the sole current Story acceptance PR, based on `main@ee15f5c494d70ac6ffb01e7171ad3358db40387c`. It reuses the merged Product text authority and isolated replay path from #2694/#2697; no second persistence or text authority is introduced.

### User-visible slice
- The existing Product Editor exposes only ordinary framed Stories without rich/table ownership.
- A Story may have an existing terminal CR/LF/CRLF paragraph marker. The textarea displays only the editable body; save reconstructs and preserves that exact canonical marker.
- Any new paragraph/control character is rejected before HTTP. The submitted command remains one Unicode-scalar `replace_story_range` intent; the server derives authoritative before-state.
- On ACK, the browser verifies exact durable `/current`, authoritative Reader Scene, fresh reopen/reload and anonymous denial. An uncertain POST or post-ACK read locks further mutation.

### Physical CI
CLOUD-B02 reuses real OIDC/HTTPS, genuine server, SQLite revision graph, isolated PUB parser/replay, pinned Apache POI `Sample3.pub`, a real file picker and Playwright Chromium. It requires exactly one CSRF-protected Story commit and emits a source-neutral receipt. Private fixture labels, paths and Story contents are scanned before artifact upload.

Current exact head: `e06d1692be1e0eee0f6e5e3a834f959d7ed8b8bd`, merge-forward on current main `d3659d2f8b1b8890ca130a47d4f75fe32ae18308`.

Local evidence on earlier ca806f4b: 45 Node tests and `dev_fast_loop` edit+feature green. Exact-head code changes were verified in hosted checks, not claimed to have been re-run locally.

Exact-head hosted checks:
- Web Editor HTTP seam: [38354688886](https://github.com/Lalalalendia/rar2/actions/runs/38354688886) — SUCCESS after adding the missing static module.
- Chaptera server package: [38354688751](https://github.com/Lalalalendia/rar2/actions/runs/38354688751) — initial 336/337 tests passed including new physical Axum Story module test; one unrelated quota lease heartbeat test expired under parallel load; single failed-job retry underway, no test budget/lease behavior weakened.
- CLOUD-B02 real OIDC/HTTPS PUB Story browser acceptance: [38354688683](https://github.com/Lalalalendia/rar2/actions/runs/38354688683) — in progress, *not* accepted.
- Required merge authority: [38354688854](https://github.com/Lalalalendia/rar2/actions/runs/38354688854) — blocked by current CI; recheck after exact physical receipts.

Root cause fixed from c556ccef: `/editor/story-line-endings-v1.mjs` returned HTTP 404 in both the synthetic Editor HTTP harness and real embedded Axum assets. This head embeds that exact existing module, adds the CSP/no-cache/nosniff route, manifest inventory and server integration test, and repairs the synthetic HTTP route. The two-parent merge preserves previously merged temporary-editor resource modules and independent work.
Earlier source-safe failures were diagnostic: run 38349157420 exposed textarea CR/LF normalization; run 38350839234 proved the over-strict no-control filter left Sample3 with no eligible Story. This head preserves the immutable terminal marker instead of weakening the writer guard.

### Explicit non-claims
This PR is one Chromium, one-scalar, plain-Story acceptance only. It does **not** close the full Notion task: no second browser engine, caret/IME/paste matrix, Story-group Undo/Redo, authoritative overset verdict, or authorized edited IDML/ODG download and target-consumer reopen. It is not Pilot/Production GO and does not claim native PUB Save.
